COBOL words
notes: kb/Work PB65 (2026-08-18): ONE screen (DataBinder.ScreenRepositoryIntrinsicName) asked by every declaration funnel — data-name, condition-name, index-name, file-name, paragraph/section name — rejects (COBOLNET1649) a user-defined word spelling an intrinsic-function-name the REPOSITORY identifies (FUNCTION name INTRINSIC, or every catalogued name under FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC); LENGTH/RANDOM/SIGN/SUM are reserved words already. A catalogued name the REPOSITORY does not identify stays a legal user-defined word (SQRT as a table, MOD as an item — the golden's control) and its FUNCTION-less spelling a data reference. Editions: the REPOSITORY function-specifier is 2002+ (85 has no REPOSITORY).

subject: COBOL words
notes: An externalized name may be referenced as program-name in a CALL statement: every arm of the 8.4.6.3 scope search matches Node.CallName, the externalized name, per 14.9.4.4 GR3 b)'s routing through 8.3.2.2. Identical to Node.Name for a program with no AS phrase. kb/Work PB303.

subject: COBOL words
notes: The CANCEL half of the same reference site: ProgramTable.Cancel resolves through the identical ResolveVisible, so CANCEL matches the externalized name for the same reason and by the same code. kb/Work PB303.

subject: COBOL words
notes: The program-address-identifier's ENTRY operand: 8.4.3.13 GR1/GR2 already say 'the outermost program identified by the externalized program-name', and EntryOf now matches - and the returned ProgramPointer now carries - Node.CallName. kb/Work PB303.

subject: COBOL words
notes: An externalized name may be referenced as method-name in an INVOKE statement. 14.9.23.2 gives INVOKE no word form for the method at all - only literal-1 or identifier-2 - and 14.9.23.4 GR2 a) routes that literal through 8.3.2.2, so the method roster is keyed on OoMethodSymbol.ExternalizedName. The golden invokes by the AS literal and reaches the method; the declared method-name does not resolve, which is what this rule requires. kb/Work PB303.

subject: Numeric literals
notes: The lexer's FLOAT_BODY (and its DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA twin FLOAT_COMMA_BODY, kb/Work PB98) is exactly the form — a fixed-point literal, the letter E without intervening spaces, a fixed-point exponent; the sign-adjacent twins (function-argument regions, SUBSCRIPT mode) keep -1.5E3 one token (kb/Work R17).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). 'shall include a decimal point' is the lexer's shape (a point-less 1E10 is a user-defined word, §8.3.1.1 — it is diagnosed as an undefined name, which it is); 'from 1 to 36 digits' is checked at the ONE normalizer both funnels share (COBOLNET1661 — a 40-digit significand); a 36-digit significand seeds a floating-point numeric-edited item exactly (the golden's E1).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99), RANGE DETERMINATION REPLACED 2026-08-31 by owner decision D-B (kb/Work PB156 + PB195 + PB276). 'a maximum of four digits' - COBOLNET1661 for a fifth (1.0E12345, which used to reach Roslyn as an overflowing C# double literal, CS0594). The IMPLEMENTOR-DEFINED maximum / minimum exponent VALUE is documented in CONFORMANCE.md Sec.7 A.1 item 82 and enforced at compile time, and it is now ONE range for every statement position: the DECIMAL128 range, about 1E-6176 to 9.99E+6144, in EVERY arithmetic mode (ExpressionBinder.CheckLiteral) - so 1.0E+400 evaluates and 1.0E+9999 / 1.0E-9999 are COBOLNET1661. ⛔ THE PER-POSITION SPLIT THIS REPLACED is what the previous note published: a literal in a NATIVE arithmetic expression or statement was screened against binary64 (about 4.9E-324..1.8E+308, so 1.0E+400 was rejected) while the identical program compiled under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL. Two rules remain, and they are different rules rather than different positions: a VALUE clause on a FLOAT-* item keeps the RECEIVER's binary form (Sec.13.18.63.3 SR2 - 'permissible values within the range indicated by the PICTURE clause or the USAGE clause', and a FLOAT-* subject has no PICTURE; DataBinder.FitsBinaryFloat, which is that screen's only surviving caller), and a VALUE on a fixed-point or floating-point numeric-edited item has no bound beyond the receiver's PICTURE (PIC 9E+9999 VALUE 1.0E+9999). The two lanes are witnessed SEPARATELY: pb99-floating-literal-range carries only the VALUE-clause entries and pb99-floating-literal-range-statement only the statement ones, because the negative harness asserts that SOME diagnostic contains COBOLNET1661 and a shared file let the VALUE entries satisfy it alone.

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99). A zero significand with a nonzero exponent (0.0E+5), a negative zero significand (-0.0E+0) or a negative-signed exponent (0.0E-0) is COBOLNET1661 — in a VALUE clause, a level-88 and a statement alike (the ONE normalizer).

subject: Numeric literals
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB99), COMPLETED 2026-08-31 by owner decision D-B (kb/Work PB156 + PB195), and CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (kb/Work PB263 + PB264). D-B's claim recorded here was that the literal's value - significand x 10^exponent - is carried EXACTLY in EVERY position through ONE rendering, NumericRenderer.LiteralNum. THAT CLAIM WAS NOT TRUE OF TWO POSITIONS WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN, and this row's five goldens were all VALUE-clause or arithmetic-operand positions, so none of them could have contradicted it. The CALL argument lane and the INVOKE argument lane do not reach LiteralNum at all: they render operand text through the raw EmitText.UnscaledLit helper, which returned the literal's own source text as a binary64 Real NumX for the E-form. The generated C# then handed a double to ManagedPointer<long|Int128>.Cell(...) and did not compile - conforming source rejected by a raw Roslyn CS1503 with no COBOL diagnostic at all (measured both carrier arms). UnscaledLit now honours its own scaled-integer contract for BOTH notations via TryUnscaledParts, taking the (significand, power of ten) pair exactly and never expanding it to text; the CALL lane funnels both of its non-place arms through one carrier build, and the two new goldens pin the four-cell table (two notations x BY CONTENT / BY VALUE, all four displaying the same value) plus the INVOKE arm. The evidence set now covers the argument positions the word EVERY always claimed.

subject: Figurative constant values

subject: Figurative constant values

subject: Subscripts
notes: kb/Work PB201 (2026-09-04) closes the last unevidenced arm. All THREE determinations of GR1 are pinned separately. a) ALL - pb62 covers all three ranges GR1a defers to (a fixed OCCURS count, an OCCURS DEPENDING object, a dynamic-capacity current capacity) and the multi-dimension rightmost-varies-fastest order; the arm is vacuous at 85, which has no functions for which the subscript ALL is allowed. b) arithmetic-expression-1 - pb136 (compound expressions), pb41 (the integrality condition itself: a non-integer result raises EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT under checking ON, via CobolTable.OccScaled/CobolNum.HasFraction), and pb201_position_operand_carriers (the CARRIER axis - FLOAT-LONG, FLOAT-SHORT, PIC 9(20) COMP and BINARY-DOUBLE UNSIGNED operands each select their occurrence; every one emitted uncompilable C# before PB201). c) index-name-1 [+/- integer-1] - pb170 (E(IX)), pb50 (E(IX + 1)) and 85/index_name_r7_windows (T(IX + 1) at the 85 edition). The implementor-defined index-to-occurrence mapping GR1c reserves is the identity (an IndexCell holds the occurrence number). The renderer is not the adjudicator: any operand PositionRead cannot render routes to the D18 materializer, whose arithmetic-expression grammar decides admissibility - so a shape 8.8.1.1 does not admit cannot parse, and the drift test pins the carrier set to the runtime overload set in both directions.

subject: Subscripts
notes: kb/Work PB201 (2026-09-04). CobolTable.At is the ONE occurrence-number to element mapping and it is edition-independent - no edition branch - so the 1..n bound holds identically at every edition; ec_bound_subscript pins the NAMED condition under >>TURN EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT CHECKING ON with a USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION declarative and RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT. With checking OFF the reference continues into a re-defaulted scratch slot, the implementor choice 13.18.38.4 GR7 leaves open by making out-of-bounds occurrence content undefined, and the only posture COBOL-85 can take since it has no exception conditions. PB201 added the piece that was missing on the way IN: every wide carrier (an Int128 >18-digit item, an unsigned BINARY-CAPACITY container, and an alphanumeric image FromAlphanumeric decodes to up to 38 digits) now narrows through CobolNum.Position, which SATURATES. A plain (long) cast wraps, and a wrapped position can land back inside 1..n - turning a condition this rule requires to be detected into a silent wrong answer.

subject: Function-identifier
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB61 — the LENGTH/BYTE-LENGTH folds enumerated from the rule branches; one builder for a runtime-length group; SR6 decided from the definition before binding). SR6 'if a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows … the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments' — decided ONCE, from the DEFINITION (the catalog signature, or a REPOSITORY user function's USING formals — SR6 names function-prototype-name-1 too) and BEFORE any argument binds, on every route: FUNCTION UPPER-CASE (1:4) drew the §15.3 arity error (the empty list bound first; only RANDOM, MinArgs 0, reached the SR6 arm) and keyword-omitted UPPER-CASE (1:4) under FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC died as 'not defined' (the MinArgs guard sent it to the data path). Now COBOLNET1543 (SR6/SR8) on all of them; ResultRefMod no longer carries an SR6 arm. Negatives pb61-sr6-function-keyword-refmod (85+), pb61-sr6-keyword-omitted-refmod and pb61-sr6-udf-prototype-refmod (2002+); FunctionRefModSr6SweepTests sweeps the CATALOG — every argument-permitting row in both forms draws 1543 (never 1504/1639), every zero-argument row (CURRENT-DATE (1:8), the standard's own D.14.3.6 shape) does not.

subject: Reference-modification

subject: Reference-modification
notes: The POSITIVE half (a function-identifier IS admissible as identifier-1) and the NEGATIVE half (it shall be an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function) are both enforced. Before fix-queue PB8 the shape was a COBOL0001 parse error at every edition, so neither half could be reached. A non-conforming class is rejected with COBOLNET1629; national and alphanumeric results are covered by the golden, and the user-defined-function result reference-modifies through RefModPlace using the RETURNING item's own category.

subject: Reference-modification
notes: Found unenforced by the PB8 sibling sweep, not by PB8's own repro: MOVE A (3:4)(2:2) COMPILED CLEAN and silently returned A(2:2), because dataReferenceSuffix* admits unlimited ref-mods and the resolver kept only the first of each carrier while the DEFAULT-mode form outranked the SUBSCRIPT-mode one. subject: Reference-modification
notes: kb/Work PB201 (2026-09-04), completing kb/Work PB170/PB219. SR4 carries 8.8.1.1 to BOTH reference-modification bounds exactly as 8.4.2.3.2 carries it to a subscript, so the rule is enforced as one screen shared with the subscript arm rather than a second copy. ACCEPTED side: a compound arithmetic expression in either bound (pb8 - FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(...)(IX + 1:3); pb50 - (ZERO + 2:3)) and every legal numeric CARRIER in the position (pb201 - a FLOAT-LONG and a PIC 9(20) COMP leftmost-position, each of which emitted CS1503 before PB201). notes: Condition 1 of the compatibility determination - 'For each dynamic-capacity table in either group there is a corresponding table in the other group as specified in 8.5.1.12.2, Positional correspondence' - is the dynamic-capacity arm of the ONE positional walk (kb/Work PB204). Correspondence is 8.5.1.12.2 sentence 2's 'at least one of them is a dynamic-capacity table and they occupy the same relative byte positions within their groups', computed over DataItem.ByteWidth, which already carries 8.5.1.12.3's two collapse conventions by construction (a dynamic-length item is zero bytes; a dynamic-capacity table carries no Occurs so a parent sums one element). The relation is CONSULTED at the activation boundary 14.8.2.2 / 14.8.3.2 name, through OoConformance.DescriptionMismatch - the one comparator shared by the Format-2 CALL, CALL RETURNING and INVOKE. POSITIVE: pb204_vlg_boundary crosses a matched dynamic-capacity pair at position 3 and the callee's growth returns to the caller. NEGATIVE: pb204-nested-vlg-table-correspondence puts a dynamic-capacity table opposite a non-table at the same position and is rejected naming this rule. 8.5.1.12.2's last-sentence latitude (a dynamic-capacity table beyond the shorter group's last character corresponds to a space-filled fixed-length table) is implemented in VariableLengthCompatibility.Tail.

subject: Variable-length groups
notes: Condition 2 - 'For each pair of corresponding tables, these tables match, as specified in 8.5.1.12.3, Matching' - is the same walk's matching arm: 8.5.1.12.3 sentence 2's 'the byte length of their elements is equal and their elements are compatible', the second conjunct RECURSING into the same relation (VariableLengthCompatibility.Elements) because a table of variable-length groups is exactly the shape the condition exists for. Sentence 3's 'the dynamic-capacity table is considered to be the same length as the corresponding table' when only one side is dynamic, and sentence 4's single-element length when both are, are applied as the pair's position advance - a fact about a PAIR, which is why it cannot live on either item. POSITIVE: pb204_vlg_boundary's 3-byte elements match and the crossing recovers the callee's capacity by dividing the carried content by that element width. NEGATIVE: pb204-nested-vlg-element-width corresponds two tables of 3- and 4-byte elements and is rejected naming this rule.

subject: Variable-length groups
notes: Condition 3 - 'For each dynamic-length elementary item in either group there is a corresponding dynamic-length elementary item in the other group as specified in 8.5.1.12.2' - with 8.5.1.12.2 sentence 1's 'start at the same relative byte positions within their groups' as the correspondence and 8.5.1.12.3 sentence 1's 'Two dynamic-length elementary items always match, regardless of their definitions' as the matching. POSITIVE: pb204_vlg_boundary and pb204_vlg_invoke each pair a dynamic-length item across the boundary against a group whose FIXED members are split differently (1+2 against X(3), and 2+1 against X(3)), so the rule is observed to key on byte position and not on the declaration tree. NEGATIVE: pb204-nested-vlg-position (an argument/formal pair) and pb204-nested-returning-incompatible (a RETURNING pair, through 14.8.3.2) each displace the item by one byte and are rejected naming this rule.

notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB129): the _outermost final-transfer flag is now cleared by EVERY recursion - BoundNegate, BoundPower and BoundComputedOperand join BoundBinary - so a division under a unary minus, an exponent base or an operand wrapper computes at the D2 guard scale with truncation and the receiver's ROUNDED mode binds to the final transfer only (14.7.4.3 GR3-GR10; 8.8.1.2 r1's treated-as-a-single-operand). Pinned twice: (1/3) ** 0 under PROHIBITED is exactly 1.00 (the CA5 sibling - the leak reinstated the pre-CA5 spurious EC-SIZE-TRUNCATION), and (A/B) ** 2 = 1 * (A/B) ** 2 = 11.1111 (the leak made multiplying by one change the value).

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB158, landed 2026-09-02). The rule is GR2's four-rank hierarchy (1st unary +/-, 2nd exponentiation, 3rd multiply/divide, 4th add/subtract). The IMPLEMENTATION was already correct and is unchanged: powerExpression puts a full unaryExpression in its base position, so `- 2 ** 2` binds as (-2)**2. What was PARTIAL was the EVIDENCE - rank 1 over rank 2 was pinned NOWHERE, and it is the one rank whose answer differs from every mainstream language, so a regression would have looked like normal behaviour. tests/conformance/2023/pb158_arith_precedence_spine now pins all four ranks in one labelled golden with every expected value derived from GR2/GR3 rather than from a run: R1 `- 2 ** 2` = 4 (rank 1 over 2), R2 `2 ** 3 * 4` = 32 (2 over 3), R3 `2 + 3 * 4` = 14 (3 over 4), R4 `2 ** 3 ** 2` = 64 (GR3 left fold), R7 `8 / 4 / 2` = 1 (GR3 left fold on /), and R5/R6 as the parentheses-vs-precedence discriminator. It also replaces the previous evidence's dependence on pb69 T11, where the precedence fact was INCIDENTAL to a golden about the Int128 carrier and would have vanished silently if that expression were ever rewritten.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: Citation re-validated INDEPENDENTLY: `--check 8.8.1.2 "the order of execution of consecutive operations of the same hierarchical level is from left to right"` => OK §8.8.1.2 3). || UPHELD, with my own evidence rather than the adjudicator's. Derived first: every level left-folds, exponentiation included — the standard states no right-associativity exception for `**`, so `2 ** 3 ** 2` = (2**3)**2 = 64, not 512. READ: `ExpressionBinder.BindChain` is `foreach (var child in StatementBinder.Children(node)) { if (child is AddOpContext or MulOpContext) op = child.GetText()[0]; else { var x = BindExprCore(child, context); acc = acc is null ? x : new BoundBinary(acc, op, x); } }` — a strict left fold serving BOTH AdditiveExpressionContext and MultiplicativeExpressionContext; and `ExpressionBinder.BindPower` is `acc = BindExprCore(bases[0], context); for (int i = 1; i < bases.Length; i++) acc = new BoundPower(acc, BindExprCore(bases[i], context));` — the same left fold for rank 2. I ALSO CHECKED THE CHILD ENUMERATOR the adjudicator took on trust: `StatementBinder.Children` is `for (int i = 0; i < node.ChildCount; i++) yield return node.GetChild(i);` — plain index order, no filtering, so no operand can be skipped and no pair re-ordered. `CompileTimeExpressionEvaluator.EvalArith`, the only other walker of this tree, left-folds identically over `node.ChildCount`. || TEST EVIDENCE VERIFIED BY READING BOTH GOLDENS AND THEIR .out FILES, not by trusting the citation: (a) tests/conformance/2014/func_expr_arg.cob header says verbatim '** folds LEFT per 8.8.1.2 r3', its body has `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION MAX(2 ** 3 ** 2, 1)` and func_expr_arg.out asserts `POW=00064` — right-folding gives 512, so it discriminates rank 2 and cites this exact rule; (b) tests/conformance/2002/arith_standard.cob has `COMPUTE W1 = 2 / 7 * 7` into PIC 9V9(5) with hand-derived §8.8.1.5 arithmetic in the header, and arith_standard.out asserts `W1=200000` — `2/(7*7)` = 0.0408 would print 004081, so rank 3 left-to-right is pinned, in the SDIDI lane. Both are spec-derived (hand-derived expectations, ISO citations in the headers), neither is a differential, neither is nist:/characterization:/MatchesLegacy. Rank 4 (`A - B - C`) has no golden, but it is the SAME `BindChain` loop already discriminated at rank 3 by (b) — associativity is decided once, in the binder, and no renderer re-associates (I verified `CombineCore` emits self-parenthesized forms only). Rank 1 is prefix-unary, where 'left to right' has no content. || I ALSO CHECKED THE SUBSCRIPT FAST PATH, a second evaluator the adjudicator did not consider: `ReferenceResolver.RenderSegment` splices `+ - * / ( )` into C# text, and C# gives those operators the same precedence and the same left associativity as COBOL, and `**` has no case arm so it routes to the D18 materializer — so rule 3's ORDER holds there too. (That path's VALUE defect — C# integer division — is recorded against GR-8.8.1.2-1; it is not an ordering defect.) subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB158, landed 2026-09-02). The rule is Table 3's symbol-adjacency matrix. subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB136): both defects of the D10 transitional subscript evaluator closed. (1) The splitter's new-segment logic now handles a depth-0 '(' - after ')' or a literal it always opens a NEW subscript; after an IDENTIFIER the split is DECLARATION-INFORMED (a name with no OCCURS cannot be subscripted, so its '(' begins the parenthesized-expression subscript the spec's own NOTE 2 prints, while `DOG (BAKER (I) 3)` keeps BAKER's paren as its own subscript) - the rule-5 restructuring the batch-8 note asked for, threaded as an optional predicate so the intrinsic-argument caller keeps its exact behavior. PB41's scaled-operand routing caught only segments with scaled OPERANDS; the all-integer quotient was exactly the case it could not see.

subject: Arithmetic expressions
notes: CONFORMS as of 2026-08-03 (fix-queue PB28, landed this session). Rule 6 has three parts. r6a (zero base requires exponent > 0) and r6c (negative base requires an integer exponent) are mandatory 'shall' requirements setting EC-SIZE-EXPONENTIATION, Fatal in Table 14. MEASURED ACROSS EVERY REACHABLE COMBINATION, not sampled: native at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023, and ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL at 2023 - all five raise both legs and leave the receiver unmodified per SS14.7.5. Checked in the same pass rather than left to be discovered as a fourth leg.

notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-08-31 (owner decision D-C; kb/Work PB167), CORRECTED THE SAME DAY (kb/Work PB266). r3: 'When operand-2 is less than zero, the result shall be equivalent to the evaluation of the arithmetic expression (1 / (operand-1 ** FUNCTION ABS (operand-2)))' (cite.py --check verified, both halves). This is an EQUIVALENCE and not implementor latitude - r2's latitude is scoped 'When the value of operand-2 is greater than zero' - and under Sec.8.8.1.5.2's per-operation 34-digit rounding the reciprocal form is a DIFFERENT value from exp(-|p| x ln b): it carries one extra correctly-rounded division and no negated exp argument. ⛔ THE FIRST LANDING'S NOTE CLAIMED THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE CODE DID, in both of its sentences. It said the development 'develops every other negative exponent through the same SDIDI exp/ln core as the positive one, so the r3 identity holds by construction rather than by luck'; measured, it held in 21% of sampled cases, BY LUCK (2 ** -0.25 answered ...4762332146 where 1 / (2 ** 0.25) is ...4762332141). It also said 'the INTEGER arm has honoured it whole since PB145'; the past-loop-bound escape carried the sign INSIDE the exponent, so r3 held below |n| = 500000 and broke above it - a discontinuity at the loop bound. And no pin on the row could see either: pb167's two negative legs and MinusHalfExponent were all -1/2 (the one exponent PowCore short-circuited), pb145's B ** NN and MinusOne_...PastLongRange are base -1 (the |b| = 1 parity shortcut), and HalfPastTheLoopBound uses a POSITIVE exponent. THE CONSTRUCTION NOW: r3's reciprocal is written ONCE, at the top of Pow, over PowMagnitude(b, |operand-2|) - so every arm below it is r3-correct by construction, PowCore needs no -1/2 twin to keep in step, and the divergence is closed at the 34th significant digit where a relation between two SDIDI intermediates and an exact cancellation could both see it (pb167's R3GEN / R3PW7 / R3FAR / R3NEAR / R3DLT legs, and a 10-row unit theory spanning the non-integer, in-bound-integer and past-bound arms). ⚠ ONE VISIBLE CONSEQUENCE, pinned: an out-of-range negative exponent now takes its EC name from r3's own expression rather than from where the final value lands, because the operation that leaves the range is the INNER power. 2 ** -600000 reports EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW and 0.5 ** -600000 EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW; before the hoist they answered the other way round (pb145's R3OVER / R3UNDR legs). ⚠ r3 is an IDENTITY requirement, not an accuracy one, and honouring it COSTS accuracy here: the true 34-digit 2**-0.25 is ...4762332149, so the reciprocal form is 8 ulp out where the direct form was 3. That is why the fix is the literal expression and never a tolerance.

subject: Standard-decimal arithmetic

subject: Simple relation conditions

subject: I-O status
notes: kb/Work PB328, LANDED (the write halves; item 6 b) was kb/Work PB323 and item 6 a) 3. is measured here for the first time). RULE: I-O status = 37 for four distinct reasons, each checked separately. 6) a) 1. (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'the EXTEND or OUTPUT phrase is specified but the file will not support write operations': OK, 6) a) 1.) -- CONFORMS since PB328: FileConnector.Open asks HostFile.PermitsWrite for EXTEND and OUTPUT on a Present file before OpenCore. Measured on a worktree build at 17c11fd4 with three compiler-created files made read-only: BEFORE, OPEN EXTEND answered SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00' (the relative and indexed EXTEND arms only Attach(), so nothing probed writability) and the keyed WRITE that followed reported '00' before CLOSE lost it as '30'; AFTER, 37/37/37. OPEN OUTPUT was already 37/37/37 because the keyed OUTPUT arm eagerly calls RecordFraming.WriteStore. 6) a) 2. (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'the I-O phrase is specified but the file will not support the input and output operations that are permitted for the organization of that file when opened in the I-O mode': OK, 6) a) 2.) -- the status-side statement of 14.9.27.4 16); see GR-14.9.27.4-16 for the full forensic record. Measured BEFORE: SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00'; AFTER: 37/37/37. 6) a) 3. (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'the INPUT phrase is specified but the file will not support read operations': OK, 6) a) 3.) -- CONFORMS, and now MEASURED rather than assumed: the answer is neither the write probe (INPUT is deliberately outside it) nor GR3's presence short-circuit, because the file here is fully observable -- only the FILE is denied read while its directory stays listable, so File.GetAttributes succeeds and HostFile.Probe answers Present. It is the organization's own eager read -- the sequential StreamReader, the keyed Attach() -- whose UnauthorizedAccessException reaches '37' through FileConnector.Open's catch. Probed on a worktree build with icacls /deny :(R) on the data files themselves: OPEN INPUT answered '37' on sequential, relative and indexed, with GetAttributes succeeding on all three (so the presence probe was NOT the producer). This sub-case had been the unexamined premise of PB328's INPUT exclusion; it is asserted now because an exclusion resting on an unmeasured claim is how a gap ships. 6) b) (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'insufficient authority exists to access the file': OK, 6) b)) -- CONFORMS since kb/Work PB323: the three-state HostFile.Probe distinguishes an absent file from a present-but-unobservable one, FileConnector.Open answers 14.9.27.4 3) from it for INPUT/I-O/EXTEND, and FileRegistry.DeleteFile takes the same probe for 14.9.10.4 GR14/GR16. The clause's own caveat -- 'The ability to detect this is processor dependent' -- is honoured rather than leaned on: every arm detects. OVER-FIRE MEASURED for each producer: a read-only file still OPENs INPUT '00' on all three organizations, a writable file still opens I-O '00', and a NEW file under a directory this process may write but not list still opens OUTPUT '00' (14.9.27.4 18) makes OUTPUT a creation that never consults presence). COVERING TESTS: unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests establishes every precondition for real -- a read-only attribute or mode 0400 for the write cases, a DACL deny ACE or mode 000 for the observation cases, a file-level deny-read for 6) a) 3. -- and verifies each with a raw stream open rather than with the subject under test; on a host that cannot deny anything to this process the class asserts POSITIVELY that this process is permission-bypassing, so a broken helper goes red instead of vacuously green. No conformance golden can reach any of these arms: the corpus runner compiles a .cob and compares its output, with nowhere to express the precondition. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 -- the '37' family is emitted at every edition and not gated (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3; Annex E.2 item 18 is a clarification that '37' is allowed, not a 2023 introduction).

subject: INITIALIZE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152), COBOLNET1727. 'Hexadecimal-alphanumeric literal' is a DEFINED TERM and the screen is written to it, not to a paraphrase: 8.3.3.2.2 gives the alphanumeric literal exactly two general formats - format 1 ("..." / '...') and format 2 (X"..." / X'...') - and 'hexadecimal-alphanumeric' names FORMAT 2, so a one-character format-1 literal such as "Z" is NOT admitted however short it is. One byte is exactly two hexadecimal digits (8.3.3.2.3 SR5). Before the screen the decoder took raw[0] for ANY shape, so INITIALIZE ALL TO "AB" silently became 'A'. The 2026-08-30 analysis that scoped this work carried the paraphrase 'a one-character alphanumeric OR one-byte hex literal', which would have shipped an under-reject; the printed page (PDF 307 / folio 277) was rendered and read to settle it. PB151's own golden pb151_options_fill was written with the format-1 spelling and is repaired to X"51" by this landing - 0x51 IS 'Q', so its expected output is unchanged byte for byte.

subject: INITIALIZE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152). All five GR5 arms. ⛔ GR5 b/d resolve through FigurativeConstants.FillChar - the compiler's ONE definition of the alphanumeric high and low value, which 8.3.3.6.4 GR6 makes a PROGRAM-COLLATING-SEQUENCE-dependent fact rather than a constant - and NOT through a second map. One rule, two places, two answers, and the arm with the private copy was the one that disagreed with the rest of the compiler. GR5 a is kept SEPARATE from GR5 d on purpose: 'a string of binary zeros' is the literal zero byte while 'the alphanumeric low value character' is the collating minimum - they coincide natively and diverge under a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE. pb152_options_initialize_arm_agreement asks all three consuming arms the same HIGH-VALUES question in one program.

subject: INITIALIZE clause
notes: LANDED 2026-09-02 (PB152). GR6's second sentence - with no INITIALIZE clause the content of items without predefined initialization values 'is undefined or specified by the implementor' - is what makes PicInfo.DefaultInitializer's space/zero seed a conforming choice, and it stays EXACTLY that seed: FillFor returns null when the clause is absent, so the whole no-clause population (every program in the corpus) is byte-unchanged. That invariant is a unit test rather than an assumption, because a regression in it is a corpus-wide wrong answer. The determination is documented in CONFORMANCE.md as required by 4.2.16.

subject: INTERMEDIATE ROUNDING clause
notes: || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

notes: LANDED 2026-08-17 (with PB60 / AR-15.67.3-5). subject: Configuration section
notes: LANDED 2026-08-17 (with PB60 / AR-15.67.3-5). The container's configuration section applies to each directly or indirectly contained program: DataBinder.InheritConfiguration copies the whole configuration-derived state (SPECIAL-NAMES — DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA, CURRENCY SIGN, CLASS names, ALPHABETs, switch mnemonics and status condition-names; OBJECT-COMPUTER's PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE; SOURCE-COMPUTER's DEBUGGING MODE; the REPOSITORY function/intrinsic/property specifiers) into every containee before it binds; the device-name mnemonics (Format 4, DISPLAY UPON / ACCEPT FROM) were already inherited by MnemonicRegistry's enclosing-unit walk — a second, tree-walking mechanism for the same rule, correct today and noted for folding into InheritConfiguration when the environment division gets a bound model. Implicit entries (the implied CURRENCY SIGN '$', the native alphabet) inherit as the defaults. Goldens: the 2023 one (six SPECIAL-NAMES/OBJECT-COMPUTER legs through a contained program, plus OPTIONS) and the 85 one (the edition-invariant five).

subject: File control entry
notes: ALL FOUR SENTENCES OF GR3 MEASURED. (1) The TIMING lead - "The association occurs at the time of execution of an OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement that referenced file-name-1" - is FileRegistry.OpenCore's single Associate call, ahead of the Table-19 arbitration and OUTSIDE the RETRY loop (the content is read once per statement, not once per attempt); the SORT/MERGE implicit opens reach the same dispatch through CobolFile.OpenInput/OpenOutput. pb324_assign_using_dynamic moves two different names into data-name-1 and reads both files back through ONE connector, and its DELB=00 leg proves DELETE FILE acts on the association the last OPEN established rather than re-resolving. (2) GR3 a) - device-name-1/literal-1 "in the source unit that specifies the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement" - is the non-dynamic arm of FileConnector.Associate(spec, dynamic), which the emitter feeds with the EXECUTING unit's own ASSIGN target rather than with whatever was registered first. (3) GR3 b) - data-name-1 "in the runtime element that executes the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement" - is the dynamic arm, and the two PB673 goldens are what discriminate it: pb673_external_assign_executor has TWO programs describing ONE external file connector (13.18.22.4 GR4 a), the second activating LAST and the first executing the OPEN, and pins that the record lands in the EXECUTOR's file (CHKB=05, CHKA=00, READA=AAAAA); pb673_recursive_assign_linage does the same across ACTIVATIONS of one RECURSIVE unit whose data-name-1 is in LOCAL-STORAGE (CHKI=05, CHKO=00). Before kb/Work PB673 both answered with the last INSTALLER's data item, silently, at status 00. (4) The closing sentence - the statement is unsuccessful when the association cannot be made - is 9.1.13.6 item 2's '31', pinned by pb324_assign_using_dynamic's BLANK=31 leg. The CONTENT rules that decide when it cannot be made are GR4's implementor determination, adjudicated on its own row (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-73 / DOC-A.1-10). Edition-invariant: 12.4.5.3 GR3 is unchanged across 85/2002/2014/2023, and the 85 arm rides conformance:85/pb324_assign_using_85.

subject: ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause
notes: GAP -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB193) - the ALTERNATE-key twin of GR-12.4.5.12.4-3, and it carries a SECOND requirement that one does not: 'The number of alternate record keys for the file shall also be the same as that used when the physical file was created.' Both halves are now recorded and compared. IndexedConnector.CatalogKeys writes every alternate key's window, DUPLICATES phrase, 12.4.5.6.4 GR6 SUPPRESS WHEN value and collating sequence into the catalog in declaration order (the order key numbers are assigned in), and FixedFileAttributes.Conflicts compares the key COUNT before the descriptors, so an added or missing alternate index is itself the 14.9.27.4 GR10 file attribute conflict condition and the OPEN is unsuccessful with '39'. The descriptor's scope and its derivation are the same as GR-12.4.5.12.4-3's. Pinned by open_fixed_attribute_conflict_ix step I3: a connector whose prime key agrees but which declares an ALTERNATE RECORD KEY the file was never built with gives '39'.

subject: LOCK MODE clause
notes: OWNER DECISION, kb/Work PB371, 2026-09-02 — CONFORMS + a witness pinning the refusal. §12.4.5.9.3 SR1 forbids the LOCK MODE clause "for a file that is the subject of an APPLY COMMIT clause". The LOCK MODE clause is CLAIMED; the antecedent is the APPLY COMMIT clause (ISO §12.4.6.3), Annex A.4.3 item 2 of the declined commit-and-rollback module, which COBOLNET1709 refuses BY NAME at every site (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §4 item 2, §5 row A.4.3). No compilable program can create the antecedent, so the rule is vacuously satisfied and holds. ⛔ NOT DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT: this rule's subject is LOCK MODE, a facility A.4.7 claims, and §4.2.7 discharges non-support through user documentation that declines COMMIT AND ROLLBACK — never LOCK MODE. The `commit-and-rollback-only` derived selector NAMES this row and deliberately excludes it for that reason. Editions is 2023 because the APPLY COMMIT clause is a COBOL-2023 addition (Annex E.3.2 item 2). The witness writes the rule's OWN forbidden pairing, so the verdict is forced back to a real adjudication the day A.4.3 is claimed.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "The RECORD DELIMITER clause may be specified only for variable-length records" is NOT enforced, and the licence is express rather than inferred. §4.2.6 ¶3, second sentence: "Although this warning mechanism shall identify processor-dependent elements that are not supported, it is not required to diagnose syntax errors within this unsupported syntax" (cite.py --check OK). The clause is unsupported whole — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 26 for the STANDARD-1 arm (Annex A.3 item 26) and §7 A.1 item 150 for the feature-name arm — and COBOLNET1778 names it at every edition, which is the obligation §4.2.6 ¶3 does impose. Enforcing SR1 anyway was considered and REJECTED as a rejects-legal-source risk, not skipped: SR1's own NOTE makes variable-length-ness partly an implementor determination (A.1 items 147-148, both still open), and §9.1.7.2 makes a LINE SEQUENTIAL file's records variable with no RECORD clause written at all, so a test keyed on FileModel.Varying would refuse legal source in order to enforce a rule the standard excuses. The golden's four files are all SR1-legal (RECORD IS VARYING), so nothing here depends on the unenforced case.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "The implementor shall specify the names available for use as feature-name-1" is DISCHARGED, and discharged in the negative: the set specified is EMPTY, filed as docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 Annex A.1 item 150. That is a specification and not an omission — A.1's preamble classes item 150 as optional and defines the class as "Optional: The element may be provided at the implementor's option" (cite.py --check A.1 OK). The compiler agrees with the register: every spelling written in the feature-name-1 position draws COBOLNET1778 naming the clause as unsupported, so no word is silently accepted as a delimiter selector and §12.4.5.11.4 GR4 never has a method to look up. The DOC row for the same obligation is DOC-A.1-150, whose verdict differs by design — that row asks whether the OPTIONAL ELEMENT is provided (it is not), this row asks whether the implementor answered the question (it did).

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "Any method used shall not be reflected in the record area or the record size used within the function, method, or program" is the rule that makes this implementation's method admissible, and the golden measures it directly. Records of 3 and 8 bytes are written to four variable-length files and read back; §13.18.43.4 GR15 stores the byte count of the record just read into the DEPENDING item, and the count read back is 03 then 08 on every file — the 4-byte little-endian length prefix (Annex A.1 item 151) is stripped before the record area is filled and never enters a record size the program can see. The DEPENDING item is deliberately forced to 99 before each READ so the measurement is GR15's stored count and not the leftover MOVE that sized the WRITE, and the displayed text is reference-modified to the reported length so nothing depends on what a short READ leaves in the tail of the area.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "If STANDARD-1 is specified, the external medium shall be a tape drive" is unsatisfiable here and the non-support is documented: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 26, whose ground is Annex A.3 item 26 — "The STANDARD-1 phrase of the RECORD DELIMITER clause is dependent upon a reel type of device" — and §4.2.6, which makes the decision to claim a processor-dependent element the implementor's, requires the absence to be specified in user documentation (this row), and adds that "Language elements that pertain to specific processor-dependent elements for which support is not claimed need not be implemented" (all cite.py --check OK). COBOL.NET provides no reel device at all — the same determination §2 rows 28-30 and 33-34 already record for CLOSE REEL/UNIT and OPEN WITH NO REWIND. The row closes on a DIAGNOSIS, not on silence: COBOLNET1778 is raised at bind for every occurrence at 85/2002/2014/2023, in both the IS and the optional-word-omitted spelling.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "If STANDARD-1 is specified, the method used for determining the length of a variable-length record shall be that specified in ISO/IEC 1001:2012, 7.1.2" rides GR2's decline: the method is the tape-interchange framing of a standard this implementation neither implements nor could exercise, having no reel device (docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 26, Annex A.3 item 26). §4.2.6's "Language elements that pertain to specific processor-dependent elements for which support is not claimed need not be implemented" is the carry-over licence — the §4.2.6 analogue of Annex A.4.1's second paragraph, and it is what reaches from item 26's PHRASE to this rule. What happens instead is §12.4.5.11.4 GR5's implementor method, documented as Annex A.1 item 151 in §7. Witnessed by the named decline at every edition rather than by silence.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "If feature-name-1 is specified, the method used for determining the length of a variable-length record is that associated with feature-name-1 by the implementor" has an EMPTY domain here, and that is a documented posture rather than a gap. The licence is NOT Annex A.3 — item 26 reaches only the STANDARD-1 phrase — but Annex A.1 item 150, which the standard classes as optional ("This item is optional"), read with A.1's preamble ("Optional: The element may be provided at the implementor's option") and §4.2.7's obligation to identify what is claimed. docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 A.1 item 150 records the determination as "Not provided.", which is exactly the shape owner decision kb/Work PB280 Q1 (2026-09-02) closes as DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT through the `a1-optional-not-provided` selector. The row closes on a diagnosis: a feature-name written anyway draws COBOLNET1778 by name at every edition.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "If the RECORD DELIMITER clause is not specified, the method used for determining the length of a variable-length record is specified by the implementor" — specified, and now documented, as Annex A.1 item 151 in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7: a 4-byte little-endian binary length prefix per record for record sequential, relative and indexed files (one implementation, RecordFraming, shared by every organization), and the line delimiter for LINE SEQUENTIAL, which is §9.1.7.2's own rule. The licence to add a header at all is §9.1.7.2 ("In record sequential files the length of each record is determined by any information the implementor may add to the record on the physical storage medium (such as record length headers)"); the §9.1.13.6 "externally-defined boundaries" sentence that RecordFraming's header used to cite is the I-O status 34 rule about writing past a FILE's end and was corrected in this change set. GR5's ANTECEDENT is witnessed directly: golden file F4 writes no RECORD DELIMITER clause, draws no diagnostic (asserted as the complement) and reads its 3- and 8-byte records back at those lengths.

subject: RECORD DELIMITER clause
notes: "At the time of a successful execution of an OPEN statement, the record delimiter is the one specified in the RECORD DELIMITER clause in the file control entry associated with the file-name specified in the OPEN statement" — no delimiter is established at OPEN, because neither alternative of the clause is supported (GR2/GR3 by Annex A.3 item 26 and §4.2.6; GR4 by Annex A.1 item 150 and §4.2.7). §4.2.6's "Language elements that pertain to specific processor-dependent elements for which support is not claimed need not be implemented" carries the decline to this rule. What the OPEN does establish is §12.4.5.11.4 GR5's implementor method, and the golden shows it holding across an OPEN OUTPUT / CLOSE / OPEN INPUT round trip on all four files — identically whether the clause was written or not, which is what §12.4.5.11.4 GR1 guarantees a program can see. Nothing is captured on FileModel for this clause, deliberately: a stored delimiter nothing reads would be a lookup no test could ever contradict.

subject: RECORD KEY clause
notes: GAP -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB193). The rule - 'The data description of data-name-1 or data-name-2 as well as their relative location within a record shall be the same as that used when the file was created' - states a requirement and no consequence where it is written; 14.9.27.4 GR10's file attribute conflict condition is the mechanism that detects a violation, and until the persisted fixed-file-attribute catalog landed there was nothing recorded to compare against, so the rule had no effect at all. NOW: IndexedConnector.CatalogKeys puts the prime key's byte window into the catalog written when the OPEN statement creates the file (GR18 / GR17), FixedFileAttributes.Conflicts compares it on every later OPEN, and a mismatch is the unsuccessful OPEN with I-O status '39' (9.1.13.6 item 7). THE RECORDED DESCRIPTOR IS THE KEY'S WINDOW PLUS ITS COLLATING SEQUENCE, and that is the whole of 'the data description ... as well as their relative location' this implementation can act on: 12.4.5.12.3 SR2 confines a record key to category alphanumeric or category national, 12.4.5.12.4 GR1 makes key equality a relation condition under the file's collating sequence (recorded, by weights - FixedFileAttributes.Fingerprint), and both native sequences are one code-unit ordinal over the UTF-16 substrate (CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-33 / DOC-A.1-188), so two descriptions sharing a window and a sequence order every key value identically whatever their category. Pinned by open_fixed_attribute_conflict_ix step I2: a six-byte prime key window over a file created with a four-byte one gives '39'.

subject: SAME clause
notes: OWNER DECISION, kb/Work PB371, 2026-09-02 — CONFORMS + a witness pinning the refusal. §12.4.6.4.3 SR11: "A file or record area that is subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause shall not be specified with another file or record area that is not subject to an APPLY COMMIT clause." The SAME clause (§12.4.6.4) is CLAIMED and supported; the antecedent is the APPLY COMMIT clause, Annex A.4.3 item 2, refused by name (COBOLNET1709). No accepted program can put a file in an APPLY COMMIT clause, so the rule cannot be violated. ⛔ NOT DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT — the verdict field would speak about SAME, a claimed facility; see the `commit-and-rollback-only` selector, which names this row among its exclusions. Editions 2023: the APPLY COMMIT clause is a COBOL-2023 addition (Annex E.3.2 item 2).

subject: SAME clause
notes: OWNER DECISION, kb/Work PB371, 2026-09-02 — CONFORMS + a witness pinning the refusal. §12.4.6.4.4 GR3: "The file and record area of a file subject to commit and rollback may not be shared with another such file or record area unless it has been closed, a commit or a rollback has been executed and the APPLY COMMIT clause for the file has been deactivated." ⚠ ITS SHAPE IS NOT SR-12.4.6.4.3-11'S and it therefore gets its OWN witness: SR11 forbids mixing a commit-subject file with one that is NOT subject, while GR3 says "another SUCH file" — BOTH files subject to commit and rollback. The SAME clause (§12.4.6.4) is CLAIMED and supported; the antecedent is the APPLY COMMIT clause (ISO §12.4.6.3), Annex A.4.3 item 2, refused BY NAME by COBOLNET1709, so no file is ever subject to the facility and the rule cannot be violated. ⛔ NOT DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT: the verdict field would speak about SAME, a claimed facility, and §4.2.7 discharges non-support through user documentation that declines commit and rollback — never SAME. The `commit-and-rollback-only` derived selector names this row among its exclusions for that reason. Editions 2023: the APPLY COMMIT clause is a COBOL-2023 addition (Annex E.3.2 item 2).

subject: File description entry
notes: Annex A.4.8 (items 1 FORMAT clause §13.18.24, 2 SELECT WHEN clause §13.18.51) is an OPTIONAL language element (§4.2.7) for which no support is claimed — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 Annex A.4 table, row 'A.4.8 | FORMAT and SELECT WHEN file handling | Not claimed', which is the WHOLE of the §4.2.7 user documentation for this module (§4's four documented-non-support facilities are MCS, commit/rollback, VALIDATE and screen handling — there is no §4 item for A.4.8, so no §4 reference may be invented). Annex A.4.1 carries the licence from the two named clauses to every associated rule: 'Any associated syntax rules, general rules, other rules, exception conditions, and I-O status values are also optional, even if not explicitly listed.' The row closes on a DIAGNOSIS, not on silence: conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-declined; conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-choice-combination; conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-no-optional-word. COBOLNET1705 is raised at bind for EVERY occurrence and is an Error, not the COBOLNET1560 accept-inert band, because an inert FORMAT changes which bytes reach the medium (§13.18.24.4 GR1) and an inert SELECT WHEN selects the wrong record description entry (§13.18.51.4 GR1) — a wrong answer, not a missing facility. Measured 2026-09-02: refused at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 and under --permissive.

subject: Data description entry
notes: Format 1's level-number domain, enforced as the intersection of two independent screens rather than a fourth copy of a set: the 13.18.33.3 section screen bounds the VALUE, and the 13.18.33.4 GR2b/GR2c format arms remove 66 and 88 from any entry that is not written in the renames or condition-name format. What is left for a format-1 entry is exactly 77 or 1 through 49. The 2023 positive is the over-rejection guard proving the legal 66, 77 and 88 shapes still compile.

subject: Data description entry
notes: Both spellings of the failure are witnessed, because SR4 makes them one rule: an explicit FILLER at level 77, and an OMITTED entry-name, which SR4 says is 'as though the filler format of the entry-name clause were specified'. A screen testing only for the literal word FILLER would pass the second.

subject: Data description entry
notes: All three legs verified against the pinned compiler. `01 A PIC X(4). 01 B REDEFINES A BASED PIC X(4).` -> COBOLNET0881 'BASED and REDEFINES may not be specified together'. `... REDEFINES A CONSTANT RECORD ...` -> COBOLNET1549 quoting SR3 verbatim. `... REDEFINES A IS TYPEDEF ...` -> COBOLNET1529 'the TYPEDEF and REDEFINES clauses are mutually exclusive'. Editions: BASED, CONSTANT RECORD and TYPEDEF are all post-1985 clauses, so at --std 85 the rule has no reachable subject (the clauses themselves are edition-gated by VersionConformancePass ParseArm). Test coverage is partial: the named negative pins only the BASED leg; the CONSTANT-RECORD and TYPEDEF legs are probe-verified with no repo test. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#BindEntry (CONSTANT RECORD arm ~2742-2765, COBOLNET1549 citing SR3; BASED arm ~2821-2826, COBOLNET0881) + DataBinder.cs#RegisterTypeDecl (~757-759, COBOLNET1529)

subject: Data description entry
notes: kb/Work PB486 — TWO of the rule's four obligations hold, TWO are enforced nowhere. HOLD: (i) 'the entry-name clause shall immediately follow the level-number' — the grammar shape `levelNumber dataName? dataDescriptionBody DOT` admits the entry-name in no other position; (ii) 'If no entry-name clause is specified, it is as though the filler format ... were specified' — BindEntry's `isFiller = cobolName is null || FILLER`; (iii) 'If the TYPEDEF clause is specified, the data-name format ... shall also be specified' — RegisterTypeDecl rejects an unnamed TYPEDEF (COBOLNET1529). FAIL: 'The REDEFINES clause ... shall immediately follow the entry-name clause' and 'the TYPEDEF clause shall immediately follow the entry-name clause'. `01 B PIC X(4) REDEFINES A.` and `01 T PIC X(4) IS TYPEDEF.` both compile and RUN clean at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 (probes p_sr4_redef.cob / p_sr4_typedef.cob). The clause list is a set, not a sequence, and nothing re-reads the written order. See finding data-description-entry-p2/F1. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4#dataDescriptionEntry:212 + #dataDescriptionClauses:266 (`dataDescriptionClause*` — position-blind); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#BindEntry:2186 (clause `foreach` at ~2228, order-insensitive); #RegisterTypeDecl:745

subject: Data description entry
notes: kb/Work PB519 — The BASED leg is enforced and cites SR5 verbatim (`01 B IS EXTERNAL BASED PIC X(4).` -> COBOLNET0881). The REDEFINES leg is enforced NOWHERE and is not merely permissive: `01 A PIC X(4) VALUE "ABCD". 01 B REDEFINES A IS EXTERNAL PIC X(4).` compiles clean and `DISPLAY A` prints four SPACES at every edition — CallBindExternalAndGlobal re-bases the redefines ANCHOR's whole class onto the run-unit ExternalStore cell (its own comment: 'an EXTERNAL record that is also a redefines anchor folds its whole class onto the shared backing'), so A silently loses its VALUE. Editions: the REDEFINES leg is live from 1985; the BASED leg from 2002. See finding data-description-entry-p2/F3. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#BindEntry (~2827-2836 — the BASED x EXTERNAL arm, COBOLNET0881, quoting SR5); no site anywhere for the REDEFINES x EXTERNAL half. src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Linkage.cs#CallBindExternalAndGlobal:328 is where the unscreened combination then does damage.

subject: Data description entry
notes: kb/Work PB518 — The CONSTANT RECORD half conforms and is pinned by a spec-derived negative: `05 H CONSTANT RECORD PIC X(4)` -> COBOLNET1549 'the CONSTANT RECORD clause may be specified only in a data description entry whose level-number is 1 (ISO §13.16.3 SR6)'. (1) ONLY HALF THE RULE IS IMPLEMENTED. 'Each condition-name is subordinate to THE data-name with which it is associated' asserts a relation with a positive and a negative side: the condition-name resolves through that data-name and its containing groups, and it resolves through NOTHING ELSE. The positive side is genuinely solid -- I widened the adjudicator's three probes to nine and every one is right: qualification by a NON-IMMEDIATE ancestor (`IS-A OF G1`, which the adjudicator never tried -- they only tried the negative `IS-A IN G2`), full qualification, a three-deep hierarchy where G, M and S each serve as qualifier, an 88 on a level-77 item, an 88 on a level-01 elementary item, an 88 on an alphanumeric GROUP, subscripting inherited from the conditional variable (`IS-X (1)` F / `IS-X (2)` T), SET through a non-immediate qualifier, and the ambiguity diagnostic COBOLNET1639 when two identically-named 88s make an unqualified reference non-unique. The NEGATIVE side does not exist. A condition-name reference qualified by a data-name it is NOT subordinate to is neither resolved nor diagnosed: `IF IS-A OF H1` (H1 an unrelated record that has no IS-A), `IF IS-A OF T` (an unrelated elementary item), `IF IS-A OF G2 OF G1` (both names real, no containment between them) and `IF IS-A OF G1 OF S` (real ancestors in REVERSED hierarchical order, which 8.4.2.2 forbids) ALL compile clean, exit 0, and emit `NotImplemented.Value<bool>("condition 'IS-AOFH1'")` into the generated C# -- a run-time NotImplementedCobolFeatureException. `SET IS-A OF H1 TO TRUE` likewise compiles clean, emitting `NotImplemented.Run("SET 'IS-AOFH1' TO TRUE (not a condition-name)")`. This is the two_arm_dispatch shape and I measured both arms side by side in ONE program: the DATA-name arm has the failure branch -- `MOVE "C" TO ST-CODE OF NOSUCHREC` gives COBOLNET1639 "'ST-CODE' is declared, but not under the given qualifier (NOSUCHREC)" -- while the CONDITION-name arm, the arm this rule is about, has none. So the compiler enforces subordination for data-names and merely PERMITS it for condition-names. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL. (The fallback is shared with an entirely undeclared name -- `IF NO-SUCH-COND` and `SET NO-SUCH-COND TO TRUE` behave identically -- so the missing branch is one place: the condition-name arm of the qualifier walk in ReferenceResolver, which the adjudicator itself named as this row's code-location.)
(2) THE CITED TEST CANNOT FAIL FOR THIS RULE'S REASON, so the test-ref must be cleared to empty. conformance-test:TypedefConditionTests.TwoRecordsQualifiedConditions_CompileClean asserts ONLY `ok == true` over a program whose condition-name content is `SET OPEN-ST OF DOOR TO TRUE` and `IF OPEN-ST OF DOOR AND CLOSED-ST OF GATE`. Because both of those statement forms degrade to compile-clean NotImplemented stubs when the condition-name does not resolve, I took that test's EXACT source, changed only the condition-name qualifiers to nonsense (`OPEN-ST OF NOSUCHREC`, `NOT-A-COND OF GATE`), and it still compiled clean at --std 2002, exit 0. Its only real teeth are the `MOVE "C" TO ST-CODE OF GATE` line -- a DATA-name, which does have a failure branch -- so the test pins the TYPEDEF clone of ST-CODE, not condition-name subordination. It is a green gate with no power over this row (green_gates_arent_evidence), and it was also written for 13.18.58.4 GR1, a different question. With it removed the row has no closing test, which is fine and expected -- but it is now PARTIAL-untested, not CONFORMS.
Editions unchanged (85,2002,2014,2023): the qualified positive case behaves identically at --std 85, 2002 and 2014, and the missing negative branch is edition-independent.
Cosmetic defect noticed in passing, worth a sweep line: every qualified reference is rendered in diagnostics and in the NotImplemented feature string with the OF/IN separators stripped -- 'IS-AOFS', 'IS-AOFG2OFG1', 'ST-CODEOFNOSUCHREC' -- so the user is shown a name they did not write. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#BindCondition:2105 (`new Condition88 { Name = name, Parent = parent }` + `parent.Own88s.Add(cond)` — the condition hangs off its conditional variable, which is what makes it subordinate); the qualifier walk that consumes it is src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs

notes: kb/Work PB501 + PB502 — THE ASSOCIATION ITSELF IS IMPLEMENTED AND CORRECT. BindCondition builds a Condition88 {Name, Parent, Values} where Values is a list of (low, high) pairs -- singletons and THRU ranges -- and RenderCondition88 emits the disjunction of the membership tests, which is exactly 8.8.4.5 GR1/GR3 over the set GR3 says Format 3 carries. MEASURED E:/Temp/claude/E--CobolSharp/c609c011-7fda-4dbc-a369-a563a47cedd1/scratchpad/lane3/out-b3/probe/ddep3/p12c88.cob at --std 85 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023, identical on all four: single value (IS-ONE=F for WS-N=07), value set `VALUE 5 7 9` (IS-SET=T), range `VALUE 20 THRU 30` (IS-RANGE=F), a mixed set-and-ranges `VALUE 1 3 THRU 6 40 THRU 50` (MIXED4=T, MIXED45=T, MIXED2=F -- both ranges and the singleton all live), and SET condition-name TO TRUE writing the first literal back (WS-N=01, 14.9.39 GR6). p13c88.cob adds an alphanumeric singleton/range/set (A-ONE=F, A-RANGE=T, A-SET=T), a GROUP conditional variable (GRP-IS=T), a national one (N-IS=T) and a boolean one (B-IS=T). EDITIONS: level-88 condition-names with a value / value list / THRU range are core COBOL present in every edition the compiler targets; the probe is byte-identical at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023. TEST-REF LEFT EMPTY: no existing spec-derived conformance case was located whose expectations are computed from 13.16.4 GR3 / the Format-3 general format (the NIST corpus exercises level-88 heavily but nist: does not close a row). WHY PARTIAL: the compiler admits level-88 entries that match NEITHER general format, and the two failures are exactly the two constituents GR3 names. (a) THE VALUE HALF: `88 NOVAL.` has no value-clause, which Format 3 (`88 condition-name-1 value-clause .`) and Format 4 both make mandatory; BindCondition never checks that cond.Values is non-empty, RenderCondition88 joins an empty test list into the literal string `()`, and the build dies in Roslyn -- `error CS1525: Invalid expression term ')'` -- with no COBOL diagnostic (finding F2). (b) THE NAME HALF: `88 VALUE 1.` has no condition-name-1; Format 3 requires it and Format 5 of the VALUE clause (13.18.63.2, the content-validation-entry a Format-4 entry would need) requires the {INVALID|VALID} choice this entry lacks, so it is illegal at every edition -- BindCondition's first line `if (entry.dataName()?.GetText() is not { } name) return;` drops it silently and the program compiles clean, exit 0 (finding F3). (c) A THIRD leg touches GR3's 'range of values': `IN alphabet-name-1` is parsed by the grammar (`(IN IDENTIFIER)?` in valueClause) and then never read by BindCondition, so an alphabet-ordered range is evaluated in the native sequence -- finding F4, whose primary owner is 13.18.63.4 GR18 / 14.7.8, not this row. subject: BLANK WHEN ZERO clause
notes: kb/Work PB507 — UNDER-REJECTS at every edition. Probes (pinned cobol.exe, --std 85/2002/2014/2023, all identical): `01 WS-ALPHA PIC X(5) BLANK WHEN ZERO.` compiles clean and the clause is silently ignored (probe a1); `01 WS-SIGNED PIC S9(5) BLANK WHEN ZERO.` compiles and MOVE 0 leaves `0000{` rather than being rejected for the picture symbol 'S' (probe a2); `01 WS-GRP BLANK WHEN ZERO.` on a GROUP item compiles and is ignored (probe a4). The rule EXISTS in the legacy engine - src/CobolSharp.Compiler/Semantics/DataItemClassifier.cs:127 reports CBL0802 for exactly this - and was never carried into the typed-native binder, so the differential net cannot see it either (the legacy arm rejects, the greenfield arm accepts, and no greenfield test asserts the reject). Sibling witness for the same missing-validator mechanism: `01 WS-J PIC 9(5) JUSTIFIED RIGHT BLANK WHEN ZERO.` also compiles (probe c1) where the legacy engine reports CBL0804. See finding bwz-syntax-rules-unenforced. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:2306-2307 - the ONLY consumer of blankWhenZeroClause in src/Cobol.Net.*; it sets `blankWhenZero = true` and validates nothing. No sibling check exists anywhere in the typed-native tree (grep of `blankWhenZero|BlankWhenZero` over src/Cobol.Net.* returns only producers/consumers, never a diagnostic). || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85/2002/2014/2023

subject: BLANK WHEN ZERO clause
notes: kb/Work PB507 — UNDER-REJECTS at every edition. Probe a3: `01 WS-COMP PIC 9(5) USAGE COMP BLANK WHEN ZERO.` compiles clean at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 and the clause is silently dropped (MOVE 0 then DISPLAY gives `00000`, no blanking, no diagnostic). SR2 requires the subject be usage display or usage national; every other usage must be rejected and none is. Separately, the `usage national` half of the rule is currently UNREACHABLE: a numeric or numeric-edited PICTURE with USAGE NATIONAL is refused upstream as a Phase-4a residue - COBOLNET0899 via DiagnosticCatalog.NationalData, emitted at src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/PictureAnalyzer.cs:252 (probe a5) - which is owner-owned recognized-but-not-implemented non-support, not adjudicated here. Clustered into finding bwz-syntax-rules-unenforced with SR1 (same mechanism: the clause has no validator at all). || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:2306-2307 (no usage validation); the usage that reaches PictureAnalyzer.Analyze at src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:2591-2592 is never checked against display/national. || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85/2002/2014/2023 (the `usage national` arm is COBOL-2002 and later; at COBOL-85 the rule admits usage display only)

subject: BLANK WHEN ZERO clause
notes: kb/Work PB566 — Measured across every reachable receiving-operand path, and identical at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 (probe b1/b1_85): MOVE literal and MOVE identifier (probe a7 E[     ] P[     ], a9 SRC0[     ]); the figurative constant ZERO (b1 FIG); COMPUTE (a7 E3); SUBTRACT/MULTIPLY ... GIVING and DIVIDE ... GIVING ... REMAINDER (b1 GIV/GIVE/MUL/Q); VALUE ZERO initial content (a9 INIT-VALZ[     ]) and a no-VALUE item's initial content (a9 INIT-PLAIN); the INITIALIZE verb (a9 INIT-VERB); a table element under OCCURS (b1 TBL); an item cloned through TYPE/TYPEDEF and through SAME AS (c2); scaled, P-scaled and V-only pictures (c3 N/P/V); and the Report Writer SOURCE path (probe d1 writes `         END`, the 5-character BWZ column blank at a zero SOURCE). TEST-REF LEFT EMPTY DELIBERATELY: the only end-to-end test is tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/DecimalPointDifferentialTests.BlankWhenZero_OnPlainNumeric_StoresSpaces, which is AssertSameAsLegacy (a legacy differential, which cannot close a row); the one spec-derived assertion, tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/CobolLocaleEditTests.Format_BlankWhenZero_TakesPrecedenceOverLocaleEditing, exercises the LOCALE formatter (CobolLocaleEdit) and not the mainline CobolEdit.Format blankWhenZero branch, which has no spec-derived test at all. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The adjudicator measured only stores whose SENDING value is already zero (MOVE 0 / MOVE ZERO / an identifier holding zero) - the one axis GR1 holds fixed. Flipping it breaks the row: for a NONZERO sending value that STORES as zero, the MOVE arm does not blank while the arithmetic arm does, on identical items. GR1 obliges blanking 'when the item is a receiving operand and the value being stored is zero'; a PIC 9(3) item cannot hold 0.4, so the value stored is zero (the same truncated value the edit pipeline itself uses - proof: PIC ZZZ9 BLANK WHEN ZERO receiving 0.4 renders '   0', i.e. Z-suppression ran on the TRUNCATED 0 in the same Format() call whose BWZ guard tested the UNTRUNCATED 0.4). Mechanism: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolEdit.cs:79 tests `blankWhenZero && value == 0` on the raw (value, valueScale) pair, 37 lines BEFORE the mask rescale at :116 (`CobolNum.Rescale(value, valueScale, fracDigits, Truncation)`); the arithmetic emitters happen to hand it a value already at the resultant's scale, so COMPUTE/GIVING blank correctly and MOVE does not. Two-arm defect (feedback_two_arm_dispatch), and the refutation is robust to the interpretive question: under the opposite reading of 'the value being stored' (the SENDING value) the MOVE arm would be right and COMPUTE/ADD GIVING/DIVIDE GIVING wrong - so the row cannot be CONFORMS under either reading. Sibling not yet probed but visibly identical by reading: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolLocaleEdit.cs:87 `if (blankWhenZero && unscaled == 0)` also precedes its rescale, and its DeEdit at :237 shares the shape. PARTIAL rather than DIVERGES per the brief's 'two halves, one verified' rubric and for consistency with this file's GR-13.18.8.4-3 row, but the open half is a SILENT WRONG ANSWER on legal COBOL through the commonest verb in the language, not merely an unprobed edge. Identical at --std 85/2002/2014/2023. test-ref is empty, so nothing was over-claimed there; the row still cannot close. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolEdit.cs:78-79 (`if (blankWhenZero && value == 0) return new string(' ', pattern.Length);` - ahead of all editing) is the single formatter every store funnels through; the flag is threaded by src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/ArithmeticEmitter.cs:258 (BwzFlag), src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Roslyn/RuntimeApi.cs:1067 (EditCompose), src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/DataDivision/ValueInitializer.cs:238-244 and src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/DataDivision/GroupImageCodec.cs:93; the locale twin is CobolLocaleEdit.Format(..., blankWhenZero:). || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85/2002/2014/2023

subject: BLANK WHEN ZERO clause
notes: kb/Work PB508 — The usage-display arm CONFORMS and is measured three ways, not merely by reading the flag: `01 WS-PLAIN PIC 9(5) BLANK WHEN ZERO.` is rejected as an arithmetic RESULTANT with COBOLNET1675 citing ISO 14.9.2.3 SR2 (`ADD 0 TO WS-PLAIN`, probe a6) and as an arithmetic OPERAND with COBOLNET0844 citing ISO 8.8.1.1 (`COMPUTE WS-NUM = WS-PLAIN + 5`, probe a7) - both of which are only correct if the subject really is category numeric-edited - and the item edits and de-edits through the numeric-edited machinery (probes a7/a9). PARTIAL because the predicate hard-codes `usage is Usage.Display` where SR2 expressly admits usage NATIONAL as well: a `PIC 9(5) USAGE NATIONAL BLANK WHEN ZERO` subject would fall through to the plain-numeric return at PictureAnalyzer.cs:356 and never be defined numeric-edited. That arm is presently unobservable - national-form numeric data is refused upstream as a Phase-4a residue (COBOLNET0899 / DiagnosticCatalog.NationalData at PictureAnalyzer.cs:252, probe a5) - so this is a LATENT gap that will surface silently when national numeric lands, not a live wrong answer. See finding bwz-gr2-national-not-promoted. No spec-derived test discriminates the category: tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/ValueLiteralClassTests.LegalShapes_StillCompileStrict carries `01 A PIC 999 VALUE "000" BLANK WHEN ZERO.` but its expectation `[000]` is the same under either category, so it does not close this row. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/PictureAnalyzer.cs:342-352 - `if (anyEdit || (blankWhenZero && digits > 0 && !signed && usage is Usage.Display))` returns PicInfo with PicCategory.NumericEdited. || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85/2002/2014/2023 (the national subject is COBOL-2002 and later)

subject: BLANK WHEN ZERO clause
notes: kb/Work PB509 — TWO ARMS, ONE IMPLEMENTED. The MOVE / de-editing arm CONFORMS and is measured: a BLANK WHEN ZERO item holding all spaces sent to a numeric receiver yields zero (probe a7 N[00000]), to a signed scaled numeric receiver yields +0 (a7 N2[000000{], a9 DEEDIT-SIGNED[0000{]) and to a numeric-edited receiver yields the edited zero (a7 E2[     0.00]) - which is exactly what ISO 14.9.25.4 GR6d1 requires of a numeric-edited sender, and is only non-exceptional because GR3 makes all-spaces a possible editing result. The named test-ref asserts that arm at the locale formatter and cites 13.18.8.4 explicitly. The OTHER arm DIVERGES: GR3 says the value is considered zero whenever `the object of an operation is a numeric or numeric-edited data item`, and a relation condition's second operand is precisely what this standard calls the object (8.8.4.2.1). With `01 WS-PLAIN PIC 9(5) BLANK WHEN ZERO.` blanked and `01 WS-ZERONUM PIC 9(5) VALUE 0.`, `IF WS-PLAIN = WS-ZERONUM` is FALSE (probe a9 REL-NUMITEM-NE), and the same for a PIC ZZZ99 BLANK WHEN ZERO subject (REL-EDIT-NE); the compiler falls to 8.8.4.2.5 and compares the numeric operand as alphanumeric characters against five spaces. Note the drafting evidence for the broad reading: GR1 one rule earlier says `receiving operand` where GR3 deliberately says `the object of an operation`, and `object of an operation` occurs exactly ONCE in the whole standard (grep), so it is not a term of art for the MOVE receiver. See finding bwz-gr3-relation-condition. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolEdit.cs:271-325 (DeEdit - a space in a digit position contributes zero, and the EC-DATA-INCOMPATIBLE round trip at :319 is run WITH blankWhenZero so all-spaces is a legal editing result), threaded from src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Emit/NumericRenderer.cs:313-318. The DIVERGENT arm is src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Emit/ConditionRenderer.cs:178-180 - `if (OperandText.IsString(r.Left) || OperandText.IsString(r.Right)) return $"CobolString.Compare(...)"` - a numeric-edited operand is a STRING operand, so the whole relation is routed to the alphanumeric comparison before the numeric branch at :186 is ever reached; BlankWhenZero is consulted in this file only at :464 (StringMembershipExpr, the level-88 membership image), never to value an all-spaces sender as zero. || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85/2002/2014/2023

subject: CLASS clause
notes: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 row A.4.14 (VALIDATE — Not claimed) + §4 item 3, which already named CLASS a validation clause. Licence: Annex A.4.1, "An implementation shall accept the syntax and provide the functionality for an optional element only when support for that language element is claimed by the implementor", and its second sentence carrying the licence to the module's unlisted rules — which is the sentence CLASS needs, because Annex A.4 never LISTS this clause. OWNER DECISION, kb/Work PB375, 2026-09-02: the clause is DECLINED WITH VALIDATE, on §13.16.2's own ground — the printed Format-1 validation-clauses group opens with `[ class-clause ]` and maps it to "13.18.11, CLASS clause" (RENDERED, PDF p394 / folio 364) — and §13.18.11.1 leaves it no content outside the module. Refused BY NAME (COBOLNET1708) where it drew a bare "COBOL0307: unexpected 'CLASS'" before. Editions are the DATA-DESCRIPTION clause's band, not the word's: CLASS itself is reserved at all four editions (§12.3.7 SPECIAL-NAMES CLASS clause), so at --std 85 this entry is an ordinary syntax error rather than this decline.

subject: CLASS clause
notes: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 row A.4.14 (VALIDATE — Not claimed) + §4 item 3. Licence: Annex A.4.1 and its second sentence. OWNER DECISION kb/Work PB375, 2026-09-02 — the CLASS clause is DECLINED WITH VALIDATE. This rule is the clause's own statement of that confinement: "The CLASS clause takes effect during the content validation stage of the execution of a VALIDATE statement. The CLASS clause is ignored during the execution of any statement other than a VALIDATE statement." With no VALIDATE statement implemented there is no stage for it to take effect in, and the clause is refused by name (COBOLNET1708) rather than accepted and ignored.

subject: CLASS clause

subject: CLASS clause
notes: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 row A.4.14 (VALIDATE — Not claimed) + §4 item 3. Licence: Annex A.4.1 and its second sentence. subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19) — DETERMINATION, documented (CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 27): the sets whose implementor correspondence to the native set is the IDENTITY — NATIVE (§12.3.7.4 GR7 d, by definition), STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2 (GR7 c: the correspondence is implementor-defined, and the native set's first 128 characters ARE ISO/IEC 646 IRV), UTF-16 (the D-N1 substrate) — are CLAIMED, their conversion being the identity (the golden's byte-exact round trip); an alphabet whose on-medium representation would differ (a literal-phrase alphabet's remapped ordinals; UTF-8/UCS-4 as variable-width medium encodings) is the DOCUMENTED Annex A §A.3 item 27 non-support — COBOLNET1672, never a silent identity (the negative). Rule --check verified at 13.18.13.4 1).

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): on OPEN the on-medium coded character set is the referenced one — for every CLAIMED set that is the native encoding itself (the identity correspondence), which the golden's write-then-read round trip observes; a non-identity set never reaches OPEN (refused at compile time, GR-13.18.13.4-1's determination).

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: Annex A.4.8 (items 1 FORMAT clause §13.18.24, 2 SELECT WHEN clause §13.18.51) is an OPTIONAL language element (§4.2.7) for which no support is claimed — docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 Annex A.4 table, row 'A.4.8 | FORMAT and SELECT WHEN file handling | Not claimed', which is the WHOLE of the §4.2.7 user documentation for this module (§4's four documented-non-support facilities are MCS, commit/rollback, VALIDATE and screen handling — there is no §4 item for A.4.8, so no §4 reference may be invented). Annex A.4.1 carries the licence from the two named clauses to every associated rule: 'Any associated syntax rules, general rules, other rules, exception conditions, and I-O status values are also optional, even if not explicitly listed.' The row closes on a DIAGNOSIS, not on silence: conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-declined; conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-choice-combination; conformance:negative/a48-format-clause-no-optional-word. COBOLNET1705 is raised at bind for EVERY occurrence and is an Error, not the COBOLNET1560 accept-inert band, because an inert FORMAT changes which bytes reach the medium (§13.18.24.4 GR1) and an inert SELECT WHEN selects the wrong record description entry (§13.18.51.4 GR1) — a wrong answer, not a missing facility. Measured 2026-09-02: refused at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 and under --permissive.

subject: CODE-SET clause
notes: kb/Work PB110 (2026-08-19): without a CODE-SET clause the native character set is assumed for data on the external media — every file ever written by this compiler takes this rule (the Latin-1 boundary codec, COBOLNET_DESIGN §18 item 13); the golden's clause-bearing file behaves identically because its set's correspondence is the identity.
