subject: CONTROL clause
notes: The one grammar rule accepts both spellings - (CONTROL IS? | CONTROLS ARE?) - and nothing downstream can tell them apart, so they are synonyms by construction. Witnessed both ways: rw_suppress writes CONTROL IS, pb205_control_ref_mod writes CONTROLS ARE.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: kb/Work PB205. Previously rejected as a side effect under the WRONG rule: report-section names are not in the storage forest, so the operand failed ordinary name resolution and drew the 8.4.2.1 unresolved-operand diagnostic. SR2 now has its own arm on COBOLNET1699, asked only AFTER resolution fails - a name also declared in ordinary storage resolves there (8.4.2.1) and is not an SR2 reference, which is the 13.15.3 SR16 scan's own reasoning; both consumers share the one report-section-exclusive name set.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: The shape arm (kb/Work PB177 arm C) rejects an operand subject to any OCCURS clause, recognised with DataItem.IsTable so both dynamic-capacity shapes are covered. kb/Work PB205 added the WRITTEN half: a subscript on the operand was dropped at capture, and since SR3 bars the OCCURS case and 8.4.2.3.3 SR2 bars a subscript on an item without one, no subscripted control operand is legal - it is now rejected on the spelling, not only on the item.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: kb/Work PB205 - both halves of SR4. The PERMISSION: a reference-modified operand now binds as its slice, because the capture keeps the ref-mod (ReadOperandSuffixes reads both source carriers lexically) and the emitter builds the 8.4.3.3.4 GR5 unique data item through the one ref-mod view builder (ResolveItemRefMod over RefModView), so 13.18.16.4 GR3's prior control is the slice; before this the ref-mod was dropped and CONTROL IS CX(1:3) broke on all six characters, a silent wrong answer. The RESTRICTION: a leftmost-position or length that is not an integer literal is rejected (COBOLNET1699) - unscreenable while the ref-mod never reached the binder. The omitted length CX(4:) is 8.4.3.3.2's bracketed form and runs to the rightmost position (GR5c).

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: kb/Work PB177 arm C: OdoModel.TableUnder finds an occurs-depending table anywhere under the operand. It is a separate arm from SR7 on purpose - an occurs-depending table does NOT make a group variable-length (8.5.1.12 defines that over dynamic-length elementary items and dynamic-capacity tables), so SR7 cannot reach this shape.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: kb/Work PB205. Uniqueness is of the WRITTEN reference (ReportControlRef.SameOperandAs over name + qualifiers + ref-mod), which is what SR6's own second sentence forces: two operands may 'refer to the same physical data item or to overlapping data items', so the referenced item cannot be what distinguishes them - and 13.18.57.3 SR10 could not name a level unambiguously if it were. The positive golden is the legal shape the second sentence permits (CONTROLS ARE CX(1:3) CX(4:)); the negative is the same reference twice.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: kb/Work PB177 arm C: the variable-length-group test is 8.5.1.12's - a dynamic-length elementary item or a dynamic-capacity table subordinate to the group - read through the one predicate the reference resolver already uses for 8.4.3.3.3 SR1.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: The operands are captured in written order into ReportModel.Controls and emitted in that order as AddControl calls, so index 0 is the major control and the last is the minor. The golden proves the ordering behaviourally: its first operand CX(1:3) is the level whose footing prints last at a break and whose SUM covers both minor groups, while its second operand CX(4:) breaks on its own.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: The prior control is a saved character image per control operand (the emitted get/set pair over the operand's place); the chronologically first GENERATE saves without testing, later ones test major to minor and stop at the first change, and break processing runs for that level and every lower one. kb/Work PB205 made the SAVED item the right one for a reference-modified operand: GR3 gives the prior control 'the same data description as the corresponding data item', which for such an operand is the 8.4.3.3.4 GR5 unique data item - the slice - and the golden's two overlapping-item controls could not be told apart otherwise.

subject: CONTROL clause
notes: TERMINATE runs the same control-break processing as a highest-level break, so every defined control footing prints minor to major. The golden's last two printed lines are exactly that pair (MIN=070 RUN=070 then MAJ=070) with no further detail.

notes: kb/Work PB489 + PB524 — NO OCCURS SCREEN EXISTS. Note the SIBLING message at SequentialIoEmitter.cs:155 is not an enforcement of this rule: it fires only when the operand fails to resolve to STORAGE, so a table element is caught by accident while every non-table SR1/SR2 violation walks through (see SR-13.18.34.3-2). subject: LINAGE clause
notes:
kb/Work PB523 — FOUR CONJUNCTS, TWO IMPLEMENTED. (b) 'If the LINES AT TOP or LINES AT BOTTOM phrases are not specified, the values of these items are zero' - implemented: LinageOpExpr returns the literal "0" for a null operand. (c) 'If the FOOTING phrase is not specified, no end-of-page condition independent of the page overflow condition exists' - implemented (AdvanceLinageCounter's footing arm is guarded by `_footing > 0`) and covered by the named test. (d) 'There is not necessarily any relationship between the size of the logical page and the size of a physical page' - a permission, honoured vacuously. (a) 'The logical page size is the SUM of the values referenced by each phrase except the FOOTING phrase' - NOT implemented: `_top` and `_bottom` are assigned at :133 and READ NOWHERE (grep over the file returns exactly the declaration at :105 and that one assignment), so the logical page is the page body alone. MEASURED (<lane3 scratch>/out-b3/probe/linage/p1_margins.cob, `LINAGE IS 2 LINES LINES AT TOP 3 LINES AT BOTTOM 2`, three writes): the whole output file is `
AAAA
BBBB
CCCC
` - a 7-line logical page produced as a 2-line one, with no margin lines anywhere and ONE line of separation across the page wrap where the sum requires the page-1 bottom margin (2) plus the page-2 top margin (3). p23_sum.cob reproduces it on ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL. Finding: linage-margins-evaluated-then-discarded. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs:96-105 (the COUNTER-ONLY model comment and the write-only _top/_bottom fields), :126-134 (EvaluateLinage), :155-182 (AdvanceLinageCounter); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/SequentialIoEmitter.cs:145-147 (an absent phrase emits the literal 0)

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB489 — THE PAGE SIZE IS THE WRITABLE LINE COUNT, AND THE COUNTER MACHINE BOUNDS WRITES BY IT. Both operand forms reach _pageBody through the ONE evaluator closure (literal -> a constant lambda; data-name -> a field read), and AdvanceLinageCounter treats [1, _pageBody] as the page body: a write landing ON the page size stays on the page (named test asserts LINAGE-COUNTER 5 on a 5-line body) and the next one crosses. The 'page body' naming half is carried in the model and comments. COST DISCLOSURE: what GR2 gets right is the page body's SIZE; its POSITION within the logical page is wrong for any file with a top margin, but that is GR4's obligation, recorded there - GR2 itself is clean. Also covered by conformance-test:CobolNet.Tests.Conformance.LinageConformanceTests.Gr7c4_OverflowCrossing_ResetsToOneNotModulo. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED - MEASURED, REPRODUCED TWICE, AND SILENT. GR2's sentence is 'Integer-1 or THE VALUE OF THE DATA ITEM REFERENCED BY data-name-1 specifies the number of lines that may be written or spaced on the logical page. This number is called the page size.' Two of the three operand spellings are right; the third is not. When data-name-1 is QUALIFIED, the pinned compiler uses the value of a DIFFERENT data item, with no diagnostic, and the whole page model is then built on the wrong number. The mechanism is in the binder, not the runtime: DataBinder.BindLinageClause (DataBinder.cs:1103-1105) reduces the operand's dataReference to `d.cobolWord()?.GetText()` - the FIRST word only - throwing the IN/OF qualifiers away, and ResolveFiles (DataBinder.cs:1181-1184) then resolves that bare word with `ByName.TryGetValue(ln, out var llist)` -> `op.Item = llist[0]`, i.e. the first item of that name in declaration order. MEASURED: r1_qual.cob declares GRP-A.SZ = 3 then GRP-B.SZ = 9 and writes 'LINAGE IS SZ OF GRP-B LINES'; the correct page size is 9, so 'WRITE ... AFTER ADVANCING 4 LINES' from LINAGE-COUNTER 1 must land on line 5 with no overflow. It reports EOP and LC=001 - the behaviour of a 3-line page. The control r1b_qualok.cob is the SAME source with the 9 moved into GRP-A (the first-declared group) and it reports NO-EOP / LC=005, so the two runs differ only in declaration order, which is exactly the first-match signature. u3_qual2.cob reproduces it independently over a two-level hierarchy with a counter-only observable (OUTER-A..PG-SIZE = 2, OUTER-B..PG-SIZE = 30, 'LINAGE IS PG-SIZE OF OUTER-B LINES', AFTER ADVANCING 10): the correct LC is 011, measured LC=001. Same at --std 85, 2002 and 2014. The full compile output is EMPTY - not a warning - so this is a silent wrong answer. THE SPELLING IS NOT EXOTIC, IT IS MANDATORY: 8.4.2.2.1 says 'uniqueness shall be established through qualification for each user-defined name explicitly referenced' and 8.4.2.2.3 SR1 repeats it, so in a program with two items named SZ the qualified form is the ONLY legal way to reference either one; 8.4.2.2.3 SR2 permits qualification even where it is unnecessary. Nothing in 13.18.34.3 forbids qualifying data-name-1. WHY THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED IT: he found the mechanism (finding 'linage-operand-first-word-only', his own probe p17_qual.cob showing 'LINAGE IS SZ OF GRP-B ... behaves as page size 3') but attributed it to FMT-13.18.34.2, GR-13.18.34.4-7 and SR-13.18.34.3-1 only. None of those is the rule that says the page size IS the value of the item referenced by data-name-1. GR2 is that rule, it is the row a user's wrong page size traces to, and it was left CONFORMS with a cost disclosure about the page body's POSITION while the defect in its SIZE sat in the same dossier. His code-location is also incomplete: it names only the runtime consumers (SequentialConnector.cs:103/ 133/158/168, FileModel.cs:236-252) and never the two binder lines where the value is chosen. SECONDARY (flagged, not relied on): the cited test-ref, conformance-test:CobolNet.Tests.Conformance.LinageConformanceTests.Gr26ab_CounterEqualsBody_IsFootingEopNotOverflow, is spec-derived but pins 14.9.51 GR26a/GR26b's end-of-page discrimination rather than GR2's page-size definition, and its expectation - LINAGE-COUNTER equal to the page size is a FOOTING end-of-page - contradicts GR26b's own words 'and is less than the page size' and GR26a's 'equal to or exceeds the page size'. That is a 14.9.51 question and belongs to that subject file; GR2's refutation stands on the qualification measurement alone. CORRECTED VERDICT PARTIAL: the literal form and the unique-unqualified-data-name form are implemented and measured correct (r2b_lit, r2_dn, r8_dnbound - a data-name body of 2 genuinely bounds the writes), and only the qualified spelling diverges. DIVERGES is defensible if the inventory scores a silently-wrong value over a legal and sometimes mandatory operand spelling as divergence rather than partial implementation; it is NOT CONFORMS under any reading. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/SequentialConnector.cs:103 (_pageBody), :133 (set from the evaluator), :158/:168 (the page-body bound); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/FileModel.cs:236-252 (LinageInfo.Body)

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB525 + PB526 — THE FOOTING AREA IS RIGHT; THE 'GREATER THAN ZERO' HALF CANNOT BE ENFORCED BECAUSE ZERO IS THE ABSENT-PHRASE SENTINEL. Implemented and tested: the footing area is [footing start, page size] INCLUSIVE - the named test pins a write landing exactly on the page size as a FOOTING end-of-page with the counter unmoved, and conformance-test:CobolNet.Tests.Conformance.LinageConformanceTests.Gr26b_FootingEop_AtBranchReadsPostAdvanceCounter pins the interior case. NOT implemented: 'The value shall be greater than zero'. SequentialIoEmitter emits the literal 0 for an ABSENT FOOTING phrase and the connector's guard is `_footing > 0`, so a FOOTING phrase whose data item evaluates to 0 is indistinguishable from no FOOTING phrase at all. notes: kb/Work PB201 (2026-09-04). REJECTED side: DataBinder.Odo screens data-name-1 as Category Numeric, IsFloat false, Scale 0 and raises COBOLNET0852 otherwise - a PIC 9V9 control item is rejected at every edition (pb201-odo-depending-not-integer; OCCURS DEPENDING is COBOL-85 and rule 17 has no introduction axis). The illegal shapes are unreachable or rejected: `PIC 999.. VALUE ZERO.` is a parse error (sr7g), `PIC 999,.USAGE DISPLAY.` is COBOLNET0808 (sr7h). DataBinder.cs:2342 sets `noSign = usage.noSignPhrase() is not null` from the ENTRY'S OWN usageClause, and the SR31 test at :2647-2657 runs only inside that entry's bind, so the GROUP-INHERITED arm is never asked. 13.18.60.4 GR1 (If the USAGE clause is specified or implied at a group level, it applies only to each elementary item in the group) makes a group-level USAGE PACKED-DECIMAL WITH NO SIGN apply to every elementary item -- and that is the project's OWN reading, since the group-inherited USAGE NATIONAL leg cites 13.18.40.3 SR30 by number in its message. So `01 G USAGE PACKED-DECIMAL WITH NO SIGN. 05 W1 PIC S9(4).` is exactly what SR31 forbids and it compiles clean, at two nesting depths. The entry's own arm is solid (full USAGE spelling, bare usage word, lowercase -- all COBOLNET1566), so one arm of two: PARTIAL. A second, larger fact makes the omission unmistakable rather than debatable: the group's NO SIGN phrase is dropped WHOLESALE, not merely unchecked -- FUNCTION LENGTH(G) is 3 for the signed leaf AND 3 for an unsigned leaf under the same group header, while an own-entry PIC 9(4) PACKED-DECIMAL WITH NO SIGN is 2 bytes against 3 for plain packed. subject: PICTURE clause
notes: kb/Work PB490 — Rule 1 is the taxonomy statement; its only checkable obligation is that all six named mechanisms exist and that editing is one of them, not some seventh thing. All six live in the ONE editor CobolEdit.Format and were each exercised: simple insertion (pass 1's B / 0 / '/' / ',' cases - probe p1), special insertion ('.'), fixed insertion (isFixedPlus / isFixedMinus / isFixedCurrency plus the CR and DB pairs - probe p2), floating insertion (FindFloatingPlacement - probe p2), zero suppression with spaces ('Z') and with asterisks ('*') (pass 2 - probe p1). There is exactly one editor for format 1, so the taxonomy is not written down twice; locale editing (rules 9-15) is format 2's separate path (CobolLocaleEdit) and its own rows. The defects found belong to the CONTENT of rules 3, 6 and 7, not to rule 1's enumeration. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The adjudicator's stated rationale is factually wrong on its load-bearing claim: 'All six live in the ONE editor CobolEdit.Format ... There is exactly one editor for format 1, so the taxonomy is not written down twice.' There is a SECOND format-1 editor — CobolEdit.FormatAlphanumeric — and it is where one of the four enumerated insertion types (simple insertion) is implemented for alphanumeric-edited items, which Table 7 gives 'Simple insertion' and which are format-1 items. That second editor knows nothing about the EDITING character-1: its switch is 'X'/'A'/'9' -> source char, 'B' -> space, '0' -> '0', '/' -> '/', and `_ => picture[i]` renders character-1 VERBATIM. That is exactly the sibling record GR-13.18.40.5-3's WRONG ANSWER (PIC XXTXX EDITING "T" IS ":" renders ABTCD). Counting the three sites, ONE enumerated mechanism (simple insertion) is written down three times with three different symbol sets: Format pass 1 {',','B','/','0',character-1}; Format pass 2's floating/suppression string membership `case ',' or 'B':` which drops '/' and '0' (the mechanism behind the sibling DIVERGES of rules 6 and 7); and FormatAlphanumeric {B,0,'/'} with no character-1. So three of rule 1's six enumerated mechanisms — simple insertion, floating insertion, zero suppression with replacement — each carry a WRONG-ANSWER defect on legal source per the adjudicator's own sibling verdicts. A row whose only content is 'these six mechanisms exist and are the mechanisms' cannot be CONFORMS when the existence check is the only evidence offered and half the enumerated mechanisms are demonstrably not the mechanisms the rule names. PARTIAL, not DIVERGES: the taxonomy itself is not contradicted (no seventh mechanism, none missing outright) and the format-2 locale path is correctly separate. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolEdit.cs#CobolEdit.Format || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85/2002/2014/2023

notes: kb/Work PB490 — WRONG ANSWER, silent, at COBOL-2023. Probe p4: `01 AE PIC XXTXX EDITING "T" IS ":".` then `MOVE "ABCD" TO AE` renders ABTCD. Rule 3 requires the INSERTION CHARACTER - literal-1, ':' - to occupy the same character position in the edited item as the associated symbol occupies in character-string-1, i.e. AB:CD; LENGTH is already 5, so the position exists and only its content is wrong. Mechanism: a two-arm dispatch with one arm fixed. The numeric-edited arm threads PicInfo.EditingRules through RuntimeApi.EditsArg into CobolEdit.Format(... edits:) at every emit site (MoveEmitter, ArithmeticEmitter, AcceptDisplayEmitter, StringEmitter, ValueInitializer, GroupImageCodec, NumericRenderer's DeEdit); the alphanumeric-edited arm has no such parameter at all - RuntimeApi.EditFormatAlphanumeric(value, mask) takes only the mask and CobolEdit.FormatAlphanumeric's `_ => picture[i]` default copies character-1 through verbatim. All three alphanumeric-edited emit sites drop the rules. The numeric character-1 path is correct (probe p3: PIC 99T99 EDITING "T" IS ":" MOVE 1230 -> 12:30), which is why no test caught it. subject: PICTURE clause
notes: kb/Work PB490 + PB491 — WRONG ANSWER on legal source at every edition. Rule 6 says any of the simple insertion editing symbols embedded in the floating string, or immediately to its right, are PART of the string - and rule 3's simple insertion symbols are B, 0, '/', ',' (plus character-1). The implementation hard-codes that set to {',', 'B'} in BOTH places that need it: pass 2's suppression switch (`case ',' or 'B':`) and FindFloatingPlacement's zone walk (`else if (inZone && p is ',' or 'B' ...)`, otherwise `break`). So '0' and '/' neither take the replacement character nor let the zone continue: probe p2, `01 P-SLASH PIC ++/++9.` MOVE 5 renders ' +/  5', where 6a requires a single '+' immediately preceding the first character position for which no floating insertion editing is specified, with spaces before it -> '    +5'. Table 10 admits the picture (the 'B 0 /' column is x against the floating '+ -' row and vice versa), so this is legal source. Everything else in rule 6 conforms: Table 9's sign map ('+' -> '   +5' / '   -5'; '-' -> '    5' / '   -5'; floating currency -> '   $5'), 6a's three stop conditions (PIC $$$99 MOVE 5 -> '  $05'; PIC $$$.$$ MOVE 0.05 -> '  $.05'), and 6b (PIC $$$.$$ MOVE 0 -> all spaces). Second, separate leg: rule 6's first sentence names the extended editing sign control symbols as floating insertion symbols, and that form is refused - Annex D.24's `PIC LLLL9.99F EDITING "L" FOR NEGATIVE IS "(" EDITING "F" FOR NEGATIVE IS ")"` draws COBOLNET0899 (finding pic-editing-phrase-render-gap). Primary finding: pic-suppression-string-simple-insertions. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolEdit.cs#CobolEdit.Format; src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolEdit.cs#CobolEdit.FindFloatingPlacement || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85/2002/2014/2023 (the '+', '-' and currency floating strings are 85+ and diverge identically at every edition; the extended sign-control floating form is 2023 and is unimplemented)

subject: PICTURE clause
notes: kb/Work PB490 — WRONG ANSWER on legal source at every edition, the same mechanism as rule 6. Probe p1: `01 A-SLASH PIC ZZ/ZZ.` MOVE 12 renders '  /12' and `01 A-ZERO PIC ZZ0ZZ.` renders '  012'; rule 7's 'any of the simple insertion editing symbols embedded in this string or to the immediate right of this string are part of the string' requires the replacement character in every position of the string that precedes the first significant digit, i.e. '   12' in both cases. Table 10 admits both pictures (the 'B 0 /' column is x against the 'Z *' row and the 'Z *' column is x against the 'B 0 /' row), so this is legal source. 13.18.40.4 GR15 is the corroboration that the standard means the replacement character lands there: for '/' it says the position is checked to contain 'the character slant or, if no significant numeric character appears to its left, the corresponding floating insertion character or replacement character respectively', and identically for '0', ',' and 'B'. The ',' and 'B' cases ARE implemented (PIC ZZ,ZZZ MOVE 12 -> '    12'; PIC ZZBZZ -> '   12'), which is exactly the hand-maintained-list shape. Everything else in rule 7 conforms: 7a's three stop conditions, 7b for 'Z' (PIC ZZZ.ZZ MOVE 0 -> all spaces) and for '*' (PIC ***.** MOVE 0 -> '***.**', the decimal separator kept). One reading recorded rather than charged: PIC $***.** MOVE 0 renders '****.**', overwriting the fixed currency symbol; 7b's literal text ('all character positions of the item will contain the character asterisk, but the decimal separator, when specified, will appear in the item') supports that, so it is left conforming-to-the-text and flagged for the owner rather than filed as a defect. Finding pic-suppression-string-simple-insertions. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Numeric/CobolEdit.cs#CobolEdit.Format || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85/2002/2014/2023 (identical at every edition)

notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB93). data-name-2 resolves among the PRECEDING same-level siblings only (TakeWhile before the subject, nearest match — NOTE 1) — an entry with a lower level number cannot intervene by construction (it would end the sibling list); a name that resolves to nothing, or only to a LATER sibling, is COBOLNET1654 and the entry binds as an ordinary item (no half-state).

subject: REDEFINES clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB93 sweep). A REDEFINES naming an entry that is itself a redefinition is COBOLNET1656 — error strict; under --permissive a warning with the chain semantics (the classifier chases the anchor, SR11) — the documented dialect leniency (GnuCOBOL/IBM accept chains).

subject: REDEFINES clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB93). The redefining entries FOLLOW the entries defining the area: the lookup admits preceding siblings only, so `05 A REDEFINES B. 05 B.` is COBOLNET1654 (it used to bind to the later B). The 'without intervening entries that define new storage areas' half is the ClassifyRedefinesClasses layout invariant (a redefiner overlays its target's area wherever it stands among the siblings).

subject: REDEFINES clause
notes: docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 row A.4.14 (VALIDATE — Not claimed) + §4 item 3. Obsolescence (F.2 item 5) is corroboration, never the licence (kb/Work PB198). These four live inside clauses this compiler SUPPORTS (PICTURE ×2, REDEFINES, USAGE) but describe only what those clauses do DURING THE FORMAT VALIDATION STAGE of a VALIDATE statement — A.4.1's "even if not explicitly listed" is what carries the licence to them. They have NO syntax of their own, so their witness is the statement's, not a new construct: with the statement inert the format-validation stage never runs. GR-13.18.40.4-19 already carried this verdict by hand and its identical sibling GR-13.18.40.4-15 was left blank — the one-answer-per-question drift this batch closes. ⚠ GR-13.18.40.4-14, the PICTURE symbol table, is DELIBERATELY NOT HERE: it CONFORMS with code and a golden, and its only VALIDATE text is an exception ("the symbol A is equivalent to the symbol X except within the execution of a VALIDATE statement").

subject: RENAMES clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (kb/Work PB96). The no-THRU alias inherits data-name-2's description and storage: ren.Pic = From.Pic and the resolver forwards to the FROM item's place outright (numeric stays numeric — NC252A's ADD 3500 TO RENAME-12).

subject: RENAMES clause
notes: LANDED 2026-08-18 (PB96). The THRU alias is an alphanumeric group item over the record's STORAGE WINDOW from data-name-2's first character to data-name-3's last: the span parts are the record's NON-redefining leaves that intersect the window (a REDEFINES view adds no storage; a redefining FROM / THRU maps to the area it overlays; a boundary inside a leaf is a partial part rendered as the leaf's ref-mod view). Before: every leaf between FROM and THRU was listed, views included (A / B REDEFINES A / C was 6 characters, not 4). The shorter-redefinition-as-data-name-3 case is the CONFORMANCE.md §4 determination (the leftmost-to-rightmost reading).

notes: kb/Work PB537 — ONE OF THE PROHIBITED SHAPES IS CAUGHT; EVERY OTHER ONE IS ADMITTED SILENTLY AND INERTLY. ENFORCED: a floating-point numeric-edited picture carries no symbol 'S' (§13.18.40.6 Table 10 row E), so `01 A PIC +9.9E+99 SIGN IS LEADING.` is COBOLNET1658 (probe sg_sr1_floatedit), with negative golden conformance:negative/pb66-float-edited-picture-symbols line 26 -- a spec-derived witness for that ONE shape, which cannot close the row. UNENFORCED, each probed clean and measurably INERT at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023: an UNSIGNED numeric entry `01 A PIC 9(3) SIGN IS LEADING.` (sg_sr1_unsigned, sg_sr1_9_2002/2014/2023, sg85_sr1_x_*); an ALPHANUMERIC ELEMENTARY item `01 A PIC X(3) SIGN IS LEADING.` -- the third bullet admits an alphanumeric GROUP item, never an alphanumeric elementary one (sg_sr1_alnum, sg_ed_sr1_x_85/2002/2014/2023); a NATIONAL ELEMENTARY item `PIC N(3)` (sg_sr1_national); a NUMERIC-EDITED entry `PIC ZZ9` (sg_sr1_numedit -- MOVE through it is byte-identical to the same entry without the clause); and a BIT GROUP item `01 G GROUP-USAGE IS BIT SIGN IS LEADING.` (sg_sr1_bitgroup) -- the rule's three group kinds are alphanumeric, national and strongly-typed, and a bit group item is none of them. Harm is UNDER-REJECTS only: PicInfo.SignKindFor (PicInfo.cs:593-599) is consulted for a signed NUMERIC subject alone, so an illegally-placed clause changes no width and no value. THE LEGAL ARMS ALL WORK: a signed numeric data entry (sg_sr1_signed_ok); an alphanumeric group (sg_sr1_group_ok, `G=[-012]`); a strongly-typed group whose TYPE copy carries the clause through DataBinder.cs:1956-1960 (sg_sr1_strong, `U=[-012]`); and a NUMERIC REPORT GROUP description entry (DataBinder.Reports.cs:428 -> sg_report_sign, whose report line really is `-012`). The SCREEN description entry bullet is owner-declined A.4.2 non-support (COBOLNET1560, kb/Work PB260) and is not adjudicable here. subject: SIGN clause
notes: kb/Work PB536 — THE RULE IS ENFORCED AND THE OWN-CLAUSE CASE IS RIGHT; THE CHECK RUNS ONE PHASE TOO EARLY TO SEE A GROUP-LEVEL SIGN, AND REJECTS LEGAL SOURCE. Correct today: under `FD F CODE-SET IS AL1.` an `05 N PIC S9(4).` record item is COBOLNET1672 (sg_sr3_nosep), `05 N PIC S9(4) SIGN IS TRAILING SEPARATE.` is accepted (sg_sr3_sep) and an unsigned item is not asked for a sign (sg_sr3_nosign). The compiler reports it against the CODE-SET twin §13.18.13.3 SR3 a, whose text is identical ('any signed numeric data items shall be described with the SIGN IS SEPARATE clause') -- one rule written once, which is right. THE DIVERGENCE IS THE PHASE. BindCodeSetClause is called from BindFileSection at ENTRY-BIND time, whereas the §13.18.52.4 GR1 group-SIGN propagation is the POST-BUILD InheritSignClauses pass (BindPipeline.cs:46, UsageResolved -> SignResolved), so CheckItem reads `pic.SignKind` before any group-level clause has reached the leaf. A record whose GROUP carries the clause is therefore rejected as though the leaf had no separate sign: `01 R. 05 G SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE. 10 N PIC S9(4).` under a CODE-SET FD is COBOLNET1672 (probe sg_sr3_grpsep) even though the compiler's OWN storage model gives N a separate sign -- the identical record with CODE-SET removed writes `-0012ZZ`, 7 bytes, with BYTE-LENGTH(N) = 5 (probe sg_fd_groupsign). GR1 makes the group clause apply to every subordinate signed numeric item, so that record IS described with the SIGN IS SEPARATE clause and is legal. See finding sign-codeset-check-precedes-inheritance. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:3065-3082 (BindCodeSetClause CheckItem, COBOLNET1672), called from DataBinder.cs:1011 inside BindFileSection; the pass it precedes is src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Passes/BindPipeline.cs:46 (InheritSignClauses)

subject: SIGN clause
notes: kb/Work PB493 + PB536 — RIGHT ON EVERY REACHABLE ARM; ONE FILTER THE RULE'S TEXT DOES NOT AUTHORIZE. The group clause applies to each subordinate SIGNED numeric item and to nothing else: `01 G SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE. 05 A PIC S9(3) VALUE -12. 05 B PIC 9(3) VALUE 34. 05 C PIC X(2) VALUE 'XY'.` gives `G=[-012034XY]`, 9 bytes (sg_gr1_group), and the same clause over an unsigned-only record leaves the width at 3 (sg_gr1_unsigned_child) -- the second sentence's 'only to numeric items whose picture character-string contains the symbol S'. The pass walks EVERY root section, which was measured, not assumed: WORKING-STORAGE (sg_ws_groupsign), the FILE SECTION record -- the written file really is `-0012ZZ` (sg_fd_groupsign) -- LOCAL-STORAGE (sg_ls_groupsign), and a TYPEDEF whose TYPE copy carries the clause (sg_sr1_strong). PARTIAL FOR ONE REACHABLE DIVERGENCE: the walk filters on `Usage: Usage.Display`, so a group SIGN over a subordinate of any other usage is silently not applied -- `01 G SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE. 05 A PIC S9(4) USAGE COMP VALUE -12.` keeps its 2-byte binary form (sg_gr1_comp_child). GR1 attaches no usage condition; the only usage restriction in §13.18.52 is SR2, which governs an item for which the clause is SPECIFIED, not one it merely applies to. The BEHAVIOUR is almost certainly the right determination (it is what the surveyed implementations do, and a separate sign character on a binary item has no representation §13.18.60.4 defines), but the code's stated justification -- '§13.18.52 applies only to usage-display items' at DataBinder.cs:3411, echoed at :3431 -- is not something §13.18.52 says: a real clause answering a different question. The DISPLAY-only filter also excludes the `national` usage SR2 explicitly admits; that arm is unreachable today because a signed numeric NATIONAL item is COBOLNET0899 (sg_nat_numeric), so the filter is currently observationally equivalent there. No spec-derived test anywhere in the corpus declares a group-level SIGN clause (every SIGN declaration under tests/ is elementary), so the rule's central mechanism is untested. See finding sign-group-inheritance-display-only-citation. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:3431-3448 (InheritSignClauses); DataBinder.cs:1956-1960 (the TYPE / SAME AS description copy); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs:97-102 (OwnSign); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs:593-599

subject: SIGN clause
notes: kb/Work PB493 — MEASURED, BOTH HALVES. `01 G SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE. 05 H SIGN IS TRAILING SEPARATE. 10 A PIC S9(3) VALUE -12. 05 K. 10 B PIC S9(3) VALUE -12.` gives `H=[012-]` -- the subordinate group item's own clause takes precedence FOR THAT SUBORDINATE GROUP -- and `K=[-012]`, the enclosing clause still reaching the sibling subtree that declares none (probe sg_gr2_nested). The mechanism is structural rather than enumerated: the effective spec is recomputed at each node and handed to the children, so arbitrary nesting depth and sibling independence follow by construction and cannot drift apart per level. CONFORMS but UNTESTED -- no golden or unit test in the corpus declares a nested group SIGN clause. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED ON AN ENTIRE SECTION THE ADJUDICATION NEVER REACHED: the REPORT SECTION. GR2 requires that a SIGN clause on a group item subordinate to a SIGN-bearing group take precedence FOR THAT SUBORDINATE GROUP. In a report group description entry the compiler accepts the clause at BOTH levels, emits no diagnostic, and applies NEITHER: the printable item falls back to the GR4 implementor default. Mechanism (read, then confirmed by probe): DataBinder.Reports.cs:336 declares ownSign as a PER-ENTRY LOCAL whose only consumers are DataBinder.Reports.cs:514 (PictureAnalyzer.Analyze) and :534 (DataItem.OwnSign) on the PICTURE-BEARING printable item, so a non-elementary report entry's ownSign is dropped at the end of the clause loop; and report print items are SYNTHETIC DataItems held in ReportFieldModel.PrintItem, never added to DataBinder._roots (DataBinder.cs:691 is the only entry-path _roots.Add), so InheritSignClauses (DataBinder.cs:3436-3447, foreach over Roots) cannot see them. PREMISE CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: SIGN is legal on a NON-elementary report entry -- 13.15.2's general format lists the sign-clause slot once for the whole entry at every level, and 13.15.3 SR11 (cite.py OK) restricts PICTURE, COLUMN, SOURCE, VALUE, SUM and GROUP INDICATE to elementary entries and DELIBERATELY OMITS SIGN; 13.18.52.3 SR1's third bullet admits an alphanumeric/national/strongly-typed GROUP ITEM, and a non-elementary report entry with subordinate entries is one (13.15.2 even gives it USAGE DISPLAY or NATIONAL). If the registrar instead reads SR1 as barring SIGN from a non-elementary report entry, the compiler is STILL wrong -- it must reject and does not -- but the defect then belongs on SR-13.18.52.3-1 (already PARTIAL) and GR2 would stand; that ambiguity is why this is PARTIAL and not DIVERGES. WHAT I DID TO BREAK IT ELSEWHERE AND COULD NOT: GR2 is correct, in BOTH the widen and the SHRINK direction, in WORKING-STORAGE, LOCAL-STORAGE, an FD record, an SD sort record, the LINKAGE SECTION of a called subprogram, a TYPEDEF/TYPE copy, a SAME AS copy, under OCCURS, in an OBJECT's WORKING-STORAGE and in a METHOD's LOCAL-STORAGE, at --std 85/2002/2014/2023. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:3436-3447 (InheritSignClauses: `SignSpec? effective = item.OwnSign ?? inherited;` then `foreach (var c in item.Children) Walk(c, effective);`)

subject: SIGN clause
notes: THE IMPLEMENTOR DETERMINATION IS MADE, IS CONSISTENT ACROSS FORMAT AND PARSE, AND CORRECTLY DOES NOT IMPOSE GR5/GR6. A signed DISPLAY item with no SIGN clause takes the TRAILING OVER-PUNCH: `01 A PIC S9(3) VALUE -123.` renders `12L` and `VALUE 123` renders `12C` (the IBM-ASCII tables at CobolNum.cs:544-545, '{ABCDEFGHI' positive / '}JKLMNOPQR' negative), the group image is 3 characters and BYTE-LENGTH is 3 -- the sign occupies an EXISTING digit position and no separate character position is created (probes sg_gr5_default, sg_scaled `K=[0123M]`). A signed item of a non-DISPLAY usage takes the leading-minus form (`A=[-0012]`, BinaryMinus -- sg_inert_comp). Both halves of the rule's obligation (position AND representation) were probed, in both the format and the parse direction. notes: kb/Work PB488 — TWO HALVES, ONE ENFORCED, AND THE ENFORCED ONE IS UNNAMED. LEVEL 66: `dataDescriptionBody : constantEntryBody | dataDescriptionClauses | renamesClause` makes RENAMES a WHOLE alternative, so a 66 entry cannot carry a clause list at all -- `66 R RENAMES A THRU B USAGE DISPLAY.` is COBOL0307 "unexpected 'USAGE'" and `66 R USAGE DISPLAY RENAMES A THRU B.` is COBOL0307 "unexpected 'RENAMES'", identically at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023 (probes u_sr1_66, u_sr1_66b, e_sr1_66_85/_2002/_2014/_2023). The rejection is a GENERIC PARSE ERROR, not a diagnostic naming SR1, and it is a consequence of the grammar's shape rather than of the rule being written down. LEVEL 88: UNENFORCED. `dataDescriptionEntry : levelNumber dataName? dataDescriptionBody DOT` has no per-level clause filter, so `88 C VALUE 'abc' USAGE COMP.` and `88 C USAGE DISPLAY VALUE 'abc'.` COMPILE AND RUN CLEAN, with the condition still evaluating correctly (probes u_sr1_88, u_sr1_88b, u_sr1_88_comp, u_sr1_88_idx and the edition sweep e_sr1_88_85/_2002/_2014/_2023 -- all print the condition's true branch). The clause is INERT (DataBinder.BindCondition binds a level-88 from its VALUE list alone and never reads OwnUsage), so harm is UNDER-REJECTS + SILENT, never a wrong value. No COBOLNET code is allocated for the rule. See finding usage-p1/F1. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4:231-235 (dataDescriptionBody -- the level-66 half, structural); NO SITE for the level-88 half (grep '13.18.60.3 SR1' over src/ returns nothing; DataBinder.BindCondition never inspects the clause list)

notes: kb/Work PB495 — THE RULE IS WRITTEN DOWN NOWHERE. `grep '13.18.60.3 SR2' src/` returns nothing; the ONE place that sees both usages is InheritUsageClauses, whose whole body is `Usage? effective = item.OwnUsage ?? inherited;` plus a conditional rewrite -- a PREFERENCE, where the rule demands an EQUALITY CHECK. MEASURED CLEAN and edition-invariant (--std 85, 2002, 2014, 2023): `01 G USAGE COMP. 05 A PIC 9(4). 05 B PIC 9(4) USAGE DISPLAY.` compiles and B is a 4-byte DISPLAY item inside a group whose clause said COMP, so the group's BYTE-LENGTH is 6 where the conforming spelling gives 4 (u_sr2_measure vs u_sr2_measure_ok; e85_sr2_85/2002/2014/2023 all print B=[0034]); `01 G USAGE COMP. 05 A PIC 9(4) USAGE COMP-3.` gives A a 3-byte PACKED form (u_sr2_comp_vs_comp3); a NESTED conflict `01 G USAGE COMP. 05 H USAGE PACKED-DECIMAL. 10 A PIC 9(4).` gives A the packed form of the NEAREST enclosing clause (u_sr2_nest2, LEN=3); and an intermediate GROUP that contradicts its parent, `01 G USAGE COMP. 05 H USAGE DISPLAY. 10 A PIC 9(4).`, compiles clean (u_sr2_nested_group). The LEGAL spelling works -- `01 G USAGE COMP. 05 A PIC 9(4) USAGE COMP.` gives the 2-byte binary form (u_sr2_same). Harm is UNDER-REJECTS + SILENT: the layout the compiler builds is the one the SUBORDINATE clause names, so a program written against the GROUP clause gets a record image it never asked for and no diagnostic. ONE named predicate at the InheritUsageClauses walk (`item.OwnUsage is not null && item.OwnUsage != inherited`) is the whole fix -- it already has both operands in hand. See finding usage-p1/F2. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#InheritUsageClauses (`Usage? effective = item.OwnUsage ?? inherited;` -- the subordinate's own clause silently WINS, with no equality test); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:2330-2345 (the per-entry USAGE capture)

subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB495 + PB540 — THE DIRECT-CLAUSE + ALPHANUMERIC-PICTURE CASE IS ENFORCED; THE RULE'S OTHER TWO REACHES ARE NOT. ENFORCED: `01 A PIC X(3) USAGE COMP / BINARY / PACKED-DECIMAL.` is COBOLNET0881 quoting SR3 (u_sr3_x_comp, u_sr3_x_binary, u_sr3_x_packed), as is an ALPHANUMERIC-EDITED picture `PIC XXBXX USAGE COMP` (u_sr3_alnedit); a BOOLEAN picture routes to the SR5 message and a NATIONAL picture to SR20 (u_sr3_bool_comp, u_sr20_comp). Two spec-derived negative goldens pin it edition-invariantly. HOLE 1 -- NUMERIC-EDITED. The predicate is `anyAlpha`, so an EDITED numeric picture never reaches it: `01 A PIC ZZ9 USAGE COMP.` compiles clean at all four editions, and so do USAGE PACKED-DECIMAL and USAGE COMP-5 with the same picture (u_sr3_numedit_comp, u_sr3_edit_packed, u_sr3_edit_comp5, e_sr3_edit_85/2002/2014/2023). SR3 admits only "a picture character-string that describes a NUMERIC item", and 13.18.40.4 GR3's category list (cite --check OK) makes numeric and numeric-edited SEPARATE categories -- GR11 defines fixed-point numeric, GR13 defines numeric-edited -- so the source is illegal. It is also INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT once accepted: FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH reports 1 for `PIC ZZ9 USAGE COMP` where the same picture without the usage reports 3, while the enclosing group image is still the 3-character edited image (u_sr3_edit_group prints G=[ 12xy], identical to the clean H=[ 12xy]) -- a declared width that disagrees with the item's own image is exactly what a REDEFINES window or a record image keys on. HOLE 2 -- THE SECOND LIMB. SR3 governs "an elementary data item SUBORDINATE TO A GROUP ITEM whose declaration contains" the usage, and that limb has no site at all: `01 G USAGE COMP. 05 A PIC X(3).` compiles clean at 85/2002/2014/2023 and the inherited COMP is silently DROPPED -- A stays a 3-byte alphanumeric DISPLAY item (u_sr3_group_inherit, u_sr3_group_x_measure, e85_sr3g_85/2002/2014/2023). InheritUsageClauses only rewrites a leaf whose Pic is already `{Numeric, IsFloat:false, Usage:Display}`, so a non-numeric leaf under a binary/packed group is neither converted nor diagnosed. Contrast USAGE BIT, whose inheritance arm IS written (`USAGE BIT inherited from its group requires a boolean PICTURE`, probe u_sr5_group) -- the same rule shape, one arm written, one missing. The picture-LESS shape `01 A USAGE COMP.` also compiles and then CRASHES the compiler (NullReferenceException in MoveEmitter.ConvertSource:287, probe u_sr3_nopic_measure); that belongs to 13.16.3 SR8 and is already recorded there (sibling data-description-entry-p2, findings F5/F6). See finding usage-p1/F3. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/PictureAnalyzer.cs:315-325 (`if (anyAlpha && usage is Usage.Binary or Usage.Comp5 or Usage.Packed)` -- the ONLY site); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#InheritUsageClauses (the second limb's would-be site, which validates nothing)

subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB495 — The rule has two sentences and they part company. SENTENCE 2 ("Unless the GROUP-USAGE clause is also specified or implied, the USAGE clause applies only to each elementary item in the group and not to the group itself") CONFORMS: PB79/D20 landed the GROUP-USAGE model, ResolveIndexItems propagates the group's GROUP-USAGE to subordinate GROUPS (SR2/SR3) and turns each boolean leaf bit-form, and conformance:2023/pb79_group_usage_bit measures both halves end to end with spec-computed expectations. SENTENCE 1 ("it applies only to each elementary item in the group") is implemented over a HAND-LISTED SET OF USAGES and diverges outside it. What works, measured with the pinned compiler at --std 2023: a group USAGE DISPLAY / NATIONAL (probe p53: BYTE-LENGTH 7 for 9(4)+X(3); a national leaf 2 bytes per position), a group USAGE COMPUTATIONAL / PACKED-DECIMAL / COMP-5 (probe p1: 01 G-COMP USAGE COMPUTATIONAL over two PIC 9(4) leaves is 4 bytes and each leaf 2; 01 G-PACK over two PIC 9(5) is 6 and each leaf 3), the nearest-enclosing-clause discipline (probe p4: A under a PACKED group inside a COMP group is 3 bytes, B under an intervening usage-less group is 4, an own DISPLAY clause wins at 5), a group USAGE INDEX or OBJECT REFERENCE over PICTURE-LESS leaves (probe p38: each leaf 8 bytes, `SET A TO I1` then `IF A = 2` succeeds), and USAGE BIT (the golden above). What does NOT: (a) a group-level FLOATING-POINT usage over a PICTURE-bearing leaf makes the BACKEND fail to compile - `01 G USAGE FLOAT-SHORT. 05 A PIC 9(4).` and the FLOAT-BINARY-32 / COMP-1 twins emit a `float` field for the GROUP and then index it as a record (CS1061, probes p2/p54/p55); ResolveIndexItems sheds a synthesized group-header profile for IndexItem, ObjectReference and BinaryChar..BinaryDouble but has no float arm; (b) a group-level BINARY-CHAR/-SHORT/-LONG/-DOUBLE or INDEX over a PICTURE-bearing leaf is SILENTLY DROPPED - InheritUsageClauses' inherited set is exactly `Usage.Binary or Usage.Packed or Usage.Comp5`, so probe p28's `01 G-BL USAGE BINARY-LONG. 05 A PIC 9(2).` leaves A usage-display at 2 bytes (binary-long is 4) and `01 G-BC USAGE BINARY-CHAR. 05 B PIC 9(9).` leaves B at 9 bytes (binary-char is 1). Both shapes are in fact ILLEGAL source - by GR1 the leaf's usage IS the group's, and §13.16.3 SR8 forbids a PICTURE clause "for an item whose usage is binary-char, binary-short, binary-long, binary-double, float-short, float-long, float-extended, index ..." - so the conforming answer is the named SR8 diagnostic, not a raw Roslyn error and not a silently different representation. Finding usage-group-inheritance-float-arm-crashes and usage-group-inheritance-hand-listed-set own the fix; no kb/Work note owns either today (PB79 and PB183 are landed and cover GROUP-USAGE and SR14 respectively). ⚠ The nearest-enclosing arm that DOES work is reachable only through §13.18.60.3 SR2-illegal source ("the same usage shall be specified in both entries"), which is unenforced - an under-reject owned by the §13.18.60.3 half of this subject, not re-reported here. notes: kb/Work PB572 — Three claims, all held. (1) "specifies the manner in which a data item is represented in the storage of a computer" - PicInfo.ByteForm is the single table mapping each usage to its byte representation (Zoned / Binary / Packed / PackedNoSign / Ieee32 / Ieee64) and PicInfo.StorageWidth the width that representation implies; PicInfo's own doc comment names GR4/GR11 as the licence and §4.2.16 as the documentation duty, and the forms are documented at docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 items 205/208/211/215. (2) "It does not affect the use of the data item" - measured, not assumed: probe p32 uses the SAME `PIC 9(3)` item at usage DISPLAY, COMPUTATIONAL, PACKED-DECIMAL and COMP-5 as a subscript (`TE(KD)` … `TE(K5)` all yield ABC), as a PERFORM VARYING control identifier, as the operand of a class condition (`IS NUMERIC` true for the packed and binary forms) and as a MOVE sender; probe p27 shows a signed `PIC S9(5)V99` at DISPLAY / COMP / PACKED / COMP-5 comparing equal, summing to the same value and editing to the same `-123.45` through a `PIC ---9.99` receiver. The representation still shows through DISPLAY's own conversion (usage-display renders the trailing overpunch `001234N`, the binary forms `-0012345`) - that is §14.9.11 GR1's implementor-defined conversion reading the representation this clause pins, documented at docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 item 56, and it is what sentences 1 and 3 license, not a contradiction of sentence 2. (3) "although the specifications for some statements in the procedure division may restrict the USAGE clause of the operands referred to" - the restriction sites exist and are named: §13.18.60.3 SR10 for a class-index item (probe p6: `MOVE 3 TO IX` draws COBOLNET0809), §13.18.60.3 SR14 for the pointer/object family (COBOLNET1724), the INSPECT/STRING/UNSTRING usage-display screens (conformance:negative/da7-inspect-binary-operand and its two siblings). (4) "may affect the radix or type of character representation" - PicInfo.ByteForm's radix-2/radix-10/one-byte-per-digit arms are exactly that. CONFORMS-but-untested: no single spec-derived test asserts the usage-independence of USE as such; a closing golden is the p32/p27 pair (one PICTURE across four usages, exercising subscript, PERFORM VARYING, class condition, comparison, arithmetic and edited MOVE). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Sentence 2 - 'It does not affect the use of the data item, although the specifications for some statements in the procedure division may restrict the USAGE clause of the operands referred to' - is measurably FALSE for at least one usage, and the adjudicator's own probes could not see it because every one of them held the usage axis inside the NUMERIC family (DISPLAY / COMPUTATIONAL / PACKED-DECIMAL / COMP-5, probes p27 and p32). Flip the axis to USAGE NATIONAL and the same construct that works for a DISPLAY item is refused: `01 G. 05 A PIC N(3) USAGE NATIONAL.  01 H REDEFINES G. 05 B PIC X(6).  ...  MOVE N"ABC" TO A` draws COBOLNET0899 'receiving operand A names a declared item in a reference shape COBOL.NET does not yet implement as a receiver (COBOLNET_DESIGN 1.4 - rejected rather than dropped)', while the byte-identical program with `05 A PIC X(6) USAGE DISPLAY` compiles and runs, and the same national item WITHOUT the REDEFINES also compiles and runs. The single differing factor is the USAGE clause, so the USAGE clause here does affect the use of the data item - and the refusal is not one of the procedure-division restrictions the sentence licenses (SS14.9.25 admits a national receiver for a national sender; nothing in the MOVE statement restricts the USAGE of its operands here). The compiler's own model records this as a KNOWN deferral, not an accident: PicInfo.cs's PicCategory.National doc comment says byte-addressed surfaces (REDEFINES / cells / file records) 'REFUSE national leaves loud (D-N2) until the 2-byte layout residue lands'. A self-declared open residue inside the rule's own scope is exactly what CONFORMS may not cover. Sentences 1, 3 and 4 do hold (ByteForm/StorageWidth are the single representation table; the SR10 / SR14 / usage-display screens are real restriction sites; the radix-2 / radix-10 / one-byte-per-digit arms exist). These four live inside clauses this compiler SUPPORTS (PICTURE ×2, REDEFINES, USAGE) but describe only what those clauses do DURING THE FORMAT VALIDATION STAGE of a VALIDATE statement — A.4.1's "even if not explicitly listed" is what carries the licence to them. They have NO syntax of their own, so their witness is the statement's, not a new construct: with the statement inert the format-validation stage never runs. GR-13.18.40.4-19 already carried this verdict by hand and its identical sibling GR-13.18.40.4-15 was left blank — the one-answer-per-question drift this batch closes. ⚠ GR-13.18.40.4-14, the PICTURE symbol table, is DELIBERATELY NOT HERE: it CONFORMS with code and a golden, and its only VALIDATE text is an exception ("the symbol A is equivalent to the symbol X except within the execution of a VALIDATE statement").

(3) "The alignment ... is specified in 8.5.1.6.3" - the four placement rules are implemented as a CURSOR WALK rather than a width sum, and the walk was exercised on both branches: probe q6 shows two same-level `PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT` items SHARING one byte (FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH of the group is 1) while each keeps its own value (1010 and 0101 read back distinct), and `1(3) BIT / X(1) / 1(3) BIT` occupies 3 bytes because a bit item that does not immediately follow a same-level bit item restarts at the first bit position of the next available byte. An ELEMENTARY level-01 `PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT` reports BYTE-LENGTH 1 and LENGTH 4 - the 8.5.1.6.3 NOTE excludes a level-1 elementary item from the trailing-filler rule, and WidthBits keeps its exact bit count. THE DISCRIMINATOR that makes this a representation fact and not a relabelling: probe q7 puts the same `PIC 1(8)` at three usages in one program - USAGE BIT is 1 byte, no USAGE clause is 8 and USAGE DISPLAY is 8 - so the packed form is reached only by the usage GR5 names, and the DISPLAY-form boolean keeps GR7's one character per position (SR13 b). conformance:2023/pb43_usage_bit_occupies_bits pins the occupancy with spec-computed expectations. The Usage enum's doc comment still describes USAGE BIT as mapping to the same character storage as a display-form boolean; that is the in-memory CARRIER only - every byte-boundary channel (image, BYTE-LENGTH, group layout) is packed, as measured - so the comment is stale rather than the behaviour wrong. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED -> PARTIAL. GR5's third sentence makes 8.5.1.6.3 the WHOLE of the alignment law for a USAGE BIT item, and 8.5.1.6.3's OPENING SENTENCE scopes its default placement rules to 'when neither a SYNCHRONIZED clause nor an ALIGNED clause is specified'. Two conditions displace the default arm; the adjudicator verified the default arm and neither condition. SYNCHRONIZED IS DISCHARGED - I checked and it survives: 8.5.1.6.3's own filler list makes it implementor latitude ('As defined by the implementor for a bit data item described with the SYNCHRONIZED clause. The implementor defines the positioning rules associated with any filler bit positions'), docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-195 defines it as zero bit positions and MEASURES it (conformance:2002/l1_byte_length_implicit_filler, the SBIT=1 leg, which is exactly two same-level 3-bit USAGE BIT siblings with only the second SYNCHRONIZED). ALIGNED IS NOT DISCHARGED, and it is not latitude. 13.18.1.4 GR1 is mandatory: 'An ALIGNED clause causes the subject of the entry to be aligned on the first bit of the first available byte boundary. Implicit filler bits may be generated to complete the assignment of bits as described in 8.5.1.6.3' - the two sections are interlocked, 8.5.1.6.3 names ALIGNED as a scope condition and 13.18.1.4 GR1 points back into 8.5.1.6.3 for its filler. THE CLAUSE DOES NOT EXIST IN THE COMPILER: zero hits for ALIGNED across all twelve .g4 files and zero in the binder/model. BitLayout's placement predicate is 'IsBitItem(c) && prev is not null && IsBitItem(prev) && prev.Level == c.Level' - it reads only kind and level and has NO ALIGNED (or SYNCHRONIZED) input at all, so it applies 8.5.1.6.3's default arm to items the standard puts outside that arm's scope. The result is a silently wrong storage layout, not a rejection. Everything else in 8.5.1.6.3 I re-measured and it holds, so this is PARTIAL, not DIVERGES: the mixed bit/char group's byte alignment, group image and reference modification all agree (the GR8 national two-width split does NOT exist for bit - ImageWidth and ByteWidth both route through BitLayout.Characters(BitLayout.ExtentBits)); bit GROUP items work including the 'bit group item immediately following a bit group item of the same level' arm; the level-1/77 rule and its NOTE hold; a bit leaf under OCCURS packs contiguously; the 2002 edition gate is right. notes: kb/Work PB547 — TWO OF THE THREE OBLIGATIONS HOLD OUTRIGHT; THE UNIFORM-SIZE CLAUSE HOLDS ONLY OVER THE LATIN-1 SUBSET OF WHAT THE ITEM ACTUALLY ADMITS, AND THE EXCESS IS LOST SILENTLY. HOLDS: "an alphanumeric coded character set shall be used" and "the data item is aligned on a character boundary" - probe q9 (--std 2023) gives BYTE-LENGTH == LENGTH == the declared positions for X(5), 9(5), S9(5) (an unseparate sign shares a digit position), A(5) and ZZ9; probe q71 shows a DISPLAY leaf never shares a byte and never pads (`X(1) 9(1) 1(1)BIT X(1)` is 4 bytes and G(1:1)/G(2:1)/G(4:1) read P/7/Q, i.e. the character leaves sit on byte boundaries and only the BIT leaf takes 8.5.1.6.3's own byte). HOLDS: "Each implementor shall specify the size and representation of characters stored for usage DISPLAY" - A.1 item 209 is the required item and docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-209 states it (one byte per character position, uniform at every length, no per-compilation-unit option), pinned by the spec-derived golden conformance:2023/l1_usage_display_character_size whose UNI leg measures 1/5/9 for X(1)/X(5)/X(9). WHAT IS PARTIAL - "Alphanumeric characters shall be represented in the storage of the computer as characters of UNIFORM SIZE equal to or less than the size of characters in the computer's national character set": the item admits characters the documented size cannot represent, so the size is not uniform across the item's own content. Measured (probe q50, --std 2023): `01 G. 05 A PIC X(3).` with `MOVE "A(U+00E9)(U+2603)" TO A` compiles, and FUNCTION ORD of A(1:1)/A(2:1)/A(3:1) returns 66/234/9732 - the item is holding U+00E9 and U+2603 as UTF-16 CODE UNITS, one per position, and the group image returns the same three values - while FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(A) is 3. At the byte boundary the third character is not represented at all: probe q72 writes that record to a SEQUENTIAL file and the file is exactly 3 bytes, 41 E9 3F - the snowman became '?'. Probe q80 repeats it under `>>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON` and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS comes back BLANK, so the loss is SILENT. That contradicts the implementation's OWN decided disposition, which docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-33 records for the same substitution ("the serialization substitutes '?' (0x3F) and sets EC-DATA-CONVERSION ... never silent") - the CONVERT leg was given the EC and the record/file leg was not, the two-arm shape. The rule's own words are the test: a character in an alphanumeric item is either represented at the uniform size or it is not admitted; here it is admitted, carried at 2 bytes in memory and written at 1 with a substitution nobody is told about. See finding usage-p3/F1. NOTE the neighbouring tension the row does not itself resolve: DOC-A.1-209 says the alphanumeric character is ONE byte while DOC-A.1-188 and DOC-A.1-33 say "the native alphanumeric and national repertoires are UTF-16, one code unit per character position" - the two determinations disagree about the size of the very character GR7 asks the implementor to specify. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DataItem.ElementaryByteWidth (the `_ => ElementaryImageWidth` DISPLAY arm - one byte per character position); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#PicInfo.ByteForm (Usage.Display -> NumericByteForm.Zoned); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/BitLayout.cs#BitsPerCharacter; docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-209; docs/CONFORMANCE.md#DOC-A.1-33 (the '?' substitution disposition) || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85,2002,2014,2023 (USAGE DISPLAY, explicit or implied, is a COBOL-85 element and the implied default at every edition - 13.18.60.3 SR13 b)

subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB546 — THE SIZE THE IMPLEMENTOR SPECIFIED IS NOT THE SIZE THE STORAGE USES, AND THE DISAGREEMENT DISPLACES EVERY LEAF AFTER A NATIONAL ONE. What conforms: the head of the rule and the alignment - `01 N PIC N(4) USAGE NATIONAL.` reports FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH 8 and FUNCTION LENGTH 4 (probe q11), i.e. 2 bytes per national position, and 2 IS "a multiple of the size of characters in the computer's alphanumeric character set" (1, DOC-A.1-209); `01 M PIC N(4).` reports the same, so SR13 a's implied USAGE NATIONAL agrees; national values store, compare and display (conformance:2002/national_data). THE DIVERGENCE, minimal repro (probe q73, --std 2023): `01 G. 05 N PIC N(2) USAGE NATIONAL. 05 A PIC X(2).` with `MOVE N"AB" TO N` and `MOVE "YZ" TO A`. FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(G) = 6 and FUNCTION LENGTH(G) = 6 - so A is DECLARED at positions 5-6 - yet `G(3:2)` reads "YZ" and `G(5:2)` reads two spaces. The same wrong layout crosses a CALL: probe q52 passes G BY REFERENCE to a program whose linkage is `01 W PIC X(6)` and the callee reads ORD 66 67 90 91 33 33 = A,B,Y,Z,space,space; probe q25/q27 show the identical thing through a group MOVE. MECHANISM, located and named by the code itself: DataItem.ElementaryByteWidth answers `2 * ElementaryImageWidth` for Usage.National (the documented D-N1/D-N3 model) while DataItem.IsCharacterImage's comment says a national leaf "contribute[s] their CHARACTER positions to a group image (ImageWidth = Length - never byte-doubled for national)". Two widths for one item, and the consumers split: BYTE-LENGTH / LENGTH / the declared group size take ByteWidth, the image codec and every channel built on it take ImageWidth. DataItem.IsImageCapable's own doc comment asserts the opposite - "Width-wise the codec uses ImageWidth, which IS ByteWidth for every item that reaches an image - the ONE-WIDTH invariant" - and the drift test that guards it, ImageWidthIsStorageWidthTests, carves national out by name (NationalLeaf_IsExactlyTwoBytesPerPosition asserts ImageWidth 4 / ByteWidth 8 and calls it "the ONE sanctioned divergence"), so the invariant cannot catch this and never has. THE IMPLEMENTATION ALREADY KNOWS: the FILE-record channel refuses the same shape LOUD - probe q60 gives COBOLNET0899 "national data in a file record ... the record codec is single-byte and the national character is two bytes (Phase 4a residue; ISO 8.1.2 / 13.18.60.4 GR8)" - so one of the four byte channels is honest and three are silently wrong. What the rule requires: "National characters shall be represented in the storage of the computer as characters of a UNIFORM SIZE equal to or a multiple of the size of characters in the computer's alphanumeric character set" - one size, everywhere, and the implementor's specified size is 2. EXPECTED for the repro: BYTE-LENGTH(G) = 6 with N occupying bytes 1-4 as UTF-16 (00 41 00 42, the form DOC-A.1-33 names for the storage channel) and A at bytes 5-6, so G(5:2) reads "YZ". OWNERSHIP: no kb/Work note covers this. PB327 (open) owns the FILE channel only - the EXTERNAL FD record, the national key and the national space fill - and PB231 (open) the BASED/ALLOCATE refusal; both are REJECTS-LEGAL-SOURCE shapes, whereas this is the silent WRONG-ANSWER shape, and its exact twin PB188 (landed) is the same defect for a byte-form numeric leaf: "seeds a FOUR-character window over a TWO-byte item, silently shifting every following member of the group image". SECOND, SEPARATE GAP IN THIS ROW: the rule's closing sentence ("Each implementor shall specify the size and representation of characters stored for usage NATIONAL") is A.1 item 213, and docs/CONFORMANCE.md has NO DOC-A.1-213 row - the ledger runs 208, 209, 211, 215 and DOC-A.1-209 forward-references "row 213" for the 2-bytes-per-position figure it relies on. See finding usage-p3/F2. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DataItem.ElementaryByteWidth (`Usage.National => 2 * ElementaryImageWidth`) vs src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs#DataItem.IsCharacterImage / DataItem.ImageWidth (a national leaf contributes its CHARACTER positions - "never byte-doubled for national"); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/DataDivision/GroupImageCodec.cs; tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/ImageWidthIsStorageWidthTests.cs#NationalLeaf_IsExactlyTwoBytesPerPosition (the divergence asserted as sanctioned) || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 2002,2014,2023 (USAGE NATIONAL and category national are post-1985: probe q65 gives COBOLNET0900 "national data (PICTURE symbol N / USAGE NATIONAL) requires COBOL-2002" at --std 85)

subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB487 — THE USAGE DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE SPELLING THE GENERAL FORMAT MAKES LEGAL IS SILENTLY SWALLOWED. Nothing in the rule is implemented: MESSAGE-TAG is not a lexer token, not a usageKeyword alternative, has no Usage enum member and no ParseUsage arm, so none of the rule's three claims - "a data item is a message-tag data item", "contains an implementor-defined value that identifies a message and a server or requestor", "The class and category of a message-tag data item are message-tag", and the implementor's alignment/representation/byte-count determination - has any subject. The binder even says so in its own comment (DataBinder.UsageDeclaration.cs:61: "The MESSAGE-TAG phrase is a 2023 addition (VCR row 32) and has no Usage member yet"), and the required A.1 item 212 ("USAGE MESSAGE-TAG (size and contents) ... General rule 9") has no DOC row in docs/CONFORMANCE.md. THE PREFIXED SPELLING IS AT LEAST LOUD: probe q13 gives `01 M USAGE MESSAGE-TAG.` -> COBOL0001 "no viable alternative at input 'MESSAGE-TAG'" - a raw parse error rather than the named COBOLNET0899/0900 band the rest of the staged inventory uses, but a refusal. THE BARE SPELLING IS NOT. 13.18.60.2 prints `[ USAGE IS ]` optional for EVERY usage (kb/Work PB95 landed exactly that reading), so `01 M MESSAGE-TAG.` is the legal COBOL-2023 way to declare a message-tag item - and probe q14 COMPILES IT CLEAN and runs. Probe q76 shows what it became: `01 M MESSAGE-TAG. 05 S PIC X(3).` binds M as an ORDINARY alphanumeric group (BYTE-LENGTH 3, `MOVE "ABC" TO S` works), the MESSAGE-TAG word having been dropped with no diagnostic at any severity. Where the entry is elementary the drop degrades into an unactionable compiler failure: probe q75 (`01 M MESSAGE-TAG.` + `DISPLAY FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(M)`) fails in the BACKEND with a raw `error CS0103: The name 'M' does not exist in the current context`, and probe q29 (the same entry plus `MOVE "ABCD" TO M`) CRASHES the compiler with an unhandled System.NullReferenceException at CodeGen/Verbs/MoveEmitter.cs:287. THE SWALLOW IS NOT SPECIFIC TO THIS WORD, WHICH IS WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ROW: probes q77/q78/q79 show `01 M FOOBAR.`, `01 M FOOBAR PIC X(3).` and `01 M FOOBAR BAZQUX PIC X(3).` all compiling clean and running - an arbitrary run of unknown words between the data-name and the clause list is discarded silently by the data-description-entry parse, so ANY misspelled or unimplemented clause word reaches the binder as if it had not been written. See finding usage-p3/F3. No kb/Work note owns either half. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4#usageKeyword (no MESSAGE-TAG alternative) and src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolLexer.g4 (no MESSAGE_TAG token); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/PictureAnalyzer.cs#PictureAnalyzer.ParseUsage (no arm); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs#Usage (no member); src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs:275 (the word IS reserved at 2023); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.UsageDeclaration.cs:61-62 ("has no Usage member yet, so SR14's message-tag arm and SR21 ... are forward obligations"); src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4#dataDescriptionEntry (the swallow site) || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 2023 only (Annex E.2 item 25 adds MESSAGE-TAG to the reserved words for the asynchronous-messaging facility of E.3.2 item 1, so the rule has no pre-2023 edition; probe q74 confirms COBOLNET0901 'MESSAGE-TAG is a reserved word in COBOL-2023' for a user-defined word of that name)

subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB571 — All four claims held. "a data item is an index data item" - PicInfo.IndexItem is the synthesized PICTURE-less profile, and ResolveIndexItems adjudicates a picture-less USAGE INDEX entry into a group header (usage sheds, GR1) or an elementary index item once the forest is complete. "contains a value that shall correspond to an occurrence number of a table element" - the carrier holds the occurrence number itself, not a byte offset: probe p5 SET I1 TO 3, SET IX TO I1, `IF IX = 3` is true, and `SET I1 TO IX` then `TE(I1)` subscripts correctly; conformance:2023/pb164_index_group_image pins the same fact through a group image round trip with expectations computed from the standard. "The class and category of an index data item are index" - enforced, not merely modelled: probe p6's `MOVE 3 TO IX` draws COBOLNET0809 ("a MOVE operand shall not be of class index"), and conformance:negative/pb148-display-index-item pins the DISPLAY exclusion. "Each implementor specifies the precise effect … upon the alignment and representation … including the actual value assigned for any given occurrence number" - the determination is owner decision R40 (2026-08-30) and docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 item 211: an 8-byte BIG-ENDIAN two's-complement occurrence number; probe p51 reads the bytes back through a group image (ORD 1 … 4 for occurrence 3) and probe p5 reports FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH 8. ⚠ Adjacent but NOT this rule: §13.18.60.3 SR10's closed reference list, where kb/Work PB213 (an index data item admitted as an arithmetic operand and a subscript) and PB215 (one OperandContext member serving sites SR10 separates) are both OPEN - referenced, not re-reported. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The rule's second sentence - 'The class and category of an index data item are index' - is NOT carried through to every class-sensitive site, and the adjudicator measured only the two arms that pass (MOVE -> COBOLNET0809, DISPLAY -> pb148). The class-condition arm leaks and produces a WRONG ANSWER. PicCategory has no Index member at all (PicInfo.cs:10-48); PicInfo.IndexItem is built as `new(PicCategory.Numeric, Usage.Index, ...)` (PicInfo.cs:621), i.e. the model records class/category NUMERIC and the index-ness lives only in Usage. ConditionBinder.CheckClassConditionOperand implements exactly one half of the sibling syntax rule it must honour (SS8.8.4.4.3 SR1, verified with cite.py): it rejects a strongly-typed group and then `if (pic is not { Category: PicCategory.Boolean }) return;` - so class index / pointer / object operands are never screened. Measured with the pinned cobol.exe: `01 IX USAGE INDEX. ... SET IX TO 3  IF IX IS NUMERIC` compiles clean at --std 2023 and PRINTS 'IX IS NUMERIC' (exit 0), where SS8.8.4.4.3 SR1 requires a diagnostic because IX is class index. So the compiler answers a class question about an index data item as though its class were numeric - the precise contradiction of this rule's sentence 2. (The arithmetic-operand arm the adjudicator flagged as PB213 is in fact CLOSED in this pinned tree - COBOLNET0844 fires on both COMPUTE and ADD - which makes the class-condition hole the live one, not a duplicate of PB213.) Sentences 1, 3 and 4 (occurrence-number carrier, implementor determination = 8-byte big-endian, documented at CONFORMANCE.md item 211) do hold. notes: kb/Work PB570 — Every clause of the rule was measured with the pinned compiler. "a radix of 10 is used" and "each digit position shall occupy the minimum possible configuration" - binary-coded decimal, two digit positions per byte: probe p49 moves 123 into a `PIC S9(3) PACKED-DECIMAL` inside a group and reads the group image byte by byte with FUNCTION ORD - 0x12 0x3C for +123, 0x12 0x3D for -123, i.e. the digits packed two per byte with a trailing sign nibble. notes: kb/Work PB496 — THE RULE HAS TWO LIMBS AND EXACTLY ONE IS LIVE. subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB496 — NEITHER OF THIS ROW'S TWO SUBJECTS PARSES, SO BOTH ITS LIMBS AND THE ACTIVE-CLASS HEAD IT CARRIES ARE UNREACHABLE - AND BOTH SPELLINGS ARE LEGAL COBOL THAT IS REFUSED. (1) THE ONLY PHRASE. 13.18.60.2's general format prints `OBJECT REFERENCE [ FACTORY OF ] object-class-name-1 [ ONLY ]`, and this rule states its whole meaning: with ONLY, the referenced object shall be the factory object (a) or an instance object (b) of THE SPECIFIED CLASS - no subclass, i.e. the exact narrowing of GR22 d) 1. objectReferenceUsage has no ONLY tail, so both spellings are a bare parse error: probe q56 (`01 O USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE UBASE ONLY.`) and probe q57 (`01 O USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE FACTORY OF UBASE ONLY.`) both give COBOL0307 "unexpected 'ONLY'. A period may be missing at the end of the previous sentence" at --std 2023 - a misleading message on top of the rejection, since nothing is missing. There is consequently no ONLY model anywhere: a programmer who writes the narrowing the standard provides gets a subclass-admitting reference or no program at all. (2) THE ACTIVE-CLASS HEAD carried on this row - "If ACTIVE-CLASS is specified, the object referenced by this data item shall be of the same class as the object that was used to invoke the method in which this data description entry is specified". The general format prints `OBJECT REFERENCE [ FACTORY OF ] ACTIVE-CLASS`, 13.18.60.3 SR16 independently scopes it to a factory definition, an instance definition or a method's LINKAGE/LOCAL-STORAGE (part 1 recorded that row NOT-IMPLEMENTED), and objectReferenceUsage has no ACTIVE-CLASS alternative - so the word falls into the className slot. Probe q58 declares `01 SELFR USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE ACTIVE-CLASS.` in a method's LOCAL-STORAGE (an SR16-legal position) and gets TWO diagnostics, both wrong about what the program says: COBOLNET0813 "USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE names the unknown class or interface 'ACTIVE-CLASS'" and COBOLNET0901 "'ACTIVE-CLASS' is a reserved word in COBOL-2023 and cannot be used as a user-defined word". The program did not name a class and did not use a reserved word as a user-defined word; it wrote a standard USAGE phrase the grammar lacks. Part 2's GR-13.18.60.4-22 row and its finding objref-only-and-active-class-phrases-missing already own both parse gaps, so this row records the semantic consequence rather than opening a second defect; what is NEW here and belongs with them is the DIAGNOSTIC QUALITY - the ACTIVE-CLASS pair actively misdescribes conforming source (finding usage-p3/F6). subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB496 — TWO INDEPENDENT ABSENCES, EITHER OF WHICH ALONE MAKES THE RULE UNREACHABLE. The rule governs `USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE FACTORY OF ACTIVE-CLASS`: "If the FACTORY phrase is specified, the object referenced by this data item shall be the factory object of that class" - 'that class' being the class of the object that invoked the enclosing method. So there is neither a factory-object reference model nor an ACTIVE-CLASS model for this rule to constrain, and legal COBOL-2002+ source is refused - the second diagnostic misdescribing it as a misuse of a reserved word rather than as an unimplemented standard phrase.
