subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB496 — THE PHRASE IS NOT IN THE GRAMMAR AND THE PROGRAM IS REFUSED WITH A DIAGNOSTIC THAT DESCRIBES SOMETHING IT DID NOT DO. The rule governs `USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE ACTIVE-CLASS` with no FACTORY phrase: "the object referenced by this data item shall be an instance object of that class", i.e. of the class of the object that invoked the method in which the entry appears - the self-typing idiom every OO COBOL uses for a method that returns or holds its own dynamic type. 13.18.60.2 prints it as `OBJECT REFERENCE [ FACTORY OF ] ACTIVE-CLASS`, and 13.18.60.3 SR16 scopes it to a factory definition, an instance definition, or a method definition's LINKAGE or LOCAL-STORAGE section. objectReferenceUsage has three alternatives and none of them is ACTIVE-CLASS, so the word lands in the className slot of `OBJECT REFERENCE className`. Measured at --std 2023, probe q58 puts the declaration in a method's LOCAL-STORAGE - an SR16-legal position, chosen deliberately so the scope rule cannot be the reason for the refusal - and `SET SELFR TO SELF` never gets a chance: the compile fails with COBOLNET0813 "data item 'SELFR': USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE names the unknown class or interface 'ACTIVE-CLASS' - the declared name of a typed object reference shall be a class or interface of the compilation group" and COBOLNET0901 "'ACTIVE-CLASS' is a reserved word in COBOL-2023 and cannot be used as a user-defined word (ISO 8.9)". Both statements are false of the source: the program named no class and used no reserved word as a user-defined word. So the rule has no subject, conforming source is rejected, and the rejection points the programmer at a class-name problem that does not exist. Part 2's GR-13.18.60.4-22 row and its finding objref-only-and-active-class-phrases-missing own the parse gap; what this row adds is that the ACTIVE-CLASS arm is refused even in the position SR16 makes legal, and that its diagnostics misdescribe conforming source (finding usage-p3/F6). Test-ref EMPTY - nothing measures the phrase, and nothing could while it does not parse. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolOO.g4#objectReferenceUsage:183-190 (no ACTIVE-CLASS alternative; `OBJECT REFERENCE className` swallows the word as a class name); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:280 (the declared class resolved against the compilation group - COBOLNET0813); src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs:15 (ACTIVE-CLASS reserved since 2002 - COBOLNET0901) || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 2002,2014,2023 (the ACTIVE-CLASS phrase and USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE are the COBOL-2002 OO facility - Annex A.4.10, an optional module COBOL.NET claims; probe q69 is COBOLNET0900 at --std 85)

subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB548 — EVERY SENTENCE BUT THE LAST HOLDS, AND THE LAST ONE - THE TYPE-SAFETY GUARANTEE - LEAKS THROUGH A THIRD SET ARM. HOLDS: "specifies a data-pointer data item ... that may contain the address of a data item" - probe q38 (--std 2023) sets a pointer to ADDRESS OF a WORKING-STORAGE item, rebases a BASED item through it, reads "ABCD", repoints to a second item and reads "WXYZ", compares two pointers (NE), sets NULL (equal to NULL) and copies pointer to pointer. "Each implementor defines the precise effect ... upon alignment, size, representation, and range of values" - the carrier is 8 bytes (FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH, probe q38) with no alignment padding; ⚠ the REQUIRED A.1 item 216 ("USAGE POINTER clause (alignment, size, representation, and range of values) ... General rule 23") has NO DOC row in docs/CONFORMANCE.md, so the determination the rule demands is made in code and not published - a documentation gap this row carries. "If type-name-1 is specified, this data item is a restricted data-pointer" - kb/Work PB153 landed the model: StrongTypeModel reduces both a POINTER TO T declaration and an ADDRESS OF operand to a type name, 13.18.60.3 SR18 screens the declaration shape (part 1 recorded that row CONFORMS), and probe q39 shows the legal spelling working end to end (`01 TT IS TYPEDEF STRONG. 01 PT IS TYPEDEF USAGE POINTER TO TT. 01 P TYPE PT.` accepts SET P TO NULL and SET P TO ADDRESS OF a TYPE TT item); probe q42 rebases a `TYPE TT BASED` item through it and reads the right field; probe q40 refuses ADDRESS OF a DIFFERENT strong type (COBOLNET0869 citing 14.9.39.3 SR19) and probe q49 refuses the converse direction (SR20). ⛔ WHAT FAILS - "A restricted data-pointer shall contain only the predefined address NULL or the address of a data item of the specified type." Probe q62 (--std 2023) defeats it in three statements: `01 R USAGE POINTER.` (unrestricted), `SET R TO ADDRESS OF C` where `01 C PIC X(8) VALUE "12345678"` is not of type TT, then `SET P TO R` - ACCEPTED with no diagnostic - then `SET ADDRESS OF L TO P` with `01 L TYPE TT BASED.` and `DISPLAY F1 OF L` prints "1234". A restricted data-pointer is now holding, and dereferencing, the address of an item that is not of its type; Annex D.9.2.2's whole stated purpose ("precluding the treatment of data of one type as data of another type") is gone, and the value delivered is another item's storage read under the wrong description. The governing rule is 14.9.39.3 SR19 first sentence (cite --check OK): "If identifier-5 references a restricted data-pointer, identifier-6 shall be the predefined address NULL or shall reference a data-pointer restricted to the same type" - an UNRESTRICTED pointer is neither, so `SET P TO R` shall be rejected. MECHANISM: PtrBinder.BindSetAddress screens SR19/SR20 in BOTH of its arms and its comment says so ("⛔ THE SECOND ARM, AND IT IS A SEPARATE CODE PATH - the two-arm question asked and answered"), but the plain pointer-to-pointer Format-7 assignment is a THIRD path, SetBinder.BindSetPointer (SetBinder.cs:195-231), which resolves both operands, checks only `Pic?.Category is PicCategory.Pointer`, and never consults StrongTypeModel at all. kb/Work PB153 is status LANDED and its note claims "14.9.39.3 SR19 and SR20 in BOTH arms of BindSetAddress" - true, and the arm it never counted is the one that leaks. The negative goldens follow the same blind spot: pb153-set-address-strong-to-unrestricted and pb153-set-unrestricted-to-address-of-strong pin the ADDRESS-OF directions; nothing pins pointer-to-pointer. ⚠ A citation defect at the same site: BindSetPointer's two diagnostics cite "ISO 14.9.39 Format 4" for a data-pointer SET, but Format 4 is the condition-name SET (14.9.39.3 SR6/SR7) and data-pointer assignment is Format 7. subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB549 — THE CARRIER AND THE OUTERMOST-PROGRAM RULE BOTH HOLD; THE ONLY ISO SPELLING THAT LOADS ONE DOES NOT PARSE. HOLDS: "specifies a program-pointer data item ... that may contain the address of a program" - probe q47 (--std 2023) declares `01 PP USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER.`, loads it with the address of a SIBLING OUTERMOST program, finds it NOT NULL, CALLs through it and gets the callee's output back through a USING operand, copies it to a second program-pointer (the two compare EQUAL) and sets that one to NULL (which compares equal to NULL). "Each implementor defines the precise effect ... upon alignment, size, and representation" - the carrier is 8 bytes (FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH, probe q47) over the run-unit ProgramTable, with no alignment padding; ⚠ the REQUIRED A.1 item 217 ("USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER clause (alignment, size, and representation of data; and ALLOWABLE LANGUAGES) ... General rule 24") has NO DOC row in docs/CONFORMANCE.md, so neither the representation nor the "another language for which the implementor has declared support" list is published - and no other-language support is declared anywhere, which is a permitted choice but an undocumented one. HOLDS, and this is the sentence most implementations get wrong: "For a COBOL program, the address is for an OUTERMOST program." Probe q44 declares a CONTAINED program UP3INN2 inside UP3GR24E: a direct `CALL "UP3INN2"` reaches it ("NEST"), but the program-pointer loaded with the same name comes back NULL - the contained program is not an outermost program and is correctly not addressable through a program-pointer, which matches 8.4.3.13.4 GR2 ("For a COBOL program, the address is that of the outermost program identified by the externalized program-name in its PROGRAM-ID paragraph", cite --check OK) and its GR4 NULL-when-not-locatable. ⛔ WHAT IS PARTIAL: the ONLY way ISO 2023 gives a program to a program-pointer is the program-address-identifier of 8.4.3.13.2 - `ADDRESS OF PROGRAM { identifier-1 | literal-1 | program-prototype-name-1 }` - and it is not in the grammar. Probe q48: `SET PP TO ADDRESS OF PROGRAM "UP3SUBF"` is COBOL0001 "no viable alternative at input 'PROGRAM'" plus COBOL0201 "PROGRAM is a reserved word" (measured at --std 2023; q46 the same). What COBOL.NET accepts instead is `SET pp TO ENTRY literal`, and the words TO ENTRY appear NOWHERE in the 2023 standard's SET formats (grep of specs/ISO_COBOL.md for "TO ENTRY" returns nothing) - it is the MF/IBM vendor spelling. The grammar comment at CobolParserCore.g4:1213 describes the rule as "ISO 14.9.39 Format 9 with the 8.4.3.13 program-address-identifier as the sender", but Format 9 is `SET {identifier-7}... subject: USAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB497 — THE CONSTRUCT IS RECOGNIZED AND REFUSED BY NAME, AND NOTHING BEHIND THE REFUSAL EXISTS. Measured at --std 2023: probe q21 (`01 PT IS TYPEDEF USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER TO PROTO1.` reached through `01 P TYPE PT.`) and probe q22 (the direct `01 P USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER TO PROTO1.`) both give COBOLNET0899 "data item 'P': USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER TO program-prototype-name (ISO 13.18.60 GR25)" - the SAME diagnostic whether or not the entry is a type declaration, i.e. it fires from the entry-bind arm before any rule about the shape can run. So neither half of GR25 has a subject: "If program-prototype-name-1 is specified, this data item is a restricted program-pointer" is never established (there is no restricted-program-pointer model to set - StrongTypeModel carries a data-pointer restriction only), and "A restricted program-pointer shall contain only the predefined address NULL or the address of a program with the same signature as that identified by the specified program-prototype-name" has no signature to compare against, because the program-prototype registry is the P13 repository work the docs/DIAGNOSTICS.md row names ("signature matching needs the program-prototype registry (P13); the unrestricted form is live"). Its statement-level twin 14.9.39.3 SR22 is likewise unenforced, and part 1 recorded the neighbouring declaration rule 13.18.60.3 SR19 NOT-IMPLEMENTED for the same reason - the 0899 fires first and SR19's question is never asked, twenty lines from the data-pointer twin SR18 that IS written. notes: kb/Work PB497 — RECOGNIZED, STAGED LOUD, NOTHING BEHIND IT. subject: VALUE clause
notes: kb/Work PB574 — BOTH SUBJECT SHAPES ENFORCED, AND THE PREDICATE STATES THE RULE RATHER THAN A RESIDUE. `Sr1SubjectShape` tests StrongTypeModel.IsStrongGroup then ReferenceResolver.HasVariableLengthSubordinate, the second keyed to 8.5.1.12.1's definition ("a group item whose data description has at least one dynamic-length elementary item or dynamic-capacity table as a subordinate item" -- cite.py --check OK) and NOT to occurs-depending, which is a fixed-length group. MEASURED at the pin: a STRONG TYPEDEF group reference carrying a VALUE draws COBOLNET1703 at --std 2023 and 2002 (probes sr1_strong_group, sr1_strong_2002); a dynamic-capacity table TWO levels below the subject draws it (sr1_varlen_dyncap_deep -- the walk is the whole subtree, not the immediate children); a DYNAMIC LENGTH elementary item under the subject draws it (b_sr1_dynlen_group), and the same group WITHOUT the VALUE compiles clean (b_sr1_dynlen_only, the over-rejection control). The screen runs over CompositionForest, not ConformanceForest, so `01 R TYPE T VALUE "..."` -- where the VALUE and the offending shape come from different entries -- is caught (conformance:negative/pb184-group-value-type-reference), and it fires once per WRITTEN VALUE via DataItem.ValueIsCopied so a SAME AS / TYPE copy does not re-report its source's entry. SCOPE CHECK: the code screens only `item.IsGroup`, which loses nothing -- both shapes SR1 names are by definition group items. EDITIONS: the rule text is under the ALL FORMATS heading and is edition-invariant as written; its two subject shapes are themselves post-85 constructs, so at COBOL-85 the rule has no population (the two negatives are pinned reject-at 2002+ and 2023 respectively for that reason). Annex E records no 2023 change to SR1. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — SR1 names TWO subject shapes and only ONE of them survives TYPE composition -- the [[two_arm_dispatch]] shape the adjudicator's own class doc says the CompositionForest design fixed. MEASURED WRONG-ACCEPTANCE: `01 T TYPEDEF. 05 D PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH. 01 R TYPE T VALUE "AB".` compiles and runs clean (probe r17_sr1_typedef_varlen), and the same shape with the dynamic-length item one level deeper also compiles (r32_sr1_typedef_varlen_deep). The program is NON-CONFORMING: 13.18.57.4 GR2a (cite.py --check OK) -- "the subject of the entry is a group whose subordinate elements have the same names, descriptions, and hierarchy as the subordinate elements of type-name-1" -- gives R a dynamic-length elementary subordinate, so R IS a variable-length group by 8.5.1.12.1 (cite.py --check OK), and 13.16.3 SR14 (cite.py --check OK) expressly permits TYPE and VALUE in the same entry, so the shape is legal to WRITE and SR1 is the rule that must reject it. The byte-equivalent INLINE spelling `01 R VALUE "AB". 05 D PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH.` DOES draw COBOLNET1703 (r19_sr1_inline_varlen) -- the exact accept/reject asymmetry between a TYPE reference and its inline spelling that the class doc claims was the first landing's bug and was fixed. SR1's OTHER shape does compose through TYPE (r10 at --std 2014 and r18 both draw 1703 on `01 R TYPE T VALUE "AB"` with a STRONG T), which is what makes this one arm, not the whole rule. ROOT CAUSE, measured, is upstream of this pass: the TYPE clone DROPS the DYNAMIC LENGTH clause -- `MOVE "ABCDE" TO D IN R` then FUNCTION LENGTH(D IN R) prints 1 through a TYPEDEF (r20) but 5 inline (r21), a silent WRONG-ANSWER defect in its own right -- so ReferenceResolver.HasVariableLengthSubordinate is asking a composed tree that no longer carries the fact. That does not rescue the row: the rule is unenforced on a reachable, legal-to-write population. The cited negative pins only the INLINE dynamic-capacity spelling at 2023 (tests/conformance/negative/pb184-group-value-variable-length-subject.cob -- `01 GV VALUE "ABCDE". 05 GB PIC X OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY ...`), so no test covers the composed shape. Everything else the adjudicator claimed re-measured clean: the 8.5.1.12.1 predicate excludes occurs-depending correctly, the strong arm fires at 2002/2014/2023, the Format-2 table carrier reaches SR1 (r11), and IsGroupValueSubject's item.IsGroup narrowing loses nothing. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.GroupValue.cs#Sr1SubjectShape (:190-197) called from #CheckGroupValueDeclarations (:74-93) -> DiagnosticCatalog.GroupValueSubjectShape (COBOLNET1703); the pass is declared in src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Passes/BindPipeline.cs:43; the subject predicate is #IsGroupValueSubject (:174-176), which reads BOTH VALUE carriers (RawValue = format 1, TableValues = format 2, per SR16)

The claim this row carried since 2026-08-18 - that SR2's ALL FORMATS reach was covered because 'the item VALUE and the condition-name VALUEs share the funnel' - named only TWO of the three literal carriers. The FORMAT 2 (table) literals of BuildTableValueSpecs reached the emitter through NO screen at all, so `05 B PIC 9(4) COMP OCCURS 2 VALUE "0012" FROM (1) TO (2).` compiled clean at strict 2023 while its format-1 twin was COBOLNET1657. notes: RE-RECORDED 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB598) — the SUBJECT of each sentence, which this row had right for what SR4 forbids and wrong for what it admits. SR4 is three sentences: a category sentence, then 'Alphanumeric literals in the VALUE clause of an elementary item shall not exceed the size indicated by an explicit PICTURE clause' and 'Alphanumeric literals in the VALUE clause of an alphanumeric group item shall not exceed the size of the group item'. The 2026-09-04 landing (PB206) closed both size sentences, which had silently TRUNCATED, and this row was recorded CONFORMS on that evidence — but the screen it landed was reached by the three level-88 call sites in BindCondition carrying the CONDITIONAL VARIABLE's size, so it also applied the elementary-item sentence to a subject neither sentence names. `01 XV PIC X. 88 XC VALUE "cd".` became COBOLNET1740, legal source rejected, and GnuCOBOL differential case syn_misc:388 flipped from AGREE_ACCEPT to WE_REJECT_THEY_ACCEPT. A Format-3 entry is `88 condition-name-1 value-clause .` (13.16.2), which admits no PICTURE clause, so no EXPLICIT picture indicates a size; SR33 makes that level-88 entry the subject of the entry; 8.5.1.3.2 item 3 gives a condition-name entry 'no true concept of level', so it is neither of 8.5.1.3.1's record subdivisions; and 13.18.63.4 GR19 gives it its conditional variable's characteristics only IMPLICITLY, which is exactly what 'explicit' excludes. The three subjects the rule addresses are now a TYPE, ValueSubject, built only by ForElementary / ForGroup / ForConditionName, so a call site cannot compose a size the standard does not give it. The category sentence is unaffected and still binds a condition-name (SR4 is an ALL FORMATS rule). And the standard defines what an oversize condition-name literal MEANS, which a size rule would make dead text: 8.8.4.5.3 item 2 sends the comparison to the relation-condition rules, so it never compares equal; 14.9.39.4 GR6 -> 13.18.63.4 GR7 -> 14.6.8.5 places it 'with space fill or truncation to the right'. The 85 golden pb598_condition_name_value_size derives every one of those answers from the rules before measuring them; the pb206 negatives and ConditionNameValueSizeTests.TheSizeSentencesStillBindAnElementaryAndAGroupSubject are the drift proof that withholding the size from a condition-name did not withhold it from the two subjects the sentences do name (that test was measured RED against a deliberately over-withholding build). A FIGURATIVE operand remains exempt by rule (8.3.3.6.4 GR2). Error at every edition: Annex E.2 item 27's 2023 size change is scoped to numeric-edited items (COBOLNET1570).

notes: kb/Work PB553 — THE PROHIBITION HOLDS; THE PERMITTED SIGNED SPELLING IS A PARSE ERROR. The grammar makes a non-literal or non-integer subscript unrepresentable, so the rule cannot be violated: MEASURED, `FROM (1.5)` is COBOL0001 "unexpected '1.5'" (probe sr19_noninteger_subscript) and `FROM (K)` naming a level-78 constant is COBOL0309 "A literal value is expected here, not a data-name" (sr19_word_subscript). Both are GENERIC parse errors: the rule is enforced by the grammar's shape, not written down, and no diagnostic names SR19. BUT `INTEGERLIT` is unsigned digits only, while 8.3.3.3.2 says "If a sign is used, it shall appear as the leftmost character of the literal" and "An integer literal is a fixed-point numeric literal that contains no decimal point" (both cite.py --check OK) -- so `+1` IS an integer numeric literal and SR19 admits it. MEASURED: `VALUE "AB" FROM (+1) TO (+3)` is COBOL0001 at --std 2023 (b_sr19_signed) -- legal source rejected, with a parse error the user cannot map to a rule. The same unsigned-only rule serves `occursBound`, so `01 T PIC X OCCURS +3.` is also a parse error (c_occurs_signed): the defect is a grammar-wide pattern at every integer-literal position, not a VALUE-clause one. Overflow is handled safely rather than correctly -- a subscript too wide for Int32 becomes 0 and then trips the SR20 range check, so it is rejected, but as an out-of-range subscript. See findings value-clause-p1/F9. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4:635-640 (valueClauseTablePhrase -- `FROM LPAREN integerLiteral (COMMA? integerLiteral)* RPAREN` and the TO twin), resolving to src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4:563-565 (`integerLiteral : INTEGERLIT`) and src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolLexer.g4:791 (`fragment INT_BODY : [0-9]+`); the value is read at src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:3192 (`int.TryParse(il.GetText(), out int n) ? n : 0`)

At entry the subprogram displays IN=[12345]: the linkage VALUE did NOT take effect at activation, so the caller's storage is intact (the negative half). `INITIALIZE L ALL TO VALUE` then displays INIT=[ZZZZZ] and the CALLER sees AFTER=[ZZZZZ] -- the VALUE took effect exactly at the INITIALIZE and wrote through to the caller's storage, which is also the right answer for 14.2.3 GR8 (BY REFERENCE aliasing). notes: kb/Work PB562 + PB565 — GR21 IMPORTS FOUR RULES INTO FORMAT 4; THREE OF THE FOUR ARE WRONG OR UNREACHABLE. MEASURED at STRICT --std 2023 (probe gr21rw, a TYPE DE group written to a LINE SEQUENTIAL file and read back, columns counted mechanically): (GR7, JUSTIFIED) `03 COLUMN 1 PIC X(5) JUSTIFIED RIGHT VALUE "AB"` prints [   AB] at columns 1-5 -- GR7 says "initialization is not affected by a JUSTIFIED clause", and the IDENTICAL item in WORKING-STORAGE prints [AB   ] (probe gr7just), so the two paths disagree and the report path is the wrong one. (GR7, editing) `03 COLUMN 8 PIC XXBXX VALUE "ABCDE"` prints [AB CD] at columns 8-12 -- GR7 says "no editing takes place", 13.18.63.3 SR11 says editing characters in an alphanumeric-edited picture "do not cause editing of the initial value", and 13.18.63.3 SR34 makes SR11 apply to Format 4 explicitly; the same item in WORKING-STORAGE prints [ABCDE]. (GR8) `03 COLUMN 16 PIC ZZZ9 BLANK WHEN ZERO VALUE "0000"` prints four SPACES at columns 16-19 -- GR8 says BLANK WHEN ZERO "has no effect on initialization" for an alphanumeric literal; the same item in WORKING-STORAGE prints [0000]. The controls in the same run are right: `COLUMN 22 PIC ZZZ9 BLANK WHEN ZERO VALUE ZERO` blanks (NOTE 1's case) and `COLUMN 28 PIC ZZZ9 VALUE 12` prints [  12]. (GR9) NOT REACHABLE: `03 COLUMN 1 PIC X(3) OCCURS 3 VALUE "AAA"` draws COBOLNET0899 "OCCURS in a report group description (ISO 13.18.38 repeating entries) is not yet implemented" (probe gr21occ), so GR9's Format-4 population is refused on legal source. (GR1, float approximation) unmeasured -- no float printable item was built. ONE MECHANISM, THREE WRONG ANSWERS: routing a VALUE through the SOURCE clause's implicit MOVE applies exactly the three transforms GR21's imports exclude. Reported as a finding. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/ReportWriterEmitter.cs:128-160 FieldImage -- `case FieldValueSource v: source = ValueOperand(v.Raw); break;` followed by the unconditional `return move.ConvertSource(source, f.PrintItem);`, i.e. a Format-4 VALUE is pushed through the SAME implicit-MOVE conversion the SOURCE clause uses (13.18.53.4 GR1). The printable item carries Justified and BlankWhenZero from src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Reports.cs:535-536 and its edit mask from the PICTURE, and ConvertSource honours all three. The GR9 leg has no vehicle: DataBinder.Reports.cs:434-437 refuses report-group OCCURS by name (COBOLNET0899). || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 2002, 2014, 2023 -- MEASURED byte-identical at 2002, 2014 (probe edrw2002/edrw2014) and 2023 (probe gr21rw). FieldImage carries no version predicate, so the pre-2002 leg is reasoned, not measured: the repeating/positioning vehicles used to reach it (multiple COLUMN) are themselves gated to 2002+ by COBOLNET0900. notes: kb/Work PB506 — THE RULE IS UNIMPLEMENTED AND FAILS SILENTLY WITH A WRONG ANSWER. SENTENCE 1 ("successive operands are assigned to successive repeating printable items, horizontally and then vertically") -- probe gr23rw: `03 COLUMNS ARE 1 6 11 PIC X(3) VALUE "AAA" "BBB" "CCC".` prints `AAA  AAA  AAA` at columns 1/6/11, compiling CLEAN at STRICT 2023 with no diagnostic. SPEC-DERIVED EXPECTED: `AAA  BBB  CCC`. SENTENCE 2 ("If no further operands remain, assignment begins again from the first operand") -- probe gr23wrap: the same entry with only two operands `"AAA" "BBB"` prints `AAA  AAA  AAA`; expected `AAA  BBB  AAA`. SENTENCE 3 (suppressed items still consume operands) is unreachable while sentences 1-2 are unimplemented. THE MECHANISM IS VISIBLE, not merely inferred -- probe gr23glue: a single-COLUMN `03 COLUMN 20 PIC X(12) VALUE "XX" "YY".` prints `XX"YY`, i.e. ExtractValue's GetText() glued the operand tokens into the raw text `"XX""YY"` and the literal decoder then read the doubled quote as an escaped one; in the X(3) case the same glue (`AAA"BB"C`) is simply truncated to `AAA`, which is why the three columns look like a replication. So a multi-operand Format-4 VALUE today produces either a corrupt single value or a silently replicated first operand, never the spec's per-repetition assignment. Reported as a finding; the fix is structural (a per-repetition operand list on the field model), not a guard. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:2975-2992 ExtractValue -- `var item = value.valueItem().FirstOrDefault(); ... return item.GetText() is { } raw ? NormalizeIfNumericLiteral(raw) : null;` collapses the WHOLE operand list to one string; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Reports.cs:439-440 (the report-section caller) and DataBinder.Reports.cs:161 `public sealed record FieldValueSource(string Raw)` -- the model carries ONE scalar per field, so there is nowhere for a per-repetition operand list to live; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/ReportWriterEmitter.cs:134 emits that single value into every repetition of the entry's COLUMN list. The Format-1 sibling of the same glue IS rejected (DataBinder.cs:2404-2409, COBOLNET1585) -- the report path is the arm that was never given the check. || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 2002, 2014, 2023 -- MEASURED byte-identical at 2002 and 2014 (probe edrw2002/edrw2014) and 2023 (probes gr23rw, gr23wrap, gr23glue). ExtractValue and FieldValueSource carry no version predicate; the pre-2002 leg is unmeasured because the multiple COLUMN repetition vehicle is 2002-gated (COBOLNET0900). Annex E carries no 2023 item touching GR23. (13.18.63.3 SR35, the syntax rule that admits the multi-operand form, is already recorded DIVERGES on its own row in the sibling part.)

SR-39 in particular was REFUSED by the deriver as an all-formats editorial rule and the refuter overturned that: format 5's general format is the only one printing VALUE / VALUES WITHOUT the IS / ARE connectives, with a separate [ IS / ARE ] bracket governing { INVALID / VALID } — so SR-39 is the rule that licenses that detached bracket and is genuinely format-5's.

subject: ADD statement
notes: READ: the grammar alternative `ADD (CORRESPONDING | CORR) dataReference TO dataReference roundedPhrase? arithmeticOnSizeError? END_ADD?` (CobolParserCore.g4:851) and CorrespondingBinder.BindAddCorresponding (25-29), `add.CORRESPONDING() is not null || add.CORR() is not null ? Bind(CorrVerb.Add, add.dataReference(), ...) : new BoundUnsupported(...)`. The two spellings are ONE grammar alternative and ONE boolean disjunction feeding ONE Bind call, so there is no second dispatch arm that could carry different behaviour -- the equivalence is structural rather than a pair of parallel code paths (the two-arm-dispatch failure shape does not apply here). Neither token is edition-gated: no ConstructRegistry row in tests/version-matrix/constructs.json mentions CORR or CORRESPONDING, and Annex E carries no ADD entry, so the batch default editions stand. TEST HONESTY: the golden cited exercises the CORRESPONDING spelling on ADD; the CORR spelling is exercised on SUBTRACT (conformance-test:CorrespondingDifferentialTests.SubtractCorr_TargetMinusSource_CorrToken), through the sibling alternative at CobolParserCore.g4:890 and the identical `sub.CORRESPONDING() is not null || sub.CORR() is not null` disjunction -- so the CORR-on-ADD spelling specifically has no test of its own. Adding `ADD CORR SRC TO DST` to an existing CORR golden would make the coverage exhaustive; nothing about the code makes it a risk. || UPHELD, with evidence the record did not have. The structural argument is only sound if the two spellings are also indistinguishable to the LEXER, which I checked rather than assumed: Core/CobolLexer.g4:455 `CORR : 'CORR' ;` and :459 `CORRESPONDING : 'CORRESPONDING' ;` are both UNCONDITIONAL token rules -- no `{isXXXX()}?` version predicate on either -- and ANTLR's maximal-munch keeps CORRESPONDING whole rather than splitting it into CORR + a word, so neither spelling can degrade into a data-name at any edition. Had CORR been edition-gated or context-sensitive, `ADD CORR X TO Y` would have fallen to grammar alternative 2 and bound CORR as an ADDEND -- a silent wrong answer -- which is the failure mode this check rules out. Also verified: alternative 1 precedes alternative 2, so the Format-3 parse always wins, and BindAddCorresponding's `else` arm is unreachable (BindAdd routes here only when `addOperandList()` is null, which only alternative 1 produces). I also independently confirmed the edition claim per ground rule 4: Annex E (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:42847 onward) lists no ADD substantive change, and the rule text carries no edition qualifier, so the batch default 85,2002,2014,2023 is the derived answer, not a copied one. CONFORMS-but-thinly-tested is the correct outcome here (ground rule 3), and the record's own honesty note about the CORR-on-ADD spelling stands.

notes: Rule (--check OK, §14.9.3.3 1): data-name-1 shall be described with the BASED clause. The level number of such data description entries shall be 1 or 77' — so a based entry is never in an FD and has no containing group, and the only legal reference to it is the bare name that `dref.ChildCount == 1` admits. notes: kb/Work PB231 (the POINTER third, 2026-09-05) CLOSES this row. The byte-window carriage gate DataBinder.ByteWindowResidueOf now has NO residue: every leaf kind reaching it is carried, so GR3's 'the amount of storage to be allocated is the number of bytes required to hold an item as described by data-name-1' is computed and observed for EVERY legal data-name-1 this compiler admits. The pointer third was the last one, and its mechanism is the only one that is not a byte layout: a class-pointer / class-object item holds a MANAGED REFERENCE, which is not a byte sequence, so it rides the same storage area's MANAGED SLOT (StorageCell.SlotAt / CobolPtr.SlotRead, addressed through Place.SlotWindow at the byte offset its RESERVED bytes occupy). The reservation is what keeps GR3 a byte quantity: 13.18.60.4 GR23 leaves the size to the implementor ('Each implementor defines the precise effect of the USAGE POINTER clause upon alignment, size, representation, and range of values of the data item in the storage of the computer') and COBOL.NET pins EIGHT, so conformance:2002/pb231_based_pointer_leaf ALLOCATEs 01 P USAGE POINTER BASED, windows the cell through a second BASED PIC X(8) entry - a shorter cell would raise EC-BOUND-PTR at the dereference, 13.18.5.4 GR4 - and reads bytes 1 and 8 with FUNCTION ORD as 33 33 (the space) BOTH BEFORE AND AFTER the pointer is given a real address, which is the assertion that the value is not in the image while the eight bytes are still allocated. notes: Rule re-read in context at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 14.9.4.4 1) under the 'FORMATS 1 AND 2' heading; citation validated (`cite.py --check 14.9.4.4 "The instance of the program, function, or method that executes the CALL statement is the activating runtime element."` -> OK, General rules 1). Expected behavior derived before reading code: the CALL's executing INSTANCE (not its compilation unit) is the activating runtime element, so (a) the called program's name is resolved in the ACTIVATOR's 8.4.6.3 scope, (b) control returns to that instance, and (c) anything that names the activating element (FUNCTION MODULE-NAME(ACTIVATING), the module stack, and the container-instance handle a CONTAINED callee reaches its GLOBAL storage through) must answer per ACTIVATION. || UPHELD (the verified half): ProgramTable.CallProgram takes `callerPath` (CallEmitter.EmitCall supplies `callState.SelfPath`; EmitterState.cs#CallUnitState documents it as 'the emitted unit's qualified program path - the CALL/CANCEL calling-path argument (8.4.6.3); set per unit'), passes it to ResolveVisible, and pushes a PER-ACTIVATION frame `_owner.Modules.Push(n.Name, OutermostName(n), n.ParentPath is not null)` inside the `n.Active++` / try-finally pair; tests/conformance/2023/pb36_module_name_invoke_activation.out pins R-STACK=[PB36MNREC;PB36MNREC;PB36MNREC;PB36MODNAME; ] and R-ACT=[PB36MNREC], so the module-name view of the activating element IS per activation, and C-ACT/I-ACT/D-ACT cover the program and method cases. || REFUTED (why this is not CONFORMS): the adjudicator verified only the module-name/depth view and read `Node.Instance`/`Node.Active` as proof that 'instance identity is real'. It is not maintained across nested activations. Read ProgramTable.CallProgram lines 180-233: for an INITIAL or RECURSIVE unit it does `inst = n.Factory(ParentInstance(n)); n.Instance = inst;` and the `finally` restores ONLY `n.Active--`, the module frame and the EC masks - `n.Instance` is NEVER restored to the outer activation's instance. ProgramTable.ParentInstance reads exactly that field (`_byPath[n.ParentPath].Instance`), and ProgramEmitter.EmitProgramClass emits a contained program's container handle as `private readonly {parent.ClassName} __outer;` assigned once in the constructor, with every inherited GLOBAL item reaching container storage through it (`private ref {type} {b.Field} => ref {b.Path};   // GLOBAL item of a containing program (ISO 13.18.27 GR2)`, BinderDriver.BindUnitData building `__outer.` prefixes). So for a RECURSIVE container R containing C: R#1 calls C -> C is a cached singleton (`inst = n.Instance ??= n.Factory(ParentInstance(n))`) with __outer = inst1; R#1 calls itself -> inst2, `R.Instance = inst2`; inst2 calls C -> the SAME cached C, still bound to inst1, so the callee reads and writes the OUTER activation's storage. The reverse is broken too: after inst2 returns, `R.Instance` still names inst2, so a per-activation callee constructed from inst1's CALL gets a TERMINATED instance as its activating element. Reachable on conforming source: the WORKING-STORAGE composition is loud-staged (DiagnosticCatalog.RecursiveContainedWs, negative fixture tests/conformance/negative/recursive-contained-ws.cob) but LOCAL-STORAGE is not, and 13.18.27.3 SR1b (`cite.py --check 13.18.27.3` -> OK) permits IS GLOBAL on 'A data description entry whose level-number is 1 that is specified in the file, working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section' - so `PROGRAM-ID. R RECURSIVE.` + `LOCAL-STORAGE SECTION. 01 LS-G PIC 9(4) GLOBAL.` + a contained C that references LS-G compiles and answers with the wrong activation's automatic data. SECOND, INDEPENDENT HALF: the recursive attribute is not per-containment either - BinderDriver.MakeUnit sets `recursive` ONLY from this unit's own PROGRAM-ID clause plus `if (isFunction) recursive = true`, while 11.10.4 GR4 (`cite.py --check 11.10.4 "The RECURSIVE clause specifies that the program and any programs contained within it are recursive."` -> OK) makes every program contained in a RECURSIVE program recursive, so those containees take the cached-singleton instance model (last-used state) instead of the per-activation instance this rule's 'instance ... is the activating runtime element' requires. What would close the row: an activation STACK of instances per node (push/pop around `inst.Call`) so ParentInstance answers 'the instance that is executing the CALL', __outer rebound per activation for a contained callee, the 11.10.4 GR4 attribute inheritance, plus a golden with a RECURSIVE container, a LOCAL-STORAGE GLOBAL item and a contained callee printing it at two depths. Editions: no Annex E delta touches this rule (E.2's only CALL entry is item 1 bullet 3, the ON OVERFLOW removal), so the batch default applies.

CobolArgAdapt.StoreReturn's whole overload set is (long, ulong, Int128, UInt128, string) over `WriteNumericCell` (which handles ManagedPointer<long|ulong|Int128|UInt128> and nothing else), while ProgramEmitter.EmitCallMethod emits the value UNCAST - `RuntimeApi.ArgAdaptStoreReturn("__ret", PlaceRenderer.Read(ret))` when `!CallEmitter.CallPlaceIsString(ret)`. DataItem.ElementType is `Pic?.ClrType`, and PicInfo.ClrType maps PicCategory.Pointer -> `ManagedPointer`, ProgramPointer -> `ProgramPointer`, ObjectReference -> the emitted class type; CallPlaceIsString covers none of those (it tests RedefViewPlace / IsGroup / StoreAsImage - itself gated on `Category: PicCategory.Numeric` - / Alphanumeric / NumericEdited / National / Boolean / IsFloat). So a program whose PROCEDURE DIVISION RETURNING item is a USAGE POINTER, PROGRAM-POINTER or OBJECT REFERENCE linkage item emits `CobolArgAdapt.StoreReturn(__ret, <ManagedPointer-typed expr>)`, for which NO overload is applicable and ManagedPointer declares no conversion operators - a Roslyn CS1503 on generated user source, not a COBOL diagnostic, and nothing upstream rejects it: DataBinder.CallBindLinkage's RETURNING arm only checks `FindLinkageRoot`, and the class restriction 14.2.2 SR2 imposes applies to data-name-1 (BY VALUE formals), never to data-name-2 - SR5 (`cite.py --check 14.2.2 "Data-name-2 shall be defined as a level 01 entry or level 77 entry in the linkage section."` -> OK) imposes no class limit, and neither does 14.9.4.3 SR7 on identifier-3 (`cite.py --check 14.9.4.3 "Identifier-3 shall reference a data item defined in the file, working-storage, local-storage, or linkage section."` -> OK). Derived expectation first: bare CONTINUE must be EXACTLY equivalent to `CONTINUE AFTER 0 SECONDS`, which by GR1 means (a) no suspension, (b) no exception -- 0 is not less than zero, so EC-CONTINUE-LESS-THAN-ZERO cannot be set even under CHECKING ON -- and (c) execution continues with the next executable statement. The failure shape to look for is a bare CONTINUE that behaves OBSERVABLY differently from the AFTER-0 spelling under some ambient state. READ: ControlFlowBinder.BindContinue (ControlFlowBinder.cs:57-62) -- `if (cont.arithmeticExpression() is not { } secs) return new BoundNop();` -- and StatementEmitter.Visit(BoundNop) (StatementEmitter.cs:147) returns false emitting nothing, so control simply falls to the next emitted statement. COMPARED the two spellings for OBSERVABLE difference rather than assuming: the AFTER-0 leg emits `CobolTiming.ContinueAfter((double)(0L), true)` (checked-in generated output, tests/conformance/2023/continue_after.g.cs), and ContinueAfter with 0.0 takes neither the `seconds < 0.0` arm nor the `secs == 0` sleep -- it returns having touched nothing. Under `>>TURN ... CHECKING ON WITH LOCATION` the AFTER form additionally wraps itself in `ExceptionState.EnterStatement("CONTINUE", loc, ...)` / `ExitStatement` (exception_statement_ambient.g.cs:151-156), but that pair is SAVE-and-RESTORE (ExceptionState.cs:79-88) and nothing raises inside it, so LastStatement/LastLocation are identical afterwards to what a bare CONTINUE leaves -- FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATEMENT and FUNCTION EXCEPTION-LOCATION cannot tell the spellings apart. It is not: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolLexer.g4 line 436 defines a dedicated token 'COMMIT : 'COMMIT' ;', and genericClause (CobolExpressions.g4) is 'IDENTIFIER (IDENTIFIER | literal)*' over the IDENTIFIER TOKEN -- not over cobolWord, which is the rule that lists COMMIT as a context-sensitive user word (CobolWords.g4). So in 'ioControlParagraph : I_O_CONTROL DOT (ioControlClause DOT?)*', genericClause consumes only 'APPLY' (no APPLY token exists, so it lexes as IDENTIFIER), the COMMIT token matches no alternative of ioControlClause, the loop exits and COMMIT is left unmatched -> a syntax error. 12.4.6.3.2's format is 'APPLY COMMIT ON [ [ file-name-1 ] [ identifier-1 ] ]...', so the clause is LOUDLY REJECTED, not silently swallowed. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: no program this compiler accepts can be subject to an active APPLY COMMIT clause, so GR7's guard 'the file is not subject to an active APPLY COMMIT clause' is VACUOUSLY SATISFIED and the unconditional releases are correct for everything that compiles. DeleteShared performs ReleaseAllExcept and ReleaseSingle without consulting LocksEffective, unlike its own siblings RewriteShared ('if (phrase == FileRecordLock.WithLock && LocksEffective(meta, st, name))') and WriteShared. It is benign TODAY only because LocksEffective's first line is 'if (meta.LockMode == FileLockMode.None) return false;' so a SHARING-only connector can hold no lock to release -- an accident of another method's guard, not a check on this one. subject: DISPLAY statement
notes: UNDER-REJECTION: legal-looking source the standard FORBIDS is accepted and compiled. Rule: 'Identifier-1 shall not reference a data item of class message-tag, object, or pointer.' (cite.py --check 14.9.11.3 OK, rule 1.) READ BindDisplay in full: for each operand child it does exactly one screen -- ExpressionBinder.ScreenIndexNameOperand for a bare INDEX-NAME (13.18.38.3 r7, kb/Work R16, landed) -- and NO class screen. Grepped src/Cobol.Net.Compiler for any class-based exclusion on a DISPLAY operand: the only pointer/object screens in the tree are ConditionBinder's 8.8.4.2.3 SR5 object-relation check, StatementValidation.ContainsNonOrderableLeaf (strongly-typed group ordering), ReferenceResolver.RefModExclusion (8.4.3.3.3 SR1) and DataBinder.Linkage's BY VALUE formal-class check -- none of them on this path. WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS to a forbidden operand: FieldOperand binds a BoundFieldOperand, and at emit OperandText.FieldAsString falls through every arm of its final 'p.Item.Pic switch' (Alphanumeric / NumericEdited / National / Boolean / Numeric / float are enumerated; PicCategory.Pointer, PicCategory.ProgramPointer and PicCategory.ObjectReference are not) to the default arm '_ => $"{PlaceRenderer.Read(p)}.ToString()"'. So 'DISPLAY WS-PTR' over '01 WS-PTR USAGE POINTER.' compiles clean and prints ManagedPointer.ToString() -- a value with no COBOL meaning -- and 'DISPLAY WS-OBJ' over an OBJECT REFERENCE item prints the CLR object's ToString(). Both classes are fully modelled here (PicInfo.cs:296/302, carriers 'ManagedPointer' and the object-reference type; DataBinder.Ptr.cs / DataBinder.Oo.cs), so this is reachable from ordinary source, not theoretical. THE THIRD CLASS IS VACUOUS AND SHOULD NOT BE COUNTED AS PASSING: class message-tag has no Usage member at all (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:60-68 states the MCS facility is unmodelled and deliberately gets no dead enum member), so no message-tag operand can be constructed -- the rule's third arm is satisfied by absence, not by a check. FIX SHAPE (structural, per one_rule_one_place): the exclusion is a CLASS-set screen and IntrinsicArgumentRules.ClassOf already computes CobolClass for any BoundOperand including Pointer / Object; the screen belongs beside ScreenIndexNameOperand as a reusable operand-class gate, because the identical 'shall not be of class X' shape recurs across statement operand slots -- sweep for the siblings rather than adding one inline test in BindDisplay. WOULD CLOSE: that screen plus negative fixtures conformance:negative/display-pointer-operand and conformance:negative/display-object-operand. || UPHELD, and WIDENED. I read OperandText.cs end to end and confirmed the fall-through: FieldAsString's terminal switch enumerates { IsUnsignedWideBinary }, { Numeric, IsFloat: false }, { Numeric } (float), and { Alphanumeric or NumericEdited or National or Boolean }, then '_ => $"{PlaceRenderer.Read(p)}.ToString()"'. I also confirmed the PicCategory enum's tail is ObjectReference, Pointer, ProgramPointer (PicInfo.cs:36-47) -- three categories with no matching arm, so all three take the default. WIDENING, with citations I ran myself: 'class pointer' in this standard spans THREE categories, not one -- 8.4.3.11.4 GR1 'Data-address-identifier creates a unique data item of class pointer and category data-pointer', 8.4.3.12.4 GR1 '... of class pointer and category function-pointer' (--check OK), 8.4.3.13.4 GR1 '... of class pointer and category program-pointer' (--check OK), and 8.8.4.2.3 item 11 speaks of 'two operands of class pointer where each operand is of the same category'. So the missing screen must exclude data-pointer, function-pointer AND program-pointer, plus class object -- a four-category set, not the two shapes the note names; a fix that special-cases USAGE POINTER and OBJECT REFERENCE would leave USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER (a modelled category here, PicCategory.ProgramPointer, live since P10 Step 7) still printing a CLR ToString(). That is exactly the feedback_model_the_rule_shape_not_one_case failure the fix must avoid, and it reinforces the adjudicator's CLASS-SET fix shape over an inline per-usage test. Verdict DIVERGES stands.

notes: DERIVED FIRST: leg (a) is chunking - repeat the transfer leftmost-first until the item is exhausted - when the sending size exceeds the device's single-transfer size; leg (b) is left-alignment when the device is the wider of the two. READ: AcceptDisplayEmitter.EmitDisplay is one `sink.Write(image)` / `sink.WriteLine(image)` with no length test, no loop, no wrap and no padding, over a `System.Console` / `System.Console.Error` byte stream. LEG (b) HOLDS trivially: the stream write deposits the characters left-to-right starting at the current position and adds nothing, which is 'the transferred data is stored aligned to the left in the receiving device'. LEG (a) IS UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: there is no device transfer size for the sending item to exceed. THAT VACUITY IS THE UNVERIFIED HALF - it is sound only if GR2's determination genuinely is 'unbounded', and that determination is nowhere written down (see GR-14.9.11.4-2: Annex A.1 item 58 has no docs/CONFORMANCE.md row). ProgramTable.RunMain additionally sets that stream's encoding to BOM-less UTF-8 so the 8.1.2 repertoire survives the device boundary. TEST: conformance-test:DisplayUponTests.Upon_OutputDevices_And_Default_GoToStdout is spec-derived (its [Fact] comment cites '14.9.11.4 GR8 default') and runs through CobolNet.CompileAndRun - the greenfield, not the legacy oracle - asserting that `DISPLAY 'A-DEFAULT'` with no UPON lands on stdout alongside the explicit SYSOUT and CONSOLE displays, in order. subject: DISPLAY statement
notes: CONFORMS BY VACUITY, and the vacuity is a documented determination rather than an accident. READ EmitDisplay: the only two devices this compiler can emit to are System.Console and System.Console.Error -- the 14.9.11.4 GR8 standard display device and the SYSERR routing established by AcceptDisplayBinder.DisplayOutputDevices / BindDisplayUpon and written up in docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.1 item 59. Both are line-structured streams on which vertical positioning IS applicable (WriteLine performs it), so GR11's antecedent -- 'vertical positioning is not applicable on the device' -- is FALSE for every device the implementation offers, and there is no positioning to ignore. The claim is recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md A.3 row 24 ('DISPLAY positioning ignored when N/A | 14.9.11 | Claimed | Console device; positioning is a no-op where inapplicable'), which matches spec A.3 item 24 -- 'If positioning is not applicable on the hardware device, the operating system will ignore the positioning specified or implied by the DISPLAY statement' (cite.py --check A.3 OK). NO TEST-REF, deliberately: the antecedent is unpopulatable by declaration, so no spec-derived test can exist for this row; it is CONFORMS-but-untestable, not CONFORMS-but-untested. What would change the verdict is the arrival of a device (a printer / reel mnemonic) for which vertical positioning is inapplicable -- at that point GR11 needs real code and this row must be re-adjudicated. || UPHELD with my own reads. I re-located A.3 item 24 in the spec independently (specs/ISO_COBOL.md, Annex A.3 'Processor-dependent language element list' begins at the section-a-3 anchor; item 24 is the DISPLAY positioning row, text verbatim as quoted) and confirmed it is the A.3 counterpart of GR11 rather than of GR9. I re-derived the device closure from the code rather than from the doc: AcceptDisplayBinder.BindDisplayUpon admits ONLY names in DisplayOutputDevices and errors COBOLNET0817 otherwise, and EmitDisplay's sink expression is a two-valued ternary over System.Console / System.Console.Error -- there is no third sink expression anywhere in the emitter, so no unread arm can reach a non-line-structured device. This is the one row where a CONFORMS legitimately costs nothing further, because the antecedent is closed by the implementation's own device set, and the note already names the single event that would reopen it. NOTE the vacuity is contingent, not permanent: it is voided the moment DisplayOutputDevices grows a name, so the eventual Format-2 / printer work must re-adjudicate this row rather than inherit the Claimed.

notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.12.4 "When native arithmetic is in effect, the quotient is the result of dividing the dividend by the divisor"` -> OK, GR 1). DERIVED FIRST: the quotient is dividend/divisor, and under a standard mode it is the value of the arithmetic expression (dividend / divisor) evaluated per 8.8.1.5. READ: ArithmeticEmitter.EmitDivide forms every quotient as `num.Combine(q, "/", divisorX, RcvFor(r, ise), outermost: true)`; NumericRenderer.CombineCore's first arm is `if (StandardDecimal || ...) return op switch { ... "/" => CobolDec.Div(DecOperand(a), DecOperand(b), IntermediateMode) ... }` — the SDIDI (decimal128) expression evaluation 8.8.1.5 defines, with the receiver's ROUNDED applied only at the final transfer in StoreArith; the native arm falls to CombineNative, which divides at the receiver's own scale + ROUNDED mode (8.8.1.3 leaves the native intermediate implementor-defined, so this is latitude, not divergence). NATIVE HALF verified by RoundedDifferentialTests.DivideGivingRounded_ModeIs (`DIVIDE 10 INTO 25 GIVING R ROUNDED MODE IS NEAREST-EVEN` asserted = 002, i.e. 25/10 = 2.5 -> 2, a hand-derived spec value, not a legacy diff) and by OnSizeErrorDifferentialTests.DivideByZero_FiresOnSizeError_ReceiverUnchanged (14.7.5 case 2). STANDARD-DECIMAL HALF verified by the enabled golden tests/conformance/2023/pb84_standard_decimal_intermediate_consumers with its .out. UNVERIFIED HALF — the rule's third named mode: 'When standard-decimal arithmetic, OR STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic is in effect'. DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY outright with COBOLNET0806 ('an obsolete feature (ISO 8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported'), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md row 2 records it 'Not claimed'. That clause of GR1 therefore cannot be exercised at all — one half of a two-half rule, so PARTIAL per the batch bar rather than CONFORMS. TO CLOSE: implement a binary128 intermediate (or an owner decision recording the non-support against D13), plus a golden dividing under each of the three modes. || UPHELD (independent evidence): I read NumericRenderer.cs:349-389 (CombineCore) and :438-465 (Divide) end to end. The SDIDI arm is entered on `StandardDecimal || ((a.Dec || b.Dec) && !a.Real && !b.Real && !_rcv.Real)` and returns `CobolDec.Div(DecOperand(a), DecOperand(b), IntermediateMode)` with scale 0/Dec:true — it does NOT consult `_outermost` or `_rcv.Rounding`, so the receiver's ROUNDED really is deferred to the StoreArith transfer (14.7.7 rule 3 NOTE 1: 'The ROUNDED phrase applies only to this transfer of data' — `cite.py --check 14.7.7` OK). The native arm's `Divide` with `_outermost` true computes at `ds = _rcv.Scale`, `mode = _rcv.Rounding` in one step. RoundedDifferentialTests.DivideGivingRounded_ModeIs is `AssertOutput(..., "002")` — a hand-derived value, NOT `AssertSameAsLegacy` (the same file's BareRounded_DivideGiving_MatchesLegacy is the legacy form and is correctly NOT cited) — so ground rule 3 is satisfied. The STANDARD-BINARY half is genuinely unreachable: no code path constructs ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary past BindDeclarations, and `NumericRenderer.StandardDecimal` names only StandardDecimal/Standard. PARTIAL stands.

subject: DIVIDE statement
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.12.4 "The dividend is identifier-2 or literal-2. The divisor is identifier-1 or literal-1"` -> OK, GR 2). DERIVED FIRST: in EVERY format the dividend is the id-2/lit-2 slot and the divisor the id-1/lit-1 slot — which means INTO's first operand is the DIVISOR and BY's first operand is the DIVIDEND, the one role-mapping a compiler can silently invert. READ: BindDivide binds `var a = host.Expr.BindExpr(aCtx)` with the comment 'INTO: the divisor; BY: the dividend', then INTO-with-GIVING returns `BoundDivideGiving(dividendX, a, ...)` where dividendX = BindExpr(into.divideIntoOperand()) and BY-with-GIVING returns `BoundDivideGiving(a, divisorX, ...)` where divisorX = BindExpr(byPhrase.divideOperand()); the record is `BoundDivideGiving(BoundExpr Dividend, BoundExpr Divisor, ...)`, so both map correctly. The REMAINDER branch repeats the same mapping through its two conditional expressions (`dividend = intoPhrase ? BindExpr(i.divideIntoOperand()) : a` / `divisor = intoPhrase is not null ? a : BindExpr(b.divideOperand())`) — checked arm by arm, both arms correct. Format 1 (no GIVING) makes each identifier-2 both dividend and receiver: EmitDivide is called with dividend null and reads `num.FieldNum(r.Place)` per receiver — the identifier-2-as-dividend reading. GR2b (item identification, content of the resulting item) — every identifier operand binds to a BoundNumRef Place and renders through PlaceRenderer, so subscripts/ref-mods are evaluated where the operand is read; with more than one receiver both operands are materialized into locals by ArithmeticEmitter.Snapshot before any store (14.7.7 GR4 + NOTE 3). GR2c (literal value) — a literal operand binds through ExpressionBinder.NumLiteral to BoundNumLiteral, and the literal-after-INTO case (`DIVIDE 3 INTO 10 GIVING Q`) reaches it through BindOperandExprCore's LiteralContext arm. TEST: the enabled golden tests/conformance/2023/pb45_function_in_sending_operands.cob writes BOTH `DIVIDE FUNCTION SQRT(W-Z) INTO W-Q GIVING W-R` and `DIVIDE W-Q BY FUNCTION SQRT(W-Z) GIVING W-R` with the hand-derived comment '9 / 2 = 4 (truncated)' and a .out — the same numeric answer from the two opposite operand orders is exactly the discriminating test for this role mapping. RoundedDifferentialTests.DivideGivingRounded_ModeIs adds `DIVIDE 10 INTO 25 GIVING R` = 25/10, pinning that the INTO operand is the divisor. || UPHELD (independent evidence, with the test claim re-measured): I re-derived GR2 from specs/ISO_COBOL.md:23659-23665 and then read ArithmeticBinder.cs:94-139 arm by arm without looking at the adjudicator's mapping first — Format 1 (:127-129) BoundDivideInto(a=divisor, intoRecv), Format 2 (:122-125) Dividend=BindExpr(divideIntoOperand), Divisor=a, Format 3 (:131-136) Dividend=a, Divisor=BindExpr(byPhrase.divideOperand()), Format 4 (:108/111) dividend=BindExpr(i.divideIntoOperand()), divisor=a, Format 5 (:109/112) dividend=a, divisor=BindExpr(b.divideOperand()). All five correct against the figures at :23527-23630. The pb45 evidence is genuinely DISCRIMINATING and I verified the operands from the source (W-Z=4 so SQRT=2, W-Q=9) and the .out (DIV-INTO=0004, DIV-BY=0004): an inverted INTO mapping would print 0000 (2/9 truncated). subject: DIVIDE statement
notes: Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.12.4 "the remainder is the result of multiplying the subsidiary quotient and the divisor and subtracting the product from the dividend"` -> OK, GR 7). DERIVED FIRST: remainder = dividend - (subsidiary-quotient * divisor), with dividend/divisor as defined in GR2 and the subsidiary quotient as defined in GR6c. READ: EmitDivideRemainder builds `var product = new NumX($"({qt} * {divisor.Expr})", qs + divisor.Scale)` — qt is the GR6c subsidiary quotient at the quotient receiver's scale, and the NumX scale qs + divisor.Scale is the exact scale of the product so the subtraction aligns radix points without loss — then `NumX remainder = num.Combine(dividend, "-", product, rcv)`. That is GR7's expression literally, over the SAME snapshotted dividend/divisor GR2 defines (both materialized by Snapshot(num.FixedLane(...)) before the quotient store, so a quotient receiver aliasing a sender cannot poison it). notes: kb/Work/PB406.md — ⚠ THE STANDARD'S OWN CROSS-REFERENCE IS DEFECTIVE and the verdict is given on the only coherent reading. GR3 sends a CALLED-program EXIT PROGRAM to '14.9.18, GOBACK statement, General rules 3 and 4' - but §14.9.18.4 GR3 is the NOT-under-control case ('operates as if executing a STOP statement') and GR4 is the within-a-METHOD case. Taken literally a called-program EXIT PROGRAM would stop the run unit, contradicting both §14.9.14.1 ('marks the logical end of a called program') and GR2's own condition split. The rules that actually match the stated condition are §14.9.18.4 GR1 (the RAISING phrase raises the condition in the ACTIVATOR) and GR2 (terminate, return to the calling statement, deliver the header RETURNING value, and run the implicit CANCEL if the program is INITIAL). VERIFIED FAITHFUL against the canonical PDF page 655 (printed 625) - the transcription is not the source of the error; the standard prints 'General rules 3 and 4'. All three legs of the intended reading measured GREEN on the pinned compiler: (1) RAISING propagation - conformance-test ExitProgramRaising_InCalledProgram_Propagates (CAUGHT: EC-USER-EXIT / AFTER-CALL); (2) header RETURNING - PROBE out-b2/probe/gr3-returning/p.cob, a called program with PROCEDURE DIVISION RETURNING LK-R ending in EXIT PROGRAM, expected R=0042/END, observed R=0042/END; (3) the INITIAL implicit CANCEL - PROBE out-b2/probe/gr3-initial-cancel/p.cob calls an IS INITIAL subprogram twice, each activation returning via EXIT PROGRAM, expected N=1/N=1/END, observed N=1/N=1/END. GOBACK GR1a (a non-COBOL activator) is implementor-defined and out of scope. || REFUTED: DIVERGES — REFUTED by probe + positive control. I accept the adjudicator's premise that §14.9.14.4 GR3's printed cross-reference ('14.9.18, GOBACK statement, General rules 3 and 4') is defective -- I re-read §14.9.18.4 in the transcription and GR3 is the not-under-control/STOP case and GR4 the within-a-METHOD case, neither of which can apply, so the incorporated rules are GOBACK GR1 and GR2. But that reading IMPORTS GOBACK GR1b, whose gate is explicit and singular (cite.py --check 14.9.18.4 OK, 1) b)): 'an exception condition is raised in the activating runtime element IF CHECKING FOR THAT EXCEPTION CONDITION IS ENABLED IN THE ACTIVATING RUNTIME ELEMENT'. The compiler gates on the WRONG element. CallEmitter.cs#EmitRaisingStage keys on r.Enabled, which is the TURN state baked in at bind time in the RAISING (called) program -- its own comment says 'The TURN decision was baked in at bind time' -- and when that is off and the name is nonfatal it stages NOTHING (`if (!r.Enabled) { if (!r.Fatal) { emit a comment; return; } }`). The activator's enabling state, the only one GR1b names, is never consulted at the staging end. Result: a legal program whose activator has checking enabled and a matching USE declarative silently never runs its handler. The adjudicator verified three legs (RAISING propagation, header RETURNING, INITIAL implicit CANCEL) and all three do hold, but each was probed with checking ON in BOTH elements, which is exactly the configuration that hides this gate; the axis the subject holds fixed was never flipped. NOTE THE INTERPRETIVE ALTERNATIVE, recorded so a fix-time reader can re-adjudicate rather than inherit me: one could argue from §14.6.13.1.1 ('During the execution of any statement, if checking for an exception condition is not enabled, the exception condition will not be raised') that the sub's own state suppresses the raise. I reject it because GR1b is the SPECIFIC rule for this statement, it localises the raise to the activator, and it names the activator's state as the sole test; under the compiler's reading GR1b's qualifying clause would have nothing left to do. Even if that alternative were adopted, this row could not stand at CONFORMS: the enabling-locus edge was simply never measured, which is PARTIAL by the standing cost rule.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/CallEmitter.cs#EmitExitProgram; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/CallEmitter.cs#EmitRaisingStage; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/DispatchEmitter.cs

notes: kb/Work/PB413.md — BindGoTo resolves procedure-name-1 through the procedure table and emits BoundGoTo(range.Start); a SECTION procedure-name transfers to that section's FIRST paragraph and execution then falls into the section's following paragraphs (probe p10: GO TO S-TWO prints S-TWO-FIRST then S-TWO-SECOND). A qualified procedure-name resolves to the named section's copy (probe p17: GO TO DUP-P IN S-TWO reaches S-TWO's DUP-P, not S-ONE's). The optional word TO is genuinely optional -- 'GO PARA-A.' transfers (probe p2), matching the PDF p660 general format where only GO is underlined. At 85 an ALTER-target paragraph's GO TO binds to BoundGoToAlterable whose INITIAL value is the WRITTEN target, so the unaltered transfer is still GR1's; ALTER and the target-less form are both gated off at 2002+ (COBOLNET0810/0811). CONFORMS-but-untested: the only GO TO tests on disk are legacy-oracle differentials (AlterSwitchesDifferentialTests, SectionDifferentialTests, ControlFlowDifferentialTests), which by schema cannot close a row. GR1 is unconditional: 'When a GO TO statement represented by format 1 is executed, control is transferred to procedure-name-1.' Inside ANY inline (Format-2) PERFORM the transfer DOES NOT HAPPEN: the target procedure is never entered, and control instead resumes at the statement FOLLOWING END-PERFORM. A legal COBOL program silently executes the wrong statements. The adjudicator's three probes (p2 no-TO, p10 SECTION target, p17 qualified name) all placed the GO TO at paragraph top level, which is the one context where it works -- the whole class of GO TOs written inside an inline PERFORM body was never measured, and that is the classic COBOL escape idiom. MECHANISM (read, then confirmed by probe): StatementEmitter.cs:111 emits a format-1 GO TO as `__pc = <target>; break;` -- the `break` is meant to leave the dispatcher `switch (__pc)` so the outer while re-dispatches at the new pc. But C# `break` binds to the NEAREST enclosing breakable construct, and ControlFlowEmitter.EmitPerformLoop (lines 249-282) emits every inline PERFORM as a REAL C# loop: `for` for TIMES (:260), `do{}while` for UNTIL TEST AFTER (:263), `while` for UNTIL (:267), nested `while`s for VARYING (EmitVarying), `while(true)` for UNTIL EXIT (:275), and `do{}while(false)` for the bare inline PERFORM (:278). Inside any of those the `break` exits the PERFORM LOOP, not the dispatcher; __pc is assigned and then overwritten by the ordinary fall-through increment when the case ends. The transfer is silently discarded. The proof that this is a known-shape omission and not a design choice is three lines away: EXIT PERFORM is emitted as `goto __pexit<pid>` against a real label (EmitPerform :244/:246) precisely because `break` cannot cross the loop -- GO TO was left on `break`. This is the two-arm-dispatch shape: the F3 (Format-3) arm emits imperative-statement-1 INLINE with no enclosing loop (EmitExceptionPerform), so a GO TO out of imp-1 transfers CORRECTLY (my probe g7) -- one arm right, the other wrong, and only the right one was ever probed. BLAST RADIUS MEASURED, not assumed: EVALUATE (g10) and SEARCH ... WHEN (g11) both transfer correctly, so the defect is confined to -- and universal within -- the inline PERFORM body, at EVERY control shape and at --std 2023 and --std 85 alike. GR-14.9.17.4-2's value-driven transfer inherits the identical bug: ControlFlowEmitter.EmitGoToDepending (:47) ends with the same bare `break`, so an in-range GO TO ... DEPENDING inside an inline PERFORM is lost the same way -- that row is already PARTIAL so it does not move the burn-down, but the fix is one fix. PREMISE VALIDATED before calling it a defect: nothing in the standard licenses this as undefined. 14.9.28.4 GR2 makes only OVERLAPPING PERFORMs undefined (a second PERFORM passing through the first's exit) -- my probes contain ONE PERFORM and a GO TO, so GR2 does not reach them. 14.9.28.4 GR4 puts the inline PERFORM's statements squarely inside the statement stream, GR7 and NOTE 2 to GR6 expressly contemplate a GO TO in that flow, and 14.9.17.1's NOTE about an unsatisfied perform exit is informative and speaks to the out-of-line return mechanism, not to whether the transfer occurs. The transfer is required. CORRECTED VERDICT: DIVERGES, not PARTIAL -- the edge is not unverified, it is verified BROKEN, and it produces a wrong answer on legal source with no diagnostic. A separate under-rejection found while probing this row and belonging to §8.4.2.2.1, NOT to this rule (record it there, do not re-file it here): an unqualified reference to a paragraph-name duplicated across two OTHER sections requires qualification per 8.4.2.2.1 rule 1/rule 6, but ProcedureTableBuilder.ResolveProcedure falls through to `_paraIndex` (the global FIRST-DEFINED paragraph) with no ambiguity check, so it compiles clean and picks one silently (probe g3).  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/ControlFlowBinder.cs#BindGoTo; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetAlterBinder.cs#AlterGoTo; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/ProcedureTableBuilder.cs#ResolveProcedure

notes: kb/Work/PB414.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.19.4 "If condition-1 is true and NEXT SENTENCE is specified in the THEN phrase, the ELSE phrase, if specified, is ignored and control is transferred to an implicit CONTINUE statement immediately preceding the next separator period"` -> OK, General rules 4) (FORMAT 2). MECHANISM (read): the binder emits BoundNextSentence; StatementEmitter.Visit(BoundNextSentence) renders `goto {SentenceEndLabel};`, and DispatchEmitter.EmitParagraphBody plants `__sent{pc}_{k}: ;` at each inter-sentence boundary of any paragraph that contains a NEXT SENTENCE anywhere -- that C# label IS the implicit CONTINUE the rule names, and a label is zero-duration, consistent with the 14.9.9.4 GR2 treatment of implicit CONTINUEs. In the LAST sentence SentenceEndLabel is null and the emitter falls through to `__pc = CurrentPc + 1`, the paragraph fall-through. Container discovery is drift-proof rather than hand-maintained: ContainsNextSentence recurses over the generated StatementChildren() enumeration, and a missed container would emit a goto with no label -- a loud backend compile failure, never a silent misjump. MEASURED on the four shapes where 'the next separator period' could plausibly be got wrong, each chosen because a naive lowering gives different output: (1) plain -- true, NEXT SENTENCE in THEN, ELSE present: the ELSE is ignored, the rest of the sentence after END-IF is skipped, the following sentence runs (p6-next-sentence-then -> 'NEXT-SENTENCE-BODY' only). (2) inside an INLINE PERFORM in the same sentence: control must leave the LOOP as well, because the next period is after END-PERFORM -- prints 'ITER-1' then 'AFTER-SENTENCE', no second iteration (b1-nextsent-in-inline-perform). (3) inside an EVALUATE WHEN arm in the same sentence (b2-nextsent-in-evaluate -> 'AFTER-SENTENCE' only). (4) nested two IFs deep, both tails skipped (u5-nextsent-nested). Paragraph/section boundaries: last sentence of a paragraph falls through to the next paragraph (p14-next-sentence-last -> 'NEXT-PARA-RAN'); last sentence of a SECTION falls into the next section (b3-nextsent-last-of-section -> 'S2-RAN'); inside an out-of-line PERFORMed paragraph the PERFORM still returns (b4-nextsent-in-performed-para -> 'SUB-SENTENCE-2' then 'BACK-IN-MAIN'). EDITIONS: legal at all four; 4.2.12 requires an implementation to SUPPORT archaic elements and to IDENTIFY them, and COBOLNET0903 fires as a warning at 2023 only -- measured across --std 85/2002/2014/2023 (probe ed). ONE DEFECT, NOT IN THE BEHAVIOUR BUT IN THE CITATION: every site in the tree that describes this mechanism cites GR6, and GR4 -- the THEN-phrase arm actually being implemented -- is cited NOWHERE. Ten sites, all GR6; see finding IF-F3. TEST-REF EMPTY: the only NEXT-SENTENCE test in the Cobol.Net tree is RedefinesSubscriptedViewDifferentialTests.NextSentence_SkipsTrailOfOwnSentence, which does exercise this rule but asserts against a legacy-baked DifferentialGolden, so it is a regression net and cannot close the row. || REFUTED: DIVERGES — REFUTED, with a measured WRONG ANSWER on strictly-conforming Format-2 source. GR4 (cite.py --check 14.9.19.4 "If condition-1 is true and NEXT SENTENCE is specified in the THEN phrase" -> OK, General rules 4)) requires that control be transferred to an implicit CONTINUE statement IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE NEXT SEPARATOR PERIOD -- so every statement remaining in the current sentence after the IF is skipped. When the NEXT SENTENCE is lexically inside an INLINE PERFORM and the sentence is the LAST sentence of its paragraph, this compiler instead resumes at the statement following END-PERFORM, in the SAME sentence. notes: kb/Work/PB426.md — Sub-rule (b) CONFORMS and was measured: "If the sending operand is a figurative constant, the number of digits is the same as the number of digits in the receiving operand ... If the receiving item is not an integer, the number of digits includes both those to the right and the left of the decimal point" - MOVE ALL "7" TO PIC 9(3)V9(2) stores 77777, spanning the fraction positions (probe mvl23/l23_figurative_digits). Sub-rules (a) and (c) DIVERGE, and the divergence is a silent wrong answer on ordinary source at every edition. (a) requires "the number of digits is the number of character positions in the sending data item unless the number of character positions is greater than 31, in which case THE RIGHTMOST 31 CHARACTER POSITIONS ARE USED"; (c) says the same for a literal. FromAlphanumeric applies no cap, so a sending operand of 39 or more digit characters overflows the Int128 accumulator and wraps to a negative value, whose magnitude is then stored. Measured, identically at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023: `01 A40 PIC X(40) VALUE "1234567890123456789012345678901234567890". 01 R9 PIC 9(9). MOVE A40 TO R9.` stores 838277934 where the rule gives 234567890 (rightmost 31 characters -> the unsigned integer 123456789012345678901234567890, then 14.6.8 decimal-point alignment into 9 digit positions) - probe mvl23/l23_realistic. The same 40-character value written as a LITERAL gives the same wrong answer, which is sub-rule (c) (probe mvl23/l23_literal31), and into PIC 9(31) it gives 7560297064841152750825838277934 against the rule's 0123456789012345678901234567890 (probe mvl23/l23_unsigned_int). The observed digits are exactly the low-order digits of the SIGNED Int128 wrap of the full 40-digit parse, which identifies the mechanism precisely. A 35-character sender is correct (789012345), confirming the threshold is the carrier, not the receiver. THE 31-POSITION CAP IS THE ROOT CAUSE, NOT AN INCIDENTAL MISS: the standard caps the sending size at 31 digits precisely so no implementation carrier can be exceeded, and below the wrap the cap is invisible because both readings truncate high-order to the receiver's digit count - which is why no test caught it. Such a move COMPILES CLEAN and then aborts at run time with CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: "MOVE to group 'GR' with a dynamic-length / dynamic-capacity member (a variable-length group has no fixed record window) - the Tier-C byte island". Measured on FOUR distinct legal, COMPATIBLE-group shapes, identically at --std 2014 and 2023: (1) equal length, differing fixed leaves - X(5)+dyn -> X(2)+X(3)+dyn (probe mvgr9/gr9_equal_diffshape); (2) a FIXED group into a variable-length one, which 8.5.1.12.1 expressly permits ("either both operands may be variable-length groups or only one of the operands may be") - probe mvgr9/gr9_fixed_to_varlen; (3) unequal lengths, the GR9b case - probe mvgr9/gr9_varlen_short; (4) a dynamic-CAPACITY table member - probe mvgr9/gr9_dyntable2. The report-file predicate is available at bind time — FileModel.ReportNames is populated from the FD's REPORT(S) clause (DataBinder.cs:1001) and SequentialIoEmitter.EmitFileRegistration already branches on `file.ReportNames.Count > 0` — but SequentialIoBinder.BindOpen never consults it, and no consumer of BoundOpenMode anywhere in src/Cobol.Net.* screens the mode against the file kind (searched: every `BoundOpenMode.` site, every `ReportNames` site, StatementValidation, VersionConformancePass, FlagConformancePass). This is my own search, not the dossier's silence. MEASURED (probe/open-p1): rpt1.cob (`OPEN INPUT RPTF` on an FD carrying `REPORT IS RP1`) and rpt2.cob (`OPEN I-O RPTF`) both compile clean at --std 2023 and at --std 85; rpt3.cob (`OPEN OUTPUT RPTF`) is the legal control and also compiles. Expected: a compile-time rejection of INPUT and of I-O. §13.18.46's own general rule states the stronger sibling restriction — a REPORT-clause file may be referenced in the procedure division only by USE, the WHEN phrase of PERFORM, CLOSE, or “the OPEN statement with the OUTPUT or EXTEND phrase” — so the same one screen discharges both.
