subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB330. “An OPEN statement that specifies file-name-1 more than once shall not be specified in imperative-statement-1 of an exception-checking PERFORM statement” (cite.py --check 14.9.27.3 … OK, rule 3). Implemented and correct, including the half a naive implementation misses. CheckCrossStatementBans walks region A (imperative-statement-1 only, matching the rule's scope) and FLATTENS the whole statement — `op.openClause().SelectMany(oc => oc.openFileSpec())` — before grouping, so a duplicate is caught whether it repeats inside ONE mode group or ACROSS two, which is what “specifies file-name-1 more than once” means over a format whose file list is a repeated group. Case-folded with ToUpperInvariant, so the COBOL word's case-insensitivity is honoured. MEASURED (probe/open-p1): xsopen.cob, whose imperative-statement-1 is `OPEN OUTPUT F1 INPUT F1` (the CROSS-group form, which the existing test does not exercise), is rejected COBOLNET1616 at --std 2023. The existing test covers the same-group form (`OPEN INPUT F1 F1`). Editions: 2023 only — Annex E item 19 introduces the facility (“Inline exception processing. The PERFORM statement is enhanced to allow checking for exception conditions inline”), Annex E being the 2014→2023 change list, and the compiler agrees (--std 2014 adds COBOLNET0900 “the Format-3 (exception-checking) PERFORM requires COBOL-2023”), so below 2023 there is no construct for the rule to govern. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED ON THE RULE'S READING, WHICH THE ADJUDICATION NEVER WEIGHED. The mechanism it located is real and I could not break it: EcBinder.ExceptionPerform.cs#CheckCrossStatementBans walks region A = p.statementBlock() (the grammar puts the WHEN/OTHER/COMMON/FINALLY bodies in their own contexts, so region A really is imperative-statement-1), flattens openClause()->openFileSpec() so a repeat is caught across mode groups as well as inside one, and case-folds. 13 probes confirm it: rejected COBOLNET1616 for the cross-group form, a case-different spelling (f1/F1), the OPEN nested in IF/END-IF and in EVALUATE, one instance carrying WITH NO REWIND, three occurrences over three groups, the [WITH] LOCATION head form, and a nested F3 PERFORM's own imp-1; correctly SILENT for two different files, a dup in a WHEN body, in WHEN OTHER, in FINALLY, and in a Format-2 inline PERFORM (not an exception-checking PERFORM). BUT THE ROW IMPLEMENTS ONLY ONE OF TWO READINGS OF 'specifies file-name-1 more than once', and the evidence runs against the one chosen. (a) FAMILY: every sibling imp-1 ban forbids the MULTI-OPERAND form - CLOSE 'specifies more than one file-name' (14.9.6.3 r3), DELETE FILE 'more than one file-name' (14.9.10.3 r4), VALIDATE 'more than one identifier' (14.9.50.3 r6), INITIALIZE 'Identifier-1 shall be specified only once' (14.9.20.3 r2), MERGE/SORT banned outright. On the duplicate reading OPEN is the sole outlier: it would ban a thing that is already erroneous everywhere while permitting exactly the multi-operand form its four siblings forbid. (b) PHRASING: when this standard means 'no duplicates' it says so - 'The same category shall not be repeated' (14.9.20.3 r6, the same clause as r2), 'A given class name', 'A particular user-defined word', 'Any particular screen-attribute'; 8 of the 9 unambiguous duplicate rules carry such an anchor and 14.9.27.3 r3 carries none. (c) PURPOSE: 14.9.27.4 GR25c - an unsuccessful OPEN in imp-1 transfers control to the WHEN phrase, so the file-names after the failing one never open; GR20 defines resumption for that partial execution ONLY on the declarative path ('processing resumes at the next implicit OPEN statement'), and RESUME NEXT STATEMENT is equally legal in a WHEN phrase (14.9.33.3 r1). Banning the multi-file OPEN in imp-1 is what closes that hole; banning a duplicate does not touch it. MEASURED, and this is the whole finding: OPEN OUTPUT F1 F2 F3 inside imperative-statement-1 of a Format-3 PERFORM COMPILES CLEAN and runs at --std 2023, while the same shape written as CLOSE F1 F2 is rejected COBOLNET1612 and VALIDATE N M is rejected COBOLNET1607. The compiler switched readings exactly where the rule text switched from 'more than one X' to the operand tag - and it did so TWICE: INITIALIZE N M in imp-1 also compiles clean (COBOLNET1614 is a duplicate check, 14.9.20.3 r2 is not), the sibling this defect predicts. The honest counter-evidence: 14.9.28.3 r14 does use a bare operand tag for a duplicate rule ('If file-name-1 or file-name-2 is specified in a WHEN phrase, IT shall not be specified more than once...') - but it anchors with 'it' after naming a specific instance, and its 'unless all such instances' tail makes the duplicate sense explicit. 14.9.27.3 r3 has neither. PARTIAL, not DIVERGES: the implemented ban is a strict SUBSET of the wider reading (a duplicate is also two operands), so nothing legal is rejected and the narrow branch is genuinely implemented and pinned by a spec-derived test. What CONFORMS cannot survive is that the row's whole claim rests on a reading the adjudicator did not derive, that the rule's own family, phrasing convention and stated purpose all contradict, and whose wider branch has ZERO enforcement. Settle the reading first; if the wider reading holds, the row is closer to NOT-IMPLEMENTED than to CONFORMS. Editions 2023 upheld (E.2 item 19 checked). One incidental: the cited test's own file carries a broken sibling - PerformFormat3Tests.BareAndFilePairedSameName_Rejected1600 has the body of MultiFileDeleteInImp1_Rejected1613 and asserts COBOLNET1613, so the 14.9.28.3 r15 branch it names is untested.

notes: kb/Work PB319 LANDED, after kb/Work PB316 (landed). ONE SITE, FULL ANTECEDENT. The rule (cite.py --check 14.9.27.3, both its leading conjunct and its two disjuncts: OK, rule 8) is a syntax rule of the OPEN STATEMENT about file-name-1, which 14.9.27.2's general format defines as that statement's operand; 12.4.5.15.3 has exactly ONE general rule and NO syntax rules, so SR8 is the standard's only source of a LOCK MODE requirement anywhere. The second copy, in DataBinder.BindFileControl, fired off the SELECT clause alone and had to DROP the antecedent, because a file control entry sees no OPEN statement and the I-O-CONTROL paragraph is not bound until after it. notes:
kb/Work PB325 (landed). RULE (--check 14.9.27.4 "'X' at an intersection indicates that the specified statement, used in the access mode given for that row, may be used with the open mode given at the top of the column"): Table 20 licenses each (statement, access mode, open mode) triple; every BLANK cell is an unsuccessful execution whose status 9.1.13.7 names -- item 7 '47' for READ/START not open input or I-O, item 8 '48' for WRITE (a: access sequential and not open extend/output; b: access random or dynamic and not open I-O/output), item 9 '49' for REWRITE/DELETE RECORD not open I-O. Table 20 was read from the PDF (page 709) as well as the transcription, because the load-bearing signal here is a BLANK CELL and the OCR of a blank is not self-evident: Random x WRITE and Dynamic x WRITE carry X under Output and I-O only, and the Extend column of both rows is empty.
IMPLEMENTATION. The ACCESS MODE is the sole branch discriminator and lives in ONE place, KeyedConnector.Access (the abstract base RelativeConnector and IndexedConnector now share); the open mode is only ever the screen that follows. Each connector's Write opens with 'bool sequentialRelease = Access == KeyedAccess.Sequential', takes item 8 a)'s arm when true and item 8 b)'s when false; SequentialConnector.Write carries item 8 a) directly (12.4.5.5.2 SR2 admits only ACCESS SEQUENTIAL for a sequential file); READ/START answer item 7 and REWRITE/DELETE item 9 in both keyed connectors and in SequentialConnector; the blank Random x START row is enforced one level up, at bind, by KeyedIoBinder.BindStart's 14.9.41.3 SR1 screen (COBOLNET0862).
EVIDENCE. conformance:2023/l1_table20_seq_relative and conformance:2023/l1_table20_indexed walk EVERY cell of Table 20 that conforming source can reach -- 4 open modes x {READ, WRITE, REWRITE, START, DELETE RECORD} over sequential, relative and indexed organizations at all three access modes, 139 observations, each expected value derived from Table 20 plus 9.1.13.7 items 7/8/9 and every one observed. conformance:negative/pb325-start-random-access pins the blank Random x START row on BOTH keyed organizations at all four editions. The Random/Dynamic x WRITE x Extend cell is UNREACHABLE from conforming source -- 14.9.27.3 SR2 confines the EXTEND phrase to sequential access -- so it is pinned at the runtime by unit:Table20WriteOpenModeTests, whose four defect facts go RED if the open mode is put back into the branch predicate (measured) while its eight control facts stay green.
WHAT WAS FIXED. RelativeConnector.Write and IndexedConnector.Write selected the branch with '_access == KeyedAccess.Sequential || Mode == FileOpenMode.Extend'; the disjunct routed a random- or dynamic-access connector opened EXTEND into the sequential-release branch, whose own screen accepts extend, so the WRITE appended a record and reported '00' where item 8 b) requires '48'. That made a run-time answer depend on a bind-time syntax rule (SR2) that is enforced nowhere -- kb/Work PB318 -- so the runtime is now correct independently of it.
EDITIONS: Table 20 is version-invariant; the DELETE RECORD row for a sequentially-accessed relative/indexed file and the dynamic access mode ride the relative/indexed I-O modules present at every edition adjudicated here, and the negative fixture was observed rejecting at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023.

notes: NOT-IMPLEMENTED -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB193; PB329 Part 1). Before: FileStatus.cs had no '39' constant and no connector read a persisted physical-attribute catalog, so the validated set was empty BY OMISSION and a program that opened a file under a contradicting FD read silently wrong data. WHAT LANDED: FixedFileAttributes is the persisted catalog - a sidecar beside the data file (<file>.cbattr) holding the 9.1.6 attributes COBOL.NET records - written at the two moments 14.9.27.4 makes the OPEN statement CREATE the file (GR18's OUTPUT; GR17's absent OPTIONAL I-O/EXTEND), which is where 9.1.6 fixes them, and removed with the file by DELETE FILE across the whole success family. FileConnector.Open performs GR10's comparison BEFORE OpenCore (an unsuccessful OPEN leaves the file unaffected, GR25) and returns FileStatusCode.FixedAttributeConflict '39' (9.1.13.6 item 7) on a mismatch; both OPEN dispatch arms reach it (the plain registry Open and the sharing-active SharedOpenAttempt). THE VALIDATED SET VARIES BY ORGANIZATION, which GR10 says in so many words that it may: 'The implementor defines which of the fixed-file attributes are validated during the execution of the OPEN statement. The validation of fixed-file attributes may vary depending on the organization or storage medium of the file.' COBOL.NET validates exactly what the file's own storage FIXES - for EVERY organization the ORGANIZATION itself (9.1.6's primary attribute, of which 9.1.6 names exactly three: sequential, relative and indexed); for RELATIVE and INDEXED additionally the record type, the minimum and maximum logical record size and (indexed) the key count and each key's window, DUPLICATES, SUPPRESS WHEN value and collating sequence, because those stores' structure IS those attributes; for SEQUENTIAL nothing further, because 9.1.7.2 puts a sequential file's record lengths in the data and in the reading program ('In record sequential files the length of each record is determined by any information the implementor may add to the record on the physical storage medium (such as record length headers)' - COBOL.NET adds none to a fixed-length one) and 9.1.13.2 items 3, 5 and 7 answer the resulting disagreement with the SUCCESSFUL '04', '06' and '09' rather than a refused OPEN. A UNIFORM set was implemented first and MEASURED WRONG: it rejected legal source on this repository's own corpus - 2002/io_status_04, 2002/rw_suppress, 2002/rw_suppress_bare, 2002/rw_present_when, 2002/oo_object_report and 2023/declined_rw_present_varying_control all went red, every one the write-a-file-then-read-it-back idiom, and rw_suppress degraded into an infinite READ loop - and it was a second mechanism for the job RecordLayoutNotice already does. A file whose attributes are NOT recorded supplies nothing to compare and opens normally. Probe before: OPEN INPUT of a RELATIVE 10-byte file through a LINE SEQUENTIAL 40-byte FD gave '00' and an empty record; after: '39'.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB328, LANDED. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.27.4 'If the I-O phrase is specified, the file shall support the input and output statements that are permitted for the organization of that file when opened in the I-O mode': OK, 16)): 'If the I-O phrase is specified, the file shall support the input and output statements that are permitted for the organization of that file when opened in the I-O mode. If the file does not support those statements, the I-O status value for file-name-1 is set to '37' and the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful. The successful execution of an OPEN statement with the I-O phrase sets the open mode of the file connector referenced by file-name-1 to open in the I-O mode.' TWO halves. HALF 2 (the open mode is set) was already conforming: FileConnector.Open assigns Mode and sets _openMode from the success family. HALF 1 (the '37') was the defect. WAS: the only producer of '37' for a write-incapable file was the shared catch (UnauthorizedAccessException) around OpenCore, which fired for SEQUENTIAL only because that organization's I-O and EXTEND arms open write-capable streams; the relative and indexed I-O arms merely Attach() (a READ of the store), so writability was never probed. Probed on a worktree build at 17c11fd4 with three files created by the compiler and then made read-only (a real host attribute, not a simulation): OPEN I-O answered SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00' on the SAME condition; the keyed successes were then believed downstream (READ '00', REWRITE '00') and the loss surfaced only as a '30' at CLOSE on a file whose MD5 was unchanged. The identical omission made OPEN EXTEND answer SEQ '37', REL '00', IDX '00' where 9.1.13.6 6) a) 1. requires '37' (cite.py --check 9.1.13.6 'the EXTEND or OUTPUT phrase is specified but the file will not support write operations': OK, 6) a) 1.); OPEN OUTPUT was already '37' on all three because its keyed arm eagerly calls RecordFraming.WriteStore. NOW: the write-capability question is an OPEN-CONTRACT question, asked ONCE above the organizations. HostFile.PermitsWrite (IO/FileSupport.cs) asks the host for a writable handle (FileMode.Open + FileAccess.Write + FileShare.ReadWrite, nothing written) and answers false only on UnauthorizedAccessException; every other IOException propagates so 9.1.13.6 1)'s '30' stays mapped in the one place. FileConnector.Open calls it for I-O, EXTEND and OUTPUT on a Present file, after GR10's '39' and before OpenCore, so every organization -- including one added later -- inherits the answer instead of re-earning it. GR16 names no organization and Table 20 is why it cannot: REWRITE sits under the I-O column for sequential, random AND dynamic access, so 'supports the statements permitted in the I-O mode' entails write capability whatever the organization. RE-PROBED after the fix on the same three read-only files: OPEN I-O 37/37/37, OPEN EXTEND 37/37/37, OPEN OUTPUT 37/37/37 -- nine cells. OVER-FIRE MEASURED, not assumed: the same read-only files still OPEN INPUT '00' and READ their record on all three organizations (a read-only file supports everything Table 20 permits in the input mode), and a WRITABLE file still opens I-O '00' and rewrites on all three. GR25 ('If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, the file is not affected', cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK, 25)) holds through the probe: content MD5 and last-write time are identical after the refused open. INPUT IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE PROBE and the exclusion is required, not an optimization -- probing write for INPUT would refuse an OPEN the operating environment carries out perfectly, and 9.1.13.6 6) a) 3.'s read-capability question is answered by the organization's own eager read (measured on all three: see GR-9.1.13.6-6). BOTH HALVES OF GR16 ARE COVERED, not just the one that was defective: the rule says the file must support the input AND output statements the I-O mode permits, and Table 20 lists READ under the I-O column beside REWRITE, so a file this process may WRITE but not READ is equally '37'. Measured with icacls /deny :(RD) -- read DATA only, so a raw write open still succeeds and HostFile.PermitsWrite accepts the file -- OPEN I-O answered '37' on sequential, relative and indexed, produced by the organization's own eager read rather than by the write probe; unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests.OpenIo_PresentAndWritableButNotReadable_Is37 asserts the write-probe premise first so the two halves cannot be confused. COVERING TESTS: unit:FileAuthorityPresenceTests establishes the precondition for real (a read-only attribute on Windows, mode 0400 on Unix) and verifies it with a RAW write open rather than with the subject under test; its nine GR16 cells were shown to FAIL (7 of them -- the four keyed I-O/EXTEND cells, the two keyed OPTIONAL cells and the GR25 inertness assertion) with the check disabled, and the three sequential cells and three OUTPUT cells stayed green, which is exactly the two-arm fingerprint the defect had. unit:HostFileProbeDriftTests keeps the question singular: PermitsWrite is banned outside FileConnector and its call count in the OPEN contract is pinned at one. No conformance golden can reach this arm -- the corpus runner compiles a .cob and compares its output, with nowhere to express 'and first make this file read-only'. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 -- GR16 is version-invariant and docs/CONFORMANCE.md determines the '37' family is emitted at every edition, ungated.

notes: RULE: 'Upon successful execution of the OPEN statement, the current volume pointer is set: a) To point to the first or only reel/unit in the physical file if INPUT or I-O is specified. b) To point to the reel/unit containing the last record in the physical file if EXTEND is specified. c) To point to the newly created reel/unit in the physical file for an unavailable file if EXTEND, I-O, or OUTPUT is specified.' cite.py --check 14.9.27.4: OK (§14.9.27.4 19)). DERIVATION: §9.1.10 (Current volume pointer) states 'The current volume pointer is a CONCEPTUAL ENTITY used in this document to facilitate exact specification of the current physical volume of a sequential file. The status of the current volume pointer is affected by the CLOSE, OPEN, READ, and WRITE statements.' (cite.py --check 9.1.10: OK) — it is not a programmer-visible register and has no COBOL surface. Its only observable consequences are reel/unit swaps (§14.9.30.4 GR23 READ, §14.9.51.4 GR24 WRITE) and CLOSE unit processing (§14.9.6.4 Table 14). COBOL.NET's storage medium is single-unit mass storage, asserted in code at FileRegistry.CloseReelUnit ('CLOSE … REEL/UNIT on a disk medium: a no-op … the file is on a non-reel/unit medium') and CloseNoRewind, so every physical file has exactly ONE reel/unit and arms a), b) and c) all designate that same and only unit whichever mode is specified. There is nothing the rule can require that a single-unit medium does not already satisfy, and no state a program can observe that would disagree. TEST: unit:FileStatusDisciplineTests.CloseReelUnit_AbsentOptional_NoUnitProcessing is the spec-derived test that pins the single-unit medium model (§14.9.6.4 GR6 / §9.1.13.2 6)) this verdict rests on. ⚠ THE PREMISE IS APPLIED INCONSISTENTLY ELSEWHERE: the same non-reel/unit medium that makes GR19 vacuous is what makes GR11's '07' MANDATORY, and that arm is missing (see GR-14.9.27.4-11 and finding open-no-rewind-07-arm-missing). subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB370. The emitted sequence is exactly the rule's order. EmitOpen emits the registry call, then EmitStoreFileStatus (a — the value is placed in the I-O status), then EmitUseHook. Inside the generated __IoCheckEc the body runs: `ExceptionState.SetIo(__ec!, IsFatalIoStatus(__st), ...)` when the name's checking bit is on (b — the level-3 EC-I-O condition associated with the status value, mapped by ExceptionCatalog.IoEcOfStatus per §9.1.13.1), then `__EcPerform(__ec!, __f)` consults the installed Format-3 PerformFrame FIRST (c), and only if that returns NoMatch do the F1 file-name / open-mode USE tiers and the outward GLOBAL walk run (d). §14.9.28.4 GR17's 'Any USE declarative that would normally match the exception condition is ignored' is what makes c) exclude d), and the emitter's own comment states it. PROBE (out-b1/probe/open-gr25): OPEN INPUT of an absent non-optional file with a `USE AFTER STANDARD EXCEPTION PROCEDURE ON FN` declarative → the declarative runs and reports status 35, and the file is NOT created (a + d, and 'the file is not affected'); the same OPEN inside `PERFORM ... WHEN EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR ... END-PERFORM` → the WHEN body runs and the declarative does NOT (c), after which the run unit terminates abnormally naming EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR — which is §14.9.28.4 GR20's own tail ('If the exception condition was fatal, execution continues as specified in 14.6.13.1.3'), not a defect. CONFORMS-but-untested: no existing spec-derived test pins the OPEN-specific a-b-c-d ordering (conformance:2023/f3_perform_handler_turn_off_all covers the Format-3 machinery but not through an I-O statement). || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED, downward to PARTIAL. The rule has a leading requirement and then four ordered actions: 'If the execution of the OPEN statement is unsuccessful, THE FILE IS NOT AFFECTED and the following actions take place in the following order: a) ... b) ... c) ... d)'. VERIFIED HALF -- the a-b-c-d machinery is right and I could not break it. EmitOpen emits the registry call, then EmitStoreFileStatus (a), then EmitUseHook; inside __IoCheckEc the order is SetIo (b), then the F3 PerformFrame via RunTopFrame (c), then, only when no WHEN matched, the F1 file-name and open-mode USE tiers, the F3 __EcDispatch tier and the outward GLOBAL walk (d) -- which is what 14.9.49.4 GR6 requires. I also closed the leg the adjudicator left unexercised: its probe ran a FORMAT 1 USE only, but GR25 d) names 'USE FOR EXCEPTION or USE AFTER EXCEPTION', so I probed a FORMAT 3 declarative (USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR under >>TURN ... CHECKING ON) on an unsuccessful OPEN INPUT: it runs, with FS=35, EXCEPTION-STATUS=EC-I-O-PERMANENT-ERROR and EXCEPTION-FILE=35FN. The 9.1.13.1 status->EC map in ExceptionCatalog.IoEcOfStatus matches the standard's list digit for digit. UNVERIFIED-AND-VIOLATED HALF -- 'the file is not affected'. The adjudication tested this in the only direction that cannot lose data (an absent file is not CREATED by a failing OPEN INPUT). I tested the destructive direction and it fails. Connector FA holds po.dat open INPUT under SHARING WITH NO OTHER; connector FB, a plain SELECT on the same physical file, executes OPEN OUTPUT. 9.1.13.9 1) a) and Table 19 (whose 'sharing with no other' existing column is 'Unsuccessful open' in EVERY request row) make that OPEN unsuccessful with status 61, so GR25's own consequent applies and the file shall not be affected. The compiler reports 00 and TRUNCATES po.dat to zero bytes -- the record 'KEEPTHIS01' is gone. That is wrong-answer-with-data-loss on legal source, and it is GR25's own text that is violated, not merely the detection rule's. I checked the counter-hypothesis before charging it: every unsuccessful OPEN the implementation DOES recognise leaves the file intact -- 61 on a sharing-active incoming connector returns before c.Open(mode) is ever called, 41 returns at the top of FileConnector.Open, and 35/37/30 all return before or from the failing stream construction (I confirmed 61 and 41 by probe with the content re-read intact, and the OS-level conflict variant gives 30 with the file intact). So the failure is confined to spec-unsuccessful opens the implementation misclassifies as successful, whose ROOT cause (FileRegistry.Open consults the physical-file table only when the INCOMING connector is sharing-active) is already booked DIVERGES under GR-14.9.27.4-22/-23 -- I am not re-booking that defect, I am recording that GR25's leading clause is therefore unsatisfied and was never measured. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL by the rubric; not DIVERGES, because the four ordered actions that are the substance of the rule are correct and probed. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 for sub-rules a) and d); sub-rules b) and c) ride the exception-condition facility and the Format-3 exception-checking PERFORM, 2002 introductions, so they are adjudicated at 2002 / 2014 / 2023.

subject: OPEN statement
notes: kb/Work PB324 (landed). This rule is a pointer -- 'Additional rules affecting the execution of the OPEN statement are given in 12.4.5, File control entry, General rules 3 and 4' (cite.py --check 14.9.27.4 OK, 26) -- and both referred rules now hold. GR3 b) (cite.py --check 12.4.5.3 OK, 3) b)): 'When the USING phrase of the ASSIGN clause is specified, the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is associated with a physical file identified by the content of the data item referenced by data-name-1 in the runtime element that executes the OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement.' GR3's lead sentence fixes the timing (cite.py --check 12.4.5.3 OK, 3): 'The association occurs at the time of execution of an OPEN, SORT, or MERGE statement that referenced file-name-1.' (ISO 14.6.13.1.3 #5/#7)'). subject: PERFORM statement
notes: Two mechanisms realize it. (a) Every frame VISITED during a resolution is marked Handling for the whole walk and skipped by any nested resolution, so an exception raised inside imp-2/3/4 cannot re-enter this PERFORM's WHEN arms nor a suspended inner frame's - the covering test raises inside the handler and shows it falling through to the fatal default instead of being re-caught. (b) The frame is popped in the `finally` BEFORE the FINALLY block is entered, so imp-5 executes with no frame installed - literally 'as if these statements were specified in a format 2 PERFORM statement'. In practice most conditions cannot even arise inside imp-2..5 because GR14's implicit TURN OFF ALL is in force there (EmitRunF3 / the FINALLY PushAllCheckingOff), and §14.6.13.1.1 raises nothing whose checking is disabled; the Handling flag is what covers the residue (a fatal raise, or a handler-local >>TURN that re-enables a name).  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Exceptions/ExceptionState.cs#RunTopFrame (:815-833); src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Exceptions/PerformFrame.cs#Handling; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/ControlFlowEmitter.cs#EmitExceptionPerform (frame pop before FINALLY, :108)

notes:
kb/Work PB331 LANDED. RULE: 'The LOCK phrase shall not be specified in the same READ statement as the IGNORING LOCK phrase.' (cite.py --check 14.9.30.3 OK.) 'The LOCK phrase' means WITH LOCK and NOT WITH NO LOCK: the standard names them apart in this very statement - GR11 b) 'except when the NO LOCK phrase is specified' and GR11 d) 'the record lock ... is set only if the LOCK phrase is specified on the READ statement' (both cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 OK).
THE RULE NOW HAS A CHECK, AND IT IS THE RULE'S OWN SHAPE. `FileLockBinder.CheckIgnoringLock` raises COBOLNET1818 when the IGNORING LOCK alternative of 14.9.30.2's contention bracket is written together with WITH LOCK from the retention bracket, and NOT when it is written with WITH NO LOCK. Both READ arms reach it: SequentialIoBinder.BindRead and KeyedIoBinder.BindRead each bind the retention bracket first and pass it in, so the two-arm shape cannot be half-fixed. MEASURED at --std 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023: `READ SQF NEXT RECORD IGNORING LOCK WITH LOCK ...` -> `error COBOLNET1818: READ on file 'SQF': the LOCK phrase shall not be specified in the same READ statement as the IGNORING LOCK phrase (ISO 14.9.30.3 SR3)`, exit 70, at every edition.

The forbidden pair WAS rejected before, but by the grammar's collapse of the two printed brackets into one slot rather than by SR3 - and that collapse also rejected the LEGAL pair IGNORING LOCK WITH NO LOCK. `FileLockBinder.CheckRecordLockPhrase`'s doc comment claimed to enforce 'IGNORING LOCK and WITH LOCK are mutually exclusive' while its body tested only `file.LockMode is { Kind: LockKind.Automatic }`, which is SR4; that false traceability claim is gone from the source. subject: READ statement
notes: RULE: 'The open mode ... shall be input or I-O. If it is any other value, the execution of the READ statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status value for file-name-1 is set to 47.' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'the I-O status value for file-name-1 is set to 47' -> OK 14.9.30.4 2). All five READ entries open with the SAME two-part guard: `if (!IsOpen ...) return 47` and `if (Mode is Output or Extend) return 47`, so all four not-input/not-I-O states are covered -- never opened, closed, open OUTPUT, open EXTEND. notes: kb/Work PB338. RULE items a-e. cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'The file position indicator is unchanged.' -> OK 14.9.30.4 10) a). KEYED ARM DIVERGES on (a) and (d): ReadLockGovern is called AFTER the physical read (its own summary admits the shape), so by the time the 51 is stamped RelativeConnector/IndexedConnector have already set _fpi/_fpiKey/_fpiArrival, _inclusive=false, _positioner='R' and _lastSlot/_lastReadPrime -- (a) violated -- and IndexedConnector.ReadRandom assigns `_refKey = keyIndex` on its THIRD line, before any lookup, so a Format-2 conflicted read also changes the key of reference -- (d) violated. EXPECTED FROM SPEC: with the FPI unchanged by the conflict, B's next sequential READ selects the same record -> B2=00 AAAAA RK=0001. RRN 1 is silently skipped and never made available to B. NO EXISTING TEST COVERS THE DIVERGENT ARM: unit:CobolFileLockTests.ReadShared_SequentialOrdinals_Conflict51_AndAdvancingOnLockSkips and conformance:2002/file_sharing_seq exercise ONLY the sequential organization (whose pre-read check is correct), which is why this has stood green -- test-ref left empty deliberately.

subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB338. RULE items a-d. cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'any prior record lock associated with that file connector is released by the execution of the READ statement' -> OK 14.9.30.4 11) a). ITEMS b, c, d CONFORM. ApplyReadLockDiscipline: b -- `else if (meta.Multiple && phrase == WithNoLock) ReleaseSingle(...)`, reached because wantLock is false for WithNoLock, and only at completion of a successful read; c -- the `_ => meta.LockMode == FileLockMode.Automatic` arm auto-locks; d -- `WithLock => true` is the only manual-mode acquisition. LocksEffective correctly suppresses ACQUISITION (never the conflict CHECK) per 12.4.5.9.4 GR1a/b1 and GR3. ITEM a DIVERGES. GR11a ties the release to 'the execution of the READ statement', and 12.4.5.9.4 GR6 is explicit -- 'Execution of any I-O statement except START releases any previously locked record in that file for that file connector' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 <that text> -> OK 12.4.5.9.4 6)). The standard distinguishes deliberately: 11b says 'at the completion of the SUCCESSFUL execution', 11c/d say 'successfully accessed record', 11a says neither. The code gates 11a on success at BOTH call sites: ReadLockGovern early-returns on `statusJustRead[0] != '0'`, and ReadShared calls ApplyReadLockDiscipline only inside `if (ok && ...)`. So an at-end, 46, 47 or 51 READ leaves the prior lock standing. This is a TWO-ARM defect: the governed MUTATING verbs in the same file release unconditionally before the operation (WriteShared and RewriteShared and DeleteShared each call ReleaseAllForConnector / ReleaseAllExcept outside any success test) -- only READ gates it. OBSERVED (probe/gr11a/GR11A.cob, two SHARING ALL OTHER + LOCK MODE MANUAL sequential connectors, single record locking): A1..A3 = 00 with WITH LOCK (A ends holding ordinal 3); A4-ATEND=10; then C walks the file: C1=00, C2=00, C3=51 BBBBB. EXPECTED FROM SPEC: A's at-end READ is an executed I-O statement, so it released A's lock on ordinal 3 -> C3=00 CCCCC. conformance:2002/file_sharing_seq exercises 11a only across SUCCESSFUL reads (its READA3 line), so the divergent path is uncovered -- test-ref left empty.

subject: READ statement
notes: RULE: 'If the IGNORING LOCK phrase is specified on the READ statement, the requested record is made available, even if it is locked.' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'the requested record is made available, even if it is locked' -> OK 14.9.30.4 12). BOTH ARMS VERIFIED. Sequential: ReadShared guards the whole conflict block with `if (phrase != FileRecordLock.Ignoring && f.ReadEligible)`, so an IGNORING LOCK read falls straight through to f.Read and the locked record is delivered. Keyed: ReadLockGovern wraps only the conflict block in `if (phrase != FileRecordLock.Ignoring)`, and the physical read has already happened, so the record is likewise made available. ApplyReadLockDiscipline maps Ignoring to wantLock=false, so an IGNORING LOCK read neither acquires nor (under multiple locking) releases -- consistent with 14.9.30.3 SR3/SR4, which bar combining IGNORING LOCK with LOCK and bar it entirely under automatic locking. Grammar carries it (recordLockPhrase: IGNORING LOCK | WITH? NO LOCK | WITH? LOCK, ordered so WITH NO LOCK is not shadowed) and the 2002 introduction gate fires on the bound phrase (VersionConformancePass.GateStatement -> Constructs.RecordLockPhrase2002). COVERING TEST: conformance:2002/file_sharing_seq line 'READ F-B IGNORING LOCK' -> golden 'IGNB=00 AAAAA' while A holds ordinal 1's lock -- the record IS made available, exactly the rule. Spec-derived (its header derives every line from 9.1.16 / 14.9.30 GR7-GR12).

subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB338. RULE items a-c. cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'any implicit move resulting from the presence of an INTO phrase is executed' -> OK 14.9.30.4 13) (the transcription runs item c flush-left at spec line 26243, so the checker attributes the sentence to 13) b); the sentence is verbatim under GR13). ITEM a: both emitters call EmitStoreFileStatus on every path and the connectors set the FPI inside the success path only. ITEM b: EmitUseHook emits __IoCheck / __IoCheckEc after the status store, consuming the declarative's RESUME action; the AT END imperative is guarded by `if (FileStatus(name)[0] == '1')` so a 3x/4x/5x exception cannot take it. VERIFIED BY PROBE (probe/gr13b/GR13B.cob -- a USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR PROCEDURE ON F plus a READ on a closed connector): output 'DECLARATIVE FS=47' then 'AFTER-READ FS=47' -- the declarative ran, AT END did not, and control returned to the end of the READ so the following statement executed, which is GR13b's non-fatal tail exactly. ITEM c: on success the emitters store the record image into the record area (EmitImageInto over FileModel.AreaRecord, the LARGEST record description per 13.4.2), then the INTO move, then NOT AT END / NOT INVALID KEY -- the order GR13c states. 'the AT END phrase or the INVALID KEY phrase is IGNORED': verified by CA15, where a SUCCESSFUL 06 read does not take AT END and delivers the record ('1:ABCDE FS=06'). The keyed emitter's INVALID KEY branch is `if (st[0]=='2')` and its NOT-branch `else if (st[0]=='0')`, so on success only the NOT-phrases run. conformance:2002/file_collating_seq exercises NOT AT END firing on successful keyed reads. || REFUTED: DIVERGES — The adjudicator read item (a) as only 'the connectors set the FPI inside the success path' and never tested its CONDITIONAL half. GR13a is not 'the FPI is set' -- it is 'the I-O status ... is updated AND, IF THE RECORD OPERATION CONFLICT CONDITION DID NOT OCCUR, the file position indicator is set', i.e. under a conflict the FPI must not move (the same requirement GR10a states affirmatively). On the KEYED arm FileRegistry.ReadLockGovern is called AFTER the physical read (its own doc-comment admits the shape: 'the keyed shape is post-read'), so RelativeConnector.ReadSequential / IndexedConnector.ReadSequential have already executed '_fpi = s; _fpiValid = true; _positioner = R' before the 51 is stamped at FileRegistry.cs:585 -- whose comment 'FPI kept (GR10a)' is exactly backwards for this arm, since 'kept' there means 'kept as the read left it', not 'unchanged'. The 53/54 lock-denial return from ApplyReadLockDiscipline is post-read on the same arm and breaks item (a) identically. Items (b) and (c) do hold, and item (a) holds on the sequential arm (ReadShared checks NextReadOrdinal before entering the connector), so this is the classic two-arm defect -- one arm fixed, the sibling never was -- and one arm conforming is not CONFORMS. Verdict DIVERGES rather than PARTIAL because a wrong answer is produced silently: the conflicted record is skipped and never delivered. Same root cause as the adjudicator's own GR10 DIVERGES row (it found the mechanism there and did not carry it back to GR13, which restates the same requirement); one fix -- moving keyed lock governance ahead of the physical read, or snapshotting/restoring the FPI on a conflict -- closes both rows. The cited test-refs do not save it: SequentialFileIoSpecTests.LineSequential_OverLengthRecord..., FileIoDifferentialTests.ReadNotOpen_Status47... and conformance:2002/file_collating_seq all exercise items (b)/(c) or the sequential organization only; none puts a record-operation conflict on a keyed connector, which is why this stood green.

SequentialConnector.Read carries two record-sequential legs, both setting shortLong -> FileStatusCode.RecordLengthShortLong and both returning through ReadSucceeded (so the read IS successful and the record IS delivered): the FIXED leg (`if (n < RecordWidth) shortLong = true`, n==0 being EOF) and the RECORD IS VARYING leg (`if (n < VaryMin || n > VaryMax) shortLong = true`). subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB327 (LANDED 2026-09-05). The rule has three parts and ALL THREE now conform. (1) A short record right-pads the record area with trailing spaces -- the else arm is 'LastReadLength = line.Length; image = Fit(line)'. (2) THE SPACE IS THE RECORD AREA'S OWN: 'If the record-area associated with file-name-1 is specified implicitly or explicitly as alphanumeric, a trailing space is defined to be the alphanumeric space character. If the record-area associated with file-name-1 is specified implicitly or explicitly as national, a trailing space is defined to be the national space character' (cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 OK). FileConnector.FitRecord is the ONE record-area fit and pads a national area with the national space's two bytes 00 20 on the area's own even boundary (13.18.60.4 GR8; D-N1), where it used to pad 20 20 -- which is not a space at all but U+2020. The emitter tells the connector which area it has (EmitNationalAreaRegistration -> CobolFile.RegisterNationalArea), reading the record's OPERAND category so an elementary national record and a GROUP-USAGE NATIONAL one (13.18.29.4 GR2b) answer alike; TrimRecordEnd is the write-side inverse and sheds national spaces in pairs. THE LEG WAS PREVIOUSLY UNREACHABLE: a national record area was refused at COBOLNET0899 before it could be read. (3) A long record truncates on the right, succeeds with '06', and the next READ serves the remainder. conformance:2002/pb327_national_line_sequential_fill observes part 2 by ORD over the record area's shared byte view: 001/033 pairs (the national space), never 033/033.

notes: kb/Work PB329 (LANDED 2026-09-05). RULE: 'If the execution of the READ statement is successful but the record area contains one or more characters not in the implementor-defined character set for a line sequential file, the I-O status in the read file connector is set to 09.' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'the record area contains one or more characters not in the implementor-defined character set for a line sequential file' -> OK 14.9.30.4 16); cite.py --check 9.1.13.2 'A READ statement for a line sequential file has successfully executed but the record contains one or more characters that are not in the implementor-defined character set for a line sequential file' -> OK 9.1.13.2 7). WHAT THE RULE DELEGATES TO IS NOW DETERMINED: Annex A.1 item 115 (Line sequential character set, required + documented) is answered at docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-115 -- every character at or above U+0020 is a member, the C0 controls below it (CR, LF and HT included) are not -- and LineSequentialCharacterSet is its one executable copy. SequentialConnector.Read's line-sequential arm tests the DELIVERED record area through the shared predicate and ReadSucceeded lands 09 ahead of 06/04, because GR16 is stated after GR15 and asks only that the read be successful. The test is CHARACTER-wise, not byte-wise: a national record area is read two bytes at a time as UTF-16BE (14.9.30.4 GR15's own alphanumeric/national split, D-N1), so N"CD"'s 00 43 00 44 bytes are two members and not two control characters. MEASURED on the built cobol.exe: before, a line sequential READ of a line holding 0x00 reported STATUS=00; after, 09, with the record still delivered (FUNCTION ORD of the byte = 1). Goldens walk 09 (READ), 71 (WRITE, 14.9.51.4 GR23), 71 (REWRITE, 14.9.35.4 GR17d), 9.1.13.10 item 1's unchanged medium, and the set boundary (0x7F and 0xFF are members) at all three editions the organization exists in.

subject: READ statement
notes: RULE: 'Regardless of the method used to overlap access time with processing time, the concept of the READ statement is unchanged; a record is available to the runtime element prior to the execution of imperative-statement-2 or imperative-statement-4, if specified, or prior to the execution of any statement following the READ statement...' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'a record is available to the runtime element prior to the execution of imperative-statement-2' -> OK 14.9.30.4 17). This implementation uses NO overlapped/asynchronous access method: every READ is a synchronous call on the connector, and both emitters place the record-area store FIRST inside the success block -- SequentialIoEmitter.EmitRead emits EmitImageInto(area, tmp) then EmitReadLengthStore then EmitStoreFileStatus then the INTO move then NotAtEnd; KeyedIoEmitter.EmitRead emits EmitImageInto then the RRN move-back inside `if (st[0]=='0')`, with the INTO move and NOT AT END / NOT INVALID KEY in the following guarded block. So imperative-statement-2 and imperative-statement-4 and every following statement observe the record already in the record area. Verified as OUTPUT by CA15, whose DISPLAY of REC immediately after each READ shows the record just read ('1:ABCDE', '2:FGH   '), and by every probe in this batch (probe/seqprev, probe/relprev, probe/gr14long) where the DISPLAY after the READ carries the delivered record. The rule imposes nothing further on a non-overlapped implementation.

subject: READ statement
notes: kb/Work PB338. RULE: 'Unless otherwise specified, at the completion of any unsuccessful execution of a READ statement, the content of the associated record area is undefined, the key of reference is undefined for indexed files, and the file position indicator is set to indicate that no valid record position has been established.' cite.py --check 14.9.30.4 'the file position indicator is set to indicate that no valid record position has been established' -> OK 14.9.30.4 18). RECORD-AREA LEG CONFORMS: both emitters store the image only inside the success branch, so the area is UNCHANGED -- a documented refinement of 'undefined', asserted by conformance-test:FileIoDifferentialTests.ReadNotOpen_Status47_AtEndNotTaken_RecordAreaUnchanged. KEY-OF-REFERENCE LEG CONFORMS vacuously (IndexedConnector._refKey simply survives, which 'undefined' permits). FPI LEG DIVERGES on the lock-denial path. The ordinary unsuccessful paths are right (at-end and '14' set LastReadUnsuccessful and clear _fpiValid; '51' is correctly exempted by GR10a's 'otherwise specified'), but a 53/54 record-lock-limit denial is NOT exempted by any rule and IS unsuccessful per 12.4.5.9.4 GR7 -- 'Any I-O statement that attempts to obtain a record lock that would exceed either limit is unsuccessful and receives an I-O status that indicates that condition' (cite.py --check 12.4.5.9.4 <that text> -> OK 12.4.5.9.4 7)). In FileRegistry.ReadShared the denial is discovered AFTER `f.Read(out image)` has already succeeded, which ran FileConnector.ReadSucceeded -- advancing the FPI, setting PrevOpWasSuccessfulRead and CLEARING LastReadUnsuccessful -- and the registry then only overwrites the status; ReadLockGovern's keyed twin is the same shape. OBSERVED (probe/lock54/LOCK54.cob -- one relative connector, ACCESS DYNAMIC, LOCK MODE MANUAL WITH LOCK ON MULTIPLE RECORDS, 20 records, sixteen READ NEXT ... Same source, same SD, opposite result. SECOND, INDEPENDENT LEG (edition): at --std 2023 the explicit MOVE is REMOVED and errors COBOLNET0902 (exit 70), while the RELEASE ... FROM QUOTE form compiles with NO diagnostic at all (exit 0) -- 'according to the rules specified for the MOVE statement' is not applied at any edition. A wrong result at run time is a GENERAL-rule failure. This is a PERMISSION, not an obligation: with more than one record description, whatever lies outside the current record's range is undefined, so any deterministic content conforms. CODE (read, not assumed): BindReturn:255-260 deliberately resolves the record area through file.AreaRecord - the LARGEST record's view (13.4.2) - rather than Records[0], so a multi-01 SD is not truncated; EmitReturn:167 calls SequentialIoEmitter.EmitImageInto(rt.RecordArea, tmp), which writes CobolString.Store(image, record.ImageWidth). (iii) A RETURN AFTER THE AT END CONDITION SETS EC-SORT-MERGE-RETURN - NOT IMPLEMENTED. notes: kb/Work PB348. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.34.4 'The implied MOVE statement does not occur if the execution of the RETURN statement was unsuccessful.' -> OK, 14.9.34.4 rule 5 b). GR5 decomposes into six obligations. VERIFIED CONFORMING: (a) the same RETURN without INTO runs first - EmitReturn emits the store before the move. (b-not-occur) the move sits INSIDE the success arm, so an unsuccessful RETURN skips it. (b-both) 'The record is available in both the record area and the data item referenced by identifier-1' - pinned by SortMergeDifferentialTests.Return_Into_MovesRecordToReceiver (AssertSpecPinned; AREA= and INTO= both print the returned record). (b-size / RECORD IS VARYING) 'The size of the current record is determined by rules specified for the RECORD clause ... the implied move is an alphanumeric group move' - 13.18.43 GR16a makes the sending operand the DEPENDING byte count. The emitter moves the WHOLE area, but EmitImageInto space-fills the area beyond the record (CobolString.Store pads with spaces), so the two are observationally identical; probe p11 (SD RECORD IS VARYING FROM 6 TO 12 DEPENDING ON WS-LEN, receiver PIC X(12) pre-filled with '*') prints LEN=12 INTO=[1AAAAAAAAAAA] and LEN=06 INTO=[2BB         ] - the 6-byte record left-justified and space-filled, exactly GR16a. notes: kb/Work/PB443.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.37.3 "Identifier-1 shall not be reference-modified"` -> OK, Syntax rules 1) (ALL FORMATS). NO CODE ANYWHERE IMPLEMENTS THIS RULE. I searched the whole pinned tree for a §14.9.37 citation (15 hits in src/, all in doc comments or GR-side code) and for any reference-modification screen on the SEARCH operand; there is none. The binder does not merely fail to screen -- it takes `.cobolWord()`, the BASE name only, and discards the whole `dataReferenceSuffix*` tail unread, so the reference modifier is thrown away rather than diagnosed. MEASURED (probe sr1refmod, all four editions): `SEARCH E(1:3) AT END ... WHEN K(IX) = 03 ...` over `05 E OCCURS 5 INDEXED BY IX` compiles with ZERO diagnostics and runs identically to the legal `SEARCH E` form -- both print HIT 03. Under §4.2.2 (`cite.py --check 4.2.2 "An implementation shall provide a warning mechanism that optionally may be invoked by the user at compile time to indicate violations of the general formats and the explicit syntax rules of standard COBOL"` -> OK) the implementation owes a compile-time indication of this violation and provides none at any strictness setting -- the only strictness axis the CLI exposes is `--permissive`, which moves the other way. SAME MECHANISM as SR2 sentence 2 and SR3 sentence 2, and as the WRONG-ANSWER qualification defect: see finding search-p1-F1.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SearchBinder.cs:24 `string tableName = drefs[0].cobolWord()?.GetText() ?? drefs[0].GetText();` and :83 the same expression over s.dataReference() for SEARCH ALL. Grammar: dataReference = `cobolWord dataReferenceSuffix*` where dataReferenceSuffix includes refModPart (src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:480-498).

notes: kb/Work/PB443.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.37.3 "The data description of identifier-1 shall contain an OCCURS clause with an INDEXED phrase and identifier-1 shall not be subscripted at the level for which the SEARCH is applicable"` -> OK, Syntax rules 2) (ALL FORMATS). BOTH sentences measured; NEITHER conforms, which is why this is DIVERGES rather than PARTIAL. SENTENCE 1 (OCCURS ... INDEXED required) IS DETECTED, at the WRONG STAGE and under the WRONG CITATION. The condition is tested (IndexNames.Count == 0) but the result is a BoundUnsupported, which the emitter renders as a run-time NotImplementedCobolFeatureException, not a diagnostic. MEASURED (probe sr2noindex): compiling a program whose SEARCH names an OCCURS table with no INDEXED phrase produces NO output and rc=0; running it prints 'BEFORE' and only then throws 'a COBOL feature that is not yet implemented was reached at run time: SEARCH table E without INDEXED BY'. Worse (probe sr2_dead): put the same SEARCH in a paragraph that is never performed and the program compiles clean AND runs to completion printing 'OK-NO-DIAGNOSTIC' -- a syntax-rule violation shipped with no indication at all. Two further problems in that one line: it MISCITES itself as `ISO §14.9.37 SR1` when the INDEXED requirement is SR2 (SR1 is the reference-modification prohibition) -- in BOTH copies, :29 and :88 -- and it labels a USER error as a COMPILER gap ('not yet implemented'), which mis-routes the reader. SENTENCE 2 (identifier-1 shall not be subscripted at the searched level) IS NOT IMPLEMENTED AT ALL. MEASURED (probes sr2subscr, sr2sub2, all four editions): `SEARCH E(IX)` and `SEARCH E(2)` both compile with zero diagnostics and run identically to the legal `SEARCH E` -- HIT 03 -- because :24 keeps only `.cobolWord()` and drops the subscriptPart. Note SR3 makes the subscripted spelling legal for the SUPERORDINATE levels, so a correct screen must count subscripts against the table's nesting depth rather than ban them outright. §4.2.2 owes a compile-time indication for both sentences. Mechanism shared with SR1/SR3 -- finding search-p1-F1 (the discarded operand suffix) and search-p1-F2 (no compile-stage syntax-rule checker).  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SearchBinder.cs:24-29 (BindSearch: base-name resolve, then `if (table.IndexNames.Count == 0) return new BoundUnsupported($"SEARCH table '{tableName}' without INDEXED BY (ISO §14.9.37 SR1)")`) and :83-88 (BindSearchAll, the identical pair). BoundUnsupported lowers to a RUN-TIME throw at src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/StatementEmitter.cs:211 `Visit(BoundUnsupported n) => _ctx.Writer.Line(LoudStmt(n.Feature))`.

THE PERMISSION HALF CONFORMS AND WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. A table nested inside another table is searchable and gives the right answer: probe sr3_nest_ox over `05 OUTER OCCURS 3 INDEXED BY OX / 10 INNER OCCURS 4 INDEXED BY IX`, with K(2,3) = 07, OX = 2 and `SEARCH INNER(OX) ... WHEN K(OX, IX) = 07` prints HIT 03 -- the inner index is the one varied, the outer subscript is supplied by the user in the WHEN phrase exactly as §14.9.37.4 GR1 requires (`cite.py --check 14.9.37.4 "The subscript that is used to determine the occurrence of each superordinate table to search is specified by the user in the WHEN phrases"` -> OK). The literal spelling `SEARCH INNER(2)` gives the same answer (probe sr3_nest_lit). THE REQUIREMENT HALF ('the subscripting is still required') IS NOT ENFORCED. Probe sr3_nest_bare: the bare `SEARCH INNER`, with the superordinate subscript omitted, compiles with zero diagnostics and prints HIT 03 at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023. It gives the same answer only because the operand's subscripts are discarded either way (SearchBinder.cs:24), which is precisely why the omission cannot be detected: there is nothing downstream that would ever notice. PARTIAL, and the unenforced half rides finding search-p1-F1/F2.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SearchBinder.cs:24-38 (the table is resolved by base name and the scan index/bound come from the table symbol, not from the operand's subscript list); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SearchBinder.cs:83-88 for SEARCH ALL.

notes: kb/Work/PB444.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.37.3 "If the END-SEARCH phrase is specified, the NEXT SENTENCE phrase shall not be specified"` -> OK, Syntax rules 4) (ALL FORMATS). NO CODE IMPLEMENTS THE RULE. A tree-wide grep for 'NEXT SENTENCE' in src/ returns only the archaic warning, the bound node, the emitters and doc comments -- nothing anywhere pairs a scope terminator with a NEXT SENTENCE phrase, for SEARCH or for any other statement carrying the same prohibition. MEASURED (probe sr4_endsearch_nextsent, all four editions): `SEARCH E AT END DISPLAY "NONE" WHEN K(IX) = 03 NEXT SENTENCE END-SEARCH DISPLAY "TAIL".` compiles and runs. At 2023 the only output is the unrelated COBOLNET0903 archaic warning about NEXT SENTENCE itself; at 85, 2002 and 2014 there is NO diagnostic at all. The program then prints 'NEXTSENT', i.e. the NEXT SENTENCE fired and jumped past the terminal period -- the compiler gave the illegal combination a meaning instead of rejecting it. §4.2.2 owes a compile-time indication. WHY THE RULE EXISTS AND WHY THE SILENCE IS HARMFUL: with END-SEARCH present the SEARCH no longer runs to the sentence's period, so 'the next separator period' that §14.9.37.4 GR1a names for NEXT SENTENCE is no longer the statement's own end; the standard forbids the pair rather than define which wins. Accepting it makes this compiler's answer a de-facto extension. Rides finding search-p1-F2.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SearchBinder.cs:21-75 / :81-117 -- neither binder inspects s.END_SEARCH() at all, and no site pairs it with a BoundNextSentence. The only NEXT SENTENCE handling in the tree is the archaic-feature warning at src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Validation/VersionConformancePass.cs:670-672 (COBOLNET0903) and the lowering at src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/StatementEmitter.cs:199 / DispatchEmitter.cs:297-330.

kb/Work/PB388.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Identifier-2 shall reference a data item of class index"` -> OK, Syntax rules 2) (FORMAT 1). Read with SR3 (`cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "If identifier-1 references a data item of class index, arithmetic-expression-1 shall not be specified"` -> OK), which is a sibling part's row: the two sending lanes are disjoint - a NUMERIC identifier sender is arithmetic-expression-1, a CLASS-INDEX identifier sender is identifier-2 - so SR2's operative content is that an identifier sender which is not a valid arithmetic operand shall be class index.

THE COMPLEMENT IS ENFORCED, AND I MEASURED IT ACROSS SIX SENDER CATEGORIES (all --std 2023; the alphanumeric and group legs also at --std 85, identical): alphanumeric `PIC X(4)` -> COBOLNET0844 (b1_alnum_send); alphabetic `PIC A(4)` -> 0844 (m6_alpha_send); group -> 0844 (b4_group_send); national -> 0844 (m1_natl_send); boolean `PIC 1(4) USAGE BIT` -> 0844 (m2_bool_send); numeric-edited `PIC ZZZ9` -> 0844 (m3_edited_send). The legal lanes both work: `SET IX TO WS-I` with WS-I USAGE INDEX (b2_index_send) and `SET WS-I TO WS-X`'s rejection (b3).

WHY THIS IS PARTIAL AND NOT CONFORMS - two measured reservations:
(a) EVERY ONE OF THOSE REJECTIONS CITES section 8.8.1.1, NOT SR2, because the rule is not written down anywhere: nothing in the tree asks 'is this sender class index'. The screen SR2 is riding is one whose scope is actively contested in this codebase - kb/Work PB172 (landed) records that widening the 8.8.1.1 intrinsic screen to the index-name window over-rejected six NIST IF programs and had to be narrowed again. A future narrowing of 8.8.1.1 would silently delete SR2's only enforcement, because no test names SR2 as its subject.
(b) THE ONE PATH THAT REACHES SR2's QUESTION DIRECTLY REPORTS A FALSE FACT. `SET IX TO P1` with P1 USAGE POINTER (probe k2_ptr_send_index) emits TWO errors, the first of which is `COBOLNET1639: 'IX' is not defined - no declaration in this source element gives the name 'IX'`. IX IS defined - it is the INDEXED BY index-name of the table two lines above. The cause is SetBinder.cs:336: a POINTER on either side re-routes to BindSetPointer, which calls ctx.Refs.Resolve on the index-name as if it were a data item; the receiver rejection (COBOLNET0869) then follows. The source is correctly refused, but the first thing the user is told about their program is untrue.

Test-ref: conformance:negative/pb155-set-to-edited (enabled in tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json) is `SET IX TO XE` over a numeric-edited sender with a spec-derived expectation, and conformance:negative/pb172-set-to-alphanumeric-function names SR1/SR2 in its own header. Both pin the complement; neither pins the positive half (a class-index identifier-2 accepted where an arithmetic expression is not).  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): No code implements SR2. The complement is enforced incidentally by the section 8.8.1.1 arithmetic-operand screen reached through src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs:351 and :369 `host.Expr.BindIndexWindowExpr(...)` (COBOLNET0844). The pointer/program-pointer/object re-routes that bypass that screen are SetBinder.cs:329-343 (BindSetTo) and :359 (BindSetUpDown -> PtrBinder.TryBindSetUpDown).

subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work/PB212.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "If identifier-1 references a data item of class index, arithmetic-expression-1 shall not be specified." -> OK, Syntax rules 3). THE RULE PAIRS THE RECEIVER'S CLASS WITH THE SENDER ALTERNATIVE: when identifier-1 is a class-index DATA item (USAGE INDEX), the only legal senders in Format 1 are index-name-2 and identifier-2 - and 14.9.39.4 GR2b confirms it by defining ONLY that case ('If identifier-1 references an index data item, the content of index-name-2 or of the data item referenced by identifier-2 is placed in the index referenced by index-name-1 unchanged' - cite.py OK). There is no general rule for an index data item receiving an arithmetic expression, because the syntax rule forbids the shape. NO CODE IMPLEMENTS IT. BindSetTo collects receivers through SetTargetOf (which asks only 'index-name or resolvable receiving item?') and binds the sender through host.Expr.BindIndexWindowExpr with no reference back to the receivers' class; a grep of the pinned tree for a 14.9.39.3 SR3 citation finds nothing, and the only receiver-side screen anyone has written down for SET is the one PB212 says is MISSING (SR1). MEASURED at --std 2023 and --std 85 (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr3_idxdata_arith.cob / sr3_idxdata_expr.cob / sr3_idxdata_arith_85.cob): with `01 IXD USAGE INDEX.` beside a table indexed by IDX, `SET IXD TO 3.` and `SET IXD TO N + 1.` both compile clean (exit 0, no diagnostic) and run. The legal shapes still work (sr3_idxdata_idxname `SET IXD TO IDX`, sr3_idxdata_ident2 `SET IXD TO IXE`), so this is pure under-rejection, not a mis-selected format. HARM: silent under-rejection - the program is not conforming and no other compiler need accept it, and because the store is the ordinary Format-1 numeric store the index data item is written with a raw expression value rather than an occurrence-derived index, which GR2b never sanctions. OWNERSHIP: OPEN register note PB212 owns the SET receiver's CLASS screen (SR1) and its stated fix - 'extend ScreenResultant ... with 14.9.39.3 SR1's own citation' - would NOT close this row: SR3 is not a rule about what the receiver may be, it is a rule about which SENDER alternative the receiver's class admits, and a resultant-class screen has no sender to look at. Reported as a new finding (the SR3/SR4 sender-alternative pair). EDITIONS ARE INFERRED, NOT READ: specs/ISO_COBOL.md carries only the 2023 text. Format 1 exists in every edition (SET index assignment is core COBOL-85 table handling) and Annex E carries no 2014->2023 change for it; the 2023 sender spelling is arithmetic-expression-1 where 85 wrote integer-1, which narrows the shape but not the rule.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs#BindSetTo (:345-351) and #SetTargetOf (:435-438) - the Format-1 receiver/sender pair is bound with no class relation applied

subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work/PB212.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "If identifier-1 references a numeric data item, index-name-2 shall be specified." -> OK, Syntax rules 4). THE TWIN OF SR3 ON THE OTHER RECEIVER CLASS, and the stricter of the two: when the Format-1 receiver is a NUMERIC data item the sender shall be index-name-2 - not arithmetic-expression-1 and not identifier-2. 14.9.39.4 GR2c is the confirming half ('If identifier-1 references a numeric data item, that item is set to the occurrence number of the table element referenced by index-name-2' - cite.py OK): the ONLY defined semantic for a numeric Format-1 receiver is 'receive an occurrence number from an index-name'. A numeric value assignment is MOVE's or COMPUTE's job, not SET's. NO CODE IMPLEMENTS IT - same site, same absence as SR3. MEASURED at --std 2023 and --std 85: with `01 N PIC 9(4).` (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr4_num_literal.cob, sr4_num_literal_85.cob) `SET N TO 3.` compiles clean and prints N=0003; `SET N TO M + 1.` (sr4_num_expr) prints N=0008; and `SET N TO IXD.` with `01 IXD USAGE INDEX.` (sr4_num_ident2) prints N=0002 - identifier-2 into a numeric receiver, which SR4 forbids just as firmly as the literal does. The legal shape (sr4_num_idxname_legal, `SET IDX TO 4. SET N TO IDX.`) gives N=0004. THE SAME GAP IS ALREADY LOAD-BEARING INSIDE THE TEST SUITE: tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/FlagDirectiveTests.cs:618 (Compile_RangeExceptionForIndex_NotFlagged_OnPlainNumericReceiver) uses `SET N TO 3.` with N PIC 9(4) as its fixture and asserts only the absence of a FLAG-02 warning - a green test standing on source SR4 forbids (feedback_green_test_can_hold_a_gap_open). HARM: silent under-rejection. PB212 (open) owns SR1 only; its ScreenResultant-style fix cannot see the sender and so cannot close SR3 or SR4. EDITIONS INFERRED as for SR3.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs#BindSetTo (:345-351) and #SetTargetOf (:435-438)

notes: kb/Work/PB454.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Mnemonic-name-1 shall be associated with an external switch, the status of which may be altered." and "The implementor defines which external switches may be referenced by the SET statement." -> both OK, Syntax rules 5). THE RULE IS LOCATED AND CHECKED, AND DIVERGES IN THREE MEASURED WAYS. (1) WRONG STAGE. SwitchBindSet looks the operand up in ctx.Data.SwitchMnemonics and, on a miss, returns `BoundUnsupported($"SET '{name}' TO ON/OFF - not a SPECIAL-NAMES external-switch mnemonic (ISO 14.9.39 F3 SR5)")`. BoundUnsupported is not a diagnostic: it is emitted as a run-time throw. MEASURED (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr5_not_a_mnemonic.cob): `SET NOPE TO ON.` with NOPE undeclared compiles CLEAN at --std 2023 (exit 0, no diagnostic) and then dies with `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... not a SPECIAL-NAMES external-switch mnemonic (ISO 14.9.39 F3 SR5)`. A syntax rule shall be decided by the compiler, not by generated code that only runs if the statement is reached. (2) THE OPTION-2 LENIENCY ADMITS WHAT SR5 FORBIDS. DataBinder.Switches.cs:492 registers `ids.Length >= 2 ? ids[1] : implName` - i.e. when the SPECIAL-NAMES entry writes NO mnemonic-name (Option 2: `SWITCH-1 ON STATUS IS SW-ON`), the SWITCH-NAME itself is entered in the mnemonic table. MEASURED (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr5_switchname_no_mnemonic.cob): `SET SWITCH-1 TO ON.` compiles, runs, and the ON STATUS condition then reads true. A switch-name is an implementor-name (8.3.2.3.11), never mnemonic-name-1, so the statement is not conforming; the code comment at DataBinder.Switches.cs:24-27 calls it 'legacy-parity leniency' and argues no conforming program changes meaning - true, but the leniency is UNCONDITIONAL, not gated on --permissive or on a dialect axis, so the strict compiler has no way to reject it. (3) THE IMPLEMENTOR-DEFINITION HALF IS UNDOCUMENTED. SR5's second sentence makes 'which external switches may be referenced by the SET statement' an implementor definition, and Annex A.1 item 191 requires it to be documented when the facility is provided. docs/CONFORMANCE.md contains no occurrence of the word 'switch' at all, and DataBinder binds ANY cobolWord as switch-name-1, so the set is unbounded and unstated. Also measured: a switch-STATUS condition-name in the mnemonic slot (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr5_condname_as_mnemonic.cob, `SET SW-ON TO ON.`) takes the same clean-compile/run-time-throw path. EDITIONS INFERRED: Format 3 and the SPECIAL-NAMES switch clause are version-invariant 85->2023 (the spec carries no Annex E change for either).  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetAlterBinder.cs#SwitchBindSet (:184-187, the BoundUnsupported arm) and src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Switches.cs:492 (SwitchMnemonics.TryAdd registering the switch-NAME when no mnemonic is written)

notes: kb/Work/PB390.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Condition-name-1 shall be associated with a conditional variable." -> OK, Syntax rules 6). THE RULE IS CHECKED, AT THE WRONG STAGE, AND ITS DISCRIMINATING CASE IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. ConditionOf resolves a level-88 condition-name (which by construction HAS a conditional variable - BindSetCondition then resolves `cond.Parent` as the store target), so the rule's substance is realized for the legal case: probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr6_level88_legal.cob (`01 WF PIC X VALUE 'N'. 88 WF-YES VALUE 'Y'.` then `SET WF-YES TO TRUE.`) prints WF=Y. THE DISCRIMINATING CASE is the OTHER kind of condition-name COBOL has: a SPECIAL-NAMES switch-status condition-name (8.8.4.6) is a condition-name that is NOT associated with a conditional variable, and SR6 exists precisely to exclude it from Format 4. MEASURED (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr6_switch_condname.cob): with `SWITCH-1 IS SW-M ON STATUS IS SW-ON.`, `SET SW-ON TO TRUE.` compiles CLEAN at --std 2023 (exit 0, no diagnostic) and dies at run time with `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: SET 'SW-ON' TO TRUE (not a condition-name)`. Two defects in that one line: the syntax rule is decided by generated code instead of a compile-time diagnostic (identical mechanism to SR5, SR7 and 14.9.13.3 SR2), and the message is factually wrong - SW-ON IS a condition-name, it is merely not one associated with a conditional variable, which is what SR6 says and what the diagnostic should say. EDITIONS INFERRED: Format 4's TO TRUE arm is version-invariant 85->2023.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs#BindSetCondition (:449, `if (host.Cond.ConditionOf(dref) is not { } cond) return new BoundUnsupported(...)`)

notes: kb/Work/PB455.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "If the FALSE phrase is specified, the FALSE phrase shall be specified in the VALUE clause of the data description entry for condition-name-1." -> OK, Syntax rules 7). THE WHOLE FALSE ARM IS ABSENT, so the rule has nothing to constrain. BindSetCondition's first line refuses every `SET ... TO FALSE` outright with a BoundUnsupported whose own text names the rule ('the VALUE ... WHEN SET TO FALSE phrase, COBOL-2002+, ISO 14.9.39 SR7'), and the 88-item model carries no WHEN SET TO FALSE value to check against. MEASURED (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr7_false_with_phrase.cob): the LEGAL program `01 WF PIC X VALUE 'Y'. 88 WF-YES VALUE 'Y' WHEN SET TO FALSE 'N'.` + `SET WF-YES TO FALSE.` compiles CLEAN at --std 2023 (exit 0, no diagnostic, no COBOLNET0900 edition gate) and then aborts at run time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException. That is REJECTS-LEGAL-SOURCE delivered as a crash, the worst of the three shapes: a user gets a green build and a run-time abort. The ILLEGAL program the rule is actually about - the same SET with `88 WF-YES VALUE 'Y'.` and no WHEN SET TO FALSE phrase (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr7_false_without_phrase.cob) - takes the identical path, so the compiler cannot tell the conforming case from the non-conforming one. Also measured: at --std 85 the WHEN SET TO FALSE phrase and the SET ... TO FALSE statement both parse without a COBOLNET0900 introduction gate (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr7_false_with_phrase_85.cob), which is a separate edition-gate gap on the 13.18.63 VALUE clause side. EDITIONS: the FALSE phrase of the VALUE clause and the Format-4 FALSE arm are a COBOL-2002 addition (INFERRED - Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change, and FALSE is not among E.2's newly reserved words, so the arm predates 2023; COBOL-85 Format 4 had TO TRUE only).  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs#BindSetCondition (:444-445, `if (b.TRUE_() is null) return new BoundUnsupported("SET condition-name TO FALSE ...")`)
