notes: kb/Work/PB456.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Identifier-3 shall be any item of class object that is permitted as a receiving item." -> OK, Syntax rules 8). TWO HALVES; ONE FULLY MEASURED, ONE ONLY PARTLY. HALF 1 - 'any item of class object' - CONFORMS. OoBindSetObjectRef screens every receiving operand and reports COBOLNET0867 naming SR8. MEASURED (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr8_nonobject_receiver.cob): `01 WX PIC X(4).` + `SET WX TO C.` -> `error COBOLNET0867: SET 'WX': the receiving operand of an object-reference SET shall be a USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE data item (ISO 14.9.39.3 SR8)` at compile time, exit 70; and the legal counterpart, a UNIVERSAL receiver (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr8_universal_ok.cob, `01 U USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE.` + `SET U TO C.` + `INVOKE U 'PING'`) runs and prints PONG. Identical at --std 2002; at --std 85 the whole OO surface is gated by COBOLNET0900 first. HALF 2 - 'that is permitted as a receiving item' - PARTLY SCREENED, and that is why this is not CONFORMS. What 8.4.3 makes class-object-but-not-a-receiving-item is the set of IMPLICITLY-defined object references (the predefined references, and references returned from an object property, an object-view, an inline method invocation, or a function). Measured coverage: EXCEPTION-OBJECT IS screened (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr8_exception_object_receiver.cob -> COBOLNET0848 citing 8.4.3.6 SR1) though a SPURIOUS COBOLNET1639 "'EXCEPTION-OBJECT' is not defined" is emitted FIRST, so the user reads a name-resolution error before the real rule; SELF as a receiver is refused, but only as a bare parse error (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr8_self_as_receiver.cob -> COBOL0001 'no viable alternative at input SETSELF'), never by the rule; an OBJECT-VIEW receiver produces a three-diagnostic cascade under the wrong name (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr8_inline_invocation_receiver.cob, `SET C AS CIMPLO TO U.` -> COBOLNET1639 "'AS' is not defined" + COBOLNET0867 "SET 'AS'" + COBOLNET0901 'AS is a reserved word'), and a function-result or inline-invocation receiver is not probed at all because no dataReference shape carries them. ALSO NOT COVERED BY THIS SCREEN AT ALL: the screen only runs when the Format-5 re-route selects it, and that re-route requires the SENDER to be a bare data reference (SetBinder.BindSetTo :329-343 via OoBinder.OoExtractBareReference). With a literal or expression sender an object-reference receiver never reaches OoBindSetObjectRef - see the SR9 row for the measurement. TEST-REF (refined after the checkpoint line was written): conformance-test:OoSpineTests.SetObjectRef_Violations_0867 is the spec-derived covering test - a [Theory] whose doc comment derives from 14.9.39 F5 SR12/SR9/SR8 and which asserts COBOLNET0867 for `SET N4 TO U.` (a PIC 9(4) receiver, SR8's rejection) and for `SET U TO SUPER.` (SR9's SUPER clause). It covers the conforming halves only; it does not exercise the non-bare-sender escape, so it does not close the row.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/OoBinder.cs#OoBindSetObjectRef (:866-889 - the per-target loop: the EXCEPTION-OBJECT arm then the `Pic is not { Category: PicCategory.ObjectReference }` arm, both COBOLNET0867/0848)

subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work/PB456.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Identifier-4 shall be an object reference; the predefined object reference SUPER shall not be specified." -> OK, Syntax rules 9). THE SUPER HALF CONFORMS. The grammar deliberately admits SUPER (objectReference : dataReference | NULL_ | SELF | SUPER) so the binder can give the rule's own message, and it does: MEASURED (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr9_super_sender.cob) `SET U TO SUPER.` -> `error COBOLNET0867: SET . TO SUPER: SUPER shall not be the sending operand of an object-reference SET (ISO 14.9.39.3 SR9)` at compile time, identical at --std 2002 and 2023, exit 70. THE 'SHALL BE AN OBJECT REFERENCE' HALF IS ENFORCED ONLY FOR A BARE-REFERENCE SENDER, AND THE ESCAPE IS MEASURED. For a bare data reference it is right: scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr9_nonobject_sender.cob (`01 WX PIC X(4).` + `SET U TO WX.`) -> COBOLNET0867 "the sending operand shall be an object-reference data item, NULL, SELF, or a class-name (ISO 14.9.39.3 SR9/SR12/SR13)". BUT Format 5 is selected by a SEMANTIC re-route whose precondition is `OoBinder.OoExtractBareReference(tv.arithmeticExpression()) is { } senderDref` - the sender must be EXACTLY one bare dataReference. A literal or an arithmetic expression fails that test, the re-route never fires, and the statement stays on the Format-1 path with an object-reference item as the receiver. MEASURED: scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr9_literal_sender.cob (`SET U TO 5.`) compiles CLEAN at --std 2023 (exit 0, NO diagnostic); scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr9_literal_sender_used.cob (the same SET followed by `INVOKE U 'PING'`) and scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr9_expr_sender.cob (`SET U TO N + 1.`) both compile clean and die at run time with `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: arithmetic into a non-fixed-point target 'U'` - a message about arithmetic, naming neither SR9 nor SR1 nor SET. So for every non-bare sender the SET verb has NO operand screen at all: SR9 is not applied (the sender is not an object reference), and 14.9.39.3 SR1 is not applied either (the receiver is not class index and not an integer item - the row PB212 owns). The defect is in the SELECTION mechanism, not in OoBindSetObjectRef, which is why it is recorded here and in the SR8 row rather than under PB212. TEST-REF (refined after the checkpoint line was written): conformance-test:OoSpineTests.SetObjectRef_Violations_0867 is the spec-derived covering test - a [Theory] whose doc comment derives from 14.9.39 F5 SR12/SR9/SR8 and which asserts COBOLNET0867 for `SET N4 TO U.` (a PIC 9(4) receiver, SR8's rejection) and for `SET U TO SUPER.` (SR9's SUPER clause). It covers the conforming halves only; it does not exercise the non-bare-sender escape, so it does not close the row.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/OoBinder.cs#OoBindSetObjectRef (:862-868 SUPER arm; :930-971 the sender arms) and src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs#BindSetTo (:329-343 - the re-route that decides whether the sender screen runs at all)

subject: SET statement
notes:
kb/Work/PB388.md — Citations validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "an object reference described with an interface-name that identifies int-1 or an interface inheriting from int-1"` -> OK 10); `"if described without a FACTORY phrase, the objects of the specified class shall implement int-1"` -> OK 10); `"if described with a FACTORY phrase, the factory object of the specified class shall implement int-1"` -> OK 10).

FOUR OF THE FIVE ALTERNATIVES ARE IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED (probe file setp1_o2.py, --std 2023, one compilation group with interfaces IA / IB-inherits-IA / IZ and classes CB-implements-IA / CD-inherits-CB / CX):
- a) an interface sender that inherits int-1: `SET RA TO RB` (RA is OBJECT REFERENCE IA, RB is OBJECT REFERENCE IB, IB INHERITS FROM IA) COMPILES AND RUNS (p1a_iface_inherit -> OK). The negative control `SET RA TO RZ` is refused: COBOLNET0867 'interface IZ does not inherit interface IA' (p1b_iface_unrelated). OoConformance.cs:384-403 walks the inheritance closure, so a transitively-inheriting interface is admitted too.
- b2) a class sender WITHOUT a FACTORY phrase whose objects implement int-1: `SET RA TO OB` binds and the interface view is live - INVOKE RA "PING" prints PONG (p2a_class_impl). A SUBCLASS of the implementing class is admitted (p2c_subclass_impl -> PONG). A non-implementing class is refused: 'class CX does not implement interface IA (ISO 9.3.8.2/SET SR10)' (p2b_class_noimpl). The test is the section 11.8.4 GR2 transitive IMPLEMENTS closure.
- d) SELF: implemented at OoBinder.cs:920-926 and it is the ONE alternative in this whole rule that carries BOTH a positive and a negative spec-derived test - conformance:2002/oo_set_self_interface (expects PONG) and conformance:negative/oo-set-self-interface-not-implemented (both 'enabled' in tests/conformance/negative/manifest.json), a pair that differs only by the IMPLEMENTS clause.
- e) NULL: `SET RA TO NULL` compiles and runs (probe j2_null_iface -> OK); senderNull short-circuits every conformance test, which is right - NULL conforms to any object reference.

TWO ALTERNATIVES ARE UNREACHABLE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS PARTIAL:
- b1) a class sender described WITH a FACTORY phrase. `01 FB USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE FACTORY OF CB` is refused at DECLARATION: COBOLNET0899 'USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE FACTORY OF (a factory-object reference, ISO 13.18.60) is recognized but not yet implemented (the universal-reference wave)' (probe p3_factory_usage). The item then degrades to a UNIVERSAL reference and the SET draws a second, misleading error - 'a UNIVERSAL object reference does not conform to a typed receiver'. So the b1 leg of the rule (test the FACTORY closure rather than the instance closure) has no code and no reachable input. Note ObjectRefWideningMismatch calls `ImplementsClosure(sc, factory: false)` UNCONDITIONALLY (OoConformance.cs:381) - the factory/instance distinction b1-vs-b2 draws is not represented at all, so the day FACTORY OF lands, b1 will silently take b2's test unless this line is changed with it.
- c) an ACTIVE-CLASS sender. `USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE ACTIVE-CLASS` is not in the grammar; className is a bare cobolWord, so the word falls through and the binder mis-reports it as an undeclared class: COBOLNET0813 'names the unknown class or interface ACTIVE-CLASS' plus COBOLNET0901 'ACTIVE-CLASS is a reserved word in COBOL-2023' (probe p4_active_class).

DIAGNOSTIC DEFECT SHARED WITH SR12: every rejection on this path ends with the fixed tail '(ISO 14.9.39.3 SR12 - a universal sender needs an object view to narrow)', appended at OoBinder.cs:942 regardless of which rule the inner message actually applied. NO CODE ANYWHERE IMPLEMENTS THIS RULE, AND ITS SUBJECT CANNOT BE DECLARED. The printed USAGE clause format (specs/ISO_COBOL.md section 13.18.60.2, verified against the rendered figure notes) gives OBJECT REFERENCE three operand shapes: `interface-name-1`, `[FACTORY OF] ACTIVE-CLASS`, and `[FACTORY OF] object-class-name-1 [ONLY]`. The grammar carries the first and the third-minus-ONLY. MEASURED (probe p4_active_class, --std 2023): `01 AC USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE ACTIVE-CLASS.` -> `COBOLNET0813: data item 'AC': USAGE OBJECT REFERENCE names the unknown class or interface 'ACTIVE-CLASS' - the declared name of a typed object reference shall be a class or interface of the compilation group` plus `COBOLNET0901: 'ACTIVE-CLASS' is a reserved word in COBOL-2023 and cannot be used as a user-defined word (ISO 8.9)`. The same is true with the FACTORY OF prefix. So identifier-3 can never be 'described with an ACTIVE-CLASS phrase' and none of the rule's three alternatives (a: an ACTIVE-CLASS sender with matching FACTORY presence; b: SELF with the instance/factory placement rules; c: NULL) has a reachable input.

notes:
kb/Work/PB450.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Identifier-5 shall reference a data item of category data-pointer. Identifier-6 shall be of category data-pointer"` -> OK, Syntax rules 17) (FORMAT 7).

BOTH SENTENCES ARE ENFORCED OVER THE SHAPES THE GRAMMAR ADMITS (probes at --std 2002 and --std 2023, identical): a non-pointer identifier-6 - `SET P1 TO WS-N` with WS-N PIC 9(4) - draws COBOLNET0869 (c5_nonptr_send); a non-pointer identifier-5 - `SET WS-N TO ADDRESS OF REC1` - draws 0869 naming Format 7 (c9_nonptr_recv); a legal `SET P1 TO ADDRESS OF REC1` / `SET ADDRESS OF B1 TO P1` pair runs and prints the rebased content (c4_one_addr_recv -> B1A=[AAAA]); several pointer receivers work (c7_two_ptr_recv); `SET P1 TO NULL` works (k3_ptr_to_null), correctly, since section 8.4.3.10.4 GR1 makes the predefined address NULL a data item of category data-pointer (`cite.py --check 8.4.3.10.4 "When associated with a data-pointer, the predefined address NULL references a data item of category data-pointer"` -> OK).

WHY PARTIAL: THE SURFACE THE SCREEN COVERS IS A STRICT SUBSET OF FORMAT 7. The rendered PDF page 760 (folio 730) shows the ellipsis OUTSIDE the receiving brace, so `{ADDRESS OF data-name-1 | identifier-5}` repeats and the two alternatives may be MIXED, and identifier-6 is any operand of category data-pointer - which section 8.4.3.11 makes include `ADDRESS OF x`. Four legal statements are COBOL0001 PARSE ERRORS, so SR17 is never even asked about their operands: `SET ADDRESS OF B1 ADDRESS OF B2 TO P1` (c1_two_addr_recv), `SET P1 P2 TO ADDRESS OF REC1` (c2), `SET ADDRESS OF B1 P1 TO P2` (c3), `SET ADDRESS OF B1 TO ADDRESS OF R1` (i3_addr_to_addr). See the FMT-14.9.39.2 record and finding set1-F3.

The mirror error is in the grammar comment at CobolParserCore.g4:1253, 'SET dataReference+ TO TRUE/FALSE (COBOL-85 section 14.9.39 Format 5)', where 2023's Format 5 is object-reference-assignment. A user reading `error COBOLNET0869: ... (ISO 14.9.39 Format 4)` and then opening the standard at Format 4 finds condition-setting.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/PtrBinder.cs:191-197 PtrResolvePointer (the ONE category test, COBOLNET0869) called from :46 (the ADDRESS OF form's sender) and :54 (the sender form's receiver); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs:186-223 BindSetPointer (:200 receivers, :213 sender). subject: SET statement
notes:
kb/Work/PB450.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Data-name-1 shall be a based data item"` -> OK, Syntax rules 18) (FORMAT 7).

MEASURED BOTH DIRECTIONS at --std 2002 and --std 2023, identical at both. NEGATIVE: `01 NB PIC X(4)` in the LINKAGE SECTION, `SET ADDRESS OF NB TO P1` -> `COBOLNET0869: 'NB': the operand shall be a BASED level-01/77 item (ISO 14.9.39 SR18 / 14.9.3 SR1 - rebasing or allocating a non-BASED item is not ISO COBOL)` (probe c6_nonbased_recv). This is the right refusal AND it refuses the widespread vendor extension (rebasing a plain LINKAGE 01) rather than silently accepting it. POSITIVE: `01 B1 BASED.` rebased from a pointer taken with ADDRESS OF, then read back -> B1A=[AAAA] (probe c4_one_addr_recv). `SET ADDRESS OF B1 TO NULL` also binds (probe c8_addr_to_null), which is SR19's leg (a sibling part) but confirms the SR18 gate is not in its way.

THE 'level-01/77' WORDING IN THE MESSAGE IS ACCURATE AND NOT AN INVENTION: section 13.16.3 SR16 says 'The BASED clause may be specified only in data description entries in the linkage section, in the working-storage section, and in the local-storage section. The level number of such data description entries shall be 1 or 77' (`cite.py --check 13.16.3 "The BASED clause may be specified only in data description entries in the linkage section"` -> OK), and section 8.6.5 defines a based entry as one 'described with a BASED clause' (`cite.py --check 8.6.5 ...` -> OK). So 'based data item' and 'BASED level-01/77 item' pick out the same set.

EDGES I PROBED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. (i) The `dref.ChildCount == 1` guard restricts the lookup to a BARE name - correct, because a based entry is level 01/77 (13.16.3 SR16) and data-name-1 is a data-name, so no qualified, subscripted or reference-modified spelling is legal here; nothing legal is turned away by it. (ii) `ByName ... list[0]` looked like a same-name-shadowing hazard, so I measured it: a compilation group with a non-based `01 SHAREDX PIC X(4)` in program I2A and a `01 SHAREDX BASED` in program I2B rebases and reads the RIGHT item - SX=[BBBB] (probe i2_based_shadow) - so ByName is scoped per source element and the first-wins pick does not cross programs. CONFORMS, with the negative side pinned by an enabled spec-derived test. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED DOWNWARD on three measured grounds, two of them wrong-answer.

(1) THE SR18 SCREEN GIVES THE WRONG ANSWER IN BOTH DIRECTIONS FOR A METHOD-LOCAL NAME, and the mechanism is the bypass the file's own class doc-comment already flags. PtrResolveBased (PtrBinder.cs:200-209) reads ctx.Data.ByName DIRECTLY instead of the scope-aware SymbolTable, whose TryResolve (SymbolTable.cs:47-60) consults scope.Method.ByName FIRST. Per 8.4.6.2.1 a local name is referenced in the source element declaring it, and rule 3a says 'If the name is declared in source element B, the item in source element B is the referenced item'; 8.4.6.2.2 makes the OBJECT's data-names global, so a method's own declaration shadows them. Measured, both directions: a method-local `01 MB BASED.` (a BASED level-01 item, exactly what SR18 requires) is REJECTED as not-based; and a method-local non-based `01 SHR PIC X(4)` that legally shadows an object-level `01 SHR BASED.` is ACCEPTED as based - the SR18 verdict is decided by a name map that does not know the reference's scope. Moving the SAME declaration from the object's data division to the method's flips the verdict, which is the proof it is scope, not the declaration, being read.

(2) SR18's DOMAIN INSIDE CLASS DEFINITIONS IS A NAMED LOUD RESIDUE, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION. 13.16.3 SR16 admits BASED in the linkage, working-storage and local-storage sections - which object, factory and method definitions all have - and every such program draws COBOLNET0899 'BASED data or ADDRESS OF in a class definition's data divisions is recognized but not yet implemented'. A rule whose surface is loudly unimplemented over a whole source-element class is PARTIAL by the refuter calibration, not CONFORMS.

(3) THE ADJUDICATION APPLIES ITS OWN SR17 REASONING TO SR17 AND NOT TO SR18 - one Format, two operands, one screened conclusion. The rendered PDF page 760 (folio 730) puts the ellipsis OUTSIDE the receiving brace, so `{ADDRESS OF data-name-1 | identifier-5} ... TO identifier-6` repeats AND mixes; the adjudicator used exactly that to make SR17 PARTIAL ('THE SURFACE THE SCREEN COVERS IS A STRICT SUBSET OF FORMAT 7 ... SR17 is never even asked about their operands') while giving SR18 - which governs data-name-1 in the SAME repeated brace - a clean CONFORMS with no reservation. I reproduced the parse failures independently. SR18 is therefore never asked about the second and later ADDRESS OF data-name-1 operands.

NOT lower than PARTIAL: the outer-program single-receiver lane genuinely works in both directions, including the WORKING-STORAGE and level-77 BASED spellings 13.16.3 SR16 admits, and the rejection arm is pinned by an enabled spec-derived negative test.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/PtrBinder.cs:199-209 PtrResolveBased - `DataItem? item = dref.ChildCount == 1 && ctx.Data.ByName.TryGetValue(dref.GetText(), out var list) && list.Count > 0 ? list[0] : null; if (item is { IsBased: true }) return item;` then COBOLNET0869 citing SR18; called from :40 (SET ADDRESS OF) and :131 (ALLOCATE).

notes:
kb/Work/PB389.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Identifier-12 shall reference a data item of category function-pointer"` -> OK, Syntax rules 20) (FORMAT 8).

THE RULE'S SUBJECT CANNOT BE DECLARED, SO NONE OF ITS FOUR SENTENCES HAS AN INPUT. MEASURED (probes e1_fp_decl, e2_fp_bare): `01 FP1 USAGE FUNCTION-POINTER TO FPROTO.` and the bare `01 FP1 USAGE FUNCTION-POINTER.` both draw `COBOLNET0899: data item 'FP1': USAGE FUNCTION-POINTER (ISO 13.18.60 - a function-pointer data item)` at --std 2023, and at --std 2002 additionally `COBOLNET0900: USAGE FUNCTION-POINTER requires COBOL-2014`. The declaration is refused, so `SET FP1 TO FP2` is never reached. Format 8 has no grammar arm of its own either - it shares `SET dataReference+ TO arithmeticExpression`, and BindSetTo's category re-routes (SetBinder.cs:329-343) test Pointer, ProgramPointer and ObjectReference and stop there, so even if the item existed the statement would fall into the Format-1 arithmetic store.

THE FOUR OBLIGATIONS, NONE IMPLEMENTED: identifier-12 category function-pointer; identifier-13 category function-pointer; identifier-13 NULL-or-a-function-pointer (section 8.4.3.10.4 GR2 gives NULL that category); and the SAME-SIGNATURE test over the associated function-prototypes - the last of which needs the function-prototype registry the code comments call 'P13'. I searched beyond the dossier: `grep -rn FunctionPointer src/` returns declaration-side handling only (PicInfo.cs:115-118 documents the usage as 'recognized, STAGED LOUD', DataItem.cs:538, IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:472), and no SET site.

HARM: legal COBOL-2014/2023 is rejected, but LOUDLY and with a named, honest diagnostic, so nothing is silent. This is a section 13.18.60 declaration gap that strands SR20 rather than a SET defect; it is not an A.4 optional module, so it is not covered by any owner non-support determination.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/PictureAnalyzer.cs:554-560 - `case "FUNCTION-POINTER": edition.Error(DiagnosticCatalog.UsageFunctionPointer, ...); return Usage.FunctionPointer;` (DiagnosticCatalog.cs:399-404, COBOLNET0899 RecognizedNotImplemented). notes:
kb/Work/PB449.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Identifier-7 shall reference a data item of category program-pointer. Identifier-8 shall be of category program-pointer"` -> OK, Syntax rules 21) (FORMAT 9).

BOTH SENTENCES MEASURED, BOTH DIRECTIONS, at --std 2002 and --std 2023 (identical at both):
- identifier-8 non-conforming: `SET PP1 TO WS-N` with WS-N PIC 9(4) -> `COBOLNET0869: SET ... TO 'WS-N': a program-pointer sender shall be NULL, another USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER item, or an ENTRY program-address-identifier (ISO 14.9.39 Format 9 SR21 / 8.4.3.13)` (probe f2_pp_to_num).
- identifier-7 non-conforming: `SET WS-N TO PP1` -> `COBOLNET0869: SET 'WS-N': the receiving operand of a program-pointer SET shall be USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER (ISO 14.9.39 Format 9 SR21)` (probe f3_num_to_pp). The screen holds over a MIXED receiving list too - `SET WS-N PP1 TO PP2` is refused on WS-N (probe m4_pp_mixed_recv), because the re-route at SetBinder.cs:339 fires on the SENDER's category as well as the first target's, so it does not have the first-operand blind spot SR23's arm has.
- the legal lanes: `SET PP1 TO NULL` then `SET PP2 TO PP1` runs (f1_pp_to_pp), and several receivers work - `SET PP1 PP2 TO PP1` (f4_pp_multi), which is the printed `{ identifier-7 } ...` repetition confirmed on the rendered PDF page 760.
NULL is admitted as identifier-8, correctly: section 8.4.3.10.4 GR3 makes the predefined address NULL a data item of category program-pointer (`cite.py --check 8.4.3.10.4 "When associated with a program-pointer, the predefined address NULL references a data item of category program-pointer"` -> OK). The ENTRY sender is likewise category program-pointer by section 8.4.3.13 and takes the same receiver screen.

ONE THING THIS ROW DELIBERATELY DOES NOT CLAIM: `SET WS-N PP1 TO 4` compiles clean and throws 'arithmetic into a non-fixed-point target PP1' at run time (probe m5_pp_lit_recv). That is NOT an SR21 failure - a numeric-literal sender makes the statement Format 1, where identifier-1 is governed by SR1, and SR1's missing receiver screen is recorded as DIVERGES under SR-14.9.39.3-1 / kb/Work PB212. Recorded here so a reader does not mistake the SR21 verdict for a claim about that program.

Test-ref conformance:2002/program_pointer is spec-derived and names this rule in its own header ('SET Format 9 (14.9.39 SR21) with the 8.4.3.13 program-address-identifier sender'); it pins the positive lane (ENTRY literal, ENTRY identifier, a program-pointer sender, NULL) end to end. The rejection lane has no test; I measured it. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED DOWNWARD. The adjudication's load-bearing sentence is 'the re-route at SetBinder.cs:339 fires on the SENDER's category as well as the first target's, so it does not have the first-operand blind spot SR23's arm has'. That is true only over the shapes it measured and false in general: the sniff is `t0 OR s0`, so a Format 9 statement in which NEITHER the FIRST receiver NOR the sender is a program-pointer - while a LATER receiver is - escapes the routing entirely and SR21 is never asked.

MEASURED: `SET WS-N PP1 TO WS-M` (WS-N, WS-M PIC 9(4); PP1 USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER) COMPILES WITH ZERO DIAGNOSTICS and throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException 'arithmetic into a non-fixed-point target PP1' at run time. Both operands are IDENTIFIERS, so Format 9 (`SET {identifier-7} ... TO identifier-8`) matches syntactically, and Format 9 is the ONLY format whose receiving operand may be a program-pointer (Format 1 SR1 = class index or integer; Format 5 = class object; Formats 7/10 = category data-pointer; F14 = a CAPACITY register; F15 = numeric; F16 = dynamic-length; F17 = message-tag). So SR21 is violated by WS-N under sentence 1 and by WS-M under sentence 2, and nothing enforces it. This is NOT the case the adjudicator excused under SR1: its exclusion turned on a numeric LITERAL sender making Format 9 syntactically unavailable, and that reasoning does not reach an identifier sender.

THE ADJUDICATION CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THIS EXACT MECHANISM. Its own SR23 record states 'BindSetTo's re-routes at SetBinder.cs:329-343 also read only tds[0] (and the sender, when it is a bare reference)' and grades SR23 PARTIAL for it. SR21 rides the same two re-route lines and was graded CONFORMS. One mechanism, two verdicts - the two-arm shape.

SECOND RESERVATION, ALSO MEASURED: for a Format 9 statement whose identifier-8 is a DATA-pointer - the nearest-miss category and the mistake a user actually writes - SR21 is not the rule that fires. `SET PP1 TO DP1` and `SET DP1 PP1 TO PP2` are both refused by the DATA-pointer arm, which blames PP1, an operand that CONFORMS to SR21 sentence 1, and cites '(ISO 14.9.39 Format 4)' - a format that in ISO/IEC 1989:2023 is condition-setting, not pointer assignment. The adjudicator already logged that misnomer as a reservation making SR17 PARTIAL; it lands on Format 9 statements too.

PARTIAL rather than DIVERGES, matching the adjudication's own SR23 calibration: on every statement the compiler DOES route to Format 9, both sentences are enforced completely and the diagnostic cites SR21 by name; the defect is that an illegal statement can dodge the routing.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs:228-268 BindSetProgramPointer (:243 the receiver loop, :256 the sender), reached from :54-57 (a ProgramPointer first target with a NULL/SELF/SUPER sender) and :339-340 (BindSetTo's category re-route, which fires when EITHER side is a program-pointer); the ENTRY sender variant is :274-313 BindSetEntry (:285 the same receiver screen). Grammar: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:1223 setEntryStatement.

notes:
kb/Work/PB389.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "If identifier-7 references a restricted program-pointer, identifier-8 shall be the predefined address NULL"` -> OK, Syntax rules 22) (FORMAT 9).

THE RULE'S PRECONDITION CANNOT BE MET. MEASURED (probe f5_pp_restricted, --std 2002 and --std 2023, identical): `01 PP1 USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER TO PROTO-A.` -> `error COBOLNET0899: data item 'PP1': USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER TO program-prototype-name (ISO 13.18.60 GR25)`. The grammar accepts the phrase (a deliberate superset parse) and the binder refuses it, so no program can declare a restricted program-pointer and identifier-7 can never reference one. Both of SR22's obligations - the NULL-or-a-program-pointer restriction on identifier-8, and the same-signature test over the two associated program-prototypes - are therefore unimplemented and untestable.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH NAMING FOR THE LANDER: the UNRESTRICTED half of Format 9 is fully live (see SR-14.9.39.3-21, CONFORMS), so the only thing standing between this rule and an implementation is the prototype registry. When that lands, SR22's signature test and SR20's identical sentence for function-prototypes are the SAME check over two carriers - one rule, one place - and should not be written twice.

HARM: legal COBOL-2002+ is rejected, loudly and by name, so nothing is silent. This is a section 13.18.60 GR25 declaration gap that strands SR22, not a SET defect.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): The restricted form is refused at DECLARATION: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4:455-457 `programPointerUsage : PROGRAM_POINTER (TO cobolWord)?` parses it, and the binder stages it loud as COBOLNET0899 ('USAGE PROGRAM-POINTER TO program-prototype-name (ISO 13.18.60 GR25)'). Nothing in SetBinder.BindSetProgramPointer (SetBinder.cs:228-268) or BindSetEntry (:274-313) tests a restriction or a signature; no program-prototype registry exists (the code comments call it 'P13').

notes:
kb/Work/PB449.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Identifier-9 shall be of category data-pointer"` -> OK, Syntax rules 23) (FORMAT 10).

THE SCREEN EXISTS AND IS ORDER-DEPENDENT - one rule, two verdicts, decided by which operand happens to be written first. MEASURED at --std 2002 and --std 2023, identical:
- POINTER FIRST: `SET P1 WS-N UP BY 4` -> `COBOLNET0869: 'WS-N': a SET UP/DOWN BY receiver mixed with data-pointers (ISO 14.9.39 SR23) shall be a USAGE POINTER data item` (probe g5_mixed_upby). Correct, and it even cites SR23.
- NON-POINTER FIRST: `SET WS-N P1 UP BY 4` - the SAME two operands, swapped - compiles with ZERO diagnostics and throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException 'arithmetic into a non-fixed-point target P1' at run time (probe h6_rev_mixed_upby). The sniff at PtrBinder.cs:170 reads drefs[0], sees a numeric item, returns null, and the whole statement falls into the Format-2 index path where SetTargetOf accepts any resolvable receiver.
- The legal lane works: `SET P1 UP BY 4` after `SET P1 TO ADDRESS OF R1` runs (g1_ptr_upby), and the 2002 introduction gate fires below it - at --std 85 the same program draws COBOLNET0900 naming Format 10 (probe i5_ptr_at_85).

THIS IS THE SAME FIRST-OPERAND-SNIFF SHAPE THE FILE'S OWN COMMENT SAYS WAS FIXED FOR A DIFFERENT SYMPTOM. PtrBinder.cs:175-177 records kb/Work PB221 - 'RESOLVE to commit - the probe above only DISCRIMINATED the format ... made `SET P(XE) Q(XE) UP BY 4` diagnose COBOLNET0844 for Q and not for P: one statement, one rule, two verdicts, decided by which operand the format sniff happened to read'. That fix made the FIRST operand share the others' resolution; it did not make the format SELECTION consider more than the first operand, so the identical asymmetry survives one level up. The twin exists in the TO direction too: `SET WS-N P1 TO 4` compiles clean and crashes the same way (probe h7_rev_mixed_to), because BindSetTo's re-routes at SetBinder.cs:329-343 also read only tds[0] (and the sender, when it is a bare reference - which a literal is not).

PARTIAL rather than DIVERGES because on every statement the compiler DOES route to Format 10, SR23 is enforced completely and cites itself; the defect is that a legal-looking illegal statement can dodge the routing entirely. No spec-derived test covers either arm - tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/CobolPtrTests.cs exercises the GR18/GR19/GR20 value rules on the runtime carrier, not the operand category.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/PtrBinder.cs:163-188 TryBindSetUpDown - the FORMAT SNIFF at :169-171 (`if (host.Expr.IndexFieldOf(drefs[0]) is not null) return null; if (ctx.Refs.Probe(drefs[0]) is not { } sniff || sniff.Item.Pic?.Category is not PicCategory.Pointer) return null;`) reads ONLY drefs[0]; the SR23 screen at :180-185 then runs over drefs.Skip(1) via PtrResolvePointer. Fall-through target: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs:357-370 BindSetUpDown -> SetTargetOf.

subject: SET statement
notes:
kb/Work/PB389.md — Citation validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Identifier-9 shall not be a data-pointer restricted to a type described with the STRONG phrase"` -> OK, Syntax rules 24) (FORMAT 10).

THE RULE'S SUBJECT CANNOT BE DECLARED. The printed USAGE clause format carries `POINTER [ TO type-name-1 ]` (specs/ISO_COBOL.md section 13.18.60.2), and section D.9.2.2 rule 1 names that spelling as the way a restricted data-pointer is made (`cite.py --check D.9.2.2 "USAGE POINTER TO type-name-1"` -> OK). MEASURED (probe g4_ptr_to_type, --std 2002 and --std 2023, identical): `01 P1 USAGE POINTER TO T-A.` -> `COBOL0307: unexpected 'TO'. A period may be missing at the end of the previous sentence.` - a bare syntax error with a misleading hint, not a named refusal. With no restricted data-pointer declarable, identifier-9 can never be 'a data-pointer restricted to a type described with the STRONG phrase' and the rule has no input.

I CHECKED THE COMPLEMENT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT: the omission is in the USAGE grammar, not in a binder screen, so it is invisible to the dossier's 14.9.39 citation regex and to its 'SET' keyword derivation - neither the grammar block nor the source block returns CobolData.g4:445. `grep -n "POINTER (TO\|POINTER TO" src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4` returns only the PROGRAM-POINTER and FUNCTION-POINTER rules.

STRANDED SIBLINGS: the same missing phrase also strands SR19's second and third sentences (a sibling part's row - 'If identifier-5 references a restricted data-pointer ...'), so one grammar alternative is the whole cost. HARM: rejects legal COBOL-2002+ with an unnamed COBOL0307, which is worse than the 0899 staged-loud posture PROGRAM-POINTER TO and FUNCTION-POINTER TO get for the same shape - three sibling usages, two of them refused by name and one by a parse error.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4:445 - usageKeyword's alternative is the bare token `POINTER`, with no `(TO cobolWord)?` tail (contrast programPointerUsage at :455 and functionPointerUsage at :461, which both carry one). PicInfo.PointerItem (src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/PicInfo.cs:314-316) is a singleton with no restriction field, so the model cannot represent a restricted data-pointer either. No STRONG-phrase test appears anywhere in the SET path.

notes: kb/Work/PB457.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Data-name-2 shall reference a data item defined in the CAPACITY phrase of a dynamic-capacity-table format OCCURS clause." -> OK, Syntax rules 29). THE RULE IS REALIZED AS A FORMAT SELECTOR, NOT AS A SCREEN, AND THAT IS THE RIGHT ARCHITECTURE: Format 14's three shapes (TO / UP BY / DOWN BY) are letter-for-letter Format 1's and Format 2's, so the ONLY thing that can pick Format 14 is 'is this receiver a CAPACITY register'. DynTryBindSetCapacity asks exactly that and returns null otherwise, leaving the Format-1/2 path alone. MEASURED WORKING for the flat shape (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr29_flat_ok.cob and the shipped golden conformance:2014/dyn_capacity_set): `05 E PIC 9(3) OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN C0 FROM 1 TO 5.` + `SET C0 TO 4.` gives CAP=[ 4]; a non-register target with the same shape stays Format 2 (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr29_noncap_target.cob, `SET N UP BY 3.` -> N=0008); two receivers where the first is a register is COBOLNET1524; and 13.18.38 SR30 (DataBinder.Odo.cs:283-289 -> COBOLNET1523) forbids a duplicate register name, which is what makes the FLAT name dictionary safe. Edition gate MEASURED: --std 2002 rejects the OCCURS DYNAMIC clause with COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014', --std 2014 and 2023 compile. Annex A.4.4 makes dynamic capacity tables an OPTIONAL module, but this compiler IMPLEMENTS it, so it is required conformance here and no documented-non-support disposition (PB260/PB261/PB281-PB283) applies. NOT CONFORMS, BECAUSE THE SELECTOR HAS A MEASURED BLIND SPOT. CapacityRegisterFor demands `r.HasNoSuffix` AND a BuildTablePath that is null whenever an ancestor is itself a table, and the register is deliberately kept off ByName/Roots (DataBinder.Odo.cs:264-269), so a dynamic table NESTED inside another table has a CAPACITY register no reference can reach. 8.5.1.9.1 item 3 explicitly permits that nesting - 'it may be defined in any place, other than the file section, in which a fixed-capacity table may be defined and may be nested in any combination to the same number of levels as a fixed-capacity table'. MEASURED at --std 2023: with `05 OUT-E OCCURS 3 TIMES. 10 IN-E PIC 9(3) OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN C2 FROM 1 TO 5.`, both `SET C2 (2) TO 4.` (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr29_nested_in_fixed_sub.cob - the SUBSCRIPTED form 8.4.2.3 requires to say WHICH occurrence's capacity) and the bare `SET C2 TO 4.` (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr29_nested_in_fixed_bare.cob) are rejected with `COBOLNET1639: 'C2' is not defined - no declaration in this source element gives the name 'C2'` - a statement that is simply false, since C2 is defined by the OCCURS entry. The same for a dynamic table nested in a dynamic table (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr29_nested_in_dynamic.cob), where the OUTER register C1 works and the inner C2 does not. So SR29's 'data item defined in the CAPACITY phrase' is honoured for a proper subset of the data items the phrase can define. The root is shared with every other reference to such a register (MOVE C2 (2) TO ED fails identically), so the fix belongs in ReferenceResolver/DataBinder.Odo, not in SetBinder.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/ReferenceResolver.cs#CapacityRegisterFor (:846-855 - `r.HasNoSuffix && r.BaseName ... && BuildTablePath(capTable) is { } capPath`) driving src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs#DynTryBindSetCapacity (:377-391); registration at src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Odo.cs:280-291

notes: kb/Work/PB458.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Integer-1 shall be nonnegative and, if TO is specified, integer-1 shall be not less than the minimum capacity defined in the corresponding OCCURS clause and not greater than the expected capacity, if specified." -> OK, Syntax rules 30). (The trailing 'FORMAT 15' in the catalog's rule text is a section-heading bleed from the extraction, not part of the rule.) THE OPERAND TERMS ARE PINNED IN THE SPEC: 13.18.38.4 GR16 'Integer-4 is the minimum capacity of the table' and GR17 'Integer-5 is the expected capacity' - i.e. the OCCURS DYNAMIC FROM and TO phrases. This is a SYNTAX rule about the LITERAL alternative integer-1, so all three bounds are decidable at compile time. NOTHING IMPLEMENTS ANY OF THE THREE. DynTryBindSetCapacity never looks at the amount at all - it binds it as an ordinary index-window expression and hands it to BoundSetCapacity; a grep of the pinned tree for a 14.9.39.3 SR30 citation finds nothing (the only SR30 citation near this code is 13.18.38 SR30, the duplicate-register-name rule, which is a different rule in a different clause). MEASURED at --std 2023 against `05 WS-E PIC 9(3) OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN WS-CAP FROM 2 TO 10.` (minimum 2, expected 10), every case compiling CLEAN with exit 0 and no diagnostic: `SET WS-CAP TO 1.` (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr30_to_below_min.cob) - below the minimum, silently CLAMPED at run time to CAP=[ 2]; `SET WS-CAP TO 20.` (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr30_to_above_expected.cob) - above the expected capacity, accepted outright, CAP=[ 20]; `SET WS-CAP TO -1.` (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr30_to_negative.cob) - negative, clamped to CAP=[ 2]; `SET WS-CAP UP BY -3.` (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr30_upby_negative.cob) -> CAP=[ 2] and `SET WS-CAP DOWN BY -3.` (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr30_downby_negative.cob) -> CAP=[ 5], i.e. a negative integer-1 silently INVERTS the direction of the statement. The legal control `SET WS-CAP TO 7.` gives CAP=[ 7], and with no TO in the OCCURS clause `SET WS-CAP TO 99.` gives CAP=[ 99] (correct - the expected-capacity half of SR30 is conditioned on the TO phrase being specified). WHY THE RUNTIME CLAMP IS NOT THE RULE: 14.9.39.4's Format-14 general rules make the clamp and the EC-BOUND-SET signal the answer for a COMPUTED arithmetic-expression-4; SR30 is the separate, compile-time answer for the LITERAL integer-1, and a literal 20 against an expected capacity of 10 is a program the compiler is required to diagnose. Silent under-rejection today, with the DOWN BY / UP BY sign inversion the most user-visible symptom. Edition gate MEASURED as for SR29 (COBOLNET0900 at --std 2002; clean at 2014 and 2023).  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs#DynTryBindSetCapacity (:377-391 - the amount goes straight to host.Expr.BindIndexWindowExpr with no literal screen) and src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/SetEmitter.cs#EmitSetCapacity (:94-102, the runtime SetCapacity/CapacityUpBy/CapacityDownBy calls that clamp instead)

notes: kb/Work/PB453.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "If FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO or NEAREST-TO-ZERO is specified, identifier-14 shall reference a numeric data item" -> OK, Syntax rules 31). NO SET FORMAT 15 EXISTS ANYWHERE. src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:1184-1195 lists ten setStatement alternatives and none of them begins `SET CONTENT`; a tree-wide grep for `SET CONTENT`, `setContent`, `CONTENT OF`, FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO, NEAREST-TO-ZERO, FLOAT-INFINITY, FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER and FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER-SIGNALING finds NO grammar rule, NO binder and NO emitter - the words occur only as rows in src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs (so they are reserved, and therefore not usable as user words either) and, for IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE, as the name of the unrelated 15.43/15.58/15.83 intrinsic-argument screen. MEASURED at --std 2023 and --std 2014: every Format-15 shape is a RAW PARSE ERROR, not a staged not-implemented diagnostic. `SET CONTENT OF N TO FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO.` with `01 N PIC S9(4).` (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/f15_farthest_numeric.cob) -> `COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'SETCONTENT'` + `cannot parse construct near 'CONTENT'` + `unexpected 'TO'` + `unexpected '.'`, exit 65; the SIGN form (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/f15_farthest_sign.cob) and the IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE form (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/f15_nearest_range.cob) add `missing token before 'SIGN'` / `missing token before 'IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE'`; identical at --std 2014 (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/f15_farthest_numeric_2014.cob). So the whole format is REJECTS-LEGAL-SOURCE, and the rejection violates the project's own loud-staging doctrine: a recognized but unimplemented construct is COBOLNET0899/COBOLNET1518 naming the feature, never a four-diagnostic COBOL0001 cascade the user cannot act on. SR31 ITSELF - 'identifier-14 shall reference a numeric data item', plus a) and b), which require the SIGN phrase whenever the item's positive and negative extremes differ in absolute value - has no code site, and neither has its violation: scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/f15_sr31_nonnumeric.cob (`SET CONTENT OF X TO FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO.` with X PIC X(4)) fails with the same parse cascade, so the compiler cannot distinguish the illegal program from the legal one. EDITIONS: SPEC-DERIVED, not read from a per-edition rule text - Annex E.2's list of words newly reserved in 2023 does NOT contain FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO, NEAREST-TO-ZERO, IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE, SIGN, FLOAT-INFINITY or the NaN words, so Format 15 predates 2023, and its floating-point siblings arrived with the ISO/IEC 60559 standard floating-point usages of 2014; recorded 2014,2023. Format 15 appears in NO Annex A.4 optional module, so it is required conformance - no documented-non-support disposition (PB260/PB261/PB281-PB283) covers it.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#setStatement (:1184-1195 - the ten-alternative dispatch has no numeric-content arm); no binder or emitter site exists

notes: kb/Work/PB458.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Data-name-3 shall reference a dynamic-length elementary data item." -> OK, Syntax rules 33). THE EXPLICIT ARM CONFORMS; THE BARE ARM HAS A MEASURED TWO-ARM HOLE. EXPLICIT SIZE OF: BindSetSize resolves the receiver and refuses a non-dynamic-length one at COMPILE time. MEASURED (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr33_nondyn_sizeof.cob and scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr33_numeric_sizeof.cob): `SET SIZE OF X TO 2.` with `01 X PIC X(8).` and the same with `01 N PIC 9(4).` -> `error COBOLNET1568: SET SIZE OF 'X': data-name-3 shall be a dynamic-length elementary item (ISO 14.9.39 Format 16 SR33)`, exit 70. The legal case runs: scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr33_ok_sizeof.cob gives D=[AB] L=2 for `01 D PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH LIMIT IS 8.` after `SET SIZE OF D TO 2.` Edition gate MEASURED: --std 2014 rejects it with COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2023', matching Annex E.3 item 17 ('Dynamic-length elementary items. The SET statement was enhanced to allow the setting of the length of a dynamic-length elementary item') - so this row is 2023 only, and it is SPEC-DERIVED. THE BARE (SIZE-OF-ABSENT) ARM, which the same format permits because `[ SIZE OF ]` is a bracket, is selected by DynTrySetSize, and its first guard is `if (targets.Count != 1 || targets[0].dataReferenceSuffix().Length != 0) return null;`. That guard is aimed at subscripts, but dataReferenceSuffix also carries QUALIFICATION, so a qualified dynamic-length item never reaches the dynamic-length peek. MEASURED (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr33_qualified_bare.cob): `01 G. 05 D PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH LIMIT IS 8.` + `SET D OF G TO 2.` compiles CLEAN at --std 2023 (no diagnostic, no COBOLNET1568, no COBOLNET0900) and dies at run time with `NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: arithmetic into a non-fixed-point target 'D'` - the statement fell through to the Format-1 numeric store. The isolating control proves it is the guard and not the qualification: scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr33_qualified_sizeof.cob, the SAME program with the explicit `SET SIZE OF D OF G TO 2.`, runs and prints D=[AB] L=2. One rule, two arms, one written (feedback_two_arm_dispatch). Unqualified bare form is fine (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr33_ok_bare.cob -> L=3). NOT A GAP: a dynamic-length item in a TABLE is not reachable at all, but legitimately - 13.16.3 SR18 forbids OCCURS beside DYNAMIC LENGTH and the compiler says so (COBOLNET1563, probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr33_table_bare.cob), so the subscript half of the guard has nothing legal to exclude and the qualification half is pure loss.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs#BindSetSize (:402-415 - the explicit SIZE OF arm, `if (!p.Item.IsDynamicLength) ... COBOLNET1568`) and #DynTrySetSize (:421-431 - the bare arm, whose `targets[0].dataReferenceSuffix().Length != 0` guard drops a QUALIFIED reference)

notes: kb/Work/PB458.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Integer-2 shall be non-negative, and shall be equal to or less than the maximum size of data-name-3" -> OK, Syntax rules 34). (The trailing 'FORMAT 17' in the catalog's rule text is a section-heading bleed from the extraction, not part of the rule.) NO COMPILE-TIME SCREEN EXISTS FOR EITHER HALF, AND THE SUBSTITUTE IS THE WRONG RULE. MEASURED at --std 2023 with `01 D PIC X DYNAMIC LENGTH LIMIT IS 8.` (13.18.19.4 GR2 makes integer-1 the maximum number of characters, so the 8.5.1.10.1 maximum size here is 8): `SET SIZE OF D TO -1.` (probe scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr34_negative.cob) compiles clean, exit 0, and the run leaves L=0; `SET SIZE OF D TO 99.` (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr34_over_limit.cob) compiles clean and leaves L=8; the bare form is the same (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr34_over_limit_bare.cob, L=8). The legal boundary case is right (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr34_at_limit.cob, `TO 8` -> L=8) and an item with NO LIMIT phrase accepts 99 (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set2/sr34_no_limit.cob, L=99), which is correct because 13.18.19.4 GR2 then makes the maximum implementor-defined. WHY THE RUNTIME CLAMP IS NOT A DEFENCE, and this is the precise point: 14.9.39.4 GR38 says (cite.py OK) 'If integer-2 is specified, the length of data-name-3 is set to integer-2, otherwise the length of data-name-3 is set to either arithmetic-expression-5, or, if arithmetic-expression-5 evaluates to a number that is greater than the maximum size of data-name-3, the length ... is set to the maximum size allowed and an EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL exception condition is set to exist.' The clamp-and-signal branch is written for arithmetic-expression-5 ONLY; for integer-2 GR38 is unconditional, BECAUSE SR34 has already guaranteed the literal is in range at compile time. The same split appears in GR37 for the negative case. So the compiler is applying the arithmetic-expression general rules to the literal alternative in place of the syntax rule it never implemented - a program the standard requires it to reject silently gets a different length instead. Edition 2023 only, MEASURED (COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2023' at --std 2014) and SPEC-CONFIRMED by Annex E.3 item 17.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs#BindSetSize (:402-415) and #DynTrySetSize (:421-431) - the amount is bound by host.Expr.BindIndexWindowExpr and the limit is carried to RUNTIME as BoundSetSize(p, amount, p.Item.DynLengthLimit, checkStorage); no literal screen at either site

notes: kb/Work/PB459.md — FORMATS 1 AND 2 — "Index-names are associated with a given table by being specified in the INDEXED BY phrase of the OCCURS clause for that table" (cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 PASS). The association IS recorded, but in ONE direction only: table → index-names (`DataItem.IndexNames`, filled at DataBinder.cs:2784), and SEARCH is its only consumer (SearchBinder.cs:28/38/45/87/110 read `table.IndexNames`). There is NO index-name → table map. `DataBinder.IndexFields` (DataBinder.cs:136) is name → C# `long` cell and carries nothing else, and SetBinder.SetTargetOf hands the emitter a `SetIndexTarget(ix.IndexField)` — a bare long with no table identity — so inside §14.9.39.4, the clause this rule exists to serve, "that table" cannot be named. Every Format-1/Format-2 consequent that depends on it is therefore absent: the "outside the limit specified in General rule 2 of 13.18.38" range test of GR2a1b / GR2a3b / GR4a (this part's siblings — GR-14.9.39.4-L2.* and GR-14.9.39.4-4 are in part 5) has NO raise site anywhere; EC-RANGE-INDEX occurs in src/ only as a >>FLAG-02 e TRIGGER (FlagConformancePass.cs:526-540) and as a catalog row (ExceptionCatalog.cs:162), never as a raise. MEASURED with the pinned compiler: probe p4_gr1_assoc — `SET IX1 TO IX2` with IX2=4, IX1 on a 5-element table and IX2 on a 9-element one, copies 4 with no check; probe p4_gr1_wrongtable — `MOVE 77 TO E2(IX1)`, IX1 being T1's index used to subscript T2, compiles and runs clean, so the association is not enforced at the subscript site either (Annex D:37407 states the concept: "An index-name may be used to reference only the table to which it is associated via the INDEXED BY phrase"). The §3.5 model — an index IS its 1-based occurrence number — makes GR2a3a's "same table ⇒ content placed unchanged" and GR2a3c's "different table ⇒ the corresponding occurrence number" the SAME machine operation, so the association is not needed for the VALUE; it is the RANGE half that the missing reverse map forecloses. Recorded PARTIAL rather than CONFORMS: the datum exists, the §14.9.39 consumer cannot reach it. See finding S4-A.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:2781-2789 (the INDEXED BY registration — `item.IndexNames.Add(idxName)` beside `_indexFields[idxName] = "_IX_"+n`) + src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Model/DataItem.cs:222 (`IndexNames`) + src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs:435-438 (SetTargetOf → SetIndexTarget(cell))  || EDITIONS (verbatim from the adjudication): 1985,2002,2014,2023

subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work/PB459.md — Citations validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 "If the value of arithmetic-expression-1 does not result in an integer" -> OK (General rules 2, the Format-1 body this row is an L-split of), plus "the EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT exception condition is set to exist", "the EC-RANGE-INDEX exception condition is set to exist" and "the content of the receiving operand is unchanged" -> all OK. ARM (a) IS THE DEFECT AND IT NEEDS NO IMPLEMENTOR LATITUDE TO REACH. When arithmetic-expression-1 does not result in an integer the standard demands three things at once: EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT set to exist, the execution of the SET statement UNSUCCESSFUL, and the content of the receiving operand UNCHANGED. MEASURED at --std 2023 (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set-p5/l21a-frac-ec) with '>>TURN EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT CHECKING ON' explicitly in force, `01 WS-F PIC 9V9 VALUE 2.5.`, `SET IDX TO 1. SET IDX TO WS-F.` -> exit 0, no exception, AFTER=[B] and OCC=0002: the fractional value was truncated to 2 and STORED. EXPECTED FROM THE SPEC: the statement fails, IDX still refers to occurrence 1, AFTER=[A], and the fatal EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT is raised (Table 13 lists it Fatal, and the runtime already has the raiser -- src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Exceptions/ExceptionState.cs:409 SubscriptError -- which the subscript path calls and the SET path never does). Repeated with a constant expression (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set-p5/l21a-noninteger, `SET IDX TO 5 / 2` under '>>TURN EC-ALL CHECKING ON') -> same silent 2. The control with checking OFF (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set-p5/l21a-frac-noec) gives the identical OCC=0002, which is licensed at that setting (14.6.13.1.1 NOTE 3) and is the proof that the TURN directive changes nothing here -- the check does not exist in either state. notes: kb/Work/PB400.md — Citations validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 "The status of each external switch associated with the specified mnemonic-name-1 is modified" -> OK (General rules 5); cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 "Mnemonic-name-1 shall be associated with an external switch, the status of which may be altered." -> OK (Syntax rules 5). THE RULE IS WRITTEN AS A CLAIM ABOUT THE READ SIDE, not about a stored bit: the switch is modified 'such that the truth value resultant from evaluation of a condition-name associated with that switch will reflect an on status if the ON phrase is specified, or an off status if the OFF phrase is specified', pointing at 8.8.4.6. So the rule is only satisfied if the SET and the switch-status condition share ONE state -- and they do: EmitSetSwitches writes ExternalSwitches.Set(name, on) and the condition reads the same run-unit SwitchStore keyed by the IMPLEMENTOR switch-name (SetAlterBinder.SwitchBindSet resolves the mnemonic through DataBinder.Switches SwitchMnemonics to that implementor name before the store is ever touched), so a second mnemonic for the same switch, or a condition-name declared in another program of the run unit, sees the SET. Scope is the run unit, matching 12.3.7 GR4 NOTE 1, and the store is an instance on RunUnit. The round trip proves the harm: MOVE ALL "*" TO WS-A then IF A-ALLSTAR displays TEST-ARM-TRUE, but SET A-ALLSTAR TO TRUE then IF A-ALLSTAR displays ROUNDTRIP-FALSE -- the one statement whose purpose is to make the condition true makes it false, silently, exit 0. The general format (§14.9.39.2 Format 7, rendered figure + figure notes) is `SET { ADDRESS OF data-name-1 | identifier-5 } … TO identifier-6` — the `…` repeats the whole receiving BRACE, so one or more receivers, freely mixed between the two spellings. The grammar splits the format into two fixed single-receiver alternatives and the plural/mixed shapes have no production. MEASURED with the pinned compiler at --std 2002: probe p4_gr12_multi_ptr, `SET P1 P2 TO ADDRESS OF BUF.` → `COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'SETP1P2TOADDRESS'` + `cannot parse construct near 'ADDRESS'`; probe p4_gr12_mixed, `SET ADDRESS OF C1 P1 TO P0.` → `COBOL0001: unexpected 'P1'`. Both are LEGAL: identifier-6 may be a data-address-identifier — §8.4.3.1.2 Format 9 lists data-address-identifier-1 as an identifier format, and §8.4.3.11.4 GR1 says "Data-address-identifier creates a unique data item of class pointer and category data-pointer" (cite.py --check 8.4.3.11.4 PASS), which is exactly what SR17's "Identifier-6 shall be of category data-pointer" (cite.py --check 14.9.39.3 PASS) requires; §8.4.3.11.3 SR5 bars it only as a RECEIVING operand. The plural receiver list DOES work in the one spelling that escapes this rule — probe p4_gr12_multi_ptr_ident, `SET P1 P2 TO P0.` with a plain data-pointer sender, parses as setToValueStatement, re-routes at SetBinder.cs:336-337 into BindSetPointer and stores into both in order (verified by reading P2 back through a BASED item: prints C1=W). So the ORDER-and-EACH semantics are right wherever the statement parses; what diverges is the set of statements that parse. Expected from the spec: `SET P1 P2 TO ADDRESS OF BUF` compiles and leaves both pointers addressing BUF. See finding S4-C.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:1261-1265 (setAddressStatement — alternative 2 is `SET dataReference TO ADDRESS OF dataReference`, ONE receiver where the format's ellipsis repeats the brace) + src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/PtrBinder.cs:52-58 (the sender form binds `[tp]`, a single-element target list) + src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs:186-223 (BindSetPointer — the plural path, reachable only through setToValueStatement)

notes: kb/Work/PB465.md — FORMAT 10 — "If arithmetic-expression-3 does not evaluate to an integer, the EC-SIZE-ADDRESS exception condition is set to exist, the execution of the SET statement is unsuccessful, and the content of identifier-9 is unchanged" (cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 PASS). All three consequents hold, and the rule is read as a VALUE rule (2.0 at scale 1 is an integer and moves by 2) rather than a spelling rule, which is what the sentence says. MEASURED at --std 2002: probe p4_gr19_nonint — `SET P TO ADDRESS OF BUF.` then `SET P UP BY A.` with `A PIC 9V9 VALUE 2.5`, checking OFF — rebasing a BASED PIC X(1) onto P afterwards reads `C=A`, i.e. offset 0, the pointer UNCHANGED (a truncating cast would have left it at offset 2). Probe p4_gr19_turn, the same program with `>>TURN EC-SIZE-ADDRESS CHECKING ON`, terminates with `EC-SIZE-ADDRESS (fatal): SET pointer UP/DOWN BY a non-integer amount (ISO 14.9.39 Format 10 GR19)`. The unit test pins both arms plus the integral-at-scale case with spec-computed expectations. ⛔ Contrast this row with GR-14.9.39.4-3: the identical rule shape on the INDEX side (Format 2, EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT) has no integrality test at all — same statement family, two arms, one finished. || REFUTED: DIVERGES — OVERTURNED. GR19's condition is exactly "arithmetic-expression-3 does not evaluate to an integer". CobolPtr.UpByReal (CobolPtr.cs:152-161) tests `!double.IsFinite(by) || by != Math.Truncate(by) || by < long.MinValue || by > long.MaxValue` and raises EC-SIZE-ADDRESS with the message "a non-integer amount" for ALL of them, so a MAGNITUDE guard is folded into GR19's raise. An amount of 1.0E19 or 1.0E30 held in a FLOAT-LONG item IS an integer value; GR19's condition is FALSE; EC-SIZE-ADDRESS must not be set - yet the run unit terminates fatally under `>>TURN EC-SIZE-ADDRESS CHECKING ON`, and with checking OFF the statement silently applies GR19's "unsuccessful ... unchanged" outcome to a case GR19 does not govern. The rule the standard supplies for this case is GR20 - "If this new address is outside the range of values allowed by the implementor for a data-pointer data item, the EC-RANGE-PTR exception condition is set to exist and the value of the data item referenced by identifier-9 is unchanged" - a DIFFERENT exception-name; and this implementation documents its own data-pointer range as UNBOUNDED (CobolPtr.cs:66-72: "The implementor data-pointer range is UNBOUNDED ... EC-RANGE-PTR is never raised at SET time"), under which no condition should be set at all and the pointer should simply move. Under either reading the EC that fires is the wrong one, so this is a wrong answer on legal COBOL, not a missing branch. 14.6.13.1.1's multiple-condition latitude does not cover it: only ONE condition is true here and the code sets the other. The note's "All three consequents hold, and the rule is read as a VALUE rule rather than a spelling rule" is true of UpByScaled and false of UpByReal - and the cited unit test could not have caught it, because UpByScaled_IsTheExactGr19ValueRule only ever calls CobolPtr.UpByScaled(p, 20|25, 1); it never touches UpByReal, the arm PtrEmitter.cs:82-92 selects for every native-float amount.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Control/CobolPtr.cs:96-112 (UpByScaled — `if (scaledBy % pow != 0) { ExceptionState.SizeAddressError(…); return p ?? ManagedPointer.Null; }` — the divisibility test IS the integrality test at the operand's own scale) + CobolPtr.UpByReal (the native-float amount arm, kb/Work PB151) + src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/PtrEmitter.cs:82-101 (the Real/scaled split that keeps the fraction alive to the runtime instead of casting it away) + src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Exceptions/ExceptionState.cs:380-390 (SizeAddressError)

Neither consequent happens; instead the bad value is coerced and APPLIED, so the table silently ends up at a capacity the program never asked for. MEASURED at --std 2014, both under `>>TURN EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT CHECKING ON`. Probe p4_gr29_neg — `05 D PIC 9(2) OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN CAP.`, `SET CAP TO 5.` then `SET CAP TO A.` with `A PIC S9(4) VALUE -3` — prints CAP1=5 then CAP2=0: the negative was carried into SetCapacity and clamped to the minimum, DESTROYING the five occurrences that existed. Probe p4_gr29_frac — the same with `A PIC 9V9 VALUE 3.5` — prints CAP2=3: truncated and applied, again shrinking the table. Expected from the spec in BOTH cases: the capacity stays 5 ("the execution of the SET statement is unsuccessful") and EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT is set to exist — Table 13 makes it Fatal, so with checking enabled the run unit takes the condition. ⛔ The GR30 clamp is being made to do GR29's job and cannot: GR30's minimum-capacity clamp is the rule for a LEGAL new capacity below the OCCURS minimum, whereas a negative or fractional arithmetic-expression-4 is rejected by GR29 BEFORE any new capacity is computed. This sits inside Annex A.4.4 Dynamic capacity tables (item 3, "SET statement, format 14: dynamic-capacity-table" — cite.py --check A.4.4 PASS), which docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 records as **Claimed**. FIVE of the six obligations are implemented and MEASURED at --std 2014 (probe p4_gr30_all over `05 E PIC 9(3) OCCURS DYNAMIC CAPACITY IN CAP FROM 2 TO 6`): a) TO — `SET CAP TO 4` → 4; b) UP BY — `SET CAP UP BY 2` → 6; c) DOWN BY — `SET CAP DOWN BY 100` → 2, the minimum clamp ("If the new capacity of the table is less than the minimum capacity defined in the corresponding OCCURS clause, the new capacity of the table shall be the minimum capacity"); "In all other cases, the new capacity of the table shall become the current capacity"; and "If the new capacity of the table is greater than the previous current capacity, new occurrences are created and are initialized as described in 8.5.1.9.5" (cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 PASS) — E(6), created by the UP BY, reads 000. The EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT arm also works: probe p4_gr30_limit, `SET CAP TO 1073741825` under `>>TURN EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT CHECKING ON`, terminates with the named condition and the message quotes GR30; the implementor maximum (1073741823) needs no user documentation — Annex A.1 items 60/61 say dynamic-capacity-table determinations "do not have to be documented". THE MISSING OBLIGATION is the expected-maximum arm: "otherwise, if an expected maximum capacity is specified for the table and the new capacity of the table exceeds that expected maximum capacity, the EC-BOUND-SET exception condition is set to exist" (cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 PASS). MEASURED: in p4_gr30_all, with the OCCURS carrying `TO 6` and `>>TURN EC-BOUND-SET CHECKING ON`, `SET CAP TO 9` yields CAP=9 (correct — the arm is nonfatal and the capacity does change) but FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS afterwards is all blanks, i.e. the condition was never set. `grep -rn EC-BOUND-SET src/` returns only the catalog row and the two comments conceding the gap. EC-BOUND-SET is item 1 of Annex A.4.4 (cite.py --check A.4.4 PASS) — the module docs/CONFORMANCE.md §5 marks **Claimed**, not Partial, so nothing itemizes this omission the way §4.2.7's second sentence requires. The comment's defence ("being nonfatal, it produces identical observable results with checking OFF") is true and beside the point: a program that TURNs the condition on, or lists it in a USE declarative, observes the difference, which is the only reason to enable it. See finding S4-F.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Tables/CobolDynTable.cs:115-139 (SetCapacity + CapacityUpBy/CapacityDownBy — the a)/b)/c) arms and the minimum clamp) + CobolDynTable.cs:88-113 (GrowTo — the EC-BOUND-TABLE-LIMIT arm with `return; // GR30: capacity unchanged`, and `for (int i = _count; i < newCount; i++) _store[i] = _seedAt(i + 1);` for the new occurrences) + src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Exceptions/ExceptionCatalog.cs:81 (EC-BOUND-SET — a catalog row, Nonfatal, with NO raise site in src/) + CobolDynTable.cs:94 (the code comment that concedes it: "EC-BOUND-SET on an explicit SET past the expected capacity (§14.9.39 GR30) stays a nonfatal staged follow-on")

subject: SET statement
notes: FORMAT 14 — "This statement shall not be executed during the execution of a SEARCH statement referring to the same table. If this rule is violated, the EC-FLOW-SEARCH exception condition is set to exist and the SET statement is not executed" (cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 PASS). Both consequents are implemented, and the guard is keyed on THE TABLE (a per-CobolDynTable counter), not on "a search is running", which is exactly the discrimination the rule's "referring to the same table" demands. Three edges measured beyond the existing golden. (1) SAME table, SEARCH ALL rather than serial — probe p4_gr31_all, `SEARCH ALL E … SET CAP TO 6` under `>>TURN EC-FLOW-SEARCH CHECKING ON`, terminates with `EC-FLOW-SEARCH (fatal): SET of a dynamic-capacity table's capacity during a SEARCH of that same table (ISO §14.9.39.4 GR31)`; both SEARCH forms share EmitSearch, so one bracket covers both. (2) DIFFERENT table — probe p4_gr31_other, two dynamic tables, `SEARCH E1 … SET C2 TO 6`, runs clean and C2 becomes 6, so the rule does NOT over-fire. (3) The checking-OFF disposition — conformance:2023/ec_flow_search_set_capacity (registered in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json) drives the fatal declarative + RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT path and asserts CAP-UNCHANGED, the value GR31's second sentence computes; it is spec-derived (its header quotes GR31 and derives the expectation from it, not from an oracle), so it closes this row. The try/finally means a SET reached from anywhere inside the scan — a PERFORMed paragraph, a declarative — is still guarded, and the `_searching` counter is nestable for a re-entrant SEARCH.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/Values/Tables/CobolDynTable.cs:115-127 (SetCapacity's `if (_searching > 0) { ExceptionState.FlowSearchError(…); return; }` — GR31's own "and the SET statement is not executed") + CobolDynTable.cs:170-175 (EnterSearch/ExitSearch, nestable) + src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/ControlFlowEmitter.cs:379-392 (EmitSearch wraps the scan in try/finally so ExitSearch runs on every `goto __searchEnd` exit path)

notes: kb/Work/PB452.md — FORMAT 15 (numeric-content) — "If FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO Is specified, the content of identifier-14 is set as follows: a) If the IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE phrase is not specified, the content is set to the value farthest away from zero permitted by the specifications of identifier-14 … b) … whichever is closer to zero … c) If the SIGN phrase is specified, the sign … otherwise … positive" (cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 PASS). No grammar surface at all. MEASURED: probe p4_gr32_content, `SET CONTENT OF N TO FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO.` over `01 N PIC S9(4)V99` → `COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'SETCONTENT'`, `cannot parse construct near 'CONTENT'`, `unexpected 'TO'`; probe p4_gr32_content_sign adds `IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE SIGN NEGATIVE` and fails the same way plus `missing token before 'IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE'` and `unexpected 'NEGATIVE'`. notes: kb/Work/PB452.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 "If FLOAT-INFINITY is specified, the content of identifier" -> OK (General rules 33). THE RULE: a Format-15 SET CONTENT OF sets identifier-14 to a canonical representation of infinity per ISO/IEC 60559:2020 Clause 3 for the basic interchange format corresponding to identifier-14's usage; the SIGN phrase decides the sign, else positive. Its syntax half is 14.9.39.3 SR32 (cite.py OK: 'identifier-14 shall reference a data item described with a standard floating-point usage') and the general format is 14.9.39.2 Format 15 (numeric-content) (cite.py OK). NOTHING IMPLEMENTS IT. NOWHERE. src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:1184 setStatement lists TEN alternatives (setLocale/setLastException/setSwitch/setEntry/setSize/setToValue/setBoolean/setAddress/setObjectReference/setIndex) and none of them is Format 15; there is no CONTENT token path, no SIGN phrase, no IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE phrase. The five value words exist ONLY as reserved-word rows (src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs:186/200/202/203/204/231/287) with no grammar or binder behind them; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/SetBinder.cs:24 BindSet has no arm to reach. Not a named documented-non-support diagnostic; not a version gate; a syntax error on legal 2014+ source. The receiving usage the rule needs IS supported -- `01 WS-F USAGE FLOAT-BINARY-64.` compiles in the same probe file, so this is not a missing receiver, it is a missing statement format. HARM: rejects legal source (a conforming 2014/2023 program cannot be compiled), and the rejection is a raw ANTLR cascade rather than a named diagnostic, so the user is told 'no viable alternative at input SETCONTENT' about a construct the standard defines. OWNERSHIP: no kb/Work note covers SET Format 15. notes: kb/Work/PB452.md — Citation validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 "the content is set to the nonzero value nearest to zero permitted by the specifications of identifier-14" -> OK (General rules 36). THE RULE has three legs: a) without IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE, identifier-14 takes the nonzero value nearest to zero its own data description permits (NOTE 2 says that value may lie outside the range of the arithmetic mode in effect); b) with IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE, it takes whichever is FARTHER from zero of that value and the value nearest to zero permitted by the mode of arithmetic; c) SIGN decides the sign, else positive. subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work/PB464.md — Citations validated: cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 "the length of data-name-3 is set to 0 and an EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL exception condition is set to exist" -> OK (General rules 37) and "the result of arithmetic-expression-5 is truncated to the nearest integer" -> OK (same rule). THE RULE IS TWO SENTENCES AND ONLY THE FIRST IS SETTLED. Sentence 1 (not a nonnegative number -> length 0 + EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL) is implemented at CobolDynString.cs:53-57 and is closed by a spec-derived golden: tests/conformance/2023/ec_storage_not_avail.cob drives WS-FRAC = -0.5 and WS-NEG = -1 under '>>TURN EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL CHECKING ON' and pins 'FRAC LEN=00 EC[EC-STORAGE-NOT-AVAIL...]' / 'NEG LEN=00 EC[...]' plus an in-range negative control that raises nothing -- and the fractional-negative case is the one that proves the ORDER is right (the sign test is on the evaluated value at full precision, before truncation, which is why SetEmitter.cs:119 renders the amount as a double rather than casting to long in generated code). Gating the raise on checkStorage is CORRECT, not a shortcut: 14.6.13.1.1 NOTE 3 (re-derived -- cite.py --check 14.6.13.1 FAILED and --find placed it at 14.6.13.1.1) says 'An exception condition is set to exist only if checking for that condition is enabled by default or by the TURN compiler directive.' SENTENCE 2 IS THE UNVERIFIED EDGE. The standard's words are internally in tension -- 'truncated to the NEAREST integer' -- and this is the phrase's ONLY occurrence in the whole document (grep of specs/ISO_COBOL.md), so there is no sibling use to calibrate it against. The code picks toward-zero truncation ((long)newLen at :65). MEASURED at --std 2023 (scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/probe/set-p5/gr37-nearest): with LIMIT 9 and a nine-character value, WS-A = 2.7 gives L(2.7)=02 and WS-B = 2.2 gives L(2.2)=02 -- so 2.7 truncates DOWN, where a 'nearest integer' reading would give 3.
