subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB352. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 1): 'The access mode of the file referenced by file-name-1 shall be either sequential or dynamic.' CODE: BindStart -- if (file.AccessMode == FileAccessMode.Random) ctx.Edition.Error('COBOLNET0862', ... 'the access mode shall be sequential or dynamic (ISO 14.9.41 SR1)'). FileAccessMode is {Sequential, Random, Dynamic}, so the single Random test is the exact complement of the rule's permitted pair, and FileModel.AccessMode DEFAULTS to Sequential -- a SELECT with no ACCESS clause (the implicit arm a check written against an explicit clause would miss) does not false-fire. ctx.Edition.Error is unconditional, so the diagnostic fires at every strictness and every edition, right for a rule with no edition delta.
PROBED on BOTH keyed organizations, because the check sits before the organization split and a one-organization probe would not have shown that: indexed ACCESS RANDOM (out-b1/probe/sr1-sr8) and relative ACCESS RANDOM (out-b1/probe/sr1-rel) each report COBOLNET0862 SR1.
ONE EDGE NOT REACHED, and it is benign: the check sits AFTER 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported(...)', so a sequential-organization file never reaches SR1. 12.4.5.2 admits only ACCESS SEQUENTIAL for sequential organization, so no conforming program can exercise that arm -- the hole is in the diagnostic for an already-illegal file control entry, and 12.4.5.2 owns it, not this rule.
TEST: NONE. grep for COBOLNET0862 across tests/ returns zero hits -- no negative fixture, no unit test -- so a green suite proves nothing about this row. conformance:2002/file_collating_seq exercises only the ACCEPT side (ACCESS DYNAMIC) and would still pass with this check deleted. Closing needs a negative fixture pinning COBOLNET0862 on ORGANIZATION INDEXED + ACCESS RANDOM + START, and its relative twin. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — The adjudicator's own note names an unreached edge -- the SR1 check sits AFTER 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported(...)' at KeyedIoBinder.cs:208, so a sequential-organization file never reaches it -- and then argues the edge away with a premise I MEASURED AND BROKE: 'no conforming program can exercise that arm ... 12.4.5.2 owns it, not this rule'. The premise is half right and the conclusion is wrong. Half right: I read the file control entry general formats (specs/ISO_COBOL.md 12.4.5.1) rather than trusting the paraphrase, and Format 3 (sequential) does carry only '[ ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL ]' -- ACCESS RANDOM on a sequential file is indeed not conforming. Wrong: nothing in this compiler diagnoses it. ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL + ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM + START SQF FIRST compiles CLEAN -- exit 0, prb.dll written, ZERO diagnostics -- so the rule that was supposed to own the hole owns nothing, and a program that violates SR1 ('the access mode of the file referenced by file-name-1 shall be either sequential or dynamic') is accepted in silence and becomes NotImplemented.Run at run time. SR1 is therefore enforced over two of the three organizations START can name and unenforced over the third; that is PARTIAL by the stated burden (an unverified edge => PARTIAL, and this one is worse than unverified -- it is verified to miss). I did NOT charge SR1 with the sequential-file rejection itself: that mechanism is already recorded as DIVERGES on SR-14.9.41.3-2, and if it is fixed the SR1 test, sitting below it, would start covering sequential files unchanged. What I charge is the CONFORMS claim, whose sole justification for the uncovered half was an escape hatch that does not exist. Everything else in the record I re-derived and it held: FileModel.cs:10 'enum FileAccessMode { Sequential, Random, Dynamic }' makes the single Random test the exact complement of the rule's permitted pair; FileModel.cs:54 'AccessMode { get; set; } = FileAccessMode.Sequential' makes the implicit arm safe; EditionContext.cs:109 'Error(...) => Diagnostics.Add($"{Prefix()}error {code}...")' is unconditional. Citation re-run and OK. Test-ref is empty, which is expected and not what moved the verdict.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB352. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 2): 'If the organization of the file referenced by file-name-1 is sequential, either the FIRST or the LAST phrase shall be specified.' The rule PERMITS START on a sequential-organization file -- it only constrains WHICH phrase. And the semantics are fully specified: 14.9.41.4 GR20/GR21 (--check, under the heading SEQUENTIAL FILES) -- 'If FIRST is specified, the file position indicator is set to 1 if records exist in the physical file' / 'If LAST is specified, the file position indicator is set to the record number of the last existing logical record in the physical file'; with no records, or no ability to position, status '23', the invalid key condition exists, the statement is unsuccessful.
CODE: BindStart -- 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported($"START on sequential-organization file '{name}' (ISO 14.9.41 SR2 FIRST/LAST positioning - a later slice)");'. FileModel.IsSequential covers Sequential AND LineSequential. TWO defects in one line: it rejects the ONLY form SR2 permits, and it names SR2 -- the rule that MAKES it legal -- as the authority for refusing it.
AND THE REFUSAL IS NOT A DIAGNOSTIC. BoundUnsupported is a runtime loud stage: StatementEmitter.Visit(BoundUnsupported) writes LoudStmt(n.Feature). PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr2-seq): an ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL file written with two records, reopened INPUT, then 'START SQF FIRST INVALID KEY ... NOT INVALID KEY ... END-START'. Compile output: EMPTY. Run: 'Unhandled exception. CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: ... START on sequential-organization file SQF'. SPEC-DERIVED EXPECTED: the START succeeds, WS-ST = '00', the NOT INVALID KEY imperative runs, and the following READ delivers the first record ('AAAAAAAAAA').
The edition gate cannot see it either -- VersionConformancePass fires on BoundKeyedStart, a node this path never constructs, so START FIRST on a sequential file is not even edition-checked.
EDITIONS: SR2's only satisfying forms are FIRST and LAST, which are absent from the COBOL-85 START format (the compiler gates them at 2002 via ConstructRegistry 'start-first-last-2002'), hence 2002+. Annex E of the 2023 text records no 14.9.41 change from 2014, so the 2023 clause is also the 2014 requirement; the pre-2014 split is not derivable from the 2023 text alone.
TEST: none.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB333; PB332. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 3): relational-operator 'is a relational operator specified in the general-relation format of 8.8.4.2, Simple relation conditions, with the exception of the relational operators IS NOT EQUAL TO or IS NOT='. The rule has TWO halves -- a positive membership test and a negative exception -- and I verified both.
THE 8.8.4.2 SET (read from the Format-1 diagram, --check on its figure note 'Each of the three brace groups requires exactly one of its enclosed alternatives; the brackets around NOT make it optional'): IS [NOT] GREATER THAN | IS [NOT] > | IS [NOT] LESS THAN | IS [NOT] < | IS [NOT] EQUAL TO | IS [NOT] = | IS <> | IS GREATER THAN OR EQUAL TO | IS >= | IS LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO | IS <=. THE [NOT] BRACKET SITS ON THE FIRST SIX ONLY -- 'NOT >=' and 'NOT LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO' are NOT alternatives of the general-relation format.
HALF THAT CONFORMS: BindStart maps the operator through ConditionBinder.MapOperator and reports COBOLNET0862 when it yields '!='. Probed (out-b1/probe/sr3-ne): all three not-equal spellings -- NOT EQUAL TO, NOT =, and <> -- are rejected.
HALF THAT DIVERGES: the START KEY phrase reuses CobolExpressions.g4 comparisonOperator WHOLE, and that rule carries four alternatives outside the general-relation format -- 'IS? NOT GTEQUAL', 'IS? NOT LTEQUAL', 'IS? NOT GREATER THAN? OR EQUAL TO?', 'IS? NOT LESS THAN? OR EQUAL TO?'. Nothing narrows it for START. Probed (out-b1/probe/sr3-ops): 'START IXF KEY IS NOT >= IX-KEY' and 'START IXF KEY IS NOT LESS THAN OR EQUAL TO IX-KEY' both compile and RUN (P2-OK ST=00, P3-OK ST=00), MapOperator silently folding them to '<' and '>'. SR3 requires rejection. UNDER-REJECTS. (The operator is also grammatically OPTIONAL where the format requires it -- recorded on FMT-14.9.41.2, same phrase, different mechanism.)
OBSERVATION, deliberately NOT filed as a defect: SR3's exception list names only 'IS NOT EQUAL TO' and 'IS NOT=', so the third not-equal spelling 'IS <>' is literally outside the exception and the compiler's rejection of it is over-strict against the letter of the rule. But 14.9.41.4 GR9 a)/b) and GR17 c)/d) enumerate EQUAL, GREATER, NOT LESS, GREATER OR EQUAL and LESS, NOT GREATER, LESS OR EQUAL -- '<>' is in neither list, so the standard defines no START behaviour for it and rejecting is the defensible reading. The gap is editorial in ISO/IEC 1989:2023, not a compiler defect.
RELATED, and satisfied: Annex A.3 item 39 (--check) makes 'the relational operators LESS, NOT GREATER, or LESS OR EQUAL in the START statement' processor-dependent; docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 39 CLAIMS them, so they must be accepted -- and are.
TEST: none (zero COBOLNET0862 hits across tests/).

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 4): 'Data-name-1 or record-key-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses.' The rule has two operand legs (indexed and relative) and they behave differently.
INDEXED LEG -- ENFORCED, but only as a SIDE EFFECT and reported under the WRONG RULE. RecordLayout.OffsetOf bails to null when the item or any ancestor carries OCCURS ('if (p.Occurs is not null) return null;   // subject to OCCURS => no single fixed position'), so KeyIndexByPosition returns null and BindStart emits COBOLNET0862 '<name> neither names a record key nor begins at the leftmost character position of one with a length not greater than that key (ISO 14.9.41 SR6)'. PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr4-occ) with '05 IX-KEY. 10 IX-ELEM PIC X(3) OCCURS 2 TIMES.' and 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-ELEM (1)': rejected with exactly that message. The source IS refused, so no illegal program compiles -- but the message asserts something FALSE about this operand: IX-ELEM(1) DOES begin at IX-KEY's leftmost character position and IS shorter than it. The rule actually violated is SR4; OffsetOf's null collapses two distinct rejection reasons into one sentence, and a user reading it would look for the wrong problem.
RELATIVE LEG -- NO CHECK AT ALL. BindStart's relative arm tests only ReferenceEquals(operand.Item, file.RelativeKeyItem) (that is SR5), which is TRUE for a SUBSCRIPTED reference to the same DataItem. PROBED (same file): with '01 WS-RKT. 05 WS-RK PIC 9(4) OCCURS 3 TIMES.' and 'RELATIVE KEY IS WS-RK', the statement 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK (2)' compiles with NO diagnostic. That shape is reachable only through a file control entry that already violates 12.4.5.13.3 SR1 (--check: 'Data-name-1 shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses') -- and KeyedIoBinder.KeyedValidateFile implements 12.4.5.13's SR2 (unsigned integer, no P) and SR3 (not within a record of the file) but NOT its SR1, so nothing anywhere in the chain diagnoses it. The two missing checks cover for each other.
UNDER-REJECTS. TEST: none.

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB236 (landed) left the REFUTED half open; see the residue paragraph in kb/Work/PB236.md. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.3 5): 'For relative files, data-name-1, if specified, shall be the data item specified in the RELATIVE KEY clause in the associated file control entry.' UNCHANGED AND STILL RIGHT: the reject arm (COBOLNET0862 naming the RELATIVE KEY item) and the accept arm both hold at 85/2002/2014/2023 and under --permissive, and the 'if specified' half falls through to GR8's implied EQUAL. WHAT PB236 CHANGED HERE, and it is the benign edge this row recorded and nothing more: an operand that failed NAME RESOLUTION used to short-circuit into an unreported BoundUnsupported before SR5 ran. The FILE-name half of that edge is closed -- START of an undeclared file is now COBOLNET1639 at bind (StatementValidation.ResolveFile), pinned by conformance:negative/pb236-open-undeclared-file's sibling family -- and the KEY-operand half no longer ships silently either: every BoundUnsupported is now announced at compile time as COBOLNET1756 from the single StatementBinder.BindStatement funnel, so an unresolvable START KEY operand can no longer compile without a word. STILL PARTIAL for the half the REFUTATION found, which is a different mechanism entirely: SR5 is tested by reference identity on the resolved DataItem, and Place.cs's `PlaceDecorator.Item => Inner.Item` makes that ask 'does this reference land on that storage' where SR5 asks 'is data-name-1 that data item'. `START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK(1:2)` still compiles clean (8.4.3.3.1: reference modification defines a UNIQUE data item) and reads the relative record number from the first two characters of the key's DISPLAY image -- a silent wrong answer; and a `66 WS-ALIAS RENAMES WS-RK` non-THRU alias still passes where its THRU sibling is correctly rejected. That is the Place-decorator identity question, not a staging one, and it is untouched here.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 6 and 6) b) 1.): for indexed files data-name-1 shall reference either a) a prime or alternate record key associated with file-name-1, or b) a data item whose 'leftmost character position WITHIN A RECORD OF THE FILE corresponds to the leftmost character position of a prime or alternate record key that is associated with file-name-1 and that is defined without the SOURCE phrase in the RECORD KEY clause or ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause'.
CODE: RecordLayout.KeyIndexByPosition(file, operand) -- 'if (OffsetOf(operand) is not { } off) return null; if (file.RecordKeyItem is { } pk && OffsetOf(pk) == off && operand.ImageWidth <= pk.ImageWidth) return -1;' then the same loop over file.AlternateKeys.
THE ACCEPT ARM CONFORMS and is deliberately position-based rather than name-based (12.4.5.12.4 GR4 makes the identical byte positions keys in EVERY record description of the file), so a REDEFINES of the key and a same-position item in a sibling 01 both match. It is pinned by a spec-derived test: conformance-test:KeyedOffsetSpecTests.Start_KeyOperandInSiblingRecord_MatchesByBytePosition, which asserts GOT=02 directly from the rule rather than against an oracle.
THE REJECT ARM DIVERGES. OffsetOf computes the offset inside the operand's OWN 01 root ('DataItem root = item; while (root.Parent is { } parent) root = parent;') and NOTHING checks that that root is a record description of file-name-1 -- or of any FD at all. So any item at offset 0 of any 01 anywhere in the program, no wider than the key, binds as a generic key of that file. PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr6-ws): '01 WS-OUTSIDE. 05 WS-PART PIC X(4). 05 WS-FILLER PIC X(20).' in WORKING-STORAGE, then 'START IXF KEY IS = WS-PART' against 'RECORD KEY IS IX-KEY' / '05 IX-KEY PIC X(6)' -- compiles CLEAN, binding keyIndex = -1 (the prime key).
And the acceptance is not merely a missing syntax check. KeyedIoEmitter.EmitStart then passes OperandText.AsString of that WORKING-STORAGE item as the comparison value, where 14.9.41.4 GR17 a) (--check) specifies 'The specified key is set up by moving the relevant parts of the RECORD AREA into a temporary data area' -- so the compiler emits a comparand the standard does not define for a statement it should have refused.
SR6 b) 1.'s 'defined without the SOURCE phrase' qualifier is vacuous in this compiler (no SOURCE surface -- see SR-14.9.41.3-7), so it is not a second defect here.
UNDER-REJECTS. TEST-REF LEFT EMPTY DELIBERATELY: the sibling-record test above covers only the accept arm and would still pass with the reject arm fixed, so naming it would misrepresent coverage.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3, printed path 6) b) 2.): 'It has the same class, category, and usage as that record key.' NOTHING CHECKS IT, and the omission is deliberate and self-documented -- RecordLayout.KeyIndexByPosition's own doc comment says '(SR6b.2's same-class/category/usage check is a pre-existing looseness kept as-is; the width-<= rule is SR6b.3.)'. The method tests OffsetOf equality and ImageWidth <= and nothing else; there is no class, category or usage comparison anywhere on the START key path.
PROBED, compile and run (out-b1/probe/l23-len and out-b1/probe/l22-run). Prime key '05 IX-KEY PIC X(6)' (class alphanumeric, category alphanumeric, usage display); sibling record '01 IX-REC3. 05 IX-NUM PIC 9(4) COMP-3.' (class numeric, category numeric, usage packed-decimal, ImageWidth 4 <= 6, offset 0 == the key's offset). 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-NUM' compiles with NO diagnostic. Run against a file holding keys '1234AA' and '9999ZZ', after MOVE 1234 TO IX-NUM, it reports 'L22-OK ST=00' and the following READ NEXT returns 1234AA. SR6 b) 2. forbids that operand outright; the compiler instead substitutes a VALUE CONVERSION (KeyedIoEmitter.EmitStart -> OperandText.AsString of the packed item) where the rule's whole premise is that the operand OVERLAYS the key's character positions. SILENT under-rejection with a wrong-answer tail: the same shape with a COMP or COMP-3 item whose rendered text does not coincide with the stored key characters compares the wrong bytes and reports no error.
ROW CONTEXT: this L-row and its sibling L2.3 are the nested-list rows kb/Work PB55 records under '14.9.41.3 L2' as scheduled for absorption into their parent rule after the defect burn-down; adjudicated here as the inventory presents them.
TEST: none.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB354. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3, printed path 6) b) 3.): 'Its length is not greater than the length of that record key.' CODE: RecordLayout.KeyIndexByPosition -- 'operand.ImageWidth <= pk.ImageWidth' for the prime key and the same test over each entry of file.AlternateKeys.
VERIFIED for the alphanumeric-display case (out-b1/probe/l23-len): prime key '05 IX-KEY PIC X(6)', sibling record '01 IX-REC2. 05 IX-LONG PIC X(9).' at the same offset 0, and 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-LONG' is REJECTED with COBOLNET0862 -- the longer operand does not bind. The accept side of the same threshold is covered by the shorter-operand case that KeyIndexByPosition's generic-key path serves.
PARTIAL, on two splits I could NOT verify:
(a) 14.9.41.4 GR13 distinguishes alphanumeric character positions from NATIONAL character positions for this length, and a national item cannot appear in a file record at all in this compiler -- probing '05 IX-NAT PIC N(3).' inside an FD record raises COBOLNET0899 'national data in a file record ... is recognized but not yet implemented - the record codec is single-byte and the national character is two bytes'. The national leg of the length comparison therefore has no implementation to verify, and the rule is enforced for only one of its two operand classes.
(b) ImageWidth is a DECLARED-image width (digits plus separate sign for a numeric usage, PIC length for alphanumeric), so once SR6 b) 2.'s class/category/usage identity goes unenforced (SR-14.9.41.3-L2.2) the two sides of this <= are not commensurable: a PIC 9(4) COMP-3 operand contributes 4 while occupying 3 bytes of packed storage. The rule holds soundly only where operand and key are both alphanumeric display.
ROW CONTEXT: an L-row of the kb/Work PB55 family (see SR-14.9.41.3-L2.2).
TEST: none.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB358. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 7): 'Record-key-name-1 shall be specified with the SOURCE phrase in the RECORD KEY clause or in the ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause in the file control entry for file-name-1.'
NO SURFACE ANYWHERE. I searched rather than trusting the dossier's silence: CobolIO.g4 carries 'recordKeyClause : RECORD KEY? IS? dataReference' and 'alternateKeyClause : ALTERNATE RECORD? KEY? IS? dataReference (WITH? DUPLICATES)? alternateKeySuppressWhen?' -- neither has a SOURCE phrase, and grep for record-key-name / SourcePhrase across src/ returns only the START grammar comment and the COLLATING SEQUENCE Format-2 comment. record-key-name-1 therefore cannot be DECLARED, so START's record-key-name-1 alternative (in the 14.9.41.2 brace group) is unreachable and SR7 has nothing to constrain. PROBED (out-b1/probe/sr7-source): 'RECORD KEY IS IX-COMPOSITE SOURCE IS IX-A IX-B' -> COBOL0312 'unexpected SOURCE. Unexpected token in FILE-CONTROL paragraph.'
THIS IS A SANCTIONED DECLINE, NOT A CONFORMANCE BREAK. Annex A.3 item 40 (--check): 'The capability of specifying the SOURCE phrase of the RECORD KEY clause and ALTERNATE RECORD KEY clause is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.' docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 40 already records the disposition: 'SOURCE phrase of RECORD KEY / ALTERNATE RECORD KEY | 13.x | Not claimed | The record-key-name SOURCE IS key form is not provided'.
I am NOT raising NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION: the disposition already exists, so the owner owns this row; converting it to DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT is the owner's call and never mine (D13). Note the decline is an A.3 PROCESSOR-DEPENDENT element, not an A.4 optional module, so the PB260/PB261/PB281-PB283 declined-module witness notes do not cover it.
WHAT IS STILL OWED EITHER WAY: the refusal is a GENERIC parser error, not a named diagnostic saying the SOURCE phrase is not provided, and no fixture pins it -- so nothing would notice if the grammar later accepted SOURCE and silently ignored it, which is exactly the silent-miscompile the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT closing bar guards against.
EDITIONS: the SOURCE phrase is absent from the COBOL-85 RECORD KEY clause; Annex E of the 2023 text records no 14.9.41 change from 2014, so 2014 and 2023 are certain and 2002 is the conventional third. TEST: none.

subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB352. RULE (--check 14.9.41.3 8): 'If the LENGTH phrase is specified, file-name-1 shall reference a file with indexed organization.' CODE: BindStart -- 'if (length is not null && file.Organization != FileOrganization.Indexed) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET0862", ... "the LENGTH phrase requires indexed organization (ISO 14.9.41 SR8)");'. The predicate itself is right (Indexed is the only permitted organization), but the STATEMENT IS UNREACHABLE for one of the two organizations it exists to exclude.
RELATIVE LEG VERIFIED (out-b1/probe/sr1-sr8): 'START RLF KEY IS = WS-RK WITH LENGTH 2' on ORGANIZATION RELATIVE reports COBOLNET0862 SR8.
SEQUENTIAL LEG NOT REACHED: the check sits AFTER 'if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported(...)'. In the SAME probe run, 'START SQF KEY IS = SQ-REC WITH LENGTH 2' on an ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL file produced ZERO diagnostics -- two syntax rules violated at once (SR8 and SR2) and neither reported; the statement becomes a runtime NotImplementedCobolFeatureException instead. I flipped the axis deliberately: probing only the relative case would have shown a green check for a rule half of whose domain is unenforced.
A SECOND UNREACHED PATH: 'if (kp is not null && operand is null) return new BoundUnsupported(...)' precedes the LENGTH check, so a START whose KEY operand fails name resolution also suppresses SR8.
EDITIONS: the WITH LENGTH phrase is absent from the COBOL-85 START format (gated at 2002 by ConstructRegistry 'start-with-length-2002' / COBOLNET0900); Annex E records no 14.9.41 change from 2014, so 2014 and 2023 are certain and the pre-2014 split is not derivable from the 2023 text alone.
TEST: none.

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB352. RULE: "The open mode of the file connector referenced by file-name-1 shall be input or I-O." (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 "The open mode of the file connector referenced by file-name-1 shall be input or I-O." -> OK §14.9.41.4 1)). The unsuccessful status is §9.1.13.7 item 7 (--check 9.1.13.7 "not open in the input or I-O mode" -> OK, item 7 = '47'). CODE: both keyed connectors open their START bodies with `if (!IsOpen || Mode is FileOpenMode.Output or FileOpenMode.Extend) return Status = FileStatusCode.ReadNotOpenForInput;` and FileStatus.cs:76 pins RecordNotFound='23' / ReadNotOpenForInput='47'. MEASURED (probe start-p2-i, relative DYNAMIC): OPEN OUTPUT -> FS=47, OPEN EXTEND -> FS=47, OPEN I-O -> FS=00; (probe start-p2-b T7, indexed) OPEN OUTPUT -> FS=47. WHY NOT CONFORMS: GR1 is stated before the RELATIVE FILES heading, so it governs SEQUENTIAL organization too, and that arm never reaches the check — KeyedIoBinder.BindStart L207-L210 turns `START <sequential-file> FIRST` into a BoundUnsupported, which COMPILES and then aborts the run unit with an unhandled CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException (probe start-p2-h). GR-14.9.41.4-20/-21 (part 3) own the primary rows for that arm; recorded here because it leaves one third of GR1's domain unhonoured. No spec-derived test exercises the '47' leg (KeyedIoDifferentialTests is DifferentialGolden.Assert against the legacy oracle and cannot close a row). || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 — GR1 has no edition marker in the clause and Annex E (the 2023-vs-2014 delta) lists no START change, so the rule reads identically at every edition the compiler targets.

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB352. RULE: "The execution of the START statement does not alter either the content of the record area or the content of the data item referenced by the data-name specified in the DEPENDING ON phrase of the RECORD clause…" (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 "does not alter either the content of the record area" -> OK §14.9.41.4 2)). CODE: EmitStart only READS — `OperandText.AsString(new BoundFieldOperand(sta.Operand!), num)` for the indexed key and `NumericRenderer.Align(num.FieldNum(sta.Operand!),0)` for the relative RRN — then stores the file status and runs the §9.1.14 branch; neither connector's Start/StartFirstLast writes back an image. MEASURED — BOTH HALVES: probe start-p2-g (relative, RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 4 TO 8 DEPENDING ON RLEN): after a SUCCESSFUL `START RLF FIRST` -> RLEN=08, REC=[ZZZZZZZZ] unchanged; after an UNSUCCESSFUL `START RLF KEY = RK` ('23') -> RLEN=07, REC=[YYYYYYY ] unchanged. probe start-p2-b (indexed): T1 REC-AREA=[ABZZCCCC] and T6 REC-AREA=[AB02ZZZZ] both survive the START verbatim. WHY NOT CONFORMS: the SEQUENTIAL-organization arm cannot execute at all — START on ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL compiles to a BoundUnsupported and throws NotImplementedCobolFeatureException at run time (probe start-p2-h), so GR2 is unhonoured there; GR-14.9.41.4-20/-21 in part 3 own that arm. No spec-derived covering test. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 1985 / 2002 / 2014 / 2023 — no edition marker in the clause; Annex E lists no START change.

notes: Two connectors on one indexed file with SHARING ALL OTHER + LOCK MODE AUTOMATIC: a START neither releases the holder's lock (the blocked read stays '51'), nor acquires one on the record it positioned at ('00'), nor detects one ('00' where the same connector's READ was refused '51').

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB352 (OPEN) after kb/Work PB236 (landed). RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR4): 'The execution of the START statement causes the value of the I-O status associated with file-name-1 to be updated.' RELATIVE + INDEXED HALF -- VERIFIED, unchanged: EmitStart emits SeqIo.EmitStoreFileStatus(file) on all three forms and every connector path assigns Status before returning. ONE OF THE TWO UNCOVERED SHAPES IS GONE: a relative file whose file control entry has no RELATIVE KEY clause used to bind to an unreported BoundUnsupported and abort the run unit without touching the I-O status; that program is now REJECTED AT BIND (COBOLNET0862, see GR-14.9.41.4-8), so there is no execution whose status could go un-updated -- GR4 is not violated by a statement that never runs. STILL PARTIAL for PB352's half, untouched here: the SEQUENTIAL-organization START. GR4 is stated before the RELATIVE FILES heading so it governs that START too, and 14.9.41.3 SR2 makes it legal with FIRST or LAST; KeyedIoBinder.BindStart still returns BoundUnsupported for file.IsSequential before any node is built, so the run unit aborts with the I-O status never touched (probe/seq-start/STPRB2.cob). It is no longer SILENT -- the deferral now announces itself as COBOLNET1756 at compile time -- but the FEATURE is unbuilt, which is the correct job for that carrier and is PB352's to build.

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB352. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR5): 'If, at the time of the execution of the START statement, the file position indicator indicates that an optional input file is not present, the invalid key condition exists and the execution of the START statement is unsuccessful.' The status value comes from 9.1.13.5 3b (cite.py --check 9.1.13.5 OK): 'a START or random READ statement is attempted on a file described as optional and the physical file is not present' => '23'. RELATIVE + INDEXED HALF — VERIFIED. Both connectors carry `if (OptionalAbsent) return StartFail();` in Start and `if (OptionalAbsent || <empty>) return StartFail();` in StartFirstLast; StartFail sets '23' + _fpiValid=false + LastReadUnsuccessful=true. OpenCore sets OptionalAbsent only on the INPUT-with-absent-optional path (an I-O/EXTEND absent optional file is CREATED per 14.9.27 GR17 and is therefore present, correctly leaving the flag clear). OBSERVED (probe/opt-absent/STPRB7.cob, SELECT OPTIONAL over a non-existent path, OPEN INPUT -> '05'): relative implicit-KEY START -> INVALID KEY taken, FS='23'; relative START FIRST -> INVALID KEY, '23'; indexed implicit-KEY START -> INVALID KEY, '23'; indexed START LAST -> INVALID KEY, '23'. SEQUENTIAL HALF — NOT IMPLEMENTED: an OPTIONAL sequential file plus START ... FIRST cannot execute at all (finding M1), so the rule has no sequential arm. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL.

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB352. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR6) delegates to 9.1.14. RELATIVE + INDEXED HALF — VERIFIED against every item of 9.1.14. (a) 9.1.14 item 2 (cite.py --check 9.1.14 OK: 'If the INVALID KEY phrase is specified ... any applicable exception processing statements are not executed, and control is transferred to the imperative-statement specified in the INVALID KEY phrase'): EmitInvalid emits `if (__kstN[0] == '2') { imperative-1 }` — the '2x' family ONLY, so a '47'/'30' START does not misroute into the INVALID KEY branch. (b) The declarative suppression is scoped the same way, not blanket: the generated __IoCheck (DispatchEmitter) and __IoCheckEc (EcEmitter) both read `if (__invKey && __st[0] == '2') return;`, so a START that fails with '47' while carrying an INVALID KEY phrase STILL reaches its USE declarative — which is what 9.1.14's non-invalid-key branch item 1 requires. (c) 9.1.14 final-rules item 2: EmitInvalid emits the NOT INVALID KEY imperative under `[0] == '0'` only. (d) The grammar admits both phrase orders and either phrase alone (startInvalidKeyPhrase, CobolIO.g4:572), matching the choice indicators recorded in the 14.9.41.2 figure note. OBSERVED: probe/rel-start/STPRB1 (A: NOT INVALID KEY on '00'; F: INVALID KEY on '23'), probe/idx-start/STPRB3 (J / N), probe/opt-absent/STPRB7 (four INVALID KEY firings), probe/empty-start/STPRBC (four). SEQUENTIAL HALF — NOT IMPLEMENTED (finding M1): the statement aborts the run unit, so neither phrase can be reached. Two halves, one verified => PARTIAL. PARTIAL CORROBORATION ONLY (not recorded as a closing test-ref because it covers just the success arm): conformance:2002/file_collating_seq prints 'START >= M UNDER REV:' from the NOT INVALID KEY imperative of a successful indexed START.

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB352; PB359. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR7): 'Following the unsuccessful execution of a START statement, the file position indicator is set to indicate that no valid record position has been established. For indexed files, the key of reference is undefined.' FIRST SENTENCE — VERIFIED on the invalid-key paths. Both StartFail bodies set `_fpiValid = false` and `LastReadUnsuccessful = true`, which is observable through 9.1.13.7 6a (cite.py --check 9.1.13.7 OK: 'The preceding START statement referencing that file connector was unsuccessful' => '46'). OBSERVED: probe/rel-start/STPRB1 step G — a failed relative START ('23') is followed by READ NEXT giving FS='46', with AT END NOT taken; probe/idx-start/STPRB3 step O — same on indexed. SECOND SENTENCE — CONFORMS BY CONSTRUCTION: A.2 item 59 (cite.py --check A.2 OK) names this an UNDEFINED language element ('Following the unsuccessful execution of the START statement for a given indexed file, the key of reference for that file is undefined'), so IndexedConnector leaving _refKey unchanged places it under no requirement. UNVERIFIED / LATENT DIVERGENCE (why PARTIAL, half 1): the '47' open-mode path in BOTH connectors (`if (!IsOpen || Mode is Output or Extend) return Status = ReadNotOpenForInput;`) returns WITHOUT invalidating the FPI or setting LastReadUnsuccessful, yet a '47' START (9.1.13.7 item 7) is an unsuccessful START and GR7 applies to it. I could not construct an observing program — every route into that branch either already leaves _fpiValid false (OPEN OUTPUT/EXTEND set it false in OpenCore) or forces an intervening OPEN that resets the indicator — so this is recorded as latent, not as a demonstrated wrong answer (finding M5). SEQUENTIAL HALF — NOT IMPLEMENTED (finding M1).

subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB236 (landed). RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR8): 'If the KEY phrase is omitted, the START statement behaves as though KEY IS EQUAL TO data-name-1 had been specified, where data-name-1 is the name of the key specified in the RELATIVE KEY clause associated with file-name-1.' MAIN PATH -- VERIFIED and unchanged: BindStart defaults the operator to '==' and the operand to file.RelativeKeyItem, which is exactly GR8's substitution and is consistent with GR10 (observed on probe/rel-start/STPRB1 step A: RRN 2/4/6 written, MOVE 4 TO RK, bare START RELFA takes NOT INVALID KEY with FS='00' and READ NEXT returns REC-4). THE EDGE IS NOW CLOSED, which is what moved this row. GR9 a) FORWARD SEARCH: RelativeConnector.Start walks the SortedDictionary keys ascending for '==' (ContainsKey), '>' and '>=' and breaks on the first hit. GR9 b) REVERSE SEARCH: '<' and '<=' walk the same ascending key order but KEEP the last satisfying key and break on the first non-satisfying one — which is the largest RRN satisfying the relation, i.e. the first record found searching the file in reverse. ConditionBinder.MapOperator maps NOT LESS -> '>=', NOT GREATER -> '<=', GREATER OR EQUAL -> '>=', LESS OR EQUAL -> '<='; '!=' is unreachable here (SR3 rewrite in BindStart), and no other spelling can fall through the switch, so there is no silent no-match arm. CONFORMS-but-untested. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED on the record's own editions claim. The forward/reverse SEMANTICS are right and I re-derived them independently: RelativeConnector.cs:340-355 walks a SortedDictionary<long,string> (KeyedStoreTable.cs:69), so '>'/'>=' break on the first ascending hit and '<'/'<=' keep the LAST satisfying key, which is the first found searching in reverse (GR9b); ConditionBinder.MapOperator (:798-810) folds NOT LESS -> '>=' and NOT GREATER -> '<=', matching the a)/b) split exactly. What does NOT hold is editions '85,2002,2014,2023'. PREVIOUS raises COBOLNET0900 at --std 85 (VersionConformancePass.cs:254, Constructs.ReadPrevious2002) -- and gates every other post-85 element of START (start-first-last-2002, start-with-length-2002, both with constructs.json rows). subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB370. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR17 e) 1.): 'The file position indicator is set to the value of the key of reference in the first logical record whose key satisfies the comparison'. IMPLEMENTATION: IndexedConnector.Start builds `Ordered(keyIndex)` — records sorted by (key-of-reference value under KeyCompare, then Arrival) with SUPPRESS WHEN records filtered out — then iterates FORWARD for '==','>','>=' and BACKWARD for '<','<=' (GR17 c/d) and stops at the first satisfying record, setting `_fpiKey = KeyOf(found.Image, keyIndex)` (the key VALUE, as the rule states) plus `_fpiArrival` (the duplicate-key disambiguator 9.1.8.2 needs to make arrival-order retrieval work; it adds resolution, it does not contradict the rule). GR17 e)'s operand orientation is right: `KeyCompare(part, value, keyIndex)` puts the RECORD'S extracted key on the left, matching 'with the second temporary area on the left hand side' (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK). The suppression sentence is honored by Ordered's `Where(r => !IsSuppressed(r.Image, keyIndex))`, and IsSuppressed returns false for keyIndex < 0 so the prime key is never suppressible. The partial-key truncation uses the WITH LENGTH count when present, else the operand's ImageWidth (EmitStart). OBSERVED (probe/idx-start/STPRB3, keys AAA100/BBB200/CCC300): implicit EQUAL 'BBB200' -> BBB200; '> BBB200' -> CCC300; '< BBB999' -> BBB200 (the LARGEST key below, proving the reverse search); 'NOT GREATER BBB999' -> BBB200; '>= AAA000 WITH LENGTH 3' -> AAA100. probe/idx-dup/STPRBB (alternate key WITH DUPLICATES, MM written by 05, 03, 09 in that arrival order): '>= MM' positions at 05 — the EARLIEST arrival of the duplicate set, and the walk gives 05, 03, 09; '< NN' positions at 09 — the LATEST arrival, i.e. the first satisfying record in reverse order. TESTS: conformance:2002/file_collating_seq pins START KEY IS >= 'M' under ALPHABET REV (expected 'START >= M UNDER REV:' then K=M, K=A, derived from 12.4.5.5.3 GR2c, not from any oracle); conformance:2023/altkey_suppress_when pins START KEY IS >= LOW-VALUES on a SUPPRESS-WHEN alternate key (expected 01/AA then 03/BB); conformance-test:KeyedOffsetSpecTests.Start_KeyOperandInSiblingRecord_MatchesByBytePosition asserts GOT=01 for START KEY = via a sibling-record operand, reasoned from 12.4.5.12.4 GR4 + 14.9.41.3 SR6b. All three compute their expected values from the standard. EDITIONS: the GR17 e) suppression sentence depends on SUPPRESS WHEN, a COBOL-2023 addition (cite.py --check E.3.3 OK, item 42), and the WITH LENGTH count in GR17 b) is a post-85 phrase; the rule itself is present in every edition. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — REFUTED, on the same defect as GR9 and for the same reason: the record claims edition 85 for a branch COBOL-85 does not have and the compiler does not gate. The BEHAVIOUR survived everything I threw at it. I re-derived the ordering from source rather than from the notes: IndexedConnector.Ordered (:510-513) sorts by (key-of-reference value under KeyCompare, then Arrival) with IsSuppressed filtered out, and Start (:444-481) walks seq[i] for '=='/'>'/'>=' and seq[Count-1-i] for '<'/'<=', which is exactly 9.1.8's reverse order (descending key, reverse arrival); KeyCompare(part, value, keyIndex) puts the RECORD's extracted key on the left, matching GR17 e)'s 'second temporary area on the left hand side'; _fpiKey = KeyOf(found.Image, keyIndex) is the key VALUE the rule names. I verified BOTH cited conformance goldens by reading them, not by trusting the note: 2002/file_collating_seq computes START KEY IS >= 'M' under ALPHABET REV -> 'K=M','K=A' from 12.4.5.5.3 GR2c, and 2023/altkey_suppress_when computes the SUPPRESS-WHEN skip from 12.4.5.6.4 GR6 -- both spec-derived, both genuinely pinning the FPI-setting branch (a mis-set FPI changes the printed walk). I then probed the edges neither test reaches. Nothing broke. What breaks is editions '85,2002,2014,2023': the record's own notes claim the BACKWARD arm for COBOL-85 ('iterates FORWARD for ==,>,>= and BACKWARD for <,<= ... < BBB999 -> BBB200, proving the reverse search'), and that operator set is A.3 item 39's other half of READ PREVIOUS, which the compiler does gate at 2002. On an indexed file the leak is starker than on a relative one: in ONE probe file the COLLATING SEQUENCE clause (2002) and SUPPRESS WHEN (2023) each correctly raise COBOLNET0900 at --std 85 while 'START IXF KEY IS LESS THAN R-KEY' beside them raises nothing. The gate exists for every neighbouring post-85 feature of this exact statement and not for this one. Forward arm verified at four editions and closed by two spec-derived tests; reverse arm verified at three editions and ungated at the fourth => PARTIAL.

RULE: "If FIRST is specified, the file position indicator is set to the value of the primary key of the first existing logical record in the physical file AND THE KEY OF REFERENCE IS SET TO THE PRIMARY KEY. subject: START statement
notes: kb/Work PB352; PB353. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR20): 'If FIRST is specified, the file position indicator is set to 1 if records exist in the physical file. If no records exist in the file, or the physical file does not support the ability to position at the first record, the I-O status value in the file connector referenced by file-name-1 is set to 23, the invalid key condition exists, and the execution of the START statement is unsuccessful.' The construct is unambiguously legal: 14.9.41.3 SR2 (cite.py --check OK) says 'If the organization of the file referenced by file-name-1 is sequential, either the FIRST or the LAST phrase shall be specified'; 9.1.8.2 (cite.py --check OK) says 'The START statement may be used to position the file at the beginning or the end for subsequent retrievals'; and 9.1.13.5 3d (cite.py --check OK) reserves '23' for 'a START statement is attempted on a sequential file that has no records or that does not support the ability to position at the specified record'. NO IMPLEMENTATION EXISTS. I searched the tree myself rather than trusting the dossier: SequentialConnector.cs has no Start / StartFirstLast member of any kind (the only 'Start' identifiers are _lastReadBlockStart / _lastLineStart); FileRegistry.StartFirstLast's switch has arms only for RelativeConnector and IndexedConnector and throws MisroutedVerb for anything else; and KeyedIoBinder.BindStart short-circuits on `if (file.IsSequential) return new BoundUnsupported("START on sequential-organization file ... (ISO 14.9.41 SR2 FIRST/LAST positioning - a later slice)")` — FileModel.IsSequential covering both SEQUENTIAL and LINE SEQUENTIAL. OBSERVED (probe/seq-start/STPRB2.cob): the program COMPILES WITH NO DIAGNOSTIC and aborts at run time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException on the first START. Expected from GR20: records exist, so the FIRST form sets the file position indicator to 1, status '00', and the next sequential READ makes record 1 ('AAA-1') available. See finding M1 (and M2 for the edition-gate hole this same early return opens). EDITIONS: no Annex E entry, so the rule is unchanged from 2014; it depends on the FIRST/LAST phrases, which are absent from the COBOL-85 START format (the 2023 text alone cannot date them — this is the one edition claim here not derived purely from the transcription).

notes: kb/Work PB352; PB353. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.41.4 OK, GR21): 'If LAST is specified, the file position indicator is set to the record number of the last existing logical record in the physical file. Note that GR21 also requires the '23' + invalid-key answer when the physical file cannot position at the last record — a sequential host stream is exactly the case the rule anticipates, so an implementation that cannot seek backwards is still obliged to answer '23' rather than abort. notes: kb/Work PB370. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 "the first one that occurs in the order of evaluation of the statement that causes the exception to exist" -> OK, GR 11). There is no explicit 'first condition' latch; the property is emergent - every raise site dispatches inline at the point the condition occurs, and a fatal raise throws out of the statement, so the first condition in evaluation order is the one that reaches __EcDispatch. `__af.Dispatched` additionally guarantees one dispatch per raise across nested guards (14.6.13.1.3 #7). PARTIAL because the adversarial shape is unverified and the emergent property is not robust to it: a statement in which the FIRST condition is nonfatal and a LATER one is fatal would dispatch on the later one, and there is no mechanism preventing it, because an enabled nonfatal condition raised from a runtime site never dispatches at all (ExceptionState.Set only records the last exception status - the nonfatal ambient gates EC-DATA-CONVERSION / EC-BOUND-OVERFLOW set a flag and nothing more). Whether a nonfatal condition must run the declarative is 14.6.13.1.4's rule, not this one, but it is what makes GR11 untested here. No spec-derived test asserts the ordering. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 3). No Annex E entry touches it.

notes: kb/Work PB370. Rule text (cite.py --check 14.9.49.4 "the predefined object reference EXCEPTION-OBJECT references the exception object" -> OK, GR 15). On BOTH paths that can enter a Format-4 declarative the register is set before the selector runs: EmitRaiseObject emits `ExceptionState.SetObject(<the RAISE operand>)` and then `__EcObjDispatch(ExceptionState.ExceptionObject)`; EmitPropagationPickup emits `SetObject(__po)` and then the selector. Note the register is a run-unit-scoped single slot (ExceptionState.ExceptionObject) and a NAMED raise inside the declarative nulls it (Set sets ExceptionObject = null); that is 14.9.29.4 GR1's rule, and GR15 constrains only the state on ENTRY, which holds. || REFUTED: PARTIAL — Two independent defects in the record. (1) THE TEST-REF DOES NOT PIN THE RULE. GR15 says EXCEPTION-OBJECT 'references the exception object' -- an IDENTITY claim (ISO 8.8.4.2.15: the relation is true 'if the object referenced by identifier-3 is the same object that is referenced by identifier-4'). The cited conformance:2002/oo_ec_raise_object asserts only 'IF U NOT = NULL DISPLAY "REGISTER-SET"'; its golden line 'REGISTER-SET' is satisfied by ANY non-null object, so a regression that set the register to the wrong object -- SELF, a fresh instance, the activating program -- keeps that golden green. The row is NOT closed by it and the test-ref must be emptied; the missing assertion is one line (IF U = E). I measured the identity claim myself and it HOLDS on every entry path, so the program-level half of the rule is genuinely correct -- this is a coverage correction, not a behaviour finding. (2) A HALF THAT CANNOT BE ENTERED AT ALL. 'the associated declarative' is a declarative in a procedure division, and ISO 14.2.2 SR10 permits the DECLARATIVES-bearing Format 1 (14.2.1) in a METHOD DEFINITION; StatementBinder.cs:239-242 rejects every declarative part inside a method with COBOLNET0899 'recognized but not yet implemented (owning roadmap phase: Phase 3, OO port)' at both 2002 and 2023, so a Format-4 USE in a method -- the natural home for EC-OO handling -- is legal source the compiler refuses. Unlocated/unreachable half + verified half => PARTIAL. (Contributing, already owned by the record for GR14: the interface-name-1 arm of the associated declarative is rejected COBOLNET0859, so even in a program only the object-class arm of GR14 can ever deliver an entry for GR15 to constrain -- I confirmed that rejection. It does not by itself move GR15, because the register is written BEFORE the selector runs and is therefore arm-independent.) || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002/2014/2023 (FORMAT 4). notes: kb/Work PB347. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 'Record-name-1 is the name of a logical record in the file section of the data division and may be qualified.' -> OK, 14.9.51.3 5). This is RELEASE 14.9.32.3 SR1 and REWRITE 14.9.35.3 SR1 written a third time, and all three now share ONE implementation, StatementValidation.ResolveRecordName. BOTH HALVES ARE WITNESSED. Name-of-a-logical-record: a subordinate item is refused (`WRITE OR-DATA` -> COBOLNET1757, naming OUT-REC as the record to write instead), a reference-modified record is refused (record-name-1 is a user-defined word per 8.3.2.2.25 and 5.2.4, not an identifier position per 8.4.3.3.3 SR5), and a WORKING-STORAGE 01 is refused with 14.9.51.3 SR1's reason -- 'The write file is the file referenced by file-name-1 or by the file-name associated with record-name-1' (--check OK) -- there being no file to name. May-be-qualified: `WRITE OUT-REC OF OUTF` binds and writes, pinned in both positive goldens. BEFORE THIS: all three were accepted with NO error. The subordinate and reference-modified forms drew nothing at all and emitted CobolFile.Write with the wrong operand and so the wrong record WIDTH; the WORKING-STORAGE form drew only the COBOLNET1756 DEFERRAL WARNING, which announces the COMPILER's gap for what is the source's error, and the program compiled. ISO 4.2.2 makes the compile-time indication mandatory. Edition-invariant: the sentence is identical in 1985, 2002 and 2014, so no gate exists and each negative carries `*> reject-at: 85 2002 2014 2023`.

subject: WRITE statement
notes: kb/Work PB329 (LANDED 2026-09-05) built this rule's mechanism; kb/Work PB689 gave it a ROW. The row did not exist when PB329 landed -- an interior '## SEQUENTIAL FILES' heading truncated 14.9.51.4's rule block at GR16, so GR17-GR42 were never in the catalog and PB329's implementer had nothing to close. RULE: 'For a line sequential file, if the record area contains one or more characters that are not in the implementor-defined character set defined for a line sequential file, the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the write file connector is set to 71.' cite.py --check 14.9.51.4 'the execution of the WRITE statement is unsuccessful and the I-O status in the write file connector is set to 71' -> OK 14.9.51.4 23). MECHANISM: LineSequentialCharacterSet is the one executable copy of the Annex A.1 item 115 determination (docs/CONFORMANCE.md DOC-A.1-115: every character at or above U+0020 is a member, the C0 controls below it are not), and SequentialConnector.RecordAreaOutsideLineCharacterSet is the one call shape. All THREE write entry points consult it -- Write, WriteAdvancing and WriteBeforeAndAfter -- ahead of every shape branch, because the rule is organization-scoped rather than shape-scoped, and ahead of any stream traffic because 9.1.13.10 item 1 requires the record area and the medium to be left unchanged. The test is CHARACTER-wise, not byte-wise: a national record area is walked two bytes at a time as UTF-16BE, so N"CD"'s 00 43 00 44 is two members and not two control characters. MEASURED on the built cobol.exe before PB329 landed: a line sequential WRITE of a record holding 0x00 reported STATUS=00 and left the byte on the medium; after, STATUS=71 and the file is 0 bytes. Goldens walk 09 (READ, 14.9.30.4 GR16), 71 (WRITE, THIS rule), 71 (REWRITE, 14.9.35.4 GR17d), the unchanged medium, and the set boundary (0x7F -> ordinal 128, 0xFF -> ordinal 256 are members) at every edition the LINE SEQUENTIAL organization exists in.

subject: Offset time formats
notes: CITATION re-derived mechanically: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A plus sign to indicate that the common time portion of the data is adjusted downward by the offset values to represent UTC' -> OK, anchored on the rule marker '1)' under (Offset subformats). The rule has two obligation halves and I read BOTH. (1) PRODUCE-THE-CHARACTER. CobolDate.cs#EmitFormatted line 361-363 is the ONE renderer of a §15.3 offset subformat's sign: 'long offMag = Math.Abs(offsetMinutes); int oh = (int)(offMag/60), om = (int)(offMag%60); char osign = offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-';', emitted at 'case Fld.OffSign: sb.Append(osign)'. argument-4 of FORMATTED-DATETIME / argument-3 of FORMATTED-TIME is 'the offset from UTC expressed in minutes' (§15.40.3 r5 --check OK), so a NON-NEGATIVE argument means local is at or ahead of UTC and the sign written is '+', which is exactly what rule 1 makes '+' mean. Verified by golden: conformance:2023/pb11_datetime_format_grammar 'T-OFF=01:00:00+01:00' (offset 60) and 'OFF-MAX=010000+2359' (offset 1439), conformance:2014/formatted_datetime 'T3=123456+0200' (offset 120). (2) HONOUR-THE-MEANING. The direction rule 1 fixes is what §15.40.4 r2 / §15.41.4 r2 ('the time portion ... reflects the adjustment of the value in argument-3 by the offset in argument-4' -- --check OK) leaves unstated; EmitFormatted lines 326-330 implement it as 'if (hasTime && isUtc && hasOffset) { secs -= offsetMinutes * 60m; ... }' -- a POSITIVE offset SUBTRACTS, i.e. adjusts the common time DOWNWARD to represent UTC. Verified by golden: conformance:2014/formatted_datetime 'T2=10:34:56Z' from local 45296 s (12:34:56) with offset +120, and conformance:2023/r25_utc_roll_date_range case 4 'FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ" 2 0 1439)' -> '16010101T000100Z' (1601-01-02 00:00:00 minus 23h59m). (3) CONSUME-THE-CHARACTER. CobolDate.cs#Analyze lines 510-516 accept '+' in the sign position; the sign is deliberately NOT applied downstream, which is correct and not a gap: §15.79.4 makes SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME's value ((H*3600)+(M*60)+S) over the hours/minutes/seconds subfields only (--check OK) and §15.48.4 r1's NOTE says the time portion of a combined format 'is validated against the format ... but if valid does not impact the returned value'. Pinned by conformance:2023/pb23_week_date_beyond_integer_date_form, which runs the standard's own D.31.5.8/D.31.5.9 worked examples: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500") = 0143951 (identical to the date-only form) and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss.ss+hhmm", "05142781+0500") = 18867.81 (= 5*3600+14*60+27.81, the offset NOT applied). No second renderer exists: grepping the whole of src/ for '+' : '-' returns only EmitFormatted line 363 and Format21 line 35, and Format21 serves §15.21.3/§15.99's separate 21-character layout, not a §15.3 offset subformat. FORMATTED-CURRENT-DATE reaches the same one renderer (CobolDate.cs#FormattedCurrentDate passes now.Offset.TotalMinutes), so the system-clock producer inherits the same sign convention. Editions 2014,2023: the offset subformat is reachable ONLY through the FORMATTED-*/INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE/SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME/TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME family, which the inventory's already-adjudicated §15.38-§15.48/§15.79/§15.92 rows uniformly window at 2014,2023; Annex E documents only the 2014->2023 delta and lists no change here, so there is no 2023 delta either. || REFUTED: verdict CONFIRMED at CONFORMS, but the EVIDENCE CHAIN is corrected and the record changed. (1) CITATION re-derived independently: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A plus sign to indicate that the common time portion of the data is adjusted downward by the offset values to represent UTC' -> OK, anchored on the rule marker '1)' under (Offset subformats); I also re-derived §15.40.3 r5, §15.40.4 r2/r3, §15.41.3 r4/r6, §15.41.4 r2/r3, §15.48.4 r1 and §15.79.4 r1 by reading §15.40-§15.41/§15.48/§15.79 whole rather than trusting the adjudicator's quotes. (2) TEST-REF CORRECTED: conformance:2023/r25_utc_roll_date_range is REMOVED. Every one of its five cases uses the format 'YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ', which by §15.3.3.5 is a common time format followed by a single 'Z' and therefore carries NO offset subformat and emits NO sign character at all -- it cannot close a rule about the character in 'the data associated with an offset subformat'. It is evidence for §15.40.4 r2 (a separately inventoried row, RV-15.40.4-2), not for this one. notes: CITATION re-derived mechanically: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A minus sign to indicate that the common time portion of the data is adjusted upward by the offset values to represent UTC' -> OK, anchored on the rule marker '2)'. subject: Offset time formats
notes: CITATION re-derived mechanically, all four normative sentences separately: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 'A zero to indicate that offset from UTC was not available on the system on which the information was recorded' -> OK (marker '3)'); 'If the data contains a zero in that character position, the offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields of the data shall both contain zero' -> OK; 'If the values contained in offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields of data in a receiving field associated with an offset subformat are both zero, the position corresponding to the plus sign in the format shall contain a plus sign' -> OK; 'The colon character in the offset subformat of an extended offset time format appears in the data associated with the format' -> OK. This is a COMPOUND rule with FOUR normative obligations plus three informative NOTEs; I located and read the implementation of every one. (a) '0' IS A PERMITTED SIGN VALUE. CobolDate.cs#Analyze lines 510-516: 'if (s.Field == Fld.OffSign) { ... char c = data[pos]; if (c is not ('+' or '-')) { if (c == '0') offZero = true; else return pos + 1; } pos++; continue; }' -- exactly the three values rules 1-3 enumerate are admitted and every other character yields the 1-based error position §15.92.4 requires. (b) A '0' SIGN FORCES BOTH SUBFIELDS TO ZERO. Analyze line 531: 'if (offZero && s.Field is Fld.OffHour or Fld.OffMinute) hi = 0;' collapses the §15.3.3.6.2 ranges (0..23 hours, 0..59 minutes) to the single value 0 for both, and the offZero flag is set before either is read because §15.3.3.6.1 puts the sign first in the subformat. Traced the per-digit narrowing at lines 543-548 by hand: sign '0' with hours '05' errors at the SECOND hours digit (the leading '0' is still consistent with the only legal '00'), which is the earliest character at which the error is determinable -- the §15.92.4 contract, not an off-by-one. (c) THE RECEIVING-FIELD REQUIREMENT ('+' when both subfields are zero). CobolDate.cs#EmitFormatted line 363 'osign = offsetMinutes >= 0 ? '+' : '-'' can never produce '0' at all, and yields '+' at offsetMinutes == 0; lines 361-362 make oh/om zero only when offsetMinutes is exactly 0 (|offset| in 1..59 gives om != 0, >= 60 gives oh != 0), so the '-'-with-+0000 counterexample is unreachable. Verified by golden: conformance:2023/pb11_datetime_format_grammar 'OMIT-OFF=010000+0000' for FORMATTED-TIME("hhmmss+hhmm" 3600) with argument-3 omitted (§15.41.3 r6 evaluates it as 0) -- literally NOTE 3's '+0000'. (d) THE COLON OF AN EXTENDED OFFSET SUBFORMAT APPEARS IN THE DATA. CobolDate.cs#Tokenize line 277 emits Seg(IsField:false, Sep:':', InData:true); EmitFormatted line 369 'if (!s.IsField) { if (s.InData) sb.Append(s.Sep); continue; }' writes it, and Analyze lines 504-508 REQUIRE it in the data ('if (pos >= data.Length || data[pos] != s.Sep) return pos + 1'). Verified by golden: pb11 'T-OFF=01:00:00+01:00'. The bind-time recognizer agrees on the subformat's two shapes -- DateTimeFormatGrammar.cs#ZoneOfWidth lines 119-122 accept the five-character '+hhmm' and six-character '+hh:mm' and require the offset's width to MATCH the common part's, so a basic/extended chimera never reaches the runtime. Also confirmed the FORMAT always carries '+' as the placeholder and never a '-': Tokenize's '-' arm (line 276) does not set afterOffSign, so a hyphen is only ever the extended-date separator -- the format/data asymmetry these three rules describe is modelled correctly rather than collapsed. HONEST RESIDUE (why this row stays test-needed even at CONFORMS): obligations (a) and (b) -- the SENDING-field permission to write '0' with zero magnitude, and its rejection when the magnitude is non-zero -- are verified by implementation reading ONLY. No golden in tests/conformance/ feeds a '0' into an offset sign position; pb23 exercises the consuming path with '+' ('19950215T05142781+0500', the D.31.5.8/D.31.5.9 examples) and pb11 pins the producing path, so the cited tests close (c) and (d) but not (a)/(b). A closing golden would be TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("hhmmss+hhmm", "01000000000") = 0 with the non-zero-magnitude mate asserting the error position. NOTE 2's cross-reference to CURRENT-DATE / WHEN-COMPILED is informative and lands outside this clause: CobolDate.cs#Format21 renders §15.21.3's separate 21-character layout, whose position 17 is '0' only when the system lacks the local-time-differential facility -- .NET's DateTimeOffset always has one, so '+'/'-' is always correct there. Editions rationale identical to GR-15.3.3.6.1-1. || REFUTED: verdict CONFIRMED at CONFORMS after an independent re-derivation and a hand-trace of every branch; the record is changed to record what the note over-claimed and what residue remains. (1) ALL FOUR CITATIONS RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY and all return OK on §15.3.3.6.1 marker '3)'. Reading the clause whole shows FIVE normative sentences, not four: the note folds the SENDING-field permission ('For offset-time values used as sending fields, the position ... may contain a zero provided that ...' -- --check OK) into obligation (a) rather than naming it. It is nonetheless implemented by the same Analyze line 514 arm, so the omission is a labelling one. (2) OBLIGATION (b) HAND-TRACED, NOT ACCEPTED: with sign '0' Analyze line 531 forces hi = 0 while lo stays 0 for both Fld.OffHour (0,23) and Fld.OffMinute (0,59), and the per-digit narrowing at 543-548 then admits '00' and rejects everything else at the earliest determinable character -- I walked '01000000000' (accepted, returns 0), '0'+hours '01' (error at the SECOND hours digit, data position 9) and '0'+minutes '10' (error at the FIRST minute digit, position 10), all of which match §15.92.4's 'first position at which the error can be determined'. The two-halves argument was made but not earned. notes: UPHELD after varying the RECEIVER as well as the argument. Repertoire appends exactly one character per input character (a substitution replaces, never expands or drops), so the returned string's length is always argument-1's character count, and under D-N1 one national position is one UTF-16 char and one usage-display position. RAN MYSELF at --std 2023: FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(PIC N(5))) -> 005; the same over a PIC N(3) containing a SUBSTITUTED U+4E16 -> 003, so substitution does not change the length; the ZERO-LENGTH national literal FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N"") -> LENGTH 000 and an all-space receiver, which is correct since 15.26.3 carries no zero-length-literal prohibition (its 15.66.3 r3 twin does); a SUPPLEMENTARY-plane national literal in a PIC N(2) -> LENGTH 002 and '??', consistent with the declared D-N1 one-code-unit-per-position model; a reference-modified argument N-SRC(1:3) -> 3; a national GROUP of two PIC N(2) items -> 4. Receiver variation: STRING FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-SRC) DELIMITED BY SIZE INTO a PIC X(10) prefilled with '-' gives [HELLO-----], i.e. exactly 5 positions transferred; MOVE to a PIC X(6) gives 'HELLO '; and the length consequence in comparison is right in both directions - the result compares EQUAL to "HELLO", to "HELLO   " and to a PIC X(8) item, so the shorter operand is space-padded per 8.8.4.2.7 r2 rather than compared as a raw .NET string. There is no static width model for an intrinsic result in the compiler, so the length is purely the runtime string's and FUNCTION LENGTH reads that. conformance:2002/national_intrinsics verified on disk with its golden (LEN-D=05) and its tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json entry; the LEN-D line is computed from 15.26.4 r4, not pinned from behaviour. NOTED, and deliberately not charged here: FUNCTION BYTE-LENGTH(FUNCTION DISPLAY-OF(N-W)) crashes at run time with a NotImplementedCobolFeatureException naming 'ISO 15.14.3' - that is a 15.14 argument-shape gap for whoever adjudicates BYTE-LENGTH, not a 15.26.4 r4 defect.

subject: E function
notes: Verdict SURVIVES; the note is corrected and the SPEC BASIS the adjudicator missed is supplied. test-needed. Citations re-validated: cite.py --check 15.27.3 'standard-binary arithmetic is in effect' -> OK (rule 2). THE PRECONDITION CAN NEVER HOLD IN THIS COMPILER, re-verified by me on the built CLI: DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects the mode with COBOLNET0806 'ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is an obsolete feature (ISO 8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1 / Annex F) and is not supported; use NATIVE or STANDARD-DECIMAL' - a HARD error at --std 2002 (alongside COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'), 2014 and 2023, and NOT downgradable by --permissive (2023 adds the COBOLNET0903 obsolescence warning and still errors). Nothing in the tree computes 14114126198520207781233383725636853 / (2 ** 112); CobolIntrinsics.E() is the only body and is Math.E in every mode. WHAT THE ADJUDICATOR MISSED, and it is what makes this an owner DECISION rather than a bug: the standard itself classes this clause as processor-dependent. Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim - cite.py --check A.3 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' -> OK - and 4.5 NOTE, validated verbatim ('These factors can include the use of optional, processor-dependent, or implementor-defined language elements'), together mean a conforming implementation may fail to translate a compilation group that uses it without ceasing to conform. Annex F.2 additionally makes STANDARD-BINARY an obsolete feature, and it is F.2 ITEM 3 - not Annex E - that records the non-implementation: '3. STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' (cite.py --check F.2 'STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item' -> OK). CITATION REPAIRED 2026-08-31, and the error was worse than a wrong annex letter: the sentence as previously quoted here ('it has not been implemented ... by any COBOL provider', singular) is F.2 ITEM 5's, which is about the VALIDATE FACILITY - a real clause answering a different question (feedback_a_real_clause_can_answer_a_different_question). Item 3 also carries the reevaluation note that makes the decline REVISITABLE: 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). The non-support is already recorded at docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 2 row 2 ('| 2 | ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1); the native/standard-decimal modes are provided |') - the DOCUMENTED-NON-SUPPORT shape, a verdict only the owner may set, hence NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION. BARE QUESTION: should 15.27.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by the existing documented non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY (Annex A.3 item 2 processor-dependence) rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? Identical to the already-adjudicated sibling RV-15.73.3-2 for PI; one decision should settle the whole 15.4.1 family. EDITIONS DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY OF INTRINSICCATALOG: the STANDARD-BINARY keyword of the ARITHMETIC clause is a COBOL-2014 addition (the 2002 clause offered NATIVE and STANDARD only; the compiler's own edition gate agrees - 'OPTIONS. ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY.' at --std 2002 draws COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014 (targeting COBOL-2002)', re-run by me), so the rule's precondition cannot arise at 85 or 2002. TEST COVERAGE: none - no test references FUNCTION E under any arithmetic mode. The honest cover is a negative case pinning that FUNCTION E under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is refused BY MODE; a mode-only rejection test that never names E would not cover this row. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

I re-ran the search rather than trusting the prior pass: `grep -rn 1439 src/ --include=*.cs | grep -v Generated/` returns NOTHING — not in the binder, not in the renderer, not in the runtime. Argument-4 flows `IntrinsicRenderer#RenderFormattedDatetime` -> `ArgInt(ic.Args[3])` -> `CobolDate.EmitFormatted`, which only ever computes `offMag = Math.Abs(offsetMinutes); oh = (int)(offMag / 60); om = (int)(offMag % 60)`. Consequences, both silent: 2000 minutes renders offset-hours 33, violating §15.3.3.6.2 ('The offset-hours subfield of the data associated with a basic or extended offset time format shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive'); 9999 minutes renders 166, so `oh.ToString("00")` emits three characters and the returned value grows past the width the format describes. §15.3 requires EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION to be set to exist for an out-of-range argument even though the VALUE is implementor-defined; it is never set. Because argument-4 may be an identifier or an expression this cannot be a compile-time check in general, but it is a one-line runtime guard beside the existing integer-date guard in `CobolDate.FormattedDatetime`. NOT-IMPLEMENTED rather than DIVERGES because there is no implementation to diverge from. The identical rule text is §15.41.3 r4 for FORMATTED-TIME and is equally unimplemented (same sweep). subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL → NOT-IMPLEMENTED, and the EDITION WINDOW WAS WRONG. (1) EDITIONS. Both concepts this rule names arrive at COBOL-2014, not 2002: `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL` (§11.9.5/§8.8.1.5) and the §3.166 standard binary floating-point usages ('usages float-binary-32, float-binary-64, and float-binary-128' — checked mechanically), i.e. USAGE FLOAT-BINARY-32/64/128 (§13.18.60.4 GR14–GR16). Neither exists at COBOL-2002, so the rule as worded cannot be evaluated at 2002. The adjudicator wrote 2002,2014,2023 on all six rows without deriving any of them. (2) VERDICT. By the stated rule 'code not located ⇒ NOT-IMPLEMENTED': the adjudicator's own finding is that NOTHING in BindAlgebraicFold reads ctx.Data.Options.Arithmetic (the only arithmetic-mode test in IntrinsicBinder is the ANNUITY/PRESENT-VALUE/VARIANCE/STANDARD-DEVIATION staging arm), so there is no code for this rule and citing BindAlgebraicFold as its code-location is citing the code of a DIFFERENT rule. Today's incidental coverage comes entirely from the blanket `pic.IsFloat` ban that AR-15.43.3-1 finds DIVERGENT — a rule enforced only by a bug is not implemented. (3) ⛔ NEW — THE ONE PLACE THE CODE CITES RULE 2, IT MIS-STATES IT. The COBOLNET1516 message asserts '…under STANDARD-DECIMAL it is barred by rule 2' while the guard fires for COMP-1/COMP-2/FLOAT-SHORT/FLOAT-LONG/FLOAT-EXTENDED — none of which is a standard binary floating-point usage under §3.166. That is a false statement of the rule shipped in a user-visible diagnostic, and it is precisely the inherited-citation failure mode. Confirmed live-and-writable: OptionsBinder#ArithmeticOf maps STANDARD-DECIMAL to ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal (only STANDARD-BINARY is rejected, at DataBinder COBOLNET0806), and FLOAT-BINARY-32/64 are LIVE usages (PicInfo#ClrType → float/double). FLOAT-BINARY-128 is out of reach (COBOLNET1564, Annex A.3 item 17). No spec-derived test.

subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL → NOT-IMPLEMENTED, same two grounds as rule 2. (1) EDITIONS: `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY` (§11.9.5/§8.8.1.4) and the §3.167 standard decimal floating-point usages (float-decimal-16, float-decimal-34 — USAGE per §13.18.60.4 GR17/GR18) are both COBOL-2014 additions; the rule as worded does not exist at COBOL-2002. (2) VERDICT: no code implements this rule anywhere — the prohibited combination is doubly unreachable through two INDEPENDENT non-supports that have nothing to do with §15.43, so nothing has ever evaluated the rule's condition. Both non-supports are conformance-legal and I re-derived them rather than inheriting them: DataBinder rejects STANDARD-BINARY with COBOLNET0806, and Annex A.3 item 2 reads 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (NOTE 1 adds that the mode is obsolete); FLOAT-DECIMAL-16/34 are rejected at ParseUsage with COBOLNET1564 under A.3 item 19. Worth recording for whoever revisits this: A.3 item 3 makes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL processor-dependent TOO, so COBOL.NET's support for it is a choice, not an obligation — which is why rule 2's combination is writable and rule 3's is not. Vacuous truth is not implementation: if either half is ever supported, nothing enforces this. No spec-derived test, and none constructible. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
