subject: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE function
notes:
REFUTER PASS. VERDICT RETAINED AT DIVERGES, AND THE DEFECT IS WIDER THAN THE ADJUDICATOR RECORDED.

CITATIONS RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.48.3 "If argument-1 is a date format, the contents of argument-2 shall be a valid date in that format." -> OK (§15.48.3 4)). cite.py --check 15.3 "If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value" -> OK (§15.3 rule 14), and I read that paragraph IN FULL because it is what forecloses every escape from the finding below: "... results in an incorrect value for that argument OR FOR THE RETURNED VALUE according to the rules specified in the function definition ... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist ... If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference."

THE VALIDATION ITSELF IS CORRECT and I re-read every leg: CobolDate#Analyze walks the tokenized format against the data, requiring each in-data separator ('-', ':', 'W', 'T', 'Z') to appear, rejecting a non-digit, a short field and any trailing character (`if (pos != data.Length) return pos + 1;`), and range-checking every subfield with per-digit narrowing - year 1601..9999 (§15.3.1.3/.5/.7, "greater than 1600 and less than or equal to 9999"), month 1..12, day-of-month against DaysInMonth, day-of-year against the leap year, week against LongIsoYear, weekday 1..7. I checked LongIsoYear against §15.3.1.7's OWN formulation (53 weeks "if the year subfield represents a common year and January 4 of that year falls on Sunday, or if the year subfield represents a leap year and January 4 of that year falls on a Saturday or Sunday") and derived that it is equivalent to ISO 8601's Jan-1-Thursday / leap-Wednesday rule, which is what ISOWeek.GetWeeksInYear implements - so the week cap is right. A nonzero result becomes ExceptionState#ArgumentError, which I read: it sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION fatal when checking is enabled and otherwise returns 0 - exactly §15.3 rule 14's disposition.

⛔ CORRECTION - THE WEEK-DATE CRASH WINDOW IS TWO DAYS WIDE, NOT ONE. The adjudicator cited only "9999W527". I recomputed .NET's ISOWeek.ToDateTime arithmetic by hand: 9999-01-04 is a MONDAY, so correction = 1 + 3 = 4 and ordinal = 52*7 + d - 4 = 360 + d, evaluated as `new DateTime(9999,1,1).AddDays(ordinal - 1)` against a 365-DAY year. d=5 gives 9999-12-31 (integer date 3,067,671, the §15.5.2 maximum - CORRECT and, usefully, the exact boundary the landed FORMATTED-DATE row pins as "9999W525"); d=6 gives 10000-01-01 and d=7 gives 10000-01-02, BOTH past DateTime.MaxValue, and BOTH throw System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException. Every §15.3.1.7 subfield rule passes for both: 9999 > 1600 and <= 9999; 9999 is a 52-week ISO year so week 52 is inside 01..52; day-of-week 6 and 7 are inside 1..7. So "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W526" AND "YYYYWwwD"/"9999W527" are both PERMISSIBLE DATA that abort the run unit with a raw CLR stack trace - neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition, where §15.3 rule 14 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result. The extended forms "YYYY-Www-D"/"9999-W52-6" and "9999-W52-7" fault identically (same Analyze leg).

CORROBORATION, NOT INHERITANCE: the landed AR-15.79.3-5 RAN this input against the sibling and its own sweep records `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` as verified crashing identically. I re-derived it here from the code and the calendar arithmetic, and extended it to d=6, which no prior record had.

ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX - bound-check the week-date reconstruction in Analyze. Do not count this row, AR-15.48.3-5 and AR-15.79.3-5 as three queue items. THE LOW BOUNDARY IS CLEAN and I checked it rather than assuming it: 1601-01-01 is a Monday and lies in ISO 1601-W01, so ISO 1601-W01-1 = 1601-01-01 = integer date 1, and no week date can underflow the epoch.

test-ref EMPTY: no test, golden or corpus program feeds this function an INVALID argument-2 at all, so neither the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION path nor the crash is pinned anywhere. EDITIONS from the standard (Annex E carries no occurrence of the name), not from IntrinsicCatalog's row. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. The new arithmetic is proven EQUIVALENT to ISOWeek over >200,000 week dates spanning 1601-9999 by unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.TheIntegerWeekArithmetic_AgreesWithISOWeek_Everywhere, which asserts its own population so it cannot pass vacuously. ⛔ THE TEST GAP THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO CLOSED: the golden carries Annex D.31.5.8's and D.31.5.9's OWN worked examples — "YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951, and "hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and its combined form both -> 18867.81 — so the §15.48.4 / §15.79.4 NOTE that the other half "does not impact the returned value" is now verified by TEST rather than by code reading.

DayOfWeek.Sunday : (DayOfWeek)wd) - Epoch).Days + 1;` computes ordinal = 52*7 + d - (jan4DayOfWeek(9999) + 3) = 360 + d against a 365-day year, i.e. 10000-01-01 and 10000-01-02, and throws System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException. NO VALUE IS RETURNED AND NO COBOL EXCEPTION CONDITION IS RAISED. §15.3 rule 14 forecloses the last escape - read in full it covers an incorrect value "for that argument OR FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" and prescribes EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or, with checking disabled, the implementor-defined result - so even on the most conservative reading (that the denoted date has no integer date form, §15.5.2 topping out at 3,067,671) a raw CLR stack trace is not a permitted disposition. WHAT IS CORRECT, re-verified by READING the conversion rather than by trying values (the PB5 lesson): Analyze reconstructs the date from whichever subfields the format carries - calendar `new DateTime(yy,mo,dm)`, ordinal `new DateTime(yy,1,1).AddDays(doy-1)`, week `ISOWeek.ToDateTime(yy,wk,...)` with Monday=1..Sunday=7 (§15.3.1.7) - and converts with `(d - Epoch).Days + 1` against Epoch 1601-01-01, which IS §15.5.2's integer date 1 (I confirmed 1601-01-01 is a Monday, and that 9999-12-31 is exactly 3,067,671 inclusive days later). THE NOTE IS HONOURED BY CONSTRUCTION: IntegerOfFormattedDate discards secondsScaled (`out _`), and the offset subfields feed no date adjustment, so a combined format's time portion is validated and cannot move the result - which is what Annex D.31.5.8 requires ("YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951; I recomputed 143951 from the epoch). The result is typed integer: catalog IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicRenderer#RenderNum returns NumX(..., scale 0).

Annex A processor-dependent item: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.' DataBinder.cs: `if (Options.Arithmetic == ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary) Edition.Error("COBOLNET0806", ...)`. PictureAnalyzer.cs case "FLOAT-DECIMAL-16": `edition.Error("COBOLNET1564", ...)`. BindAlgebraicFold contains no arithmetic-mode test of any kind. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). notes: VERDICT UPHELD, on stronger evidence than the original, with one citation corrected. CITATION FIX: the original note said '§8.8.4.2.2 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value'; §8.8.4.2.2 is 'General format' and --check FAILS on that text. The clause is §8.8.4.2.4 (--check OK: 'For operands whose class is numeric, a comparison is made with respect to the algebraic value of the operands regardless of the manner in which their usage is described ... Zero is considered a unique value regardless of the sign'). WHY THIS SURVIVES THE ATTACK AT IMPLEMENTATION LEVEL RATHER THAN BY SAMPLING: leftmost-wins is a property of ExtremeIndex ALONE - `for (int i = 1; i < xs.Length; i++) { int c = cmp(xs[i], xs[k]); if (max ? c > 0 : c < 0) k = i; }` - and is independent of the comparator passed in, so it holds identically for all six MaxString/MinString overloads (native pad-compare, the ushort[] alphanumeric-PCS weights, and the NationalCollation variant) and for OrdMaxString/OrdMinString, which is the whole family in one place. The original evidence only exhibited SAME-CONTENT / DIFFERENT-LENGTH ties, which cannot distinguish leftmost-wins from a stable comparator; the refuter added a tie between DIFFERENT CONTENTS of EQUAL VALUE, which is what the rule is actually about, and it passes on the weights overload. The NUMERIC/INDEX half remains vacuous rather than unverified, and the argument is sound: §8.8.4.2.4 makes two greatest-valued numeric arguments equal in algebraic value (and makes signed and unsigned zero one value), §15.59.4 r3 confines the SIZE question to alphanumeric and national, and under standard arithmetic §15.4.1 puts the returned value in a mode-defined intermediate data item whose characteristics come from the mode rather than from the selected argument - so two tied numeric or index arguments have no observable difference in content to choose between. CONTINGENCY WORTH RECORDING: this rule governs which of the TIED arguments is returned; whether the tie is real is RV-15.59.4-1's question, and at the boundaries documented there the 'greatest value' premise is itself wrong. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023. REFUTER'S DECISIVE CASE - an equal-value tie between DIFFERENT contents, on the non-identity-PCS weights overload: E:/Temp/rfmax/tiew.cob (RFMAXTIEW) `OBJECT-COMPUTER. XX PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE AL.` / `SPECIAL-NAMES. The rule is also robust to the RV-15.66.4-1 domain question in a way rules 2 and 3 are not: under any 1:1 correspondence, and under substitution too (one substitution character occupies one national position), the count is unchanged, so this row does not inherit their contingency. RESIDUAL, recorded and not counted against the verdict because it is the same single root already charged to AR-15.66.3-1 / RV-15.66.4-1 rather than a distinct r4 defect: for a figurative-constant or ALL-literal argument-1 there is no returned value at all, hence no length. REFNOF06: `FUNCTION LENGTH(FUNCTION NATIONAL-OF(AX))` over a PIC X(3) containing U+4E16 -> 3, i.e. the count is unaffected by a non-Latin-1 code unit. The prior pass's checks re-confirmed: `MOVE FUNCTION NATIONAL-OF(A1) TO <PIC X(9)>` is rejected `error COBOLNET0819: ... MOVE of a national sending operand to an alphabetic, alphanumeric, or alphanumeric-edited receiver is invalid (ISO §14.9.25.3 SR10 ...)`, so the result is genuinely category national. subject: NUMVAL-F function

NUMVAL-F is 2014+.

subject: PI function
notes: EDITIONS CORRECTED to 2014,2023: standard-binary arithmetic is a COBOL-2014 introduction (ConstructRegistry row 'arithmetic-standard-binary-2014', IntroducedIn 2014, ObsoleteIn 2023), so this rule cannot apply at 2002 - confirmed empirically, the sibling STANDARD-DECIMAL clause is rejected at --std 2002 with COBOLNET0900 'requires COBOL-2014'. The rule's precondition can never hold: ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY is rejected at bind time with COBOLNET0806 (DataBinder.BindDeclarations), re-verified on the built CLI as a HARD error at both --std 2014 and --std 2023 and NOT downgradable by --permissive. No code computes the exact binary128 value 16312081666030376401667486162748272 / 2**112, and none can while the mode is refused. The non-support is already recorded in CONFORMANCE.md SS2 row 2 ('ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY | 11.9.5 | Not claimed | Obsolete feature (A.3 NOTE 1)') and licensed by ISO Annex A.3 item 2, validated verbatim: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor.' BARE QUESTION: should SS15.73.3 rule 2 be recorded as discharged by that existing Annex A.3 item-2 non-support of ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY rather than carried as an open inventory GAP? TEST-REF STRUCK on review: the previously cited StandardDecimalTests.StandardBinary_DocumentedUnsupported exercises the MODE rejection and never references PI or any returned value, so it does not cover this rule - test-needed (a test pinning that FUNCTION PI under STANDARD-BINARY is refused by name would be the honest cover). || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOLNET0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).

subject: SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME function
notes: A combined WEEK-date-and-time format whose argument-2 is VALID per §15.3.1.7 aborts the run unit with an unhandled .NET exception instead of returning a value. `MOVE FUNCTION SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME("YYYYWwwDThhmmss", "9999W527T235959") TO WS-F.` at --std 2014 → 'Unhandled exception. System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException … at System.Globalization.ISOWeek.ToDateTime … at CobolNet.Runtime.CobolDate.Analyze'. Every subfield satisfies §15.3.1.7: year 9999 is >1600 and <=9999; Jan 4 9999 is a Monday so 9999 is a 52-week ISO year and week 52 is inside the permitted 01..52; day-of-week 7 is inside 1..7. The expected result is +86399.00 — D.31.5.9 makes the date VALIDATED BUT DISCARDED for this function, so the integer date form is never needed here at all; Analyze computes it unconditionally at its `else if (hasWeek) integerDate = ISOWeek.ToDateTime(...)` leg, and ISO-9999-W52-7 falls on 10000-01-02, outside DateTime.MaxValue. Even on the most conservative reading (that the denoted date is out of range and r5 is therefore violated), §15.3 fixes the disposition as EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION or the implementor-defined result — never a raw CLR stack trace, which is neither a COBOL value nor a COBOL exception condition. Sibling sweep (same Analyze line, both verified crashing identically): `FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` and `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD", "9999W527")` — the latter is the worse one, since §15.92 defines TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME as the VALIDATOR that returns an error position and can therefore never legitimately fault. Fix shape: bound-check the week-date reconstruction (and hand SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME a path that does not build integerDate at all). The rest of r5 is correct and was verified: the mandatory 'T' is required in the data (§15.3.3.7); the D.31.5.9 worked example `("YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm", "19950215T05142781+0500")` → +18867.81 with the offset correctly excluded; Feb-31 in the same format → the §15.3 default 0; the calendar boundary "99991231T235959" → +86399.00. test-needed. ⚙ FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-08-05 (fix-queue PB23). This row's ONLY divergence was the shared week-date reconstruction, and the row itself said so ("ONE ROOT CAUSE, ONE FIX"). CobolDate#Analyze no longer calls ISOWeek.ToDateTime: §15.3.1.7 fixes week 1 as "the week that includes January 4", so that week's Monday is computed directly and every later day is a plain integer offset from it — the arithmetic CANNOT overflow, which is the point, because the input is VALID and no tightening of the per-subfield range table could have prevented the fault. The result is then range-checked against §15.5.2's ceiling ("shall be greater than zero and shall be less than or equal to ... 3,067,671"), and ONLY the caller that must PRODUCE an integer date form reacts: INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION through ExceptionState#ArgumentError per §15.3 rule 14's "incorrect value ... FOR THE RETURNED VALUE" arm (implementor-defined result 0 when checking is off), while TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME still answers 0 — §15.92.4 requires any non-zero answer to be "the ordinal character position at which the first error ... was detected", and no CHARACTER of "9999W526" is in error (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid) — and SECONDS-FROM-FORMATTED-TIME still returns its seconds (§15.79.4 reads only the time subfields). THE TWO-DAY WINDOW THIS ROW RECORDS (d=6 AND d=7) IS CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, not re-derived on paper: 9999-12-31 is ISO 9999-W52-5. The new arithmetic is proven EQUIVALENT to ISOWeek over >200,000 week dates spanning 1601-9999 by unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.TheIntegerWeekArithmetic_AgreesWithISOWeek_Everywhere, which asserts its own population so it cannot pass vacuously. ⛔ THE TEST GAP THIS ROW NAMED IS ALSO CLOSED: the golden carries Annex D.31.5.8's and D.31.5.9's OWN worked examples — "YYYYMMDD"/"19950215" and "YYYYMMDDThhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"19950215T05142781+0500" both -> 143951, and "hhmmss.ss+hhmm"/"05142781+0500" and its combined form both -> 18867.81 — so the §15.48.4 / §15.79.4 NOTE that the other half "does not impact the returned value" is now verified by TEST rather than by code reading.

subject: SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: Citation validated: cite.py --check 15.83.4 'The value returned is equal to the positive algebraic value of smallest finite magnitude that may be used to increment argument-1' -> OK (rule 2), with the NOTE table read from specs/ISO_COBOL.md 33280-33291. Code READ: BindAlgebraicFold -- 'if (sig.Name == SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC) return new BoundNumLiteral(Decimalize(BigInteger.One, pic.Scale, negative: false));' -- a compile-time fold to 10^(-scale) taken BEFORE the HIGHEST/LOWEST capacity branches, so it is independent of digit count, sign and container, which is exactly what r2 says (the smallest INCREMENT, not the smallest representable magnitude of the item's range). Decimalize delegates to CobolNet.Runtime.CobolNum.FormatFunctionText, the same renderer the runtime uses for a computed intrinsic's text, so a NEGATIVE scale (trailing P) appends |scale| zeros and a positive scale inserts the point -- one rule, one place. Every row of the r2 NOTE table checked against a golden or a spec test rather than sampled: S999 -> 1, 99V9(3) -> 0.001 and S9PP -> 100 by SmallestAlgebraic_PictureIncrement_Spec (DISPLAY-exact) and by golden 2023/intrinsics_smallest_algebraic; S9(4) BINARY -> +1 by golden 2023/smallest_algebraic (MOVE to PIC +99999.999 gives '+00001.000'); BINARY-CHAR UNSIGNED -> 1 by golden 2023/intrinsics_smallest_algebraic (a usage-only item carries Scale 0). Result type is separately correct (IntrinsicResultRule.IntegerFollowsArgument1, the 15.83.1 two-row table). Citation re-derived (cite.py --check 15.83.4 with the full rule-2 sentence -> OK rule 2). THE FIXED-POINT HALF IS VERIFIED and I strengthened it: the adjudicator asserted the BINARY-CHAR SIGNED row 'cannot differ' without reading the factory, so I read PicInfo.cs:318-328 -- PicInfo.BinaryItem(usage, signed) constructs 'Scale: 0' unconditionally, the 'signed' argument affecting only Digits (BinaryDouble 19 vs 20) and the Signed flag -- so the claim is now evidenced rather than assumed; likewise CobolNum.FormatFunctionText (CobolNum.cs:608-628) was read and its scale<0 arm ('digits + new string(0, -scale)') and scale>0 arm (PadLeft then insert the point) give exactly 100 for S9PP and 0.001 for 99V9(3). subject: SQRT function
notes: CONFORMS. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.84.3 "The value of argument-1 shall be zero or positive"` -> OK §15.84.3 2). THIS IS A VALUE CONSTRAINT, SO THE DISPOSITION THE STANDARD ASKS FOR IS A RUN-TIME EC, NOT A COMPILE-TIME REJECT — §15.3 closing paragraph, read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29561: 'The rules for a function may place constraints on the permissible values for arguments... If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument... the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist... If the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist and checking for EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION is not enabled, the implementor defines the result of the function reference.' So no COBOLNET diagnostic is owed even for the literal FUNCTION SQRT(-4). READ: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Sqrt (line 28) is `Math.Sqrt(x)`, which is NaN for every x < 0, and the NaN is screened on ALL THREE arms IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderFloat can emit — I checked each rather than the one: (a) the fixed-receiver arm quantizes through CobolIntrinsics.cs#FromDouble, whose first line is `if (double.IsNaN(d)) return Exceptions.ExceptionState.ArgumentError(...)`; (b) the float-receiver / receiver-less arm (line 431) returns CobolIntrinsics.cs#RealResult(call), which is `double.IsNaN(d) ? ArgumentError(...) : d`; (c) the standard-decimal arm (line 441) wraps the SAME RealResult before CobolDec.FromDouble, so the conversion never sees a NaN either. Arm (b)/(c)'s screen exists precisely because PB13 moved the raise site out from under the unquantized render and a refuter caught it. ExceptionState.cs#ArgumentError (line 248) carries BOTH dispositions the standard names: with ArgumentFunctionChecking set it does Set("EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION", fatal: true) and throws CobolFatalException (§14.6.13.1, Table 13 Fatal); with checking clear it returns 0, the §15.3 implementor-defined default. NO SPURIOUS RAISE AT THE BOUNDARY: -0.0 satisfies 'zero or positive' and Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0, not NaN, so the screen does not fire on it. GOLDEN: conformance:2023/pb13_domain_raise_receiver_shape line 38 asserts SQRT-NEG=DEFAULT for FUNCTION SQRT(-1) written as a RECEIVER-LESS relation operand — the exact arm that had no screen before PB13 — and its header derives the disposition from §15.3/§15.4. WHAT NO TEST COVERS, verified by reading only: the checking-ENABLED throw for SQRT specifically (no fixture turns EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking on over SQRT — ExceptionState.cs#ArgumentError is the single raise site for the whole family, so this is one branch of one method, not an unaudited path), and the with-receiver COMPUTE arm for SQRT (pb13 pins that arm for ACOS, which shares FromDouble byte-for-byte). REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Citation re-derived independently, not inherited: `cite.py --check 15.84.3 "The value of argument-1 shall be zero or positive"` -> OK §15.84.3 2); the §15.3 disposition paragraph the adjudicator leans on also re-derives (`--check 15.3 "the implementor defines the result of the function reference"` -> OK §15.3 item 14), and §14.6.13.1.1 NOTE 3 (read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:21334ff, "An exception condition is set to exist only if checking for that condition is enabled") confirms that NOT recording the condition with checking off is correct. So the disposition MODEL is right. WHAT IS NOT RIGHT IS THE DETECTOR, and it is invisible to every arm the adjudicator checked because he checked the RENDER arms and not the ARGUMENT CHANNEL. THE CONSTRAINT IS TESTED ON A NARROWED VALUE, NOT ON argument-1. There is no domain guard on the SQRT body at all: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:28 is a bare `Math.Sqrt(x)` and the whole family's detection is the NaN artifact. That is sound only while the double the body receives has the same SIGN as argument-1 — and it does not. IntrinsicRenderer.Dbl -> NumericRenderer.Real (NumericRenderer.cs:697) converts an SDIDI operand as `(expr).ToDouble()`, and CobolDec.cs:310 is `(double)Sig * Math.Pow(10, Exp)`. For Exp <= -324 `Math.Pow(10, Exp)` underflows to +0.0, so a NEGATIVE SDIDI becomes -0.0 (verified at the IEEE level: (-1.0)*pow(10,-400) = -0.0, signbit -1), and Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0 — NOT NaN. Nothing downstream can recover it: RealResult and FromDouble screen `double.IsNaN` ONLY. CONCRETE, LEGAL SOURCE: under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL with `01 A PIC S9V9(30) VALUE -0.000000000000000000000000000001` (= -1E-30, 31 digit positions, legal per §13.18.40.3 SR14), `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SQRT(A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A * A)` hands the function the exact SDIDI -1E-330 — comfortably inside decimal128's exponent range, so CobolDec carries it — whose value is NEGATIVE and therefore violates §15.84.3 r2. The compiler returns 0 and sets NOTHING: no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION with checking off (where §15.3's implementor-defined result would at least be defensible), and NO RAISE EVEN WITH CHECKING ON, which §14.6.13.1.1 requires. The rule's ordinary half (a plainly negative argument) IS enforced; its underflow half is not — two halves, one verified, so PARTIAL per rule 5. THE SIBLING IN THE SAME FILE IS THE PROOF THIS IS A MISS AND NOT A DESIGN: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs:32-33 give LOG and LOG10 an EXPLICIT `x <= 0` guard that names §15.55.3 r2 / §15.56.3 r2 at the BODY, precisely so the domain verdict does not ride on a NaN artifact. SQRT's rule has the same shape and got no guard — and its own in-code comment misnames the clause it is honouring ("argument ≥ 0 (rule 1)"; r1 is the CLASS rule, r2 is the value rule). The fix is a body guard `x < 0 -> ArgumentError("§15.84.3 r2")` beside LOG's, which also closes the -0.0 case by construction. TEST-REF UNCHANGED BUT IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE ROW: pb13_domain_raise_receiver_shape line 38 is `IF FUNCTION SQRT(-1) = 0` — the checking-OFF receiver-less arm only. Nothing anywhere turns EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking on over SQRT (the adjudicator concedes this), and nothing exercises a standard-decimal argument at all. test-needed.

subject: SQRT function
notes: CONFORMS. Citation re-validated: `cite.py --check 15.84.4 "the returned value is the absolute value of the approximation of the square root of argument-1"` -> OK §15.84.4 4). The rule leaves 'the approximation' undefined, and §15.4.1 supplies the latitude for native mode, read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:29777: 'When native arithmetic is in effect, the characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor.' READ: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Sqrt line 28 is `Math.Sqrt(x)`; IEC 60559 requires sqrt to be correctly rounded, so this is the best binary64 approximation available, not merely a plausible one. ALL THREE RENDER ARMS CHECKED at IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderFloat rather than the one: (a) a float receiver or a receiver-less context (line 431) returns CobolIntrinsics.cs#RealResult(call) UNQUANTIZED, so FUNCTION SQRT(2) and a COMP-2 item holding that value are the same number — the §15.4 receiver-independence PB13 restored; (b) a fixed-point receiver (line 452) quantizes through CobolIntrinsics.cs#FromDouble at ReceiverContext.FloatWorkingScale (>=9, capped at the receiver's Int128 headroom so the PB5/PB13 9.2e9 saturation cannot reach a declarable receiver), rounding rather than truncating at the quantization point — an approximation landed at the receiver's own scale, which is what §15.4.1 leaves to the implementor; (c) SQRT's catalog row carries Codomain.None, and that is CORRECT rather than an omission — §15.84.4 states no bound on the returned value, so the FromDoubleBounded clamp (which exists for RANDOM's open [0,1) and ASIN/ACOS/ATAN's irrational pi bounds) must not apply here. THE 'ABSOLUTE VALUE' HALF IS VACUOUS BUT I CHECKED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMED IT: §15.84.3 r2 confines argument-1 to zero-or-positive, and Math.Sqrt(x) >= 0 for every x >= 0 (Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0, which is zero, not negative), so no sign correction is owed and none is missing; a negative argument is an AR-15.84.3-2 violation that takes the NaN -> EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION path instead of yielding a value at all, so it never reaches this rule. THE ABSOLUTE-VALUE HALF WAS DECLARED VACUOUS AND IS NOT, AND IT WAS DECLARED VACUOUS BY THE ONE ARGUMENT THAT FAILS. The adjudicator wrote 'Math.Sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0, which is zero, not negative, so no sign correction is owed and none is missing'. The rule does not say 'made non-negative when negative'; it says the returned value IS THE ABSOLUTE VALUE of the approximation, and IEEE abs clears the sign bit: |-0.0| = +0.0 while sqrt(-0.0) = -0.0 (verified: signbit -1 vs +1). subject: SUM function
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB252). THE PRIOR RECORD'S OWN LANE (b) DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG, and that is what this landing corrects. It read: '`case "SumScaled" or "RangeScaled"` takes AlignedArgs ... and calls CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled (`Int128 s = 0; foreach (x) s += x`) ... the alignment is escape-checked (CobolNum.RescaleEscape), so an argument that cannot be represented in the Int128 intermediate raises the size-error condition instead of wrapping.' RescaleEscape bounds each ALIGNED ARGUMENT and says nothing about their SUM: `Int128.Abs(value) > Int128.MaxValue / Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale)`. MEASURED on the compiler's own exe before the fix, inside the 31-digit cap: `P PIC S9(31) VALUE ALL '9'` beside `Q PIC SV9(7)`, `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SUM(P P P Q) ON SIZE ERROR ...` -- each aligned argument (9.99e37) passes the per-argument bound (1.70e31 at scale 7), their sum 2.9999e38 exceeds Int128.MaxValue and wrapped to -4.028e37, which at scale 7 fits a 31-digit receiver, so the phrase was NOT taken and a SIGN-FLIPPED value was stored silently. The EAE's true value (3x10^31 - 3) needs 32 digits, so Sec.14.7.5 rule 3 makes the size error condition exist there with NO implementor latitude at all. FIX: the accumulator is now `checked` under one try for the whole loop and escapes through CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SizeEscape -> CobolSizeError/EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW, which ArithmeticEmitter lands on the ON SIZE ERROR arm leaving the receiver unchanged (Sec.14.7.5 rule 1). GOVERNING CLAUSE CORRECTED IN THE SAME CHANGE: the message text had carried PB32's inherited 'ISO Sec.8.8.1.2 rule 7', which is a REAL clause answering a DIFFERENT question (arithmetic expressions are exempt from the composite-of-operands limit); the rule that makes this the size error condition is Sec.14.7.5 rule 5 -- 'if native arithmetic is in effect and the implementor defines that the range of values allowed for the intermediate data item is to be checked, when an arithmetic operation on the intermediate data item would cause the new value to be outside of the allowed range' (--check 14.7.5 -> OK). ALL THREE LANES NOW READ AND EACH IS THE Sec.15.88.4 r1 EAE: (a) standard modes -> SumDec on the SDIDI, left to right; (b) NATIVE fixed-point -> the checked Int128 accumulator, exact until the D1 boundary and then LOUD; (c) NATIVE with a float argument -> SumReal. Left-to-right accumulation is normative (Sec.8.8.1.2 rule 3, --check OK), so a partial sum that escapes the carrier IS an r5 size error even when later terms would bring the total back inside -- the modular cancellation the old unchecked `s += x` happened to deliver was two's complement's answer, not the standard's. CLOSING EVIDENCE: conformance:2002/pb252_native_carrier_boundary pins the r3 case (no latitude) and a control well inside the carrier; the drift test closes the whole exact-carrier entry-point set by reflection, so a new variadic exact function cannot ship unguarded. Both were verified to FAIL on the pre-fix build (SUM-R3-SIZE-ERROR=NO, RANGE-SIGN=NEGATIVE). EDITIONS: carried forward as adjudicated; the witness itself needs 31-digit items so it lives in the 2002 corpus (COBOL-85 caps fixed-point at 18 digits, COBOLNET0802).

subject: TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD function
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB254). The PARTIAL was leg a's UPPER half, defeated above 2**63 by the intake, not by the body. CITATIONS RE-DERIVED MECHANICALLY, none inherited: cite.py --check 15.90.4 "less than 16 010 000 or greater than 99 999 999" -> OK (15.90.4 1) a)); --check 15.90.4 "The year is not within the range 1601 to 9999" -> OK (1) a) NOTE 1); --check 15.90.4 "The date is valid" -> OK (1) d) NOTE 4); --check 15.90.3 "Argument-1 shall be an integer" -> OK (15.90.3 rule 1); --check 15.3 "results in an incorrect value for that argument" -> OK (15.3 rule 14); --check 8.3.3.3.2 "fixed-point numeric literals of 1 through 31 digits" -> OK. THE DERIVATION. 15.90.3 r1 is the WHOLE argument rule and constrains nothing but integer-ness; 15.90.4 r1a is a CATCH-ALL over both directions, so the function is TOTAL over the integers and every integer argument has a defined verdict. 15.3 rule 14 sets EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION only when evaluation 'results in an incorrect value for that argument or for the returned value according to the rules specified in the function definition' - there is no such value here, so a conforming program may pass any integer and must receive a verdict, never an abort. THE DEFECT, re-probed on this tree before the fix, not inherited from the note: (a) FLOAT lane - 01 FBIG USAGE COMP-2, COMPUTE FBIG = 1.0E19, FUNCTION TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD(FBIG) printed 00, i.e. 1) d) 'The date is valid', where r1a requires 1; the body was CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs#TestDateYyyymmddReal = 'TryIntegerArg(...) ? CobolDate.TestDateYyyymmdd(n) : 0' and the literal ': 0' tail is the verdict for VALID. (b) CHECKING-ON lane - '>>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON' with 01 BIG19 PIC 9(19) VALUE 9999999999999999999 terminated the run unit: 'abnormal run-unit termination: EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION (fatal): the intrinsic integer argument 9999999999999999999 is outside the range the function can represent (ISO 15.3)' - on CONFORMING source. (c) NATIVE/Dec lane printed 01, the right code by COINCIDENCE ONLY: CobolIntrinsics.IntegerArg substituted the checking-off default 0 for the ARGUMENT and 0 lands in the same r1a arm (0 < 16 010 000); the coincidence evaporates under checking, which is lane (b). THE FIX is at the validator, never at the shared narrowing: CobolDate.TestDateYyyymmdd now takes Int128 and answers r1a before any conversion (past the guard the value is eight digits, so the int narrowing is exact); IntrinsicRenderer's 'case "TestDateYyyymmdd" or "TestDayYyyyddd"' arm takes the WIDE intake IntArgWide -> AsIntWide, which has no raise point and, unlike AsInt, carries the U (UInt128) carrier arm as well; TestDateYyyymmddReal classifies by r1a on the VALUE, so +/-infinity and every magnitude past the window answer 1 without narrowing, and the one input that is the value of no integer (a NaN) routes to the shared 15.3 raise site and substitutes the documented implementor-defined result 1, never the 0 that would call a non-date a valid date. STRUCTURE, so the next case is automatic: the intake width is now derived from the runtime body's DECLARED carrier (Int128 = total, long = bounded), and IntrinsicCarrierAgreementDriftTests.EveryTotalIntegerArgument_TakesTheWideIntake re-derives that pairing by reflection and fails when an arm and its body disagree. The guard was proven RED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS on the shipped renderer before being trusted: reverting this arm produced 'TestDateYyyymmdd: body declares Int128 ... but the arm narrows' plus its sibling, and a stray widening of the DateOfInteger/DayOfInteger/IntegerOfDate/IntegerOfDay arm (whose 15.5.2 domain IS bounded, so the 15.3 landing is right there) produced the opposite four. THE GOLDEN that closes the row is conformance:2002/pb254_total_integer_arguments, which pins r1a's UPPER half on every carrier an integer argument can arrive on - T1 100000000 -> 1; T2 99999999 -> 2, proving the bound is EXCLUSIVE and that r1a did not swallow the boundary (MOD(99999999 10000) = 9999 > 1299, so r1b fires); T3 a 19-digit LITERAL (8.3.3.3.2 requires 1..31 digits be accepted) -> 1; T4 a PIC 9(19) item -> 1; T5 a PIC 9(31) item -> 1; T6 the 15.3 type-6 arithmetic-expression witness P18 * 100 + 62 = 2**64 + 1 995 046 -> 1; T7 a FLOAT-LONG item holding 1.0E19 -> 1 - and it runs the whole program under >>TURN EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION CHECKING ON with an ARMED CONTROL, because a checking-ON leg proves nothing if the directive is inert: leg ARMED raises the condition deliberately from FUNCTION INTEGER-OF-DAY, whose 15.5.2 argument form IS bounded, and the USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION declarative reports 'ARMED=EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION' before RESUME AT NEXT STATEMENT leaves the receiver at its 99 preset. subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes:
CITATION RE-VALIDATED BY ME: cite.py --check 15.92.4 "the value returned is the ordinal character position at which the first error in argument-2 was detected" -> OK (§15.92.4 1)).

BOTH HALVES READ IN THE IMPLEMENTATION, NEVER SAMPLED. CobolDate#TestFormattedDatetime is a one-line pass-through (`=> Analyze(format, data, out _, out _, out _, out _, leapSecond)`), so CobolDate#Analyze IS this rule and is the code-location.
(a) ZERO. Analyze returns 0 only after every format segment has been consumed AND `pos == data.Length`; every other exit is non-zero.
(b) THE ORDINAL POSITION. Every failure arm returns `pos + 1`, the 1-BASED index of the character under examination: a separator segment whose character does not appear (`data[pos] != s.Sep`), an offset-sign character that is not '+'/'-'/'0', data exhausted mid-field, a non-digit in a digit subfield, a subfield provably out of range, and the first TRAILING character (`if (pos != data.Length) return pos + 1`).

⛔ THE LOAD-BEARING PART IS "THE FIRST ERROR ... DETECTED", AND IT IS IMPLEMENTED AS PER-DIGIT RANGE NARROWING RATHER THAN A PER-FIELD CHECK — a per-field check would have reported the START of the offending field and failed the NOTE. After consuming digit k of a width-w subfield, Analyze widens the partial value into [mn, mx] by appending the w-1-k digits still to come (`mn *= 10; mx = mx*10 + 9`) and returns pos+1 the moment `mx < lo || mn > hi`. I HAND-TRACED BOTH OF THE NOTE'S OWN EXAMPLES through that loop:
 · "yyyymmdd"/"20051314": the month subfield is [1,12]; at its first digit '1' the interval is [10,19], which straddles 12, so nothing is provable yet; at '3' it is [13,13] and 13 > 12, so the return is pos+1 = 6. That is the NOTE's 6 AND the NOTE's reason ("the character '3' occupies the first position in which it can be determined that an error has occurred").
 · "yyyymmdd"/"15990316": the year subfield is [1601,9999] (§15.3.1.3's "greater than 1600"); at '1' the interval is [1000,1999], which straddles 1601; at '5' it is [1500,1599] and 1599 < 1601, so the return is 2 — the NOTE's 2, for the NOTE's reason.
I checked the subfield bounds against the spec text rather than the comments: §15.3.3.3 verbatim gives hours "00 to 23", minutes "00 to 59", seconds "< 60" with LEAP-SECOND OFF and "< 61" with ON; Analyze uses (0,23), (0,59) and (0, leapSecond ? 60 : 59). Month is [1,12], day-of-month is bounded by DateTime.DaysInMonth of the already-parsed year/month, day-of-year by the leap year, week by LongIsoYear, weekday [1,7]. The Fraction subfield is deliberately EXEMPT from narrowing, which is right — §15.3.3.2 puts no range on it.

DELIBERATE, AND CORRECT UNDER THIS RULE: `dateRepresentable` is ignored here. "9999W526" satisfies every §15.3.1.7 subfield rule yet has no §15.5.2 integer date form; §15.92.4 can only answer with the position of a character IN ERROR and none of those characters is (the identical '6' in "2009W526" is valid), so 0 is the only answer the rule admits. INTEGER-OF-FORMATTED-DATE, which must PRODUCE the integer date form, raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION on the same input — the two callers of the shared analyzer diverge exactly where their rules do (kb/Work PB23, landed).

TEST EVIDENCE — six spec-derived refs that between them hit every error CLASS the narrowing implements, and I checked each is not a net. IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.TestFormattedDatetime_ErrorPosition_2014 carries both NOTE examples plus a valid value -> 0; despite the class name it is NOT a differential — I read AssertSpec at IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.cs:26 and it compiles, runs and compares against a WRITTEN literal, with no legacy engine in the path. conformance:2014/formatted_datetime pins the same two through the golden (TF1=+000000006, TF2=+000000002) and a valid combined round-trip (FCD=+000000000). conformance:2023/pb65_leap_second_off/_on pin the LEAP-SECOND-dependent seconds bound at DIGIT granularity and I re-derived all three from the loop: "hhmmss"/"235960" -> 5 with OFF (at the '6' the interval is [60,69] and mn 60 > hi 59) and 0 with ON; "235961" -> 6 with ON (at the '6' [60,69] straddles hi 60; at the '1' it is [61,61] > 60). conformance:2023/pb23_week_date_beyond_integer_date_form pins the 0-for-an-unrepresentable-week-date reading and week 53 in a 52-week ISO year -> 7. unit:CobolDateIntegerDateRangeTests.GenuinelyInvalidData_StillReportsItsErrorPosition adds Feb 31 -> 7 and day-of-year 366 in a common year -> 7 (I re-derived both: at the leading '3' the day interval is [30,39] and mn 30 > 28, and [30,39] > 29 of a 365-day year's third digit respectively).

⚠ READ BUT NOT TESTED, named so it cannot be mistaken for coverage: a separator that does not match ("2021/06/16" against "YYYY-MM-DD"), a non-digit inside a subfield, the offset-sign arm together with §15.3.3.6.1's zero-sign-implies-zero-magnitude narrowing (`if (offZero && s.Field is Fld.OffHour or Fld.OffMinute) hi = 0;`), and a NATIONAL argument-2 (positions would be counted in UTF-16 units, one per national character position — correct by construction, but unexercised).
⚠ ONE SHAPE THE RULE DOES NOT COVER AND THE CODE ANSWERS ANYWAY: an argument-2 SHORTER than the format leaves no character in error, and Analyze returns data.Length + 1. §15.92.4 is silent on it. The standard's OWN convention for the same shape is §15.93.4 r1 c) for TEST-NUMVAL, `(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1)` — cite.py --check 15.93.4 "(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1)" -> OK — so this is a consistent implementor answer within the same standard, not a divergence. An argument-2 LONGER than the format is covered by the rule and is answered correctly (the first extra character's position).

EDITIONS from the standard: Annex E (2014->2023) carries no occurrence of TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME, so §15.92.4 is unchanged at 2023; the landed sibling AR-15.92.3-2 on this function records the same 2014,2023 window. NOT taken from IntrinsicCatalog's own row.

REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Three findings; the first is a two-arm bound where only one arm was checked, on the very method that IS this rule.
Citation re-derived by me: cite.py --check 15.92.4 "the value returned is the ordinal character position at which the first error in argument-2 was detected" -> OK (§15.92.4 1)).
⛔ (1) THE OFFSET SUBFIELD BOUNDS WERE VERIFIED AGAINST THE WRONG CLAUSE. The adjudication states it checked the subfield bounds against the spec text and names §15.3.3.3 — "hours '00 to 23', minutes '00 to 59'" — then lists "Analyze uses (0,23), (0,59)". But those two switch arms are SHARED: `Fld.Hour => (0, 23)` is joined by `Fld.OffHour => (0, 23)`, and the minutes arm is written `Fld.Minute or Fld.OffMinute => (0, 59)` — ONE expression serving TWO subfields. §15.3.3.3 governs only one of them, by its own words: cite.py --check 15.3.3.3 "The minutes subfield of the data (corresponding to mm in a common time format) shall contain a value from 00 to 59 inclusive" -> OK, and the offset subformat is NOT part of the common time format — §15.3.3.6.1 defines the offset-hours and offset-minutes subfields separately (cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.1 "two lowercase 'h' characters representing the hours portion of the offset from UTC" -> OK). The clause that actually governs them is §15.3.3.6.2, which the adjudication never located: "The offset-hours subfield of the data associated with a basic or extended offset time format shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive" / "… offset-minutes … from 00 to 59 inclusive" (specs/ISO_COBOL.md :29747, :29749). I ran that clause down expecting an invented range and the VALUES turn out right — but a bound justified by a clause that does not cover it is an unverified bound, and §15.92.4's answer is conditioned on exactly "format problems or RANGE problems". Neither `Fld.OffHour` nor `Fld.OffMinute` carries a citation in the source, while every neighbouring bound does. Rule 5: an edge unverified => PARTIAL.
⛔ (2) THE SHORT-ARGUMENT-2 ANSWER IS OUTSIDE THE RULE'S CODOMAIN, AND ITS DEFENCE IS A CLAUSE ABOUT A DIFFERENT FUNCTION. When argument-2 is shorter than the format, Analyze's `if (pos >= data.Length) return pos + 1;` yields data.Length + 1 — a position that does not exist in argument-2 — where §15.92.4 admits only "the ordinal character position at which the first error IN ARGUMENT-2 was detected". The input is REACHABLE: §15.92.3 places no size rule on argument-2 and the compiler applies none — I read the row, `Schema("§15.92.3 r1/r2", ['s','s'], cross: MatchArgument1)`, and it carries no ArgPredicate width at either position (contrast TRIM's `.WithPredicate(1, ArgPredicate.ExactWidth(1, …))` five rows above it). The adjudication defends the answer with §15.93.4 r1 c)'s `(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1)` — a real, --check-able clause that legislates TEST-NUMVAL's returned value, not this function's; that is the a_real_clause_can_answer_a_different_question shape, and it is the whole of the evidence offered. No test covers the shape and docs/CONFORMANCE.md carries no determination for it (its only §15.92 entry is item 112, the LEAP-SECOND one).
⛔ (3) THE "BOTH NOTE EXAMPLES" CLAIM IS NOT WHAT THE CODE DOES. §15.92.4's NOTE writes `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME ("yyyymmdd", A-DATE)` in LOWERCASE. Both recognisers are case-SENSITIVE: CobolDate.Tokenize's switch matches 'Y'/'M'/'D' uppercase only (lowercase falls to `default` -> `return null`, and Analyze then answers 1), and DateTimeFormatGrammar.BasicDates holds the literal strings ["YYYYMMDD", "YYYYDDD", "YYYYWwwD"], so bind-time Classify returns null and the reference is rejected with DateTimeFormatKindMismatch. The NOTE's own program does not compile. That is DEFENSIBLE — §15.3.1.2 normatively requires "four uppercase 'Y' characters … two uppercase 'M' characters", and a NOTE is not normative — but the adjudication asserts "I HAND-TRACED BOTH OF THE NOTE'S OWN EXAMPLES" and every test silently substitutes uppercase (grep for "yyyymmdd" across tests/ returns nothing). The traced program is not the NOTE's program, and the substitution was never recorded.

(2) "the total number of digits" is counted across BOTH sides of the decimal separator — the counter is incremented in the single digit arm that serves the integer and fraction parts alike. (3) "if no prior error is found" holds structurally: the cap test lives inside the digit loop, so any earlier malformation has already broken the loop or returned, and any LATER malformation is at a higher position than the digit that trips the cap — so the reported position is still the FIRST character in error under leg b. The cap is tested BEFORE the accumulator multiplies, so the value projection cannot saturate into a plausible number (the PB33/PB34 defect this ordering was written for). I read tests/version-matrix/traceability-inventory.json directly: RV-15.27.3-2 (§15.27.3, subject "E function") and RV-15.73.3-2 (§15.73.3, subject "PI function") both carry verdict NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION, editions "2014,2023" and an EMPTY test-ref, and RV-15.27.3-2's note independently records the same COBOLNET0806 mechanism re-verified on the built CLI. (2) The diagnostic is a hard Error, not a warning: DataBinder.cs:318-320 reads exactly as quoted, `Edition.Error("COBOLNET0806", ...)`, and the surrounding comment (306-320) confirms the mode is documented-unsupported at EVERY edition that has it. NOT-IMPLEMENTED would be the code-only verdict, and I considered recording it, but batch rule 6 reserves the documented-non-support disposition to the owner and the sibling rows fix the family's shape; the bare question stands as put. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). subject: TEST-NUMVAL-F function
notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: `cite.py --check 15.95.3 "Argument-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal or a data item of class alphanumeric or national."` -> OK, §15.95.3 rule 1. CODE READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified carries `["TEST-NUMVAL-F"] = Uniform('s', "§15.95.3 r1")` (line 687), screened by IntrinsicBinder.CheckArgumentClasses, which deliberately drives off the Verified table and NOT off sig.ArgKinds ("the catalog's hint column is unaudited", line 1654), calling IntrinsicArgumentRules.Violation over `Admissible('s') = [Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National]` (line 874) with the §8.3.3.6.4 GR4 candidate-set intersection. WHAT r1 EXCLUDES AND WE REJECT (verified through ClassOf1/ClassOfPlace/ClassOfCategory): class NUMERIC (a numeric literal binds BoundNumericLiteral -> CobolClass.Numeric; a PIC 9 item -> PicCategory.Numeric -> CobolClass.Numeric), class BOOLEAN (a B"..." literal carries Category Boolean, a PIC 1 item likewise), class POINTER/OBJECT, and class INDEX (ClassOfPlace's `Usage.Index` arm, which rides BEFORE the category table). WHAT r1 ADMITS AND WE ADMIT: alphanumeric literals and items, alphanumeric GROUP items (ClassOfPlace's IsGroup arm -> Alphanumeric, and a group IS a 'data item of class alphanumeric'), national literals (N"..." carries Category National) and national items, numeric-edited display items (§8.5.2.1 Table 2 puts category numeric-edited in class ALPHANUMERIC, so r1's 'class alphanumeric' reaches it — the NumericEditedDeEditing member is that class, per its own remark), and figurative constants (SPACE/ZERO present an alphanumeric or national character value, §8.3.3.6.4 GR4/GR1; the intersection test admits them, which is PB48's landed behaviour, not a hole). THE UNENFORCED HALF — CLASS ALPHABETIC. r1 names class alphanumeric or national and NOT class alphabetic, and the standard treats them as distinct: `cite.py --check 8.5.2.1 "Alphabetic"` -> OK, Table 2 row `| Alphabetic | Alphabetic |`, and `cite.py --check 15.96.3 "alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national"` -> OK, showing TRIM's r1 naming alphabetic EXPLICITLY where §15.95.3 r1 does not. This compiler cannot express the distinction at the screen: PicInfo.cs:14 documents PicCategory.Alphanumeric as "Alphanumeric (X) or alphabetic (A)", CobolClass (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:20) has no Alphabetic member, and ClassOfCategory therefore answers CobolClass.Alphanumeric for a PIC A(n) item — so `FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F(WS-ALPHA)` over `01 WS-ALPHA PIC A(10).` binds clean and runs, where r1 requires a diagnostic. This is an OVER-ACCEPT (legal source is never rejected), it is reachable at every edition the function exists in, and the datum needed to fix it already exists and is already used elsewhere (PicInfo.IsAlphabetic, PicInfo.cs:257, consulted by INITIALIZE's §14.9.20 GR5c/GR6c category matching); the 's' union is documented at IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs:869-871 as a deliberate over-approximation whose narrowing was left as 'a later refinement'. PARTIAL per rule 5: the rule has an admissible half (verified correct) and an exclusion half (one class of the exclusion, ALPHABETIC, unenforced). TEST-REF EMPTY: no negative fixture in tests/conformance/negative/ names TEST-NUMVAL-F (the pb58-numvalf-numeric / pb58-numvalf-literal negatives pin NUMVAL-F's row, a different function's clause), and no unit test asserts the TEST-NUMVAL-F screen; ZeroLengthLiteralArgumentDriftTests.TheTestNumvalFamily_IsNotSweptIn only asserts the ABSENCE of a zero-length prohibition, which is not this rule. EDITIONS from kb/Work R28's external evidence, not from IntrinsicCatalog's row. REFUTED: VERDICT SURVIVES (PARTIAL) after an independent read of the model; TWO facts are added that make the ENFORCED half weaker than the note implies, and neither of them rescues a CONFORMS. CITATIONS RE-DERIVED BY ME: `--check 15.95.3 "Argument-1 shall be an alphanumeric or national literal or a data item of class alphanumeric or national."` -> OK §15.95.3 1); `--check 8.5.2.1 "Alphabetic"` -> OK, Table 2 carries its own `| Alphabetic | Alphabetic |` row, so class alphabetic is a DISTINCT class; `--check 15.96.3 "alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national"` -> OK §15.96.3 1), which is the standard naming alphabetic where it means it and §15.95.3 r1 not doing so. THE ALPHABETIC HOLE IS CONFIRMED FROM THE CODE, not from the note: CobolClass has no Alphabetic member (its own remark says the distinction 'is not recoverable here'), PicInfo's PicCategory comment reads 'Alphanumeric (X) or alphabetic (A)' for the single Alphanumeric member, ClassOfPlace ends `p.Item.Pic is { } pic ? ClassOfCategory(pic.Category) : null` and ClassOfCategory maps PicCategory.Alphanumeric -> CobolClass.Alphanumeric — so a `PIC A(10)` item presents the singleton {Alphanumeric}, intersects the 's' set `[Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National]`, and binds clean where r1 requires a diagnostic. PicInfo.IsAlphabetic (PicInfo.cs:257) exists and MoveTable16 already keys on it, so the datum is present and simply not consulted here. TWO ADDITIONS THE ADJUDICATOR DID NOT RECORD. (i) THE ENFORCED HALF IS DIALECT-CONDITIONAL: CheckArgumentClasses' local `Report` runs `if (ctx.Edition.Permissive) ctx.Edition.Warning(DiagnosticCatalog.IntrinsicArgumentClass, ...) else ctx.Edition.Error(...)`, so under `--permissive` even the exclusions that ARE modelled (numeric, boolean, pointer, index) are a warning and the coercion runs — documented dialect-gated leniency, but it means the 'verified correct' half is verified only under strict conformance. (ii) THE SCREEN FAILS OPEN wherever the class is not statically decidable: `Violation` returns null when `CandidateClasses(op).Length == 0`, and ClassOf1/ClassOfPlace/ClassOfCategory each answer null for an operand shape they do not model (an unmodelled figurative kind, a PICTURE-less place, an unlisted category) — so the rejecting half is a partial screen even inside the classes it can express. TEST-REF CONFIRMED EMPTY BY MY OWN LISTING of tests/conformance/negative/: the eleven numval fixtures are numval-c-ambiguous-currency, pb30-numval-c-currency-class, pb58-numval-numeric, pb58-numvalf-literal, pb58-numvalf-numeric, pb58-testnumval-num, the three pb60-numvalc-* and pb73-move-numval-function-to-national; `grep -rl TEST-NUMVAL-F tests/conformance/negative/` returns NOTHING. The row stays test-needed.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL-F function
notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: `cite.py --check 15.95.4 "the returned value is the position of the fifth digit of the exponent"` -> OK, §15.95.4 1) b) (list item 5). CODE READ: NvfScan's exponent scan counts exponent digits in `ed` and returns at the FIFTH one — `while (i < n && char.IsAsciiDigit(text[i])) { if (++ed > 4) return new(Pos(), false, false, 0, 0, 0); ev = ev * 10 + (text[i] - '0'); i++; }`. `Pos()` is `i + 1` and `i` has NOT yet advanced when the guard fires, so the value returned is the 1-based position OF THE FIFTH EXPONENT DIGIT ITSELF, exactly as the rule states ("1E+12345" -> 8, the ordinal of the '5'). VERIFIED ACROSS THE RULE'S TWO NAMED MODES: the arm is MODE-INDEPENDENT — the 4-digit exponent bound is hardcoded, not threaded from DigitCapFlag (which carries only the SIGNIFICAND cap) — so the standard-decimal half is satisfied, and the standard-binary half would be satisfied by the same code if the mode were admitted (it is not: DataBinder.BindDeclarations rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY with COBOLNET0806 at every edition, the documented non-support adjudicated on RV-15.27.3-2). I do not score that as an unverified half, because the behaviour this rule names does not vary by mode in this implementation and there is no second code path to leave unread. THE 'SIGNIFICANT DIGITS' WORDING WAS ATTACKED AND DOES NOT CHANGE THE ANSWER: on a leading-zero exponent such as "1E+00005" the code returns the fifth digit's position; if 'significant' is read strictly (one significant digit, so this rule would not fire), the base argument rule still rejects the string — `cite.py --check 15.69.3 "n is one, two, three, or four digits representing the exponent"` -> OK — and §15.95.4 1) b) then asks for 'the position of the first character in error', which is that same fifth digit because the format admits only a space-string or end-of-string after the fourth. Both readings land on the same number. ORDERING ALSO CHECKED: the scan is strictly left-to-right, so a significand error or a malformed sign returns before the exponent scan is entered, satisfying the family's 'no prior error ... has been found' precedence. TEST-REF EMPTY (rule 3): nothing in tests/ writes a five-digit exponent — IntrinsicFunctionDifferentialTests.TestNumvalF_Positions_2014's four cases and the pb60_numval_one_scan golden's ET row all stay within one exponent digit. CONFORMS-but-untested; the row stays test-needed. EDITIONS from kb/Work R28's external evidence, not from IntrinsicCatalog's row. REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. The citation re-derives (`cite.py --check 15.95.4 "the returned value is the position of the fifth digit of the exponent"` -> OK, §15.95.4 1) b), list item 5) and the arithmetic the adjudicator describes is correct as far as it goes — I re-traced `if (++ed > 4) return new(Pos(), ...)` myself: `i` has not advanced past the fifth digit when the guard fires, so `Pos() = i + 1` is that digit's own 1-based ordinal ("1E+12345" -> 8, and with the figure's optional space-strings "1E+ 12345" -> 9). The verdict still costs something on TWO grounds the adjudicator argued away rather than measured. (1) THE RULE NAMES TWO ARITHMETIC MODES AND ONLY ONE CAN EVER BE IN EFFECT HERE. The rule text is 'If standard-decimal arithmetic, OR STANDARD-BINARY ARITHMETIC is in effect ...'. I read DataBinder.BindDeclarations myself: `if (Options.Arithmetic == ArithmeticMode.StandardBinary) Edition.Error("COBOLNET0806", ...)` — a hard error at every edition, so no program this compiler translates can ever have standard-binary in effect and the standard-binary half of this rule is never satisfied by anything. The adjudicator dismissed that with 'the behaviour this rule names does not vary by mode in this implementation', which is an argument about the CODE, not about whether the rule's stated precondition can hold. The batch has already settled the shape the other way: RV-15.27.3-2, whose SOLE condition is standard-binary, was adjudicated NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION as the documented-non-support shape and explicitly NOT CONFORMS — and this batch's own RV-15.95.4-1 note concedes sub-note b.3 (the standard-binary 35-digit cap) is ABSENT. One half verified, one half unexercisable is PARTIAL by the batch rule, always. (2) AN UNVERIFIED EDGE INSIDE THE STANDARD-DECIMAL HALF — THE DIGIT COUNT AND THE SPACE RULE. §15.69.3 r5 (`--check 15.69.3 "Embedded spaces in argument-1 are ignored except between the first numeric digit and the last digit that precedes a letter 'E'"` -> OK) makes embedded spaces IGNORED everywhere outside the significand, while r1's figure draws `n` as a contiguous one-to-four-digit run with [space-string] only before and after it. Those two readings give different answers for an exponent written with an interior space, and they land squarely on THIS rule's 'more than four significant digits' count: for `TEST-NUMVAL-F("1E+1 2345")` I traced the code to 6 — the digit loop exits at the space with ed=1, the trailing-space skip advances to '2', and `if (i != n) return new(Pos(), ...)` reports it — where the r5 reading makes the exponent 12345, five digits, and this rule requires the position of its FIFTH digit, 9. The implementation resolves a normative tension silently: nothing in NvfScan, its comments, the design docs or any test records that the choice was made, and the r5 except-clause is implemented for the SIGNIFICAND (`pendingSpace`) and nowhere else. An edge on which the rule's own answer changes, resolved without evidence, is PARTIAL under the batch's cost rule. TWO THINGS I CHECKED THAT DID **NOT** MOVE THE VERDICT, recorded so they are not re-litigated: the mode-independence of the 4-digit bound is CORRECT under native, because §15.69.3 r1's 'where' clause caps n at 'one, two, three, or four digits' with no arithmetic-mode qualification, so under native the fifth digit is the first character in error under leg b) generic and the same number comes back; and the 'significant digits' wording converges on the same number for a leading-zero exponent ("1E+012345" -> the code returns the position of the fifth DIGIT of the exponent, 8, which is exactly what the rule's words say). I also re-confirmed there is no second lane to leave unread — RenderDec's `alwaysDec` list excludes TestNumvalF, its switch ends `_ => null`, and there is no compile-time intrinsic folder anywhere in the compiler. TEST-REF STAYS EMPTY: I searched tests/ myself and no test, golden or unit, writes an exponent of more than one digit to any TEST-NUMVAL-F. The row stays test-needed.

subject: TRIM function
notes: cite.py --check 15.96.3 'Argument-1 shall be a data item of class alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national.' -> OK (r1). READ: IntrinsicArgumentRules.Verified["TRIM"] = Schema("§15.96.3 r1/r2", ['s','s'], cross: MatchArgument1) — position 0 declares kind 's', and Admissible('s') = {Alphanumeric, NumericEditedDeEditing, National} (IntrinsicArgumentRules.Admissible), so Violation() rejects class numeric, boolean, index, object and pointer for argument-1. §8.5.2.1 Table 2 puts alphabetic and numeric-edited under alphanumeric, so 's' is exactly r1's three classes in this model (PicCategory folds PIC A into Alphanumeric — the CobolClass enum comment). The screen is REACHED on this bespoke path: IntrinsicBinder.BindTrim calls CheckArgumentClasses(sig, operands) at line 1010 before building the node (the generic path returns earlier), and CheckArgumentClasses walks schema.At(i). Positive coverage in both admitted rows: intrinsics_trim (PIC X(10) argument-1) and pb15_result_type_follows_argument (PIC N(8) and PIC X(8) argument-1, TRIM-N=[CDE] / TRIM-X=[CDE]). Figurative ZERO passes (candidate classes include alphanumeric — §8.3.3.6.4 GR4, PB48) and pb48_figurative_zero_intrinsic_argument pins it. NOT VERIFIED BY A FIXTURE: the rejection direction — no negative fixture feeds TRIM a class-numeric/pointer argument-1 (pb58-trim-arg2 tests r2's width, pb15-trim-national-result-to-an tests the §15.96.1 result table), so the row stays test-needed on that half; the code path was read instead. Deliberate latitude recorded, NOT scored as a defect: r1 says 'a DATA ITEM', and the implementation also admits an alphanumeric/national LITERAL argument-1. That is what §15.6 Table 21 types TRIM's argument-1 as (Alph1 or Anum1 or Nat1) and what §15.3 type 2 admits ('A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or an alphanumeric literal'), and §15.96.4's own NOTE writes TRIM("aabbcc" "c" "b") — rejecting a literal would reject the standard's own example. Editions from Annex §E.3.3 item 31 (--check OK: 'The TRIM function has been enhanced…', i.e. TRIM predates 2023) plus kb/Work R28's landed primary-source decision (WG4/J4 CD 1.2 Annex D.2 lists TRIM among the 2014 introductions); NOT derived from the IntrinsicCatalog row. REFUTED: verdict SUSTAINED — attacked on three axes and it held. (a) The load-bearing latitude citation was NOT inherited: I re-ran cite.py --check 15.3 'A data item of the class alphabetic or alphanumeric or an alphanumeric literal shall be specified' -> OK (§15.3 2), and read §15.6's own legend in the transcription ('A digit immediately following the argument type indicates the argument's position in the list of arguments') beside the Table 21 TRIM row at specs/ISO_COBOL.md — 'Alph1 or Anum1 or Nat1, Alph2 … or Anum2 … or Nat2 … or Key2 or Key2 and Alph2 …'. The literal admission is the standard's, and the Key2-then-Alph2 ordering independently corroborates the FMT-15.96.2 order finding. (b) The REJECT half was re-read rather than accepted: IntrinsicArgumentRules.CandidateClasses/ClassOf1 return a FIXED class for every operand shape that could carry a forbidden argument-1 — BoundComputedOperand{Expr: BoundIntrinsicCall} → ClassOfCategory(ic.ResultCategory), BoundComputedOperand{Expr: BoundIndexRef} → Index, bare BoundComputedOperand → Numeric, BoundFigurative 'N' (NULL) → Pointer, and ClassOfPlace keys USAGE INDEX before the category table — none is in Admissible('s'), so Violation() REPORTS instead of the candidates.Length==0 fail-open. FUNCTION TRIM(FUNCTION ABS(N)) is a compile-time §15.3 rejection, not the run-time StrArgVisitor LoudValue abort (the wrong-stage family). (c) The ALL shape was checked, since FUNCTION TRIM(ALL T) puts a TableAllPlace at position 0: ClassOfPlace reads p.Item, so argument-1's class is still screened there. The editions claim was chased to its source rather than inherited — kb/Work/R28.md's 'LANDED 2026-08-08' section names the WG4/J4 CD 1.2 (2009-08-23) Annex D.2 item 4 list verbatim, and R28's earlier body explicitly warns the 2023 PDF cannot settle a 2002 window; the adjudicator used the landed half, correctly.

subject: TRIM function
notes: cite.py --check 15.96.3 'argument-2 shall be a single character that is either class alphabetic or class alphanumeric' -> OK (r2). VERIFIED for the FIRST argument-2 only. READ: Verified["TRIM"] = Schema("§15.96.3 r1/r2", ['s','s'], cross: CrossArgRule.MatchArgument1, crossClause: "§15.96.3 r2").WithPredicate(1, ArgPredicate.ExactWidth(1, "§15.96.3 r2")). Position 1 therefore carries BOTH halves of r2: the width half (PredicateViolation ExactWidth over IntrinsicBinder.KnownWidth — a literal's Length, an item's ImageWidth, which DataItem.ImageWidth keeps in character positions and never byte-doubles for national, so a PIC N(1) argument-2 measures 1 and is not falsely rejected) and the class half (CrossViolation with MatchArgument1 intersects the candidate classes of schema.MatchedPositions(), rejecting national-argument-2-with-alphanumeric-argument-1 and the converse — r2's two sentences). negative/pb58-trim-arg2 (TRIM(X3 "AB"), expecting COBOLNET1627) pins the width half. ⛔ THE GAP: TRIM is catalogued Variadic 1..inf (IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Add "TRIM") and §15.96.2 prints '[ argument-2 ] …', so argument-2 REPEATS — but Schema()'s tail parameter defaults to '\0', so ArgSchema.Tail is null and ArgSchema.At(i) returns null for every i >= 2. Positions 3, 4, … are entirely UNSCREENED: no class kind, no ExactWidth(1), and CrossViolation cannot see them either (schema.MatchedPositions() iterates Positions only, which has length 2). BindTrim binds an unbounded operand list, so FUNCTION TRIM(X3 "A" "BC") — a two-character second argument-2 — draws no diagnostic and reaches CobolIntrinsics.Trim, whose 'c[0]' silently keeps 'B' and discards 'C'; FUNCTION TRIM(X-item "A" N"X") mixes classes r2 forbids, and a class-numeric third argument passes as well. The fix shape is one table edit (tail: 's' plus a tail predicate — the ORD/ORD-MAX rows already use WithTailPredicate), not a second check. NOT VERIFIED: any fixture with two or more argument-2s — grep of tests/conformance shows every TRIM call site has at most one. Editions: the argument-2 form is the 2023 enhancement (Annex §E.3.3 item 31, --check OK), and IntrinsicBinder.BindTrim gates operands.Count > 1 below 2023 with COBOLNET1502, so r2 has no pre-2023 reach. REFUTED: verdict SUSTAINED as PARTIAL, and CONFIRMED independently — I re-read ArgSchema.At (line 172: 'i < Positions.Length ? Positions[i] : Tail', Tail null for TRIM) and CrossViolation (line 1029: 'governed = schema.MatchedPositions()', which yields only {0,1} for a two-element Positions). But the note UNDERSTATES the hole by one whole shape, and the second shape is worse because it also punches through an EDITION gate. §15.3 rule 14 (--check OK: 'When the definition of a function permits an argument to be repeated a variable number of times, a table may be referenced by … subscripting where one or more of the subscripts is the word ALL' and 'the effect is as if each table element associated with that subscript position were specified') makes FUNCTION TRIM(ALL T) LEGAL SOURCE with no position restriction, and IntrinsicBinder.TryBindAllArgument admits it because sig.RepeatsAnArgument is true (IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 69: MaxArgs == int.MaxValue; the TRIM row is Variadic 1..inf). That ALL binds as ONE operand, so: (i) operands.Count == 1, and BindTrim's edition gate 'if (operands.Count > 1 && DialectLevel < 2023) Error(COBOLNET1502)' NEVER FIRES — at --std 2014 a 3-element table gives TRIM(T(1) T(2) T(3)), i.e. the 2023-only argument-2 form, accepted silently below its edition (IntrinsicRenderer.LeadThenTail line 576 splits the flattened array as 'method(xs[0], mode, xs[1..])', so T(2..n) ARE the argument-2s at run time); (ii) every one of those implicit argument-2s escapes BOTH halves of r2, because CheckArgumentClasses walks the OPERAND list, which has one entry — no ExactWidth(1), no MatchArgument1. A PIC X(3) table element therefore reaches c[0] and silently loses two characters. A third, smaller escape, on the plain path: PredicateViolation's ExactWidth arm is 'when knownWidth is { } w && w != p.N', so a null width falls to '_ => null' — KnownWidth returns null for {IsAnyLength: true} or {IsDynamicLength: true} items and for a computed-length ref-mod, so those argument-2s are width-unscreened too. Verdict stays PARTIAL (the first written argument-2 is genuinely screened on both halves), but the fix shape is larger than 'one table edit': the tail predicate does not reach an ALL operand, and the COBOLNET1502 count must be taken over the EXPANDED argument list (IntrinsicRenderer.StaticArgCount already computes exactly that number), not over operands.Count.

subject: TRIM function
notes: cite.py --check 15.96.3 'if argument-1 is class national, argument-2 is as though a national space had been specified' -> OK (r3 b). READ: CobolIntrinsics.Trim(string s, long mode, params string[] chars) opens with 'char[] set = chars.Length == 0 ? [' '] : …' — with no argument-2 the delete set is exactly one SPACE, r3's default. BOTH sub-rules land on that one line because the typed-native model stores a national item as a C# string of UTF-16 code units, one per national character position (the emitted pb15_result_type_follows_argument.g.cs shows 'private string W_NPAD = CobolString.Store("  CDE   ", 8)' for PIC N(8) and 'CobolIntrinsics.Trim(W_NPAD, 0)'), so the national space IS U+0020 and r3.b needs no separate arm — a distinct national-space constant would be the second mechanism, not a fix. Both sub-rules are exercised: r3.a by intrinsics_trim (BOTH=/LEAD=/TRAIL= over PIC X(10) "  HELLO   "), r3.b by pb15_result_type_follows_argument (MOVE FUNCTION TRIM(W-NPAD) TO W-NR over PIC N(8) N"  CDE   " → TRIM-N=[CDE]). The renderer reaches the defaulted form correctly: IntrinsicRenderer's "Trim" arm emits Intrinsic(method, Str(arg0) + ", " + TrimMode) with no chars when Args.Count == 1. Minor observation, not scored: the second guard 'if (set.Length == 0) set = [' ']' also substitutes a space when every WRITTEN argument-2 is a zero-length string — a silent fallback, but only for source r2 already forbids (a zero-length argument-2 is not 'a single character'), and it is unreachable for a static literal, which the ExactWidth(1) predicate rejects first. Editions per Annex §E.3.3 item 31 + kb/Work R28 (TRIM introduced 2014); the no-argument-2 default is the whole of 2014-era TRIM. REFUTED: CONFORMS → PARTIAL. The DEFAULT VALUE half of r3 is right and I re-confirmed the storage model in the emitted C# myself (tests/conformance/2023/pb15_result_type_follows_argument.g.cs line 15 stores PIC N(8) as an 8-char UTF-16 string padded with U+0020, line 51 calls Trim(W_NPAD, 0)) — so r3.b needing no separate national-space constant is sustained. What is NOT right is the code's test for r3's ANTECEDENT. r3 fires 'When NO argument-2 IS SPECIFIED' — a SYNTACTIC condition, decided at bind time. CobolIntrinsics.Trim decides it at RUN TIME on 'chars.Length == 0', and then a SECOND run-time test, 'if (set.Length == 0) set = [' ']', re-applies r3's default after '.Where(c => c.Length > 0)' has emptied a set built from argument-2s that WERE specified. The adjudicator's dismissal rests on a reachability claim it did not measure ('unreachable for a static literal, which the ExactWidth(1) predicate rejects first'), and that claim is only true for STATIC literals. I read PredicateViolation (IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs line 939): the ExactWidth arm is guarded 'when knownWidth is { } w && w != p.N', so a NULL width falls through '_ => null' and fails OPEN; and IntrinsicBinder.KnownWidth (line 1317) returns null for 'BoundFieldOperand { Place.Item: { IsAnyLength: true } or { IsDynamicLength: true } }' and for a ref-mod whose length is not an int literal. So FUNCTION TRIM(X DYN-ITEM) over an ANY LENGTH / DYNAMIC LENGTH argument-2 currently holding the empty string binds clean, reaches the runtime with chars = [""], is filtered to an empty set, and SILENTLY TRIMS SPACES — r3's default applied where r3's antecedent is false. §15.3 rule 14 is explicit about what should happen instead (--check OK: 'If the evaluation of an argument results in an incorrect value for that argument … the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist'); nothing here raises it. The same fallback is reached from the table(ALL) lane whenever the ALL enumerates zero elements. One half of r3 verified (the default's VALUE, by two goldens in both classes), the other half wrong on a reachable path ⇒ PARTIAL per rule 5. The fix shape is to decide r3 at BIND time — BindTrim already knows operands.Count — and let a specified-but-empty argument-2 raise EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION rather than fall back to a space.
