notes: cite.py --check 15.96.4 'If LEADING is specified, the returned value is a character string that consists of the characters in argument-1 beginning from the leftmost character position that does not contain any argument-2' -> OK (r1). subject: VARIANCE function
notes: Citation re-derived: `cite.py --check 15.98.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows"` returns OK for section 15.98.4 rule 1. Full rule read at spec lines 33984-34005: (a) one occurrence -> (0); (b) two -> ((x1-MEAN)**2 + (x2-MEAN)**2)/2; (c) n -> SUM((xi-MEAN)**2 ...)/n, MEAN taken over the VARIANCE call's own argument list. Governing constraint read at section 15.4.1 (spec lines 29777-29795): under NATIVE arithmetic 'the value returned is an implementor-defined approximation of the value of that expression'; under standard-decimal or standard-binary 'the returned value shall EQUAL the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression'. TWO LANES, BOTH READ. (1) The constrained lane -- CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs#VarianceDec lines 169-179: mean = MeanDec(mode, xs) = Div(SumDec chain, n); then per element acc = Add(acc, Mul(d,d,mode), mode) over d = Sub(x, mean, mode); then Div(acc, n, mode). This is the EAE's operation TREE, in the EAE's order, on the SDIDI carrier (section 8.8.1.5.2) with per-operation 34-digit rounding and NO argument quantization. Dispatched unconditionally under a standard mode: IntrinsicRenderer.cs#RenderDec line 643 lists "Variance" in alwaysDec (so even an all-fixed-point argument list evaluates in SDIDI form, because the EAE divides), and line 680 emits VarianceDec(mode, DecArgList(ic)). RenderNum line 88/100 reaches RenderDec when num.StandardDecimal, which NumericRenderer.cs line 394 defines as ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal or the legacy Standard. THREE EQUIVALENCES VERIFIED BY READING, not by sampling: (i) case (a) is exact -- for n=1, Div(x, 1) is exact (CobolDec.cs#Div pre-scales then rounds a <=34-digit quotient to 34 digits, remainder 0), so mean == x, d == 0, acc == 0, and Div with a.Sig==0 short-circuits to CobolDec(0,0) at line 214: the returned value is literally (0), matching (a). (ii) Mul(d,d,mode) is BIT-IDENTICAL to the EAE's `d ** 2` -- CobolDec.cs#Pow lines 113-135 takes the integer-exponent branch for e=2 and its square-and-multiply loop performs exactly one Mul(b,b,mode) and returns it, so the substitution surrenders nothing. (iii) acc starting at 0 rather than at xs[0] (the SumDec chain shape) adds one Add(0, t), which cannot round -- Add short-circuits a zero significand at CobolDec.cs line 176. Case (b) is case (c) with n=2, and the code has one formula for all n, so no arm is unimplemented. (2) The native lane -- CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Variance lines 78-87, the same mean-of-squared-deviations in binary64, reached via RenderNum line 109 (sig.Float is true for the VARIANCE row) and RenderFloat's default arm line 403 (which also handles a table(ALL) argument through ArgArray). Section 15.4.1's native paragraph explicitly licenses an implementor-defined approximation, so binary64 is conforming there; its n=1 path also returns exactly 0 (x-x is exact in binary64). Standard-binary is out of reach entirely -- DataBinder.cs line 318 rejects ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY with COBOLNET0806 as an obsolete feature (section 8.8.1.4.1 NOTE 1) -- so that half of section 15.4.1's 'shall equal' has no code path to diverge in; flagged for the parent, not adjudicated here. Divide-by-zero on n is unreachable: MinArgs 1 (COBOLNET1504) guarantees xs.Length >= 1. TEST: tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.cob line 39 computes FUNCTION VARIANCE(1, 2, 3) under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL into a 9V9(5) receiver and the golden .out pins VA=0.66666 -- 2/3 truncated, derived in the fixture header from the EAE itself. Only n=3 is exercised; cases (a) and (b) and the native lane are verified by reading, not by a golden. ** CITATION DEFECT FOUND (behaviour is correct, traceability is not) ** -- CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs line 168 heads VarianceDec 'section 15.97 VARIANCE -- ... (section 15.97.4 r1's EAE over MEAN)' and line 181 heads StdDevDec 'section 15.85 STANDARD-DEVIATION'. Both clause numbers are another function's: `cite.py --check 15.97.4 "The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows"` FAILS (15.97 is UPPER-CASE, spec line 33918) and `cite.py --check 15.85.4 "square root"` FAILS (15.85 is STANDARD-COMPARE, spec line 33332); VARIANCE is 15.98 and STANDARD-DEVIATION is 15.86, as CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs lines 75/77/89 cite correctly. The wrong number has already PROPAGATED into a golden: pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.cob line 8 says 'VARIANCE(1 2 3)=2/3 (section 15.97.4: ((1-2)^2+0+1)/3)'. This is exactly CLAUDE.md rule 1's inherited-citation failure mode -- the derivation is right, the clause number was never re-derived. Three comment sites to repair; no code change. || REFUTED: CONFORMS -> PARTIAL. Citations re-derived independently first: --check 15.98.4 'The equivalent arithmetic expression is as follows' OK (section 15.98.4 rule 1); --check 15.98.3 OK; the format at spec line 33974; and the adjudicator's citation-defect finding CONFIRMED mechanically -- --check 15.97.4 FAILS, --check 15.85.4 'square root' FAILS, --check 15.86.4 'square root' FAILS. GROUND 1 -- A HALF OF THE GOVERNING RULE HAS NO CODE PATH AT ALL. The adjudicator itself made section 15.4.1 the governing constraint (it is what licenses the binary64 native lane), and that same paragraph imposes 'the returned value shall equal the value of the equivalent arithmetic expression' when standard-decimal OR STANDARD-BINARY is in effect. Standard-binary is NOT removed from ISO/IEC 1989:2023: section 8.8.1.4 defines it and the SBIDI (spec lines 7935-7990), and section 11.9.5 GR2 (spec line 11704) requires that 'if the STANDARD-BINARY phrase is specified, the techniques used in handling arithmetic expressions, arithmetic statements, the SUM clause, and INTEGER AND NUMERIC FUNCTIONS shall be as described for standard-binary arithmetic in 8.8.1.4' -- the NOTEs at spec lines 7938 and 11708 mark it OBSOLETE, which is not the same as deleted. There is no SBIDI evaluation of this EAE anywhere in the tree: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs lines 318-320 raise COBOLNET0806 through Edition.Error unconditionally at every --std, so a conforming program selecting that mode is REJECTED and VARIANCE's EAE exists in two of the three arithmetic modes its own governing clause names. Rule 5: 'a rule with two halves where one was verified => PARTIAL, always.' The adjudicator found this exact fact and then declined to price it ('flagged for the parent, not adjudicated here') -- pricing it IS the adjudication rule 5 requires. GROUND 2 -- THE STATED REACHABILITY EVIDENCE IS FALSE, AND THE TWO LANES DISAGREE ABOUT THE CASE IT DISMISSED. The note asserts 'Divide-by-zero on n is unreachable: MinArgs 1 (COBOLNET1504) guarantees xs.Length >= 1.' MinArgs guarantees nothing of the kind: IntrinsicBinder.cs line 572 computes `given = args.Sum(a => a is BoundFieldOperand { Place: TableAllPlace all } ? all.StaticCount ?? 1 : 1)` and Place.cs lines 162-174 make StaticCount NULL whenever any ALL level is an AllCount.Odo or AllCount.Capacity, so `FUNCTION VARIANCE(TBL(ALL))` over an `OCCURS 0 TO n DEPENDING ON` or an OCCURS DYNAMIC table passes the arity gate with given == 1 whatever the run-time count is. The guarantee actually comes from a THIRD body the adjudicator never located -- CobolTable.cs#AllArgs lines 130-135, which on an empty enumeration raises EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION and throws CobolFatalException, citing section 15.3's 'the evaluation of an ALL subscript shall result in at least one argument'. So the conclusion survives but its evidence does not, and the two VARIANCE bodies still disagree about the case: CobolIntrinsics.Float.cs#Variance line 80 carries `if (xs.Length == 0) return 0;` labelled 'EC-ARGUMENT default -- at least one argument required', while CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs#VarianceDec has NO guard and would die with an IndexOutOfRangeException inside SumDec's `xs[0]` (CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs line 140) if it were ever entered empty. Latent today, but it is the two-arm-dispatch shape and it is why the CONFORMS was not earned on the evidence given. GROUND 3 -- COVERAGE AND TRACEABILITY. The single test-ref exercises exactly ONE of the rule's three lettered arms (case c, n = 3) in ONE of the two lanes; arms (a) and (b) and the entire native lane rest on reading alone. And the row's traceability is anchored to a nonexistent clause at BOTH ends: CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs line 168 heads the body 'section 15.97 ... section 15.97.4 r1' and tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.cob line 8 derives the golden's expected value from 'section 15.97.4' -- 15.97 is UPPER-CASE, and --check fails on both -- so the closing golden's own spec anchor does not resolve to this rule. INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED AND UPHELD, so the PARTIAL is priced on the two halves above and not inflated: the Dec lane IS arithmetically faithful to the EAE. Section 8.8.1.5.4 rule 2b (spec lines 8110-8116) makes `operand-1 ** 2` exactly `(operand-1 * operand-1)`, so Mul(d,d,mode) is the EAE's own operation rather than a substitution. CobolDec.cs#AddSigned lines 175-176 short-circuit a zero significand through Round34, so the accumulator's leading Add(0, t) cannot round and the chain equals FUNCTION SUM's. CobolDec.cs#Div lines 227-235 pre-scale the numerator to 34-36 significant digits in two exact steps and fold the true division remainder into sticky before one rounding, so Div(x, 1) is exact and case (a) returns literally (0). Round34Wide enforces the decimal128 range with EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW / EC-SIZE-UNDERFLOW per section 8.8.1.5.2 rule 2 (CobolDec.cs lines 370-391), so an EAE step outside decimal128 is loud rather than silently wrapped. Dispatch re-confirmed on all three routes: IntrinsicRenderer.cs line 88 (num.StandardDecimal = ArithmeticMode.StandardDecimal or Standard, NumericRenderer.cs line 394) -> RenderDec, whose alwaysDec list at line 643 names "Variance" so even an all-fixed-point list evaluates in SDIDI form; line 109 (sig.Float is the `true` in the catalog row, IntrinsicSig field order confirmed at IntrinsicCatalog.cs lines 52-57) -> RenderFloat for native; line 107 routes a NATIVE call carrying an SDIDI raw argument back through RenderDec. NumericRenderer.FieldNum line 228 unwraps a TableAllPlace to its element, so AnyDecRaw/AnyRealArgument on a table(ALL) argument does not fault the emitter.

subject: LINAGE clause
notes: kb/Work PB489 — THE PRINTED SHAPE IS MATCHED TOKEN FOR TOKEN; THE OPERAND EXTRACTION IS NOT. The figure was RENDERED from the canonical PDF (scripts/render-spec-page.py 447 -> printed folio 417), not read from the transcription, and the transcription is faithful: LINAGE IS {data-name-1|integer-1} LINES [WITH FOOTING AT {data-name-2|integer-2}] [LINES AT TOP {data-name-3|integer-3}] [LINES AT BOTTOM {data-name-4|integer-4}], with LINAGE/FOOTING/TOP/BOTTOM underlined and IS/LINES/WITH/AT/LINES AT/LINES AT not; each data-name/integer pair in BRACES (exactly one, no choice indicators); the three phrases in three SEPARATE brackets, in the printed order FOOTING then TOP then BOTTOM. The grammar is an exact match: every optional word is independently omittable and `LINAGE 5 FOOTING 4 TOP 1 BOTTOM 1` parses and runs at --std 85, 2002, 2014 AND 2023 (<lane3 scratch>/out-b3/probe/linage/p15_minwords.cob); a phrase out of the printed order is a parse error (p14_order.cob: `LINES AT TOP 2 WITH FOOTING AT 4` -> COBOL0307), which is what an order-significant general format requires; TOP and BOTTOM are independently optional. WHERE IT DIVERGES: the operand nonterminal is the general `dataReference` (CobolParserCore.g4:480), which admits qualification suffixes, subscripts and the LINAGE_COUNTER/LINE_COUNTER/PAGE_COUNTER register alternatives, and BindLinageClause then keeps ONLY `d.cobolWord()?.GetText()` - the FIRST word - discarding everything else. A qualified data-name-1, a legal spelling under 8.4.2.2.3 SR2, therefore binds to the WRONG item (p17_qual.cob: `LINAGE IS SZ OF GRP-B` with GRP-A.SZ=3 and GRP-B.SZ=9 behaves as page size 3), and for the register alternative the first word is the QUALIFIER, so `LINAGE IS LINAGE-COUNTER OF LPF LINES` compiles clean and dies at OPEN with "LINAGE operand 'LPF' is not resolvable to storage" (p22_lcindata.cob). Finding: linage-operand-first-word-only. TEST COVERAGE: the named test compiles one instance of the format (`LINAGE IS 5 LINES WITH FOOTING AT 4`); NO test in the tree exercises the LINES AT TOP or LINES AT BOTTOM phrases, the omitted-optional-word spellings, or the phrase order. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4:151-168 (linageClause, linageFootingPhrase, linageLinesAtTopPhrase, linageLinesAtBottomPhrase); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:1101-1110 (BindLinageClause); src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:480-492 (dataReference)

notes: kb/Work PB486 — THE CLAUSE'S OWN FORMAT IS EXACT; THE ENTRY MAY CARRY IT TWICE. The figure was RENDERED from the canonical PDF (scripts/render-spec-page.py 513 -> printed folio 483), not read from the transcription: `[ SIGN IS ] { LEADING / TRAILING } [ SEPARATE CHARACTER ]`, with SIGN, LEADING, TRAILING and SEPARATE underlined and IS and CHARACTER not, LEADING/TRAILING in BRACES (exactly one, no choice indicators). `signClause : (SIGN IS?)? (LEADING | TRAILING) (SEPARATE CHARACTER?)?` is a token-for-token match and every boundary was probed: all six printed shapes parse and behave (sg_fmt_bare_lead, sg_fmt_is_lead, sg_fmt_nosign_lead, sg_fmt_nosign_trail_sep, sg_fmt_full, sg_fmt_nosign_sepchar); the `SIGN IS` bracket is a UNIT, so `PIC S9(3) IS LEADING` is a parse error (sg_fmt_is_only); the brace is enforced, so `SIGN IS SEPARATE CHARACTER` with neither alternative is rejected (sg_fmt_neither); CHARACTER is optional and non-repeatable (sg_fmt_char_twice rejected). PARTIAL FOR ONE MEASURED OVER-ACCEPTANCE: a data description entry may carry the SIGN clause TWICE and the compiler silently takes the LAST. `01 A PIC S9(3) SIGN IS TRAILING LEADING VALUE -12.` compiles and stores a LEADING over-punch (`}12`) though the program selected TRAILING first (sg_fmt_trail_lead), while `SIGN IS LEADING TRAILING` stores a TRAILING over-punch (`01K`, sg_fmt_both) -- the LAST clause wins in written order either way, and `05 A PIC S9(3) SIGN IS LEADING SEPARATE SIGN IS TRAILING VALUE -12.` compiles and DROPS the separate character position -- the enclosing group image shrinks from 5 characters to 4 (`G=[01K|]`; sg_fmt_twice / sg_fmt_sep_then_lead / sg85_dup_85 / _2002 / _2014 / _2023, identical at all four editions). Mechanism: `dataDescriptionClause*` is a plain star and DataBinder.cs:2378 assigns `ownSign` unconditionally on each pass of the clause loop, so a second SIGN clause overwrites the first with no diagnostic. Both enclosing general formats print the slot exactly once (§13.15.2 `[ sign-clause ]`; §13.16.2's own bracket) and §5.2.6.2 makes a bracket 'may be explicitly specified ... or omitted', never repeated. See finding sign-duplicate-clause-last-wins. The SCREEN SECTION alternative (CobolScreen.g4:68) is owner-declined A.4.2 non-support refused by name (COBOLNET1560, ScreenFacility.cs:89 carries the per-clause fact for signClause), owned by kb/Work PB260 -- not adjudicated here. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4:647 (signClause); CobolData.g4:276 (dataDescriptionClause alt); CobolReportWriter.g4:94; CobolScreen.g4:68; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:2377-2378; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Reports.cs:427-428

subject: SYNCHRONIZED clause
notes: The ANTLR rule is the printed figure token for token: a REQUIRED choice of SYNCHRONIZED|SYNC (no `?`, so one must be written) followed by an OPTIONAL at-most-one LEFT|RIGHT. Measured at all four editions (probe sy_elem_/sy_elem_left_/sy_elem_right_/sy_77_ x 85|2002|2014|2023, all exit 0), and the figure's complement is measured too: `SYNC LEFT RIGHT` -> COBOL0307 (probe sy_fmt_both_lr), a bare `LEFT` with no SYNC -> COBOL0307 (sy_fmt_bare_left), `SYNC IS LEFT` -> COBOL0001 (sy_fmt_sync_is; the figure has no IS). The clause is confined to the DATA DESCRIPTION entry, as the standard requires - `syncClause` is unreachable from CobolReport.g4 and CobolScreen.g4 - and a level-66 RENAMES entry rejects it at parse (probe syp_l66_sync). TWO NOTES, neither a defect of this figure. (1) The LEFT/RIGHT selection is PARSED AND DISCARDED - `clause.Context.syncClause()` is tested for null-ness at DataBinder.cs:2308 and the token is never read (one `syncClause()` call site in the whole compiler), and DataItem carries a single `bool Synchronized` - so the three format shapes are indistinguishable downstream; see finding sync-left-right-phrase-discarded on GR-13.18.55.4-4/-5. (2) The entry admits the clause MORE THAN ONCE - `01 A PIC X SYNC SYNCHRONIZED.` and `01 A PIC X SYNC LEFT SYNC RIGHT.` both compile clean at 85 and 2023 (probes sy_fmt_twice, syq_dup_sync_lr, syq_dup_sync_lr_85) - but that is the shared `dataDescriptionClauses : dataDescriptionClause*` hole already reported this batch as `sign-duplicate-clause-last-wins` against FMT-13.18.52.2; for SYNCHRONIZED the repeat is value-idempotent (both passes set the same bool), so no wrong answer follows from it here. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4:656-658 (`syncClause : (SYNCHRONIZED | SYNC) (LEFT | RIGHT)?`), reached from CobolData.g4:277 (the `syncClause` alternative of `dataDescriptionClause`); tokens at src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolLexer.g4:686-687 || editions, verbatim from the adjudication: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the figure is unchanged across all four; only the GROUP subject is edition-gated - see SR-13.18.55.3-1)

subject: VALUE clause
notes: kb/Work PB502 + PB503 + PB559 — THREE PRINTED FORMAT ELEMENTS ARE WRONG, AND TWO OF THEM ARE IN FORMAT 3. (1) OPERAND ORDER INVERTED -- REJECTS LEGAL SOURCE. The printed Format-3 figure puts `[ IN alphabet-name-1 ]` at the end of the repeated-group line and `[ WHEN SET TO FALSE IS literal-4 ]` on the FOLLOWING line, so IN precedes WHEN. The grammar writes the reverse: `(WHEN SET TO FALSE_ IS? literal)? (IN IDENTIFIER)?`. MEASURED at the pin: `88 CN VALUE "A" THRU "C" IN ALPH1 WHEN SET TO FALSE IS "Z".` is COBOL0307 "unexpected 'WHEN'. A period may be missing at the end of the previous sentence." at --std 2023 AND 85, 2002, 2014 (probes fmt_f3_in_then_when, c_fmt_f3_in_then_when_85/_2002/_2014); the grammar's own inverted order compiles (fmt_f3_when_then_in), as does each phrase alone (fmt_f3_in_only, fmt_f3_when_only). (2) `IN alphabet-name-1` IS PARSED AND DISCARDED -- SILENT WRONG ANSWER. The grammar captures it as a bare `(IN IDENTIFIER)?` and BindCondition never reads it, so every condition-name range orders under the native sequence. MEASURED: with `ALPHABET ALPH1 IS "C" "B" "A"` (which orders C < B < A), `88 CN VALUE "C" THRU "A" IN ALPH1.` and CV = "B" prints OUT where the named sequence puts B inside the range (probe d_in_alpha_range). The collating machinery EXISTS -- the same alphabet under `PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS ALPH1` makes `IF "B" < "A"` true (probe vcp1f/alph.cob prints B-LT-A) -- so this is a dropped operand at the parse->bind boundary, not a missing facility. (3) `WHEN SET TO FALSE IS literal-4` parses and its consumer is STAGED LOUD at RUN time, not compile time: `SET CN TO TRUE` works but `SET CN TO FALSE` throws CobolNet.Runtime.NotImplementedCobolFeatureException "SET condition-name TO FALSE" (probe e_set_false_literal4) -- a refusal, but after the program has already run. CORRECT ELSEWHERE: Format 1 takes exactly one literal (COBOLNET1585, fmt_f1_two_literals); Format 2's mandatory-FROM arm is first so `FROM` terminates the operand loop; Format 4's multi-literal list parses in the report section where Format 1's does not; Format 5 is refused by name (COBOLNET1708 -- the declined A.4.14 VALIDATE module, owner-declined, owned by kb/Work PB283). SUPERSET (under-rejection, not filed): the figures pair `VALUE IS` with `VALUES ARE` as one required choice and Format 1 prints ONLY `VALUE IS`, but the grammar's `(VALUE|VALUES) (IS|ARE)?` accepts `VALUE ARE`, `VALUES IS` and a Format-1 `VALUES ARE` (probes sr17_value_are_mixed, fmt_f1_values_are, c_sr17_values_f1). See findings value-clause-p1/F1 and F2. || code sites, verbatim from the adjudication: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4:614-630 (valueClause -- two arms: the Format-2 table arm and the Format-1/3/4/5 arm), :635-640 (valueClauseTablePhrase), :642-644 (valueItem); src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4:31-44 (valueClauseOperand / valueClauseRange); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#BindCondition (:2103-2158 -- the Format-3 consumer, which reads value.valueItem() and NOTHING else on the clause); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs:2365 + :3181 (BuildTableValueSpecs, the Format-2 consumer)

subject: ALLOCATE statement
notes: Read the format at specs/ISO_COBOL.md 22600-22604 (no 'Figure notes' block accompanies this diagram, so the transcribed <pre> IS the authority): ALLOCATE { arithmetic-expression-1 CHARACTERS | data-name-1 } [ INITIALIZED ] [ RETURNING data-name-2 ], with ALLOCATE / CHARACTERS / INITIALIZED / RETURNING underlined and no optional noise words. Read grammar rule `allocateStatement`: two alternatives, `ALLOCATE arithmeticExpression CHARACTERS INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` and `ALLOCATE dataReference INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` — arm-for-arm identical to the diagram, both optional phrases optional in both arms, and no scope terminator / conditional phrase (matching Table 12's empty ALLOCATE row at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:20867). Alternative order is safe because alt 1 requires the CHARACTERS token, so a bare data-name falls to alt 2 under ALL(*) prediction. The binder's `PtrBinder.BindAllocate` reads `al.dataReference()` (DIRECT children only, so data-names inside arithmeticExpression are not in the list) and indexes drefs[0] for data-name-1 / drefs[^1] for RETURNING — correct for all four legs, and the RETURNING()-null guard precedes the index so the no-RETURNING form cannot index an empty list. All five surface legs have goldens: `ALLOCATE G INITIALIZED RETURNING P`, `ALLOCATE W INITIALIZED`, `ALLOCATE 6 CHARACTERS INITIALIZED RETURNING P2` (2002/allocate_initialized), `ALLOCATE B` and `ALLOCATE 5 CHARACTERS RETURNING P` (2002/pointer_alloc). Editions: ALLOCATE appears in neither the 2023 new-features list (specs/ISO_COBOL.md 1100-1130) nor Annex E, so there is no 2014->2023 delta; it cannot be COBOL-85 because SR1 requires the BASED clause and SR3 requires category data-pointer, neither of which the 1985 standard has. || UPHELD: I re-read specs/ISO_COBOL.md 22598-22604 myself — the <pre> reads exactly `ALLOCATE ┤ arithmetic-expression-1 CHARACTERS | data-name-1 ├ [ INITIALIZED ] [ RETURNING data-name-2 ]`, brackets with NO choice-indicator bars, so INITIALIZED-before-RETURNING is a fixed order and the grammar's `INITIALIZED? (RETURNING dataReference)?` tail matches it in both arms. I re-read `allocateStatement` at CobolParserCore.g4:1244-1247 and `PtrBinder.BindAllocate` at PtrBinder.cs:99-138: for form 1 with RETURNING drefs has ONE element and drefs[^1] is it; for form 2 without RETURNING drefs has ONE element and drefs[0] is it; for form 2 with RETURNING drefs is [based, returning] and both indexes are right — all four index legs re-derived, not taken on trust. I do NOT rest on the ALL(*) prediction argument: `ALLOCATE B.` and `ALLOCATE G INITIALIZED RETURNING P.` are ENABLED goldens with byte-compared .out, which is empirical proof alt 2 is reachable. Edition re-derived independently of the code catalog: ALLOCATE is absent from Annex E (§E.2/§E.3, specs/ISO_COBOL.md 42858-44000), and §13.18.x SR16 (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:15101 — 'The BASED clause may be specified only in data description entries in the linkage section, in the working-storage section, and in the local-storage section. The level number of such data description entries shall be 1 or 77') plus §13.18.60.4 GR23's data-pointer are both post-85 constructs, so 2002,2014,2023. Not downgraded: the format-surface row is about which token sequences the grammar admits, and the BASED-record storage-shape gap found on GR3/GR4/GR7 is a data-model gap, not a surface one.

subject: CONTINUE statement
notes: Re-read the format in specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 23190 and validated it mechanically (`cite.py --check 14.9.9.2 "CONTINUE"` -> OK, returning the whole format line). Derived expectation BEFORE reading code, from the repaired Figure-notes block: CONTINUE is a required word (the printed missing underline is the C2 typo), the bracket makes the whole phrase optional, and AFTER / SECONDS carry underline rules so they are REQUIRED inside the phrase; the operand is arithmetic-expression-1 (a full 8.8.1 arithmetic expression, not a mere identifier/literal). READ: `continueStatement : CONTINUE (AFTER arithmeticExpression SECONDS)? ;` (CobolControlFlow.g4:361-363). Token-for-token identical to the derived shape: CONTINUE mandatory (so `AFTER 5 SECONDS` alone cannot parse as a CONTINUE, the Figure-notes' second argument), the group is `( ... )?` (bracket), AFTER and SECONDS are hard tokens inside it (not `AFTER?` / `SECONDS?`), so `CONTINUE 5` is rejected. The operand nonterminal is the SHARED `arithmeticExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4:208 -> additiveExpression -> multiplicative -> power), i.e. the same 8.8.1 rule PERFORM VARYING uses, so a parenthesized/compound expression, a literal, an identifier and a function reference are all admitted -- not a narrowed operand. The grammar's own header comment (CobolControlFlow.g4:359-360) records the same page-604-vs-page-732 contradiction the Figure notes do and resolves it the same way (the defining occurrence governs), so the transcription and the grammar agree rather than one having inherited the other's typo. Wired into the single `statement` rule at CobolParserCore.g4:719. EDITION (derived from Annex E, NOT from the registry's own IntroducedIn column): Annex E.3.3 item 14 at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43957 -- "Additional functionality added to the CONTINUE statement. The CONTINUE statement has been enhanced to provide the ability to pause runtime execution for a specified period of time" -- so the bracketed phrase is 2023-only while bare CONTINUE is 85-continuous. The compiler gates exactly that split: VersionConformancePass.VisitContinueStatement fires COBOLNET0900 only when `ctx.arithmeticExpression()` is present (Validation/VersionConformancePass.cs:584-589), i.e. on the PHRASE, never on the verb -- confirmed by 85/wavef_dbg_proc.cob and 85/index_name_r7_windows.cob compiling bare CONTINUE at --std 85. TESTED: 2023/continue_after exercises both operand forms (a literal `AFTER 0` and a data item `AFTER WS-N`); the constructs.json row `continue-after-2023` drives VersionMatrixTests.Construct_MatchesEditionExpectation and IntroducedConstruct_IsRejectedUnderPermissive, so the below-2023 rejection is asserted at 85/2002/2014 and is not waived by --permissive. NOT exercised anywhere: a COMPOUND arithmetic-expression-1 (`CONTINUE AFTER N + 1 SECONDS`); that is a shared-nonterminal reuse rather than a private parse, so it does not cost the verdict. || UPHELD (independent re-derivation): I re-ran all three cite checks myself -- `cite.py --check 14.9.9.2 "CONTINUE"` -> OK (General format), and read the format + Figure notes at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:23189-23212 before opening any code. I re-read CobolControlFlow.g4:361-363 and CobolParserCore.g4:719 directly. I additionally checked the two edges the adjudicator did not: (a) `unaryExpression : addOp unaryExpression | primaryExpression` (CobolExpressions.g4) admits a LEADING SIGN, so `CONTINUE AFTER -1 SECONDS` -- the literal spelling of the GR1a negative case -- parses, and `primaryExpression` admits numericLiteral / ZERO_ARITH / functionCall / dataReference / `( arithmeticExpression )`, so the operand really is the full 8.8.1 rule; (b) the SECONDS terminator cannot be swallowed by the operand, because `additiveExpression` stops at a non-addOp token and `dataReference` is single-word except for OF/IN qualification. I verified the test-refs are LIVE rather than merely present: tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json lists `continue_after` at enabled[22], and tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Conformance/VersionMatrixTests.cs:79/:124 are the two named methods; the constructs.json row `continue-after-2023` carries source `CONTINUE AFTER 0 SECONDS.` with expectDiagnostic COBOLNET0900. || REFUTED (edition-basis citation, verdict unchanged): the adjudicator wrote "E.2's new-reserved-word list at :43951 adds SECONDS". That is WRONG on both counts and I did not inherit it. Line 43951 sits inside Annex **E.3.3 item 13** (heading at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:43225 `E.3.3 Not affecting`), whose lead sentence is "**Context-sensitive words.** In order to provide enhanced functionality, the following words have either been added to the list of context-sensitive words or the context in which they are reserved has been expanded" -- SECONDS is in the CONTEXT-SENSITIVE list, not a reserved-word list. The 8.10 context-sensitive-words table at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:9578 confirms it: `| SECONDS | RETRY phrase, CONTINUE statement |`. The compiler agrees with the STANDARD and not with the adjudicator's note: CobolLexer.g4:562-568 comments SECONDS as "8.10 context-sensitive (user-legal at every edition)" and CobolWords.g4:89 re-admits it as a user word. This does not move the verdict -- the AFTER phrase's 2023 introduction rests on E.3.3 item 14, which I checked and which stands -- but the note's edition evidence was an uncited (and false) claim, exactly the failure mode CLAUDE.md rule 1 names, and is replaced above.

subject: DELETE statement
notes: LANDED (kb/Work PB134): Format 2's three measured divergences closed - `DELETE FILE [OVERRIDE] {file-name-1}...` parses (OVERRIDE was consumed AS the file-name before; the repetition was absent), and the exception phrases take the OPTIONAL word ON (5.2.3 - the arithmeticOnSizeError underline measurement's missed sibling). subject: DISPLAY statement
notes: READ: displayStatement : DISPLAY (dataReference | literal | functionCall)+ displayUpon? displayNoAdvancing? END_DISPLAY? ; displayUpon : UPON cobolWord ; displayNoAdvancing : WITH? NO ADVANCING (CobolParserCore.g4 lines 1300-1310). FORMAT 1 MATCHES the printed diagram element for element: the '...' operand repetition is '+', UPON is optional, WITH is an OPTIONAL word (it is NOT underlined in the format, and the grammar's 'WITH?' honours that), NO/ADVANCING are required, END-DISPLAY is optional, and a function-identifier is admitted in the identifier-1 slot per 8.4.3.1.2 (the grammar comment cites it). FORMAT 2 (screen) IS ENTIRELY ABSENT: there is no screen-name-1 arm, no AT [LINE NUMBER ...] [{COLUMN|COL} NUMBER ...] phrase, and no ON EXCEPTION / NOT ON EXCEPTION pair. AT (CobolLexer.g4:411), LINE (:556) and EXCEPTION (:494) are dedicated lexer tokens and NONE of them is an alternative of cobolWord (CobolWords.g4 lines 9-120 -- COL and COLUMN are, AT/LINE/EXCEPTION are not), so 'DISPLAY SG AT LINE 5 COL 10 ON EXCEPTION ...' is a PARSE ERROR, not a mis-bind. The repaired Figure notes therefore have nothing to be compared against: the AT phrase's brace-enclosed choice indicators (one-or-more, any order) and the exception pair's bracket-enclosed indicators (zero-or-more, any order -- BOTH ON EXCEPTION and NOT ON EXCEPTION admissible on one statement, either order) are unimplemented along with the format. SECOND DEFECT, Format 1 side: END-DISPLAY is accepted at EVERY --std, 85 included. src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs:151 records new("END-DISPLAY", false, true, true, true, "high", "added 2002 ...") -- R85 = false -- yet tests/version-matrix/constructs.json has no end-display-* row and VersionConformancePass has no VisitDisplayStatement (grep: only VisitAcceptStatement, which gates Constructs.EndAccept2002). So the project's own reserved-word catalog says the terminator is a 2002 introduction while the gating funnel admits it at 1985 with no diagnostic -- the ACCEPT twin at least carries a registered construct. WOULD CLOSE THE ROW: (a) the Format-2 grammar + binder + a golden, (b) an end-display-2002 construct row plus the mandatory edition-gate negative fixture at --std 85. || UPHELD (independent re-derivation): I re-read specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 23402-23433 and CobolParserCore.g4:1300-1310 and CobolWords.g4:9-120 myself. Format-1 element-for-element agreement CONFIRMED, including the two things worth naming: (i) figurativeConstant is the FIRST alternative of nonNumericLiteral (CobolExpressions.g4:499-506) which is an alternative of literal, so DISPLAY SPACE / DISPLAY ZERO bind as LITERAL operands and are not lost from the operand list; (ii) ZERO/SPACE/HIGH-VALUE are NOT alternatives of cobolWord, so the dataReference alternative (listed first) cannot steal them. Format-2 absence CONFIRMED. The keyword-omitted intrinsic reference (REPOSITORY 'FUNCTION name INTRINSIC', 8.4.3.2 SR2) is NOT an extra Format-1 gap: it arrives through the dataReference alternative and ExpressionBinder.FieldOperand resolves it (ControlFlowBinder.cs:260 states this contract). || REFUTED (method, not verdict) on the END-DISPLAY leg: the adjudicator derived the EDITION of END-DISPLAY from src/Cobol.Net.Editions/ReservedWords.Table.cs -- a catalog INSIDE the code under review, which ground rule 4 forbids as an edition source (it is the same shape as trusting a constructs.json IntroducedIn column). Re-derived independently and the CONCLUSION survives, so the verdict stands: END-DISPLAY exists in the standard only because 14.9.11.2 Format 2 gives DISPLAY the [NOT] ON EXCEPTION conditional phrases (an explicit scope terminator is meaningless for a statement with no conditional phrase), and Format 2 is the screen facility, absent from the 1985 statement; the compiler's own TWIN confirms the intended posture -- ConstructRegistry.g.cs:174 carries new("end-accept-2002", "END-ACCEPT (explicit scope terminator)", 2002, null, null, "COBOLNET0816", ...) and VersionConformancePass.cs:1362 checks it, while grep for END-DISPLAY across src/ + tests/version-matrix finds ONLY the lexer token, the grammar reference and the reserved-word row: no construct row, no Check call, no negative fixture. The DEFECT is therefore the ASYMMETRY itself (one of two twin terminators gated), which is true whatever edition number the eventual derivation assigns. Verdict PARTIAL upheld: Format 1 is implemented and spec-pinned, Format 2 is wholly absent, so neither CONFORMS nor NOT-IMPLEMENTED is available. EDITIONS held at the batch default: Annex E covers only the 2014->2023 delta and carries no DISPLAY item (grepped lines 42847-44027), and the rule text carries no edition marker, so per ground rule 4 the default stands even though Format 2 is manifestly post-1985 -- flagged here so a later edition-derivation pass narrows the Format-2 rows rather than inheriting this field.

subject: GOBACK statement
notes: kb/Work/PB407.md — PDF page 661 RENDERED (CLAUDE.md rule 1): the general format is GOBACK [ | raising-phrase | status-phrase | ] - a BRACKET enclosing CHOICE INDICATORS, so by 5.2.6.4 'zero or more of the alternatives ... any single alternative may be specified only once ... may be specified in any order'. subject: IF statement
notes: kb/Work/PB387.md — Citations validated mechanically: `cite.py --check 14.9.19.2 "IF</u> condition-1 THEN statement-1 [ <u>ELSE</u> statement-2 ] <u>END-IF"` -> OK (General formats), and `--check 14.9.19.2 "NEXT SENTENCE is an archaic feature"` -> OK. The DIAGRAM is load-bearing here, so I rendered the PRINTED page rather than trusting the OCR: PDF page 665 (printed folio 635) at 300dpi. It confirms the transcription exactly -- rules under IF, ELSE and END-IF only; NO rule under condition-1, THEN, statement-1 or statement-2. (Note the transcription has since been repaired: docs/rearchitecture/spec-reconciliation/agents/verify-p665-incorrect-figure-0.json ledgered this same figure as carrying ZERO <u> markup; specs/ISO_COBOL.md:24334 now carries it and matches the print.) So per 5.2.2 the required keywords are IF/ELSE/END-IF, per 5.2.3 THEN is an optional word, per 5.2.6.2 only the ELSE phrase is optional, and Format 2's THEN and ELSE arms are BRACES -- 5.2.6.3: 'Braces, { }, enclosing a portion of a general format indicate that the syntax element contained within the braces or one of the alternatives contained within the braces shall be explicitly specified'. DERIVED EXPECTATION: statement-1 is REQUIRED in both formats (unbracketed in Format 1; a brace alternative in Format 2), and statement-2 is REQUIRED whenever ELSE is written. GRAMMAR SAYS OTHERWISE: `ifStatement : IF condition THEN? statementBlock* (ELSE statementBlock*)? END_IF?` uses `*` on BOTH arms, and `statementBlock : statement+`, so zero statements is accepted in either arm. MEASURED with the pinned cobol.exe, all accepted rc=0 with no diagnostic: `IF X = 1 END-IF` (probe p1-empty-then); `IF X = 9 ELSE DISPLAY "E" END-IF` (p2-empty-then-else); `IF X = 1 DISPLAY "T" ELSE END-IF` (p3-empty-else); `IF A = 1.` as a complete sentence (u7-empty-format2); `IF A = 1 DISPLAY "T" ELSE.` (u8-else-then-period); and nested (u6-empty-nested). Swept at --std 85 and --std 2023 (probe empty-std85 / empty-std2023): identical acceptance, so the leniency is edition-wide and not a dialect gate. WHAT IS RIGHT: everything else in both formats. IF and condition-1 required; `THEN?` optional per 5.2.3; the ELSE phrase optional per 5.2.6.2; NEXT SENTENCE reachable in BOTH arms via statement -> nextSentenceStatement (measured p6/p7); `END_IF?` is the correct UNION of Format 1 (END-IF required) and Format 2 (no END-IF) -- Format 2 measured period-terminated at all four editions (probe ed, std 85/2002/2014/2023, identical output). A SECOND, much smaller leniency falls out of that same union: because the grammar does not separate the two formats it also admits the cross-format mixture NEXT SENTENCE + END-IF, which no single format shows -- `IF X = 1 NEXT SENTENCE END-IF` is accepted (p11-mix-nextsent-endif) and behaves per GR4. Recorded as one mechanism in finding IF-F1. Not closed by a test: the only named test, tests/CobolSharp.Tests.Unit/Overlenient/M413_OverlenientIfElseTests.cs, has THREE EMPTY [Fact] bodies -- see finding IF-F2.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolControlFlow.g4:136 (ifStatement); src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4:793 (statementBlock : statement+); src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolControlFlow.g4:365 (nextSentenceStatement)

subject: INITIALIZE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB415.md — Verified against the PRINTED page (PDF p.667 = folio 637, rendered; the OCR transcription agrees). FOUR divergences, three of which REJECT LEGAL SOURCE. (1) category-name is a THIRTEEN-alternative list enclosed by a BRACE with a pair of CHOICE-INDICATOR bars just inside it, so §5.2.6.4 gives it 'one or more of the alternatives … any single alternative … only once … in any order' — a SET. The grammar's initializeCategory is a SINGLE alternative naming only 5 of the 13 (alphabetic, alphanumeric, alphanumeric-edited, numeric, numeric-edited); BOOLEAN, DATA-POINTER, FUNCTION-POINTER, MESSAGE-TAG, NATIONAL, NATIONAL-EDITED, OBJECT-REFERENCE and PROGRAM-POINTER are a hard COBOL0001 'no viable alternative', and so is any two-word category-name (`REPLACING NUMERIC ALPHANUMERIC DATA BY …`, `G NUMERIC ALPHANUMERIC TO VALUE`) at EVERY edition including 85. The stale grammar comment blames 'lexer tokens not yet defined', but PROGRAM_POINTER, FUNCTION_POINTER and NATIONAL are already lexer tokens; the enum InitializeCategory itself models only 10 of 13 (no NationalEdited, FunctionPointer or MessageTag). (2) TO is NOT underlined in either `TO VALUE` or `THEN TO DEFAULT`, so §5.2.2/§5.2.3 make it an OPTIONAL word; the grammar requires it — `INITIALIZE G ALL VALUE` and `INITIALIZE G THEN DEFAULT` are COBOL0001, and `INITIALIZE G DEFAULT` is parsed as a second identifier-1 and reported COBOLNET1639 'DEFAULT is not defined'. (3) Over-acceptance: the ALL/category-name choice sits in a BRACE (§5.2.6.3 — one alternative 'shall be explicitly specified'), but the grammar writes `(ALL | initializeCategory)?`, so a bare `INITIALIZE G TO VALUE` compiles; the binder justifies it as '§14.9.20.2 note 2', a note that does not exist (GR2 says only that ALL ≡ all categories, which is a different question), and tests/conformance/2002/initialize_phrases.cob line 'INITIALIZE GRP TO VALUE.' PINS the over-acceptance GREEN. (4) Over-acceptance: two-word `ALPHANUMERIC EDITED` / `NUMERIC EDITED` are accepted though the printed list carries only the hyphenated words. CORRECT: the INITIALIZE keyword, {identifier-1}… repetition, the optional WITH before FILLER, the optional THEN before REPLACING, the optional DATA before BY, the {identifier-2|literal-1} brace, phrase order, and the four 2002 edition gates COBOLNET0830/0831/0832/0833 (all four fire at --std 85; bare REPLACING compiles at 85).  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4#initializeCategory; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4#initializeCategoryToValue; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4#initializeDefaultPhrase; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolData.g4#initializeStatement; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Bound/BoundInitialize.cs#InitializeCategory

subject: MOVE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB421.md — BOTH GENERAL FORMATS ARE FAITHFULLY IMPLEMENTED, and the diagram was verified as PRINTED (PDF p.694 rendered, not read off the OCR): Format 1 is MOVE {identifier-1|literal-1} TO {identifier-2}... with MOVE and TO underlined and identifier-2 in braces with an ellipsis (required, repeatable); Format 2 is MOVE {CORRESPONDING|CORR} identifier-3 TO identifier-4 with exactly ONE identifier-4 and no ellipsis. The transcription at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:25216-25230 matches the printed page character for character. Measured positive: MOVE A TO B C and MOVE A TO B, C, D bind both receivers; MOVE CORRESPONDING G1 TO G2 and MOVE CORR G1 TO G3 both run; a function-identifier as identifier-1 is admitted (correct - 8.4.3.1.2 Format 1 makes one an IDENTIFIER). Measured negative, both correct: a literal in the receiving position is rejected (COBOL0308 'A data-name is expected here, not a literal'), and MOVE CORRESPONDING G1 TO G2 G3 - a second identifier-4 Format 2 does not have - is a parse error. DIVERGENCE: moveReceivingPhrase carries a SECOND alternative, '(CORRESPONDING | CORR) dataReference TO dataReference', so the grammar admits 'MOVE <sending-operand> {CORRESPONDING|CORR} id-3 TO id-4' - a shape NEITHER general format has. It parses, MoveBinder.Bind cannot build it (move.CORRESPONDING() is null on the statement context because the token sits inside the receiving phrase, and moveReceivingPhrase() .dataReferenceList() is null), and the fall-through returns BoundUnsupported, which StatementEmitter.Visit renders as EmitCore.LoudStmt. So the program COMPILES CLEAN and dies at run time with NotImplementedCobolFeatureException: 'MOVE CORRESPONDING / unsupported MOVE form' - measured for the identifier sender (MOVE A CORRESPONDING G1 TO G2, MOVE A CORR G1 TO G2) and the literal sender (MOVE "Q" CORR G1 TO G2). Alternative 1 of moveStatement already carries the whole of Format 2, so the second alternative of moveReceivingPhrase is pure over-acceptance with no legal shape behind it. SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT AT THE SAME SITE: the section banner above the rule reads '// MOVE (14.9.24)' - 14.9.24 is the MERGE statement; MOVE is 14.9.25. The sweep rule 4 demands found this is SYSTEMIC across the grammar's statement banners: ADD cites 14.9.1 (=ACCEPT), MULTIPLY 14.9.23 (=INVOKE), SUBTRACT 14.9.42 (=STOP), ACCEPT 14.9.0 (does not exist), GOBACK 14.9.16 (=GENERATE), WRITE 14.9.46 (=TERMINATE), REWRITE 14.9.36 (=ROLLBACK), MERGE 14.9.22 (=INSPECT), RELEASE 14.9.33 (=RESUME), STRING 14.9.41 (=START), UNSTRING 14.9.44 (=SUBTRACT), INSPECT 14.9.21 (=INITIATE), ALTER 14.9.2 (=ADD). 14 of 30 banners point at a different statement - the CLAUDE.md rule-1 'inherited citation' failure mode, at scale. NO TEST covers the over-acceptance.  || CODE SITES (verbatim from the adjudication, kept because the schema's code-location is symbol-keyed, not line-keyed): src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#moveStatement; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#moveReceivingPhrase; src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#moveSendingOperand; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/Procedure/Verbs/MoveBinder.cs#Bind

subject: PERFORM statement
notes: kb/Work/PB431.md — The printed page was rendered (PDF folio 682 = page 712, scripts/render-spec-page.py 712) because the Format-3 figure is load-bearing; the render settles two things the ASCII transcription blurs: imperative-statement-1 sits on its OWN line ABOVE the outer brace (so it is unbracketed = REQUIRED, not an alternative of the WHEN group), and the mode operand really is printed `IO`, underlined. WHAT CONFORMS. Format 1's two bracket groups are independent and adjacent, and the compiler treats them so: `PERFORM P1 THRU P2 3 TIMES` = 33, `... VARYING I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL I > 2` = 22, `... UNTIL N > 20` = 22 (probe pf-fmt1-thru-times), and a SECOND control phrase on the out-of-line form is correctly a parse error (pf-fmt1-two-options). THROUGH/THRU both parse. Format 3's shape is right in every other respect: [WITH LOCATION] with WITH optional (bare LOCATION at 2023 only - the continuity invariant, since LOCATION stays a cobolWord below 2023: pf-f3-bare-location), the four open modes, the exception-name and exception-name FILE file-name forms, the fixed OTHER-then-COMMON-then-FINALLY order (writing COMMON before OTHER is rejected: pf-f3-order), the optional second EXCEPTION word, and END-PERFORM (pf-f3-full compiles and runs). The 2023 gates fire for both new constructs (COBOLNET0900 at --std 2014 for Format 3 and for UNTIL EXIT: pf-f3-at-2014, pf-until-exit-ool-gate). Reading the figure's `IO` as I-O is correct and I verified the premise rather than inheriting it: there is no standalone `IO` in the 8.9 reserved-word list, so `IO` there can only be a typesetting defect for I-O; the compiler consequently reads `WHEN EXCEPTION IO` as file-name-1 and says "unknown file 'IO'" (pf-f3-io-spelling), which is the right reading. WHAT DIVERGES - FOUR SEPARATE SHAPE ERRORS. (1) Formats 2 and 3 admit a LIST of loop-control phrases. The printed bracket around times-phrase/until-phrase/varying-phrase is a plain bracket over three stacked alternatives = ZERO OR ONE. performInlineHead is `performOptions+`. `PERFORM 3 TIMES UNTIL X > 100 ADD 1 TO X END-PERFORM` compiles clean and iterates 3 times - the UNTIL is silently discarded by BindPerformControl's FirstOrDefault (probe pf-two-options, X=3); reverse the order and the TIMES is discarded instead (pf-drop-order, X=5); three phrases drop two (pf-three-options). Reproduces identically at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023. (2) Format 3 has NO loop-control phrase at all, yet the merged inline alternative lets the head precede the WHEN phrases and EcBindExceptionPerform never reads it: `PERFORM 3 TIMES <body> WHEN EC-ALL ... END-PERFORM` compiles clean and runs the body ONCE (pf-times-with-when, X=1). (3) The varying-phrase's FROM and BY slots are typed arithmeticExpression where the figure prints {identifier-3|index-name-2|literal-1} and {identifier-4|literal-2}. That is wider AND narrower than the format: `PERFORM VARYING I FROM A + B BY B * 2 UNTIL I > 20` is accepted with no diagnostic at any --std (pf-varying-expr), while the LEGAL figurative constant `FROM ZERO` is a hard parse error (pf-zero-varying-from, pf-zeros-varying, pf-zero-varying-ool) because primaryExpression reaches ZERO only through the adjacency-rewritten ZERO_ARITH token - `FROM ZERO + 0` parses (pf-zero-plus-varying) and proves the rewriter is the gate. (2) CARDINALITY, INVERTED BOTH WAYS BY ONE MERGED RULE: `recordLockPhrase : IGNORING LOCK | WITH? NO LOCK | WITH? LOCK` reached through three free optionals made the LEGAL pair `IGNORING LOCK WITH NO LOCK` a syntax error (`no viable alternative at input 'WITH'`) while accepting `ADVANCING ON LOCK RETRY 3 TIMES IGNORING LOCK`, three alternatives out of one bracket. ADVANCING LOCK` is conforming; it was `error COBOL0001: missing token before 'LOCK'` and now compiles (golden line S2). END-READ` compiled clean, exit 0, no diagnostics. 14.9.30.2 Format 1 prints it once, after the {NEXT|PREVIOUS} braces, and 5.2.3 makes a non-underlined word one that may be omitted, not repeated. `readDirection` is now `NEXT | PREVIOUS` and the word lives in one place (negative/pb331-read-record-word-twice). subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB347 LANDED. FORMAT, rendered from the licensed PDF rather than read from the OCR (scripts/render-spec-page.py, PDF page 734 = printed 704): `RELEASE record-name-1 [ FROM { identifier-1 | literal-1 } ]`, with RELEASE and FROM the underlined required words -- the transcription at 14.9.32.2 is faithful, and the operand IS record-name-1, not identifier-1. THE DIVERGENCE THIS ROW CARRIED (over-acceptance of the record-name-1 POSITION) IS CLOSED: `RELEASE SRT-REC(1:3)` used to compile with NO diagnostic at any --std and emit CobolSort.Release(..., CobolString.RefMod(SRT_REC.AsImage(), 1, 3)), releasing a 3-character record into an 8-byte sort file; it is now COBOLNET1757 at every edition. The rule behind it: a record-name is a user-defined word (8.3.2.2.25) and 5.2.4's operand table gives that operand type 'User-defined word, including qualification and subscripting if needed' and nothing further, while 8.4.3.3.3 SR5 permits reference modification only 'anywhere an identifier referencing a data item of class alphanumeric, boolean, or national is permitted' -- its NOTE drawing the consequence, 'where data-name-n is used in a general format or syntax rule, then reference-modification is not permitted' (all three --check OK). The refusal is at BIND, not in the grammar: `releaseStatement : RELEASE dataReference` stays general because the subordinate-item half of the same rule cannot be decided by a grammar, and one rule belongs in one place. THE ACCEPTED SURFACE IS UNCHANGED and still verified in both positive goldens: FROM omitted; FROM identifier; FROM subscripted identifier; FROM reference-modified identifier (an IDENTIFIER position, where 8.4.3.3.3 SR5 does permit it); FROM alphanumeric literal; FROM figurative constants (8.3.3.6.3 SR1). EDITION LEG unchanged: the literal-1 arm is gated 2002+ (`release-from-literal-2002` -> COBOLNET0871); the functionCall arm (the deliberate PB10 addition, legal by 8.4.3.1.2) carries no gate. Annex E lists no substantive change to 14.9.32, so 2014 and 2023 are identical; the 85/2002 boundary for either FROM arm is not derivable from this document -- a dossier gap, not a verdict.

subject: RETURN statement
notes: kb/Work PB350; PB351; PB320. FORMAT RE-DERIVED FROM THE PRINTED PAGE (CLAUDE.md rule 1 - the diagram is load-bearing): python scripts/render-spec-page.py 738 (printed folio 708) renders 'RETURN file-name-1 RECORD [ INTO identifier-1 ] / AT END imperative-statement-1 / [ NOT AT END imperative-statement-2 ] / [ END-RETURN ]'. The AT END line carries NO bracket and NO choice indicators - unlike READ, whose own transcription figure note records the printed bar pair. The markdown transcription is FAITHFUL here. Therefore the AT END phrase is REQUIRED: cite.py --check 5.2.2 'They are required in order to select the functionality associated with that keyword' -> OK, and --check 5.2.6.2 'may be explicitly specified or that portion of the general format may be omitted' -> OK (brackets are the ONLY thing that makes a portion omissible). RECORD and AT are un-underlined optional words: --check 8.3.2.4.3 'uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option' -> OK. CODE: CobolIO.g4:679 returnStatement writes 'returnAtEndPhrase?' - the WHOLE phrase optional - and returnAtEndPhrase's second alternative 'NOT AT? END statementBlock (AT? END statementBlock)?' makes the AT END half of the reversed pair optional too. SortBinder.BindReturn:268-273 accepts atEnd=null (PhraseBlocks.Split returns (null, first) for the NOT-led single-block form) and SortEmitter.EmitReturn:172-180 then emits an EMPTY else arm. grep over src for returnAtEndPhrase: SortBinder.cs:269 is the ONLY consumer - no later pass enforces it. REPRO A (probe p1, out-b1/probe/p1/p1.cob): a SORT OUTPUT PROCEDURE whose body is 'RETURN SF RECORD END-RETURN. DISPLAY "R=" S-TXT.' looped 4 times. EXPECTED from the format: rejected at compile time (no AT END phrase). OBSERVED: compiles clean and runs at --std 85, 2002, 2014 AND 2023, printing R=ONE / R=TWO / R=TWO / R=TWO - past end-of-file the record area silently keeps the last record. REPRO B (probe p2): 'RETURN SF NOT AT END DISPLAY "R=" S-TXT END-RETURN.' - the NOT-only form, equally illegal (SR4 permits reversal only 'when specified', and AT END is unconditionally specified) - accepted at all four editions. SECOND MECHANISM ON THE SAME ROW: statementBlock (CobolParserCore.g4:793) is 'statement+', so a conditional statement NOT delimited by its explicit scope terminator is accepted where the format writes imperative-statement-1. Spec: 14.5.1 - 'An imperative statement specifies an unconditional action ... or is a conditional statement that is delimited by its explicit scope terminator' and 'Any statement with a conditional phrase that is not terminated by its explicit scope terminator is a conditional statement'. Probe p12 ('AT END IF WS-EOF = "N" MOVE "Y" TO WS-EOF NOT AT END DISPLAY ...' with no END-IF) compiles and runs. This one is cross-cutting - readAtEnd and every sibling conditional phrase share statementBlock. CONFORMING PARTS, verified: RECORD? and AT? (optional words), the INTO / NOT AT END / END-RETURN brackets, operand order, and the SR4 reversed pair. TWO INHERITED-CITATION DEFECTS in the implementing grammar file (CLAUDE.md rule 1's named failure mode): CobolIO.g4:687 justifies AT? with 'ISO 14.9.39 - "AT" is an optional reserved word', but 14.9.39 is the SET statement (--check 14.9.39.1 'The SET statement provides a means for' -> OK); the authority is 8.3.2.4.3. CobolIO.g4:698 heads the RELEASE block '// RELEASE (14.9.33)', but 14.9.33 is RESUME (--check 14.9.33.1 -> OK) and RELEASE is 14.9.32 (--check 14.9.32.1 'The RELEASE statement transfers records to the initial phase of a sort operation.' -> OK). No kb/Work note owns these rows; a register note is owed.

CONFORMING PARTS (read + measured): phrase ORDER in both formats; `VARYING { identifier-2 | index-name-1 }` (dataReference covers both, and BindSearch:43-49 splits same-table index / other index / data item); `AT?` -- AT is printed WITHOUT an underline, so it is an optional word per 5.2.3 and the AT-less spelling is conforming, which the grammar comment at :226 gets right; `searchWhenClause+` for Format 1; optional END-SEARCH. subject: SET statement
notes:
kb/Work/PB450.md — DIAGRAM RENDERED, NOT TRUSTED FROM OCR (CLAUDE.md rule 1): PDF pages 759, 760 and 761 (printed folios 729, 730, 731) at 300dpi -> scratchpad/lane3/out-b2/spec_p759.png / spec_p760.png / spec_p761.png. The print CONFIRMS specs/ISO_COBOL.md EXACTLY for Formats 1-14, including the four bracketing facts this row turns on: (i) Format 3's `{ {mnemonic-name-1} ... TO {ON|OFF} } ...` carries the ellipsis OUTSIDE the outer brace, so the whole switch phrase repeats; (ii) Format 4's `{ {condition-name-1} ... TO {TRUE|FALSE} } ...` has the IDENTICAL outer-brace-plus-ellipsis shape; (iii) Format 7's `{ ADDRESS OF data-name-1 | identifier-5 } ... TO identifier-6` puts the ellipsis OUTSIDE the receiving brace, so the receiving operand repeats AND MIXES the two alternatives; (iv) Format 6's six attribute keywords sit between CHOICE INDICATORS (the doubled vertical bars are visible in the render). Citations validated: `cite.py --check 14.9.39.2 "Format 6 (attribute)"`, `"Format 7 (data-pointer-assignment)"`, `"the following ... repeats the braced receiving operand"`, `"The outer braces enclose the single repeated unit; the trailing ... repeats the whole braced portion"`, `"Format 15 (numeric-content)"`, `"Format 17 (message-tag)"` -> all OK.

CONFORMING (measured on the pinned cobol.exe): F1 with a MIXED receiving list (`SET IX WS-N TO 2` -> N=[0002], probe h1_mixed_recv); F3 with BOTH repetitions (`SET SW1 TO ON SW2 TO OFF`, probe h8_switch_repeat -> S1ON/OK); F5 with several identifier-3 receivers (probe i4_multi_objrecv -> PONG); F9 with several identifier-7 receivers (probe f4_pp_multi); F10 (probe g1_ptr_upby); F11/F12 (SetLocaleDispositionTests, PB64 T1, landed); F13; F14; F16 in both the SIZE OF and the bare spellings.

FOUR DIVERGENCES MEASURED, all reproduced at every edition the format exists in:
(1) FORMAT 4's OUTER REPETITION IS A PARSE ERROR. `SET CF-A TO TRUE CG-A TO TRUE` -> `COBOL0001: unexpected 'TO'` (probe h2_cond_repeat, --std 2023). The grammar is `setBooleanStatement : SET dataReference+ TO (TRUE_|FALSE_)` (CobolParserCore.g4:1254) - one group only. This is the two-arm shape: Format 3 and Format 4 are the SAME printed shape and setSwitchStatement (:1236) was written as `SET (dataReference+ TO (ON|OFF))+`, i.e. WITH the outer repetition, while its twin two rules below was not.
(2) FORMAT 7's RECEIVING LIST CANNOT REPEAT OR MIX, and identifier-6 cannot be a data-address-identifier. Four legal statements are COBOL0001 parse errors: `SET ADDRESS OF B1 ADDRESS OF B2 TO P1` (probe c1_two_addr_recv), `SET P1 P2 TO ADDRESS OF REC1` (c2), `SET ADDRESS OF B1 P1 TO P2` (c3), `SET ADDRESS OF B1 TO ADDRESS OF R1` (i3_addr_to_addr). setAddressStatement's two alternatives each take exactly ONE receiver and the ADDRESS OF sender form is a separate alternative, so the printed cross-product is not expressible.
(3) FORMAT 2's `{ index-name-3 } ...` ADMITS A PLAIN NUMERIC DATA ITEM, SILENTLY. `SET WS-N UP BY 4` with `01 WS-N PIC 9(4) VALUE 1` compiles with ZERO diagnostics and RUNS, printing N=[0005] (probe g2_num_upby). Nothing screens it - setIndexStatement is `SET dataReference+ (UP|DOWN) BY arithmeticExpression` and SetBinder.BindSetUpDown falls through to SetTargetOf, which accepts any resolvable receiving operand.
(4) FORMAT 15 (numeric-content) HAS NO SURFACE AT ALL. `SET CONTENT OF WS-F TO FLOAT-INFINITY` -> `COBOL0001: no viable alternative at input 'SETCONTENT'` (probe h4_content_of); CONTENT/FARTHEST-FROM-ZERO/NEAREST-TO-ZERO/FLOAT-INFINITY/FLOAT-NOT-A-NUMBER appear nowhere in src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/. subject: START statement
notes:
kb/Work PB332; PB320. RULE (--check 14.9.41.2, figure note): 'START, FIRST, KEY (the phrase-leading one), LAST, LENGTH, INVALID, NOT, and END-START are underlined in the printed standard (required words); file-name-1, relational-operator, WITH, and the KEY of INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY are not underlined.' I DID NOT TRUST THE OCR FOR THIS ONE: the general format is load-bearing here and the transcription's known bias is toward falsely-restrictive syntax, so I rendered the printed diagram myself at 600 dpi (PDF page 784 = printed folio 754; the figure-note's 'page 754' is the FOLIO, PDF page 754 is a SEARCH page) and read it. The render confirms: START/FIRST/KEY/LAST/LENGTH/INVALID/NOT/END-START underlined; relational-operator carries NO brackets (required inside the KEY phrase); the {data-name-1 | record-key-name-1} BRACE group; '[ WITH LENGTH arithmetic-expression-1 ]' with WITH un-underlined; a PLAIN outer bracket over FIRST/KEY/LAST; the choice-indicator bars inside the INVALID KEY brackets; '[ END-START ]'. The transcription is faithful.
CODE: startStatement : START fileName (FIRST | LAST | startKeyPhrase)? startInvalidKeyPhrase? END_START?.
WHAT CONFORMS (probed, out-b1/probe/fmt2 and /sr5-excl): at most one of FIRST/KEY/LAST -- 'START RLF FIRST KEY IS = WS-RK' draws COBOL0001 'no viable alternative at input KEY'; the INVALID group behaves as choice indicators -- both phrases with NOT INVALID FIRST ran (G1-NOTINV), neither phrase ran (G2-ST=00), INVALID alone ran; 'INVALID <imperative>' without the optional word KEY ran (G4-INV); END-START omissible; the 2002 introduction gate on FIRST fires at --std 85 (COBOLNET0900, out-b1/probe/ed85).
WHAT DIVERGES -- two words, in opposite directions:
(1) startWithLength : WITH LENGTH arithmeticExpression makes WITH REQUIRED. WITH is not underlined, i.e. an OPTIONAL word -- 5.2.3 (--check): 'Optional words are reserved words or context-sensitive words. They are shown in uppercase and not underlined in general formats.' So 'START IXF KEY IS = IX-KEY LENGTH 3' is conforming source. Probed (out-b1/probe/fmt): rejected -- COBOL0001 'missing token before 3' plus two cascade errors. REJECTS LEGAL SOURCE.
(2) startKeyPhrase : KEY IS? comparisonOperator? dataReference makes relational-operator OPTIONAL where the rendered format requires it. Probed (out-b1/probe/ix-ops): 'START IXF KEY IS IX-KEY' compiles and RUNS (P1-OK ST=00). subject: SUBTRACT statement
notes: All three printed formats implemented and measured. PRINTED PAGE RENDERED (licensed PDF p.762, ISO/IEC 1989:2023) and matched against specs/ISO_COBOL.md line-for-line: F1 `SUBTRACT {identifier-1|literal-1}... FROM {identifier-2 [rounded-phrase]}...`; F2 adds `FROM {identifier-2|literal-2}` + `GIVING {identifier-3 [rounded-phrase]}...`; F3 `{CORRESPONDING|CORR} identifier-4 FROM identifier-5 [rounded-phrase]`; each with the bracketed CHOICE-INDICATOR size-error group and `[END-SUBTRACT]`. Underlining measured off the render: ON is NOT underlined in either size-error line (optional word) and the grammar has `ON?` in both arms (CobolParserCore.g4:840,842). MEASURED (probe dir probe/subtract): p1 F1 multi-operand + multi-receiver + per-receiver ROUNDED; p2/g6 F2 with literal-2 and with several GIVING receivers each carrying its own ROUNDED; p3/p4/m3 F3 with both CORR and CORRESPONDING, ROUNDED after identifier-5, both size-error branches, END-SUBTRACT; g7 the REVERSED phrase order (5.2.6.4 choice indicators - zero or more, each at most once, any order); h5 END-SUBTRACT as a scope terminator inside IF; h1 the FROM sender as a data reference; g9/g10 a function-identifier in both sending positions (8.4.3.1.2 makes it an identifier). The format-mixing violations the union grammar admits are narrowed back at bind and REJECTED AT COMPILE TIME with COBOLNET1689: two FROM operands under GIVING (g1), ROUNDED on the F2 sending operand (g2), operands with no FROM (g3), a literal receiver in F1 (g4), GIVING with no FROM (g5), a function-identifier F1 receiver (g11). Verified at --std 85/2002/2014/2023 (h2); ROUNDED MODE IS gates 2014+ (h3, COBOLNET0803 - 14.7.4's row, not this one). Additional spec-derived goldens touching this row: conformance:85/optional_on_size_error (ON omittable, SUBTRACT leg), conformance:2023/pb134_giving_sending_operands (F2 one sending literal), conformance:2023/pb45_function_in_sending_operands (F2 function sender). subject: USE statement
notes: kb/Work PB332; PB365. The format's four figures were compared token by token with the grammar rule. CONFORMING: the {EXCEPTION|ERROR} brace (SR6), [GLOBAL] on Formats 1 and 2 only (probe GLOBF3.cob: `USE GLOBAL AFTER EC EC-SIZE.` is correctly a parse error, GLOBF1.cob compiles), `{file-name-1}...` as fileName+ (probe SR5MIX.cob `ON F1 F2`), the four mode alternatives, `{EXCEPTION CONDITION|EC}` (SR12), `exception-name-2 {FILE file-name-2}...` as useEcEntry `cobolWord (FILE fileName)*` with the outer ellipsis as useEcEntry+, `{EXCEPTION OBJECT|EO}` (SR15) and its ONE operand. The two 2002-introduction gates fire (probes F3AT85/F4AT85: COBOLNET0877 / COBOLNET0876), and the extra `USE FOR DEBUGGING` alternative is the X3.23-1985 element correctly rejected at 2023 (probe DBG23: COBOLNET0902). DIVERGENCE 1 (rejects legal source): 8.3.2.4.3 'Within each format, uppercase words that are not underlined are called optional words and may be specified at the user's option with no effect on the semantics of the format' (and 5.2.3) makes AFTER, STANDARD, PROCEDURE and ON of Format 1, and AFTER of Formats 3 and 4, OPTIONAL words -- the figure notes measured exactly that underlining. The grammar writes `USE GLOBAL? AFTER STANDARD? (EXCEPTION|ERROR) PROCEDURE ON? useOnTarget`, i.e. STANDARD and ON optional but AFTER and PROCEDURE REQUIRED, and `USE AFTER (EXCEPTION CONDITION|EC)` / `USE AFTER (EXCEPTION OBJECT|EO)` with AFTER required. Probes (cobol.exe --std 2023; the pinned worktree's CobolControlFlow.g4 and ProcedureTableBuilder.cs are byte-identical to the main tree's, so the results are attributable to the pin): `USE ERROR PROCEDURE ON F1.` -> error COBOL0001 "no viable alternative at input 'USEERROR'"; `USE AFTER STANDARD ERROR ON F1.` -> error COBOL0001 "missing token before 'ON'"; `USE EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-ALL.` -> COBOL0001; `USE EC EC-ALL.` -> COBOL0001; `USE EXCEPTION OBJECT CF4A.` -> COBOL0001. Each is legal standard COBOL that 4.2.2 requires the implementation to accept. DIVERGENCE 2: Format 4's second brace group has two alternatives, object-class-name-1 and interface-name-1; the binder resolves only the class arm (SR17 row). Recorded but NOT counted against this row: Format 2's identifier-1 is parsed by `procedureName` rather than an identifier rule -- adequate in practice (a report group's only qualifier is its report-name, one OF/IN level, which procedureName carries), but it also admits an INTEGERLIT where 8.4.3.1 admits none. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: Formats 1-2: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023. Formats 3-4: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the EC exception-condition model and the OO exception-object model). Basis: Annex E records no 2023 change to any part of 14.9.49.2 (its only USE entries, items 19a/19b, are 14.9.49.4 GR6 declarative-selection corrections), and Annex F designates no part of the USE statement obsolete or archaic.

FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER INTRINSIC.' works.

All four re-run by me.

notes: SUSTAINED. subject: SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: Citation validated: cite.py --check 15.83.2 'FUNCTION</u> <u>SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC' -> OK (General format). The format is FUNCTION SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC ( argument-1 ) -- both words underlined and required, one required argument, no optional, alternative or repeating part, so there is nothing bracketed to accept and nothing repeated to count. Code READ, three layers. (a) SYNTAX: CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall -- 'FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*' -- carries the shape generically, with the 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 argument-list parens retyped by the lexer so a parenthesised argument is never read as a subscript or a grouping paren. (b) THE PER-FUNCTION SHAPE: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build's row Add(new('SMALLEST-ALGEBRAIC', IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, 'n', '', IntrinsicBind.Fold, false, 2023, Result: IntegerFollowsArgument1)) fixes MinArgs = MaxArgs = 1 and the 2023 window. subject: SQRT function
notes: CONFORMS. The general format, read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33307-33309, is `FUNCTION SQRT ( argument-1 )` with FUNCTION and SQRT both UNDERLINED — required words — and exactly one argument inside required parentheses; there is no optional phrase, no ellipsis, and no second format. READ, GRAMMAR: src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 line 333 — `: FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` — so the FUNCTION keyword and the name are both required at this production, and the argument list's '(' is lexed in the dedicated FNARG mode so §8.4.3.2 SR6 ('that ( is ALWAYS the argument list') holds rather than the '(' being read as a subscript or a grouping paren. The optionality of the paren group in the grammar is deliberate (it serves the zero-argument functions) and does NOT leak into SQRT: the arity is the CATALOG's. READ, ARITY: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build line 133 — Add(new("SQRT", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "n", "Sqrt", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) — MinArgs = MaxArgs = 1, enforced at IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore lines 572-579: `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)` -> COBOLNET1504 'FUNCTION SQRT takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)'. So a bare `FUNCTION SQRT` (given 0) and `FUNCTION SQRT(A B)` (given 2) are both rejected with the §15.3 citation. The FUNCTION-omitted spelling (§8.4.3.2.3 SR2, a REPOSITORY INTRINSIC declaration) is gated the same way — IntrinsicBinder.cs lines 301 and 339 both refuse to route a name written without an argument list unless sig.MinArgs == 0, which SQRT's is not. The row's IntrinsicType.Numeric matches §15.84.1's 'The type of this function is numeric'. GOLDEN: conformance:2023/pb52_intrinsic_argument_stage writes the format both ways argument-1 can be spelled (a data item, `FUNCTION SQRT(NI)`, and a literal, `FUNCTION SQRT(4)`), each pinned to 2.00 in the .out. NOT COVERED: there is no SQRT-specific arity negative fixture; the COBOLNET1504 guard is catalog-driven and generic, so a SQRT-specific one could only re-test the shared guard. EDITIONS: the format is unchanged across the four editions (SQRT is a 1989 Intrinsic Function Module amendment function); batch default.

subject: STANDARD-DEVIATION function
notes: Format read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.86.2: `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION ( { argument-1 } … )` — FUNCTION and STANDARD-DEVIATION underlined (required keywords), the parenthesised list NOT bracketed (required), and the brace-ellipsis making argument-1 one-or-more. Both halves of the format located and read. HALF 1, the keyword/name/paren shape: the grammar carries no STANDARD-DEVIATION production (grep of src/Cobol.Net.Frontend for the name returns nothing) because the form is generic — CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall is `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, and CobolExpressions.g4#functionName admits IDENTIFIER. Checked the lexer for the hyphen hazard, since CobolLexer.g4 does carry STANDARD (:536), STANDARD_BINARY/STANDARD_DECIMAL (:264-265) and STANDARD_1/STANDARD_2 (:669-670) but no STANDARD_DEVIATION token: ANTLR maximal munch gives IDENTIFIER the full 18-character 'STANDARD-DEVIATION' over STANDARD's 8, which is the documented behavior at CobolLexer.g4:261-262 ('a bare STANDARD still lexes as STANDARD, and WC-COBOL still lexes as one IDENTIFIER'). The argument-list paren is retyped FNARG_LPAREN per §8.4.3.2.3 SR6, so the list is never read as a grouping or subscript paren. HALF 2, the one-or-more arity: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build:139 declares Add(new("STANDARD-DEVIATION", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "StandardDeviation", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) — MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue, matching `{ argument-1 } …` exactly; IntrinsicBinder.cs:572-579 computes `given` and raises COBOLNET1504 'takes at least 1 argument(s)' when given < MinArgs, which catches both the bare `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION` and the empty-parens `()` form the grammar's optional group admits. IntrinsicType.Numeric matches §15.86.1 ('The type of this function is numeric'). Closing test: tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.cob line 45 writes the format `FUNCTION STANDARD-DEVIATION(2, 2, 2)`, it is registered in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json:123, and tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.out line 8 pins SD=0.0 — so the format demonstrably lexes, parses and binds. The fixture is spec-derived (its header derives every line from §15.4.1 r1 and the functions' own EAEs), not a characterization or legacy-match. Editions: Annex E (specs/ISO_COBOL.md:42847 onward) carries no STANDARD-DEVIATION entry and the clause has no edition-varying content, so the batch default stands; the editions field was NOT read off IntrinsicCatalog's own IntroducedIn column.

subject: SUBSTITUTE function
notes: kb/Work PB81 (2026-08-18): FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 { [ANYCASE] [FIRST | LAST] argument-2 argument-3 } … ) — the pair repeats, so §15.3's table(ALL) is admissible among the pairs and its elements form the pairs by position at run time (the FLAT form: CobolIntrinsics.SubstituteFlat pairs the enumerated elements; a keyword before an enumeration attaches to the pair its first element opens). subject: SUM function
notes:
Format read directly from specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.88.2 (line 33495-33499): `FUNCTION SUM ( { argument-1 } … )` — FUNCTION and SUM underlined (required), the argument-list parentheses present, and the braced argument-1 followed by an ellipsis, i.e. ONE OR MORE. Both halves READ and verified. (1) THE REFERENCE SHAPE: CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, with SUM present in CobolExpressions.g4#functionName (line 458) — needed because SUM is one of the §8.9 reserved words that is also a §8.11 intrinsic name. The keyword-omitted twin `SUM(…)` rides CobolExpressions.g4#reservedIntrinsicArgFn (`SIGN | SUM`), and IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsic lines 54-63 enforces §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 on it (COBOLNET1543 unless REPOSITORY declares SUM / FUNCTION ALL INTRINSIC) — so the abbreviated form is not accepted unconditionally. Arguments juxtapose or take the §8.3.5 separator via functionArgList. §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 is decided from the DEFINITION before binding (DefinitionPermitsArguments("SUM") is true since MaxArgs > 0), so `FUNCTION SUM (1:4)` draws Sr6ArgumentListError, not a bogus arity error; §8.4.3.3.3 SR2 rejects reference-modifying SUM's numeric result (ResultRefMod, COBOLNET1629). (2) THE 1..n MULTIPLICITY: IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build line 152 `Add(new("SUM", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "SumScaled", …))` — MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue; IntrinsicBinder.cs line 573 raises COBOLNET1504 ("takes at least 1 argument(s); 0 given (ISO §15.3)") for `FUNCTION SUM` written with no list or an empty one, and the unbounded max means no upper rejection. The ellipsis also licenses the §15.3 table(ALL) argument: IntrinsicSig.RepeatsAnArgument (MaxArgs == int.MaxValue) gates TryBindAllArgument, and its own diagnostic text names SUM as an example of a `{ argument } …` format. TESTS: tests/Cobol.Net.Tests.Unit/IntrinsicRepeatedArgumentDriftTests.cs re-reads §15.88.2's `<pre>` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md and asserts the catalog's unboundedness EQUALS the presence of the '…' character — spec-derived in the strict sense (the assertion's oracle is the standard's own text, not a hand list). tests/conformance/2023/pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges.cob exercises the repeated-argument format over ALL (fixed, ODO, dynamic-capacity, two-level, and a mixed `SUM(F(ALL) WS-E(ALL))`); pb58_argument_predicates_legal.cob exercises the plain 3-argument written form. NOT covered by a dedicated fixture: a zero-argument `FUNCTION SUM` negative case — the COBOLNET1504 arm was read in source but has no SUM-specific golden; that is a test gap, not a behavior gap (the arm is shared and exercised by other MinArgs rows).

REFUTER (verdict SUSTAINED after independent attack): the format was re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md:33494-33499 and §8.4.3.2.3 re-read whole at :6020ff. SR2 ("If intrinsic-function-name-1 or the ALL phrase is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph … the word FUNCTION may be omitted from the function-identifier; otherwise the word FUNCTION is required") and SR6 ("If a function's definition permits arguments and a left parenthesis immediately follows … the left parenthesis is always treated as the left parenthesis of that function's arguments") both check out against IntrinsicBinder.cs:57 (COBOLNET1543) and :88 (Sr6ArgumentListError, via DefinitionPermitsArguments reading MaxArgs > 0 from the catalog row). The keyword-omitted alternative `reservedIntrinsicArgFn subscriptPart refModPart*` (CobolExpressions.g4:334-346) REQUIRES the subscript group, so a bare `SUM` can never be read as a function reference — which is correct precisely because §15.88.2 has no zero-argument form, and is what keeps the report-writer `SUM OF` clause and the `SIGN` data-description clause from being swallowed. The drift test was read in full and is genuinely spec-derived: it re-scans every `#### 15.x.2 General format` block out of specs/ISO_COBOL.md, keys on the '…' character, asserts a ≥79-row floor on BOTH the spec scan and the catalog scan so the scanner cannot silently find nothing, and asserts the equivalence in both directions — it closes the UNBOUNDED half of `{ argument-1 } …`. The at-least-one half rests on reading only (IntrinsicBinder.cs:573, MinArgs 1) with no SUM-specific fixture, which rule 3 expressly permits for CONFORMS. ONE RESIDUE FOUND AND DELIBERATELY NOT COUNTED AGAINST THIS ROW: with a runtime-ranged table(ALL) the compile-time count is `all.StaticCount ?? 1` (IntrinsicBinder.cs:572), so an OCCURS DEPENDING object of 0 satisfies MinArgs at compile time and the enumerated list reaches the runtime EMPTY — CobolIntrinsics.Dec.cs#SumDec would then throw IndexOutOfRangeException on `xs[0]` and CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled would return 0. §15.3 makes exactly that case undefined ("The evaluation of an ALL subscript shall result in at least one argument, otherwise the result of the reference to the function-identifier is undefined"), so it is not a violation of this format rule; it is worth a robustness note elsewhere, not a downgrade here. Verdict held at CONFORMS.

(2) The grammar claim was NOT taken on trust: CobolExpressions.g4:333 is verbatim `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*`, and the FNARG re-typing is real — CobolLexer.g4:14 `tokens { FNARG_LPAREN, FNARG_RPAREN }` and CobolLexer.g4:119 `if (PreviousIsFunctionName()) Type = FNARG_LPAREN;` — so §8.4.3.2.3 SR6 is mechanically enforced, not asserted. notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: cite.py --check 15.91.2 "FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD" -> OK, General format; the printed format is exactly 'FUNCTION TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD ( argument-1 )' - one REQUIRED argument, parenthesised, no optional phrase, no ellipsis, no keyword. READ: (1) src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 functionCall ('FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*') accepts the written form generically - the name needs no grammar token, which is why grep finds none in the Frontend; (2) IntrinsicCatalog.cs#Build carries Add(new("TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "i", "TestDayYyyyddd", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002)) so MinArgs==MaxArgs==1 and IntrinsicBinder.cs (the 'given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs' guard) raises COBOLNET1504 on 0 or 2 arguments - the format's arity is enforced, not merely declared; (3) the result is IntrinsicType.Integer so a refModPart on the call is rejected by IntrinsicBinder's RefModFunctionResultClass arm ('is not an alphanumeric, boolean, or national function', ISO 8.4.3.3.3 SR2) - the grammar's optional refModPart* cannot over-accept here.
