(a) Citation re-derived from scratch: cite.py --check 15.91.2 "TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD" -> OK, and specs/ISO_COBOL.md 33617-33622 shows the format is one line, one bracket-free argument. (d) THE REJECT HALF was verified arm by arm, not inferred: arity at IntrinsicBinder.cs:573-579 (COBOLNET1504, reached because TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD matches no bespoke arm between the 493 edition gate and the 565 generic path, and ArgKinds "i" does not end in 'l'); the ALL subscript at TryBindAllArgument (2553-2587) rejects with AllSubscriptNotRepeatable because sig.RepeatsAnArgument is MaxArgs == int.MaxValue and this row's MaxArgs is 1; the result ref-mod at FinishIntrinsic (132-149) -> ResultRefMod (169-195), whose category comes from IntrinsicSig.CategoryOf (93-99) mapping IntrinsicType.Integer to PicCategory.Numeric - not one of Alphanumeric/National/Boolean, so SR2 fires. subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes:
THE FORMAT READ OFF THE PRINTED CLAUSE (specs/ISO_COBOL.md §15.92.2, lines 33665-33668): `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME ( argument-1 argument-2)`. FUNCTION and the function-name are UNDERLINED, so both are required key words; the two argument operands are unbracketed and carry no ellipsis, so exactly two arguments, both required, and no repetition (feedback_underlining_not_bracketing — I measured the <u> markup, I did not infer from brackets).

GENERIC HALF — the keyword/name/parenthesised-list shape. Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4: `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart* | ...` and `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`. The separator rule is what matters for THIS format: it admits BOTH the bare juxtaposition §15.92.2 itself prints and the §8.3.5 comma separator, and the corpus exercises both spellings (below). TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME is not a §8.9 reserved word, so it arrives through the ordinary functionName/cobolWord slot; hyphens are COBOL-word characters, so the name lexes whole.

PER-FUNCTION HALF — the name, the arity and the edition window — is the catalog row at IntrinsicCatalog#Build (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:310): Add(new("TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 2, 2, "ss", "TestFormattedDatetime", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2014)). ⚠ I READ THE IntrinsicSig RECORD DECLARATION (IntrinsicCatalog.cs:52-57) to confirm the POSITIONAL meaning of `2, 2` (MinArgs, MaxArgs) and of `2014` (IntroducedIn) instead of counting commas. The grammar's paren group is OPTIONAL, i.e. a superset parse; what actually makes both arguments REQUIRED and forbids a third is BindIntrinsicCore's arity gate — `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs) ctx.Edition.Error("COBOLNET1504", ...)` — so a bare `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME` (0 given) and a 3-argument call are both rejected against MinArgs=MaxArgs=2.

RESULT TYPE, since the format's clause head fixes it: §15.92.1 "The type of this function is integer" — the row's IntrinsicType.Integer, and IntrinsicRenderer.cs:334 `case "TestFormattedDatetime": return new NumX(RuntimeApi.DateFn(...), 0)` renders it at SCALE 0, i.e. as an integer.

TESTS: both separator spellings of the printed format are pinned by spec-derived programs. conformance:2023/pb23_week_date_beyond_integer_date_form writes `FUNCTION TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME("YYYYWwwD" "9999W526")` — the exact space juxtaposition §15.92.2 prints, which is the harder half and is easy to leave untested; conformance:2014/formatted_datetime and the AssertSpec theory write the §8.3.5 comma form. ⚠ NOT TESTED under this function's name: the arity REJECTIONS. The COBOLNET1504 gate is generic and catalog-driven (read at IntrinsicBinder.cs:572-579) and is exercised elsewhere (tests/conformance/2023/pb24_length_physical_keyword pins it for FUNCTION LENGTH), but no fixture gives TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME one or three arguments.

EDITIONS from the standard: Annex E (the 2014->2023 change record) carries no occurrence of the name, so the general format is unchanged at 2023; 2014 is the introduction edition the family is gated at, and the landed sibling row AR-15.92.3-2 records the same window. Not derived from the catalog row.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL function
notes:

subject: TEST-NUMVAL-C function
notes:
PB250 LANDED — the format was already correct (the printed page was re-rendered, scripts/render-spec-page.py 958 = printed folio 928, and all eight legal shapes trace through BindNumvalCFamily's positional walk); the PARTIAL was owed to (a) the >>COBOL-WORDS interaction with this format's two keywords and (b) four missing test shapes. Both are closed.

(a) THE DEFECT AND ITS ROOT CAUSE. ANYCASE and LOCALE are ISO 8.9 RESERVED words (cite.py --check 8.9 OK on both; neither is in the 8.10 table) and 7.3.10.3 SR3 therefore admits both as the EXISTING word of a >>COBOL-WORDS directive. The directive was applied by ONE mechanism only — the post-lex token retype (CobolWordsRewriter), which can reach a word solely when the lexer makes it a keyword TOKEN — and both of these words are deliberately left as bare IDENTIFIERs so the 15.94.2 / 15.68.2 phrase parses as ordinary space-separated arguments. So the directive was ACCEPTED and SILENTLY INERT in both directions: `EQUATE "LOCALE" WITH "LOCALITY"` then `TEST-NUMVAL-C(X LOCALITY FR)` rejected legal source with a COBOLNET1504 arity error naming the renamed keyword (measured), and `UNDEFINE "ANYCASE"` still ate the user's own data item as the keyword, switching on case-insensitive currency matching and injecting the compilation-unit currency with no diagnostic (measured: a wrong TEST-NUMVAL-C answer of 1 where 0 is required by 15.94.4 1)a)).

THE FIX IS THE SECOND MECHANISM, ONCE, FOR THE WHOLE CLASS. CobolWordsMap.Resolve is now the ONE reading of 7.3.10.4 GR2/GR3/GR4 (canonical for an EQUATE/SUBSTITUTE synonym, null for an UNDEFINE'd or SUBSTITUTE'd-away word, the word itself otherwise), and every by-name classifier calls it: IntrinsicBinder.KeywordWordOf — the single funnel through which EVERY section-15 phrase word is read, so TRIM, FIND-STRING, SUBSTITUTE, CONVERT, MODULE-NAME, LENGTH and NUMVAL-C/TEST-NUMVAL-C are all covered by one change — plus the parser's text predicates, the SET-statement locale categories, the ALPHABET coded-set names and CALL ... AS NESTED. CobolWordsRewriter.CanonicalWordOf/TokenIs keep the directive applied to a word EXACTLY once (the retype already re-spells what it reaches). Measured population behind the sweep: of the 552 words in 8.9 union 8.10, 447 were in the token map, 17 are lexed but were invisible to it (a multi-spelling rule publishes no ANTLR literal name) and 88 are no token at all.

TWO SIBLING DEFECTS OF THE SAME MECHANISM, ALSO CLOSED. The token map now resolves multi-spelling keywords by asking the lexer itself, and the de-reserve retype matches the token TEXT so `UNDEFINE "ZERO"` frees ZERO without freeing ZEROS and ZEROES (7.3.10.3 SR3 names one COBOL word). And SR3/SR4's category test could only ask the lexer vocabulary, so it rejected every legal directive naming one of the 31 section-8.10 context-sensitive words this compiler does not tokenize (HEX, CURRENT, LC_ALL, ANUM, BYTE, ACTIVATING, STACK, TOP-LEVEL, UCS-4, UTF-8, UTF-16 and the rest) — a generated 8.10 table now answers it, single-sourced from the spec section and drift-tested against it.

(b) TESTS. The three positive shapes the row owed (argument-1 ANYCASE; argument-1 LOCALE ANYCASE; argument-1 LOCALE locale-name-1 ANYCASE) are 2002/pb250_test_numvalc_remaining_shapes, all three verified 0 per 15.94.4 1)a); the stack-exclusion negative under this function's OWN name is negative/pb250-test-numvalc-locale-and-argument2-are-alternatives (15.94.2 + 5.2.6.2, COBOLNET1504). The >>COBOL-WORDS goldens the row asked for are 2023/pb250_cobol_words_phrase_word_equate (GR2 synonym for ANYCASE) and 2023/pb250_cobol_words_phrase_word_undefine (GR3, the user's data item bound as argument-2), with negative/pb250-cobol-words-undefined-keyword-syntax-withdrawn pinning that the withdrawn syntax is no longer available. All eight shapes of the format now have a fixture or a traced derivation, and nothing in the format binds by a rule stated in more than one place.

THE STALE COMMENT the row recorded (IntrinsicBinder.cs, "The LOCALE phrase is the A.4.9 documented non-support") is corrected in the same change set, as is the neighbouring claim that ANYCASE and LOCALE are 8.10 context-sensitive words — they are 8.9 reserved, and the argument-1 exclusion is positional, not a context-sensitivity allowance. EDITIONS unchanged at 2002,2014,2023.

subject: TEST-NUMVAL-F function
notes: CITATION RE-DERIVED: `cite.py --check 15.95.2 "FUNCTION"` -> OK, printing the format verbatim: `<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-NUMVAL-F</u> ( argument-1 )` (General format). CODE READ (not sampled): (1) the reference shape comes from the ONE generic rule `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` in src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4 — TEST-NUMVAL-F is not a reserved word (it is not in the four-word §8.9 n §8.11 set SIGN/SUM/LENGTH/RANDOM), so it arrives through `functionName` and the FNARG_LPAREN retyping makes the '(' the argument list per §8.4.3.2.3 SR6; (2) the ARITY is the catalog row's, `Add(new("TEST-NUMVAL-F", IntrinsicType.Integer, IntrinsicArity.Fixed, 1, 1, "s", "TestNumvalF", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, false, 2002))` inside IntrinsicCatalog.Build; (3) it is ENFORCED at IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore — `if (given < sig.MinArgs || given > sig.MaxArgs)` raises COBOLNET1504 "FUNCTION TEST-NUMVAL-F takes 1 argument(s); N given (ISO §15.3)". subject: VARIANCE function
notes: Rule text re-derived from specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 33974: `FUNCTION VARIANCE ( { argument-1 } ... )` -- FUNCTION and VARIANCE underlined (required), the parenthesised list not bracketed (required), the braced argument-1 followed by an ellipsis (one or more, repeatable). Each element located: (1) the surface shape is the shared Frontend rule src/Cobol.Net.Frontend/Grammar/Core/CobolExpressions.g4#functionCall -- `FUNCTION functionName (FNARG_LPAREN functionArgList? FNARG_RPAREN)? refModPart*` -- with functionArgList = `functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*`, so space- and comma/semicolon-separated repeats both parse; VARIANCE is not in reservedIntrinsicArgFn (only SIGN and SUM are) so it takes the generic FUNCTION-keyword arm. (2) The VARIANCE-specific half is the catalog row read at IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 140: Add(new("VARIANCE", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "n", "Variance", IntrinsicBind.Runtime, true, 85)) -- MinArgs 1, MaxArgs int.MaxValue. (3) That bound is ENFORCED, not decorative: IntrinsicBinder.cs#BindIntrinsicCore lines 572-579 compute `given` (a table(ALL) argument counted as its static element count) and raise COBOLNET1504 "takes at least 1 argument(s)" outside [MinArgs, MaxArgs], so the format's minimum-one is a real rejection. (4) The ellipsis itself is mechanically pinned: IntrinsicSig.RepeatsAnArgument (IntrinsicCatalog.cs line 69) is `MaxArgs == int.MaxValue`, and IntrinsicRepeatedArgumentDriftTests.RepeatsAnArgument_IsExactly_TheFormatsEllipsis READS specs/ISO_COBOL.md, extracts the '#### 15.98.2 General format' block and asserts the catalog row agrees with whether that block contains a literal ellipsis -- a genuinely spec-derived test covering VARIANCE (it iterates every catalogued row, floor >= 79). RepeatsAnArgument is also the ISO 15.3 precondition that admits the ALL subscript, and both render lanes consume the enumerated list as one array (IntrinsicRenderer.cs#ArgArray via DecArgList line 517 and the RenderFloat default arm line 403), so `FUNCTION VARIANCE(TBL(ALL))` is structurally supported. Positive exercise of the written format: tests/conformance/2023/pb56_dec_carrier_intrinsics.cob line 39, `COMPUTE VA = FUNCTION VARIANCE(1, 2, 3)`, registered enabled in tests/conformance/2023/manifest.json line 123. Editions: Annex E (spec lines 42847-44200) carries NO VARIANCE or STANDARD-DEVIATION entry, so there is no edition delta; VARIANCE is in the section 8.11 intrinsic-function-name list (spec line 9710) and is an original Intrinsic Function Module name -- editions left at the batch default, NOT read off the catalog row's IntroducedIn. NOT tested for VARIANCE specifically: the table(ALL) form (pb62_all_subscript_runtime_ranges does not name VARIANCE) and the zero-argument rejection. || REFUTER (independently re-derived; verdict UPHELD as CONFORMS). Format re-read at specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 33974 -- FUNCTION and VARIANCE underlined, list unbracketed, `{ argument-1 } ...`. Grammar confirmed at CobolExpressions.g4 line 333 (functionCall) and lines 351-353 (functionArgList); reservedIntrinsicArgFn at line 343 is SIGN and SUM only, so VARIANCE takes the FUNCTION-keyword arm as claimed. The argument-less shape genuinely reaches the arity gate rather than a zero-argument path: BindIntrinsic line 89 calls BindIntrinsicCore(name, ArgsOf(fc.functionArgList())) and ArgsOf returns [] when the optional paren group is absent, so `FUNCTION VARIANCE` draws COBOLNET1504 -- and the section 8.4.3.2.3 SR6 pre-check at line 87 only diverts a `NAME (start:length)` shape. TWO ATTACKS TRIED AND DEFEATED. (i) Reference modification of a NUMERIC function result -- the general format shows none and the grammar's `refModPart*` admits the tokens -- is rejected: IntrinsicBinder.cs#ResultRefMod lines 180-185 admits only ResultCategory Alphanumeric/National/Boolean and reports COBOLNET1629 citing section 8.4.3.3.3 SR2, so `FUNCTION VARIANCE(1 2 3)(1:2)` is loud. (ii) The grammar's OMITTED alternative inside functionArgument is not a hole in the format: IntrinsicBinder.cs lines 2452-2456 report COBOLNET1544 citing section 8.4.3.2 SR7. The ellipsis's real consequence (the section 15.3 ALL subscript) is generic and driven by sig.RepeatsAnArgument at TryBindAllArgument line 2578, the element enumerates row-major in CobolTable.cs#AllArgs, and the zero-occurrence case that section 15.3 leaves undefined is defined LOUD there (EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION + CobolFatalException, lines 130-135) -- so no VARIANCE body can be entered with an empty list today. THE VALIDATED SET VARIES BY ORGANIZATION, using the permission GR10 grants in its own third sentence: 'The validation of fixed-file attributes may vary depending on the organization or storage medium of the file.' For every organization the ORGANIZATION itself is validated - 9.1.6's primary attribute, of which 9.1.6 names exactly three ('There are three organizations: sequential, relative, and indexed'), so the recorded value is SEQUENTIAL, RELATIVE or INDEXED and 9.1.7.2's record-sequential / line-sequential distinction is NOT part of it. For RELATIVE and INDEXED the record type, the minimum and maximum logical record size and (indexed) the number of record keys and each key's window, DUPLICATES phrase, SUPPRESS WHEN value and collating sequence are validated as well, because those two organizations live in an implementor-defined store whose structure IS those attributes. For SEQUENTIAL nothing further is validated: 9.1.7.2 makes a sequential file's record lengths a property of the data and of the reading program rather than of the file, and 9.1.13.2 items 3, 5 and 7 answer the disagreement with the successful '04', '06' and '09' - writing a print, report or extract file and reading it back under a different record description is the idiom those statuses exist for, so a '39' there would reject legal source and would duplicate RecordLayoutNotice's job. The set is deliberately NOT the empty set item 50 answers for DELETE FILE: a DELETE FILE destroys the file so nothing downstream depends on the description having been right, while a relative or indexed store's structure is read back through it. The three 9.1.6 attributes outside the set for every organization are excluded because this processor cannot give them two different values, not because checking was skipped - the code set (13.18.13.4 GR7 makes it the native character set when no CODE-SET clause is written and GR2/GR6 make it the named alphabet's when one is; COBOLNET1672 refuses every alphabet whose implementor correspondence is not the identity, the A.3 item 27 non-support), the minimum and maximum physical record size (no blocking; BLOCK CONTAINS is inert under A.3 item 5), and the record delimiter (RECORD DELIMITER as a clause has no compiler surface, and the delimiter distinction that IS realized is a sequential-organization attribute, outside the set for the reason above). 9.1.6's own last sentence - whether the ability to share a physical file is a fixed file attribute - is answered NO: a sharing mode is established per file connector (14.9.27.4 GR21-GR23) and arbitrated live (9.1.15 Table 19), so it is not carried by the physical file between run units.

The determination: the interval between the `n TIMES` re-attempts is ZERO — every lock this implementation arbitrates is held by a file connector of the EXECUTING run unit, which cannot release while another statement of that run unit runs, so no releaser can execute between two attempts and a nonzero interval could only delay an identical answer.
